Saints have beaten several other interested clubs to sign exciting back rower James Bentley from Bradford Bulls on a three-year deal.
Dubbed the best player in the Championship “by an absolute mile” by former Saints’ star Leon Pryce, 19-year-old Bentley made his debut for the Bulls against Oldham last season.
He’s gone on to score 15 tries in 23 appearances and has been one of the Bulls’ standout performers.
“James is a quality young player and we are pleased to bring him to the club,” said Saints’ head coach Justin Holbrook.
“He’s powerful, strong and is consistent in his performances week in week out.
“He knows he has a lot of improvement in him, too, and he’s looking forward to developing in our system.”
Bentley played for Oulton Raiders before progressing through Bradford Bulls’ Academy ranks.
He said: “I can’t wait to get over there and get started. It was a big decision to leave, an emotional one as well but I am looking forward to be playing at the top level. It is a decision I’ve made to further my career.
“I’m expecting the step up to be hard, it’s going to be a lot faster and a lot tougher but I am looking forward to and going head first into the challenge.
“I can’t wait to get over there; some of the players that they have like Ben Barba and Jon Wilkin, are just great players. I can learn from them and become a better player.
“I’m committed to the Bulls for the rest of the season I want to finish with my time here on a high.”
rewrite:
St. Helens have secured the signing of promising forward James Bentley from the Bradford Bulls, finalizing a contract that will last for three seasons. They succeeded in this move despite competing offers from a number of rival teams. The 19-year-old talent, who former Saints player Leon Pryce called the undisputed best in the Championship, first appeared for the Bulls in a match against Oldham last year. Since that debut, he has impressed by crossing the line for 15 tries across 23 games, establishing himself as one of Bradford's most notable athletes.

Justin Holbrook, the head coach of Saints, expressed his satisfaction with the acquisition, stating that Bentley is a skilled young prospect with considerable potential. Holbrook highlighted the player's physical strength, power, and reliable week-to-week contributions, while also noting Bentley's own awareness that he can continue to grow and his eagerness to evolve within the Saints' framework.

Bentley's rugby journey began with the Oulton Raiders before he advanced through the Bradford Bulls' developmental academy. Reflecting on his transfer, he acknowledged the difficulty and emotional weight of departing but emphasized his ambition to test himself at the highest competitive tier, viewing the move as essential for his professional advancement. He anticipates the challenge of a more demanding and quicker pace of play but is enthusiastic about embracing it fully.

The young forward also conveyed his excitement about joining a squad featuring accomplished players like Ben Barba and Jon Wilkin, seeing a valuable opportunity to learn from them and enhance his own abilities. Bentley remains dedicated to concluding the current season strongly with the Bulls, aiming for a positive finish before beginning his new chapter.

Dundalk Rugby team continued their preparations for the new season with the club's first transatlantic tour in many years last week.
The Mill Road men set off for St. John's, Newfoundland, Canada at the invitation of Mr. Pat O'Callaghan, a committed and loyal supporter of the club, last Wednesday week.
A game against the locals, Swilers Rugby Club, on Friday saw the tourists come up narrowly short, though the trip remained a thundering success despite the defeat.
The highlights of the tour came off the field, however, as the 35-strong group took in some cod fishing and whale watching in Quid Vidi with the hospitality having been provided by Dr. Noel and Christine Browne.
With the Leinster league to get underway in September, the team will continue their pre-season schedule on Irish soil with the team bonding and experienced gained from the trip sure to stand them in good stead.
The Rugby Club are indebted to their sponsors who made the tour possible.
rewrite: The Dundalk rugby squad advanced their preseason training by embarking on the club's first overseas trip across the Atlantic in a long while. Their journey began last Wednesday, traveling to St. John's in Newfoundland, Canada, following an invitation from a dedicated club patron, Mr. Pat O'Callaghan. Although the visiting side suffered a close loss in a match against the local Swilers Rugby Club on Friday, the overall excursion was considered highly successful. The most memorable moments occurred away from the pitch, as the party of 35 enjoyed activities like cod fishing and observing whales in Quid Vidi, thanks to the generous hosting of Dr. Noel and Christine Browne. As the Leinster league approaches in September, the team will proceed with their domestic preparations, with the camaraderie and insights from this tour providing a solid foundation. The club extends its gratitude to its sponsors for enabling this valuable experience.

BEIJING, April 28 A court in China on Friday jailed a former chairman of Baoshan Iron and Steel, who went on to become vice mayor of Shanghai, to 17 years for bribery and graft, a state broadcaster reported.
President Xi Jinping has waged war on graft for more than four years, vowing that all corrupt officials, from powerful "tigers" to lowly "flies", will be weeded out, and warning that a failure to do so could threaten the ruling Communist Party.
Ai Baojun had used his positions to amass more than 40 million yuan ($5.8 million) in assets from 2000 to 2014, a court in the southern city of Zhangzhou ruled, according to China Central Television (CCTV)
Ai is the most senior official from China's financial hub to be sentenced in the corruption campaign. He could not be reached for comment.
The court also ruled that 5.8 million yuan of Ai's personal assets be confiscated and returned to Baosteel and to Shanghai city, CCTV said.
Ai was given a lenient sentence due to actively providing details of his crimes, which he accepted and apologised for, the court said, adding that many of the bribes were accepted by relatives without his knowledge.
China's top anti-graft watchdog stripped Ai of his party and state positions in January 2016 after an investigation found him guilty of breaking party discipline rules, as well as the crimes he was sentenced for.
According to his official biography, Ai ran Shanghai-based Baoshan Iron and Steel from 1998 to 2007 before taking up a Shanghai vice mayor post until 2013.
He then became head administrator for Shanghai's free-trade zone, the first such zone on the Chinese mainland.
Dai Haibo, a deputy secretary of the Shanghai government and former deputy head of the free trade zone, was stripped of his post in May 2015, following an investigation by the anti-corruption watchdog.
Cui Jian, vice president of the Baosteel Group, the parent of Baoshan Iron and Steel, was placed under investigation in March 2015 on suspicion of "serious disciplinary violations," a euphemism for graft.
Baoshan Iron and Steel declined to comment. (Reporting by Christian Shepherd; Editing by Robert Birsel)
rewrite:
A Chinese court has sentenced a former head of Baoshan Iron and Steel, who later served as a deputy mayor of Shanghai, to 17 years in prison on charges of bribery and corruption, according to state media reports this Friday.

The nation's leader, Xi Jinping, has spearheaded an extensive anti-corruption drive for over four years, pledging to root out dishonest officials at every level of authority. He has emphasized that such misconduct poses a significant risk to the continued governance of the Communist Party.

As per China Central Television, a court in Zhangzhou determined that from 2000 until 2014, the official, Ai Baojun, illegally obtained assets exceeding 40 million yuan (approximately $5.8 million) by exploiting his various roles. Ai represents the highest-ranking figure from China's primary financial center to receive a sentence under this ongoing initiative. Efforts to contact him were unsuccessful.

The court additionally ordered the seizure and return of 5.8 million yuan from Ai's personal wealth to both Baosteel and the Shanghai municipal government. In its ruling, the court noted a reduced sentence was granted because Ai cooperated by confessing to his offenses, expressed remorse, and stated that many bribes were received by family members without his direct awareness.

Following a probe that found him in violation of party conduct regulations and the subsequent criminal charges, China's primary disciplinary body expelled Ai from his political and governmental posts in January 2016.

Ai's career included leading Baoshan Iron and Steel from 1998 to 2007, after which he assumed the role of Shanghai vice mayor until 2013. He subsequently oversaw the administration of Shanghai's pioneering free-trade zone.

In related developments, Dai Haibo, a former deputy head of that trade zone and a Shanghai government deputy secretary, was removed from his position in May 2015 after a disciplinary investigation. Furthermore, in March 2015, Cui Jian, a vice president at Baosteel Group, was probed for alleged serious breaches of discipline, a term often denoting corruption.

Baoshan Iron and Steel offered no statement regarding the sentencing.

TULSA, Okla. (AP) - A Tulsa police sergeant will be the face of a new cable TV show aimed at looking at law enforcement work from officers' perspective.
A&E says Sgt. Sean Larkin is host of "PD Cam." The 30-minute show will offer unfiltered video from police body-worn, dashboard and helicopter cameras.
Larkin has worked for Tulsa police more than 20 years and says law enforcement has gotten negative media coverage in recent years. He says the show will help police work become more transparent.
"PD Cam" debuts July 19.
Tulsa Police Chief Chuck Jordan in 2017 canceled his department's contract with another A&E show. Critics say the real-time "Live PD" shows incidents of racial profiling and caters to viewers' worst fears and biases. Jordan said it made his city look bad.

rewrite:
A new cable television program on A&E will feature Tulsa Police Sergeant Sean Larkin as its host. The series, titled "PD Cam," intends to present law enforcement activities directly through the lens of officers. It will utilize raw footage captured by body, vehicle, and aerial cameras. Larkin, a two-decade veteran, believes the show can foster transparency, countering what he views as predominantly negative media portrayals of police work. The half-hour program premieres on July 19.

This follows Police Chief Chuck Jordan's 2017 termination of the department's involvement with "Live PD," a prior A&E series. That program faced criticism for allegedly highlighting racial profiling and exploiting public anxieties. Jordan concluded its depiction was damaging to Tulsa's reputation.

Coffee lovers, we have some bad news: No two cups of Joe are completely the same. And while you’re out here spending big bucks on your daily morning brew—it’s just one of the problems all coffee lovers understand—don’t you want to maximize its rise-and-shine powers?
Thankfully, HuffPost, the Center for Science in the Public Interest, and EnergyFiend.com teamed up to give us the scoop on just how much bang we’re getting for our buck at our favorite coffee chains. As it turns out, the milligrams of caffeine per ounce of coffee vary from chain to chain. You can view the complete round-up here.
McDonald’s coffee might be a cheap on-the-go beverage, but odds are, its caffeination powers won’t last long; one cup only contains nine milligrams of caffeine. On the other hand, Dunkin’ Donuts and Peet’s Brewed Coffees fall in the middle of the spectrum, with 12.7 and 16.7 mg of caffeine respectively. Starbucks packs a punch at 20.6 mg of caffeine, so if you need a serious wake-up call, it might be worth it to splurge on that $5 beverage. (On another note, you’ll never believe what Starbucks was almost called.)
But to get really hyped up, go for a coffee from Deathwish. This self-proclaimed brewer of the world’s strongest coffee is no lie; just one cup contains a whopping 54.2 mg per ounce of caffeine. But don’t worry, the website assures us, one cup won’t actually kill you. In fact, it turns out that you can drink way more coffee than originally thought—and actually live longer, too.
rewrite:
For coffee enthusiasts, there's an unfortunate reality: each cup of coffee is unique. As you invest in your daily ritual—a common dilemma among aficionados—it's natural to seek the most energizing option.

Fortunately, insights from HuffPost, the Center for Science in the Public Interest, and EnergyFiend.com reveal how much caffeine your money buys at popular cafes. The concentration of caffeine per ounce differs significantly across brands. Detailed findings are available through their combined report.

While McDonald's offers an affordable, convenient choice, its caffeine content is modest at just nine milligrams per cup, providing a brief boost. Dunkin' Donuts and Peet's brewed options offer moderate levels, with 12.7 and 16.7 milligrams respectively. Starbucks delivers a stronger jolt at 20.6 milligrams, making its higher price potentially justifiable for those needing a robust start.

For the ultimate surge, Deathwish Coffee claims the title of world's strongest, containing a remarkable 54.2 milligrams per ounce. Despite its alarming name, the company states a cup isn't lethal. Research even suggests that higher coffee consumption may be linked to increased longevity, allowing you to enjoy that potent brew without fear.

Don't want to watch someone else play video games? Fair enough – but Twitch has something else on tap that every kind of PC player can get behind: free games. If you're an Amazon Prime subscriber, then you automatically have access to Twitch Prime. It's a service that eliminates ads from videos, lets you grant free monthly subscriptions to support streamers, and now includes several free games each month.
Even if you'll never use the streaming service, all Amazon Prime subscribers should snag the free Twitch Prime subscription and download these free PC games from the Twitch desktop app; they're yours to keep forever. And if you do love and use Twitch, then Prime and its myriad goodies is just the cherry on top.
The selection will change monthly, so we'll keep this space updated as new games arrive. For July, Twitch is giving away a staggering 21 free games in honour of Amazon's upcoming Prime Day, with new titles rolling out daily 'til then. But some are only available for a couple days or maybe a week, so be sure to mind the dates listed below.

James Arthur "assumes everyone is bisexual".
The 30-year-old musician has weighed in on the criticism surrounding Rita Ora's new single 'Girls' - which was slammed for "exploiting" bisexuality in its lyrics, despite Rita insisting she was writing from experience - and says he isn't surprised by the star's sexuality, as in this day an age he says "most girls fancy other girls".
He said: "I did see that there was quite a bit of backlash for the song. I respect people shedding light and standing up for the LGBT community - that's a great thing.
"If that's what it is, you know, and not an attempt for publicity, then fair play. I kind of assumed everyone is bisexual these days. I think most girls I know fancy other girls, it's not something unusual in 2018.
"So Rita saying I kissed a girl doesn't make me step back in amazement. It doesn't shock. Each to their own, that's great."
The 'Say You Won't Let Go' hitmaker has admitted he doesn't "feel the urge" to explore relationships with his own sex, but insists he can "appreciate a handsome man".
He added to The Sun's bizarre column: "What percentage do I have to be to appreciate a good-looking man? I definitely think a lot of guys are handsome. I don't feel the urge to act upon it but I can appreciate a handsome man for sure."
James' comments come after Rita - who recorded her new single alongside Charli XCX, Bebe Rexha, and Cardi B - received backlash from the LGBT community when it was claimed the lyrics to her song exploited bisexuality.
Recently, Charli XCX leapt to the singer's defence, insisting the song was written using a "valid" experience Rita had had with a female.
She said: "I know from when Rita invited me to be a part of the song, this song was about a specific experience that she had with a woman.

He added that if the motivation behind the song is genuine rather than a search for attention, then that is acceptable. BARCELONA, April 30 Rafael Nadal won a record-extending 10th Barcelona Open title on Sunday by thrashing Dominic Thiem of Austria 6-4 6-1, collecting his second claycourt title in a row.
Nadal, who won the Monte Carlo Masters for a 10th time last week, romped to the title without dropping a set on the newly renamed Rafa Nadal court at the Real Tennis Club in Barcelona, and needed just 90 minutes to finish off Thiem.
Thiem had beaten the 14-times Grand Slam champion on clay in the Argentina Open last year and earned a place in the final by beating world number one Andy Murray for the first time in his career on Saturday, but he proved no match for Nadal.
The Mallorcan took a while to impose himself on Thiem on an overcast day in Barcelona with the cold weather slowing down the court.
Thiem earned the first breakpoint of the match but Nadal recovered and eventually took the first set by breaking his opponent in the 10th game.
There was no let-up in the second set from Nadal, who broke the 23-year-old Austrian twice in a row before serving for the championship. (Editing by Clare Fallon)
rewrite:
On Sunday in Barcelona, Rafael Nadal secured his tenth championship at the Barcelona Open, defeating Austria's Dominic Thiem in straight sets, 6-4, 6-1. This victory marks his second consecutive tournament win on clay. Just one week after earning a tenth title at the Monte Carlo Masters, Nadal dominated the event without losing a single set. The final was played on a court recently dedicated in his honor at the Real Tennis Club and concluded in only ninety minutes.

Thiem had previously bested the fourteen-time Grand Slam winner on clay at last year's Argentina Open and reached this final by defeating world number one Andy Murray for the first time on Saturday. However, he was ultimately overpowered by Nadal. Cool, cloudy conditions made the court play slower, and the Spaniard initially took some time to find his rhythm. Although Thiem created the first break opportunity, Nadal rallied and sealed the opening set with a break in the tenth game.

The second set saw no respite from Nadal's intensity. He secured two consecutive breaks against the 23-year-old Austrian and then confidently served to claim the trophy.

০ = 0, ১ = 1, ২ = 2, ৩ = 3, ৪ = 4, ৫ = 5, ৬ = 6, ৭ = 7, ৮ = 8, ৯ = 9
্ = See example (Hasant/Viram) ় = * (Nukta) ʼ = ' (Urdhacomma) ঽ = & (Avagrah) ৺ = ~ (Isshar) ৹ = a~ (Bengali ana sign) ৲ = Rs~ (Bengali Rupee sign) ৳ = T~ (Taka sign) । = | (Devanagari danda) ॥ = || (Devanagari double danda) ₹ = Rs (Indian Rupee sign) 卐 = +~ (Swastika sign) Zero Width Joiner = ^ Zero Width Non Joiner = ^^
These symbols will type Bengali characters first but if "~" will be followed, it will remove previously typed Bengali character and then type the symbol.
Symbols & ~ * : ^ | ' have special meaning. You can type this way & = &~ ~ = ~~ * = *~ : = :~ ^ = ^~ | = |~ ' = '~
The English symbols [ ] { } ( ) < > - + / = ; . , " ? ! % \ _ $ @ # translate into the same symbols.
Example নমস্কার can be written by typing "namaskaar"
As per Rule # 3, ligature will be rendered. ZWJ and ZWNJ characters are used to produce alternate rendering of ligature.
A consonant followed by ZWJ character will produce half-formed consonant character.
Example
প্রশ্ন = prashn
প্রশ্‍ন = prash^n
A consonant followed by ZWNJ character will produce dead consonant character.
Example
প্রশ্ন = prashn
প্রশ্‌ন = prash^^n
If two english characters are making one Bengali Vowel (i.e. ai, au), then
ZWJ character is used to separate them into two different vowels. It will not
add ZWJ character but only considered as the separator between two
vowels.
rewrite:
The Bengali numeral system corresponds to Arabic digits as follows: ০ represents 0, ১ is 1, ২ equals 2, ৩ stands for 3, ৪ denotes 4, ৫ corresponds to 5, ৬ is 6, ৭ equals 7, ৮ stands for 8, and ৯ denotes 9.

Various diacritics and signs have specific representations: the Hasant or Viram is shown with an example, the Nukta is an asterisk (*), the Urdhacomma is an apostrophe ('), and the Avagrah is an ampersand (&). The Isshar is a tilde (~), the Bengali ana sign is 'a~', and currency symbols include 'Rs~' for the Rupee sign, 'T~' for the Taka, and 'Rs' for the Indian Rupee. Punctuation marks are the single danda (|) and double danda (||). The Swastika is '+~'. Special control characters are the Zero Width Joiner (^) and Zero Width Non Joiner (^^).

When typing, these symbols initially produce Bengali characters. However, if a tilde (~) is typed immediately after, it deletes the preceding Bengali character and then inserts the intended symbol. Certain symbols carry special functions: to type them literally, one must append a tilde, such as &~ for an ampersand, ~~ for a tilde, *~ for an asterisk, :~ for a colon, ^~ for a caret, |~ for a vertical bar, and '~ for an apostrophe.

Standard English punctuation and symbols—including brackets, braces, parentheses, angle brackets, hyphens, plus signs, slashes, equals signs, semicolons, periods, commas, quotation marks, question marks, exclamation points, percent signs, backslashes, underscores, dollar signs, at signs, and number signs—are entered directly and appear identically.

For instance, the word "নমস্কার" is typed as "namaskaar". Following the system's third rule, ligatures are automatically formed. The Zero Width Joiner (ZWJ) and Zero Width Non Joiner (ZWNJ) are employed to modify these ligature presentations.

Placing a ZWJ after a consonant yields a half-form of that consonant. For example, "prashn" produces "প্রশ্ন", while "prash^n" results in "প্রশ্‍ন". Conversely, using a ZWNJ after a consonant creates a dead consonant form; "prash^^n" types as "প্রশ্‌ন".

When two English letters combine to create a single Bengali vowel sound, like 'ai' or 'au', inserting a ZWJ character between them will separate them into distinct vowels. This does not add an actual ZWJ to the output but simply instructs the system to treat the letters independently.

BRASILIA Major Latin American currencies appear more likely to hold their ground in coming months than they did in March, but they remain vulnerable to increased volatility coming from abroad, a Reuters poll showed on Thursday.
Estimates from top banks and research firms still suggest the currencies will probably give back part of their recent gains.
However, one-year forecasts for the Mexican peso and the Brazilian real against the U.S. dollar firmed from last month's poll, indicating reduced expectations of a complete reversal in the region's largest currency markets.
The 12-month forecasts strengthened for the Mexican peso to 19.875 per dollar from 20.87 in March and the Brazilian real to 3.295 from 3.35. Also gaining were the Colombian peso to 3020.0 from 3054.17 and the Chilean peso at 669.13 from 670.
Outlooks weakened for the Argentine peso, to 18.0 per dollar from 17.60 in March, and the Peruvian sol, to 3.38 from 3.36.
The Mexican peso has led gains among Latin American currencies this year, rebounding from all-time lows on hopes that U.S. President Donald Trump will not impose heavy tariffs on Mexican exports to the United States as he had threatened.
A series of interest rate increases by the Mexican central bank and its direct intervention in local currency markets with hedging contracts also explain the peso's newfound strength. As long as volatility remains low, higher interest rates should keep supporting the peso.
"Carry attractiveness has increased notably," wrote Rabobank senior strategist Christian Lawrence. "This is particularly true compared to other Latin American currencies," including Brazil, Chile and Colombia, which have cut rates over the past year.
Volatility has also declined in Brazil to around record lows, central bank chief Ilan Goldfajn said this week, despite what he called an "especially uncertain global outlook."
A source of potential instability is the U.S. Federal Reserve, which has so far raised interest rates at a very gradual pace, with no surprises. An acceleration of rate hikes could drain capital from higher-yielding emerging markets such as Latin America.
(Additional reporting by Noe Torres in Mexico City, Nelson Bocanegra in Bogota, Hernan Nessi in Buenos Aires, Ursula Scollo in Santiago; Editing by Ross Finley and Lisa Von Ahn)
rewrite:
According to a recent Reuters survey of financial institutions, key currencies in Latin America are now in a somewhat stronger position than they were in March, though they continue to face risks from external market instability. Analysts from leading banks and advisory groups anticipate these currencies will relinquish some of their recent advances.

Nevertheless, one-year projections for the Mexican peso and the Brazilian real have improved compared to last month’s survey, signaling diminished fears of a full retreat in the region’s most significant foreign exchange markets. The forecast for the Mexican peso strengthened to 19.875 per U.S. dollar, up from 20.87 in March, while the Brazilian real firmed to 3.295 from 3.35. The Colombian peso also saw a brighter outlook, moving to 3020.0 from 3054.17, and the Chilean peso edged up to 669.13 from 670. In contrast, expectations weakened for the Argentine peso, declining to 18.0 per dollar from 17.60, and the Peruvian sol, which fell to 3.38 from 3.36.

The Mexican peso has been the standout performer in the region this year, recovering from historic lows. This rebound is largely driven by optimism that U.S. President Donald Trump may not follow through on earlier threats to impose severe tariffs on goods imported from Mexico. Additional support has come from Mexico’s central bank, which has raised interest rates multiple times and actively intervened in domestic currency markets using hedging instruments. These higher rates are expected to continue bolstering the peso, provided market fluctuations stay subdued.

Christian Lawrence, a senior strategist at Rabobank, noted that the peso’s appeal for carry trades has grown significantly, especially relative to other regional currencies like those of Brazil, Chile, and Colombia, where interest rates have been reduced over the past year. In Brazil, central bank president Ilan Goldfajn recently observed that market volatility has fallen to near historic lows, even amid what he described as a highly unpredictable international environment.

A possible threat to this stability stems from the U.S. Federal Reserve. While the Fed has so far increased rates slowly and predictably, any quickening in the pace of these hikes could trigger capital outflows from higher-yielding emerging economies, including those in Latin America.

SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) -- Frankie Ferrari had 19 points and Jordan Ratinho scored 17 to help San Francisco beat Santa Clara 70-59 on Saturday night.
Ferrari and Ratinho combined to shoot 14 of 23 from the field, including 4 of 7 from 3-point range. Matt McCarthy added 12 points on 6-of-9 shooting for USF (13-12, 5-7 West Coast Conference).
The Dons used runs of 14-4 and 9-0 to open a 14-point first-half lead before going into the break with a 35-23 advantage. KJ Feagin scored 11 points, and Henrik Jadersten scored the final six, in a 19-5 spurt that made it 42-all with 14 minutes to play, but Ratinho answered with a 3 and then made a layup to push the lead back to five points. Feagin's layup trimmed Santa Clara's deficit to 58-57 with five minutes left, but Ferrari countered with a 3-point play and the Broncos made just 1 of 10 from the field from there.
Feagin had 15 points, and Henry Caruso scored 12, for Santa Clara (8-16, 5-7).
USF shot 55 percent from the field and outrebounded the Broncos 34-21.

Matt McCarthy contributed another 12 points for USF, which improved its record to 13-12 overall and 5-7 in conference play.

San Francisco established control early, using significant scoring stretches to build a 35-23 halftime lead. Santa Clara rallied after the break, with KJ Feagin and Henrik Jadersten keying a 19-5 run to tie the game. Ratinho responded with five quick points to regain the lead for USF. The Broncos closed within a point late, but Ferrari converted a three-point play, and Santa Clara then managed only one field goal in its final ten attempts.

Feagin finished with 15 points for Santa Clara (8-16, 5-7), and Henry Caruso added 12. The Dons’ win was bolstered by 55 percent shooting and a dominant 34-21 rebounding advantage.

Middle Belt youths dissociate region from Igbo quit notice
By Nkiruka Nnorom
Middle belt youths have condemned the recent quit notice issued Igbo living in the North by Arewa Youth Consultative Forum, saying Igbo, just like other Nigerians, have the right to live in any part of the country.
The youths, acting on the platform of All Middle Belt Youth Forum, AMBYF, said in a statement by the National Leader, Mr. Aluh Moses, and the National Secretary, Mr. Andzayi Jonathan, that the entire Middle Belt region was not part of the act.
According to the statement, “we condemn, in very strong terms, the so-called Kaduna Declaration by northern youths’ coalition in its entirety, as it is a deliberate act of driving wedge between northerners and easterners.
“That the Middle Belt region is not part of the northern region. Hence, the All Middle Belt Youth Forum distances itself and the entire Middle Belt region from such obnoxious declaration.”
They urged the northern youths to retract the declaration in the interest of peace and security.

The youths called upon the northern coalition to withdraw its statement to preserve national harmony and safety. They stressed that such inflammatory rhetoric threatens the country's stability. Lafia – Africa’s richest man and Chairman of Dangote Group, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, has said that he would like to be known as the biggest philanthropist on the continent.
Dangote stated this on Wednesday in Lafia while disbursing N130 million micro grant to 13,000 vulnerable and less privileged women in Nasarawa State.
“I do not only want to be known as Africa’s richest man but the biggest philanthropist in Africa. I will continue to use my resources and my voice to help shape a better Nigeria and Africa as a whole,” he said.
Dangote said he started the foundation in 1993 to improve the lives of the less fortunate and make a positive difference in the growth of Nigeria.
He said the four major goals of the foundation were health and nutrition, education, economic empowerment and disaster relief.
He explained that the grant scheme was one of the components of the economic empowerment programme of the foundation.
Dangote said it was aimed at providing disadvantaged and vulnerable women in the country with a one-off unconditional N10, 000 cash transfer to boost their household income generation.
” This we believe will help their vulnerability and meet their livelihood needs,” he added .
He explained that the programme, which was launched a few years ago, was targeted at a minimum of 1,000 women in each of the 774 local government areas across the country.
“It is estimated that we would spend about N10 billion with some states with a large population getting a little bit more.
“We at Aliko Dangote foundation are happy to continue providing support to the most vulnerable and deserving members of the society across the country,” he said. (NAN)
rewrite:
During a ceremony in Lafia, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, the wealthiest individual in Africa and head of the Dangote Group, expressed his aspiration to be recognized foremost for his charitable giving across the continent. The event involved distributing micro-grants totaling 130 million naira to 13,000 underprivileged women in Nasarawa State.

Dangote emphasized that beyond his financial status, he desires his legacy to be that of Africa's most significant benefactor. He pledged to persistently employ his wealth and influence to contribute to a brighter future for Nigeria and the wider African region. He traced the origins of his philanthropic work to the establishment of his foundation in 1993, created to enhance living conditions for the needy and positively impact national development.

The foundation, he noted, focuses on four primary areas: health and nutrition, education, economic empowerment, and disaster response. The grant initiative falls under the economic empowerment pillar. Its objective is to offer a single, unconditional cash transfer of 10,000 naira to impoverished and at-risk women, thereby augmenting their families' earnings. Dangote stated this direct support is intended to reduce their hardship and address essential living costs.

This nationwide program, initiated several years ago, aims to reach no fewer than 1,000 women in every one of Nigeria's 774 local government districts. The projected total expenditure is approximately 10 billion naira, with more populous states receiving slightly larger allocations. Dangote concluded by affirming his foundation's commitment to consistently aiding the most vulnerable and needy individuals throughout Nigerian society.

A two-year-old girl died Tuesday being struck by a car in a southwest Las Vegas hospital parking lot on April 23. (Gai Phanalasy / FOX5)
A two-year-old girl died Tuesday being struck by a car in a southwest Las Vegas hospital parking lot on April 23.
Metro Police said at about 3:13 p.m. that day, the girl was walking with her family between cars at the St. Rose Pediatrics parking lot, near Buffalo Drive and the 215 freeway. A Mercedes Benz was passing through the lot and hit her.
The driver, a 35-year-old Las Vegas man, was cooperative and stayed on the scene. No impairment was involved, police said.
The girl appeared to have a severe head injury, police said, and was taken into UMC Trauma for treatment. Police said she died on May 8 at UMC.
Metro police said the girl's mother was directly supervising her daughter when the crash happened.
Doctors called the injury "horrific," police said.
A 31-year-old woman, a two year-old girl and a six-month-old girl were also in the car, but no one inside was hurt, Metro said.

The driver, a 35-year-old local man, remained at the location and cooperated with authorities. Police confirmed he showed no signs of impairment.

The child suffered what was described as a catastrophic head injury and was transported to UMC Trauma for care. She ultimately succumbed to her injuries on May 8. Officers noted the girl's mother was actively supervising her at the time of the accident.

Three other individuals were in the vehicle—a 31-year-old woman and two other young children—but none sustained injuries. Medical professionals characterized the toddler's trauma as horrific.

ANKARA (Reuters) - The deputy chairman of Turkey's main opposition Republican People's Party (CHP) said illegal acts were being carried out in favor of the government in Sunday's referendum on expanding the powers of the presidency.
"Many illegal acts are being carried out in favor of the government right now, but 'No' will win in the end," Erdal Aksunger told reporters at his party headquarters, referring to an election board decision to accept unstamped ballots.
A statement on the High Electoral Board's (YSK) website hours before polls closed said it would count ballots that had not been stamped by its officials as valid unless they could be proved fraudulent, citing a high number of complaints that YSK officials at polling stations had failed to stamp them.
With 80 percent of ballots opened, support for the constitutional changes that could hand President Tayyip Erdogan sweeping new powers stood at 53.9 percent, according to the state-run Anadolu news agency.
(Reporting by Gulsen Solaker; Writing by Ece Toksabay)
rewrite:

Erdal Aksunger, the party's deputy leader, stated to journalists at the CHP headquarters that numerous violations were underway in support of the government. He expressed confidence, however, that the "No" campaign would ultimately prevail. His remarks followed an electoral board ruling to allow unstamped voting papers.

Shortly before voting ended, the High Electoral Board (YSK) announced on its website that it would deem unstamped ballots acceptable unless fraud was demonstrated. This decision responded to many reports that YSK officials at polling places had neglected to stamp them.

The state-operated Anadolu agency reported that with 80% of votes tallied, approximately 53.9% supported the constitutional amendments, which would grant President Tayyip Erdogan considerably expanded powers.

(Reporting by Gulsen Solaker; Writing by Ece Toksabay)

The first of 10 people killed in the Toronto van attack has been identified as an employee of a US-based investment management firm, according to a report.
Anne-Marie D’Amico worked at the Canadian headquarters of Invesco located near the mile-long stretch where Alek Minassian allegedly plowed a Ryder rental van into a lunch-hour crowd, killing 10 people and injuring 15, according to the CBC.
Peter Intraligi, president of Invesco Canada, confirmed her death to the outlet.
“Our thoughts and prayers continue to be with all those impacted by this tragic event,” Intraligi said. “I can now confirm that unfortunately one of our employees has succumbed to her injuries. Out of respect for her and her family, we will not be providing any further comments.”
Minassian, 25, was due to appear in a Toronto courtroom at 10 a.m. Tuesday. Police said that charges against the suspect would be provided at that time.
The incident began about 1:30 p.m. Monday around Yonge Street and Finch Avenue and ended when Minassian was collared about a half-hour later after trying to goad police into shooting him.
“We’re all putting our pieces together to see exactly what we have,” said Toronto police Chief Mark Saunders, adding that the attack “definitely appeared deliberate.”
Garry Clement, a former Royal Canadian Mounted Police chief and, told the CBC that he thinks the cops involved “deserve to be commended because they demonstrated a lot of restraint.”
Footage shot by a bystander showed police arresting the man as he shouted: “Kill me” and pointed an object at a cop, who replied, “No, get down!”
When the suspect said, “I have a gun in my pocket,” the officer responded: “I don’t care! Get down!”
The attack shook the usually tranquil streets of Toronto, a major tourist destination. The city, which has a population of 2.8 million, recorded 61 murders last year, Reuters reported.
“This kind of tragic incident is not representative of how we live and who we are,” Mayor John Tory told reporters.
Prime Minister Justin Trudeau called the incident a “tragic and senseless attack.”
The city’s iconic CN Tower, which is normally lit up in the evening, went dark Monday evening.

input: How much money do American teachers make? If your answer to that question is "not enough," you are definitely not wrong! But as recent teacher strikes have highlighted, some states are doing a much worse job of keeping teachers housed and fed than others. The folks at personal finance site HowMuch put together some maps of the average teacher salary in all 50 states using data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, and there is way too much variation here for our liking. The maps showing middle and high school teachers' average earnings, which you can see over at HowMuch, show a similar pattern. HowMuch averaged out the median elementary, middle and high school teacher salary to calculate the top 10 states for teacher pay overall: 1. New York: $81,613 2. Alaska: $80,627 3. Connecticut: $78,567 4. California: $76,523 5. Massachusetts: $75,720 6. New Jersey: $72,460 7. Oregon: $69,643 8. Virginia: $68,707 9. Maryland: $67,173 10. Rhode Island: $67,050 [HowMuch] Not on the top ten list? West Virginia, Kentucky, Oklahoma, Colorado and Arizona, where teachers have walked out to protest low wages and insufficient benefits in recent months. If the wave of strikes continues, maybe teachers can turn all the light blue states on the above map regular blue. Or even — dare we hope? — dark blue.
rewrite:

The financial website HowMuch visualized this disparity, creating maps from Bureau of Labor Statistics data that plot average teacher salaries nationwide. The degree of difference from one state to another is striking and concerning.

A consistent trend is visible in the separate maps for secondary school instructors available on the site. HowMuch determined an overall ranking by averaging median salaries across elementary, middle, and high school levels. The leading ten states are:
1. New York: $81,613
2. Alaska: $80,627
3. Connecticut: $78,567
4. California: $76,523
5. Massachusetts: $75,720
6. New Jersey: $72,460
7. Oregon: $69,643
8. Virginia: $68,707
9. Maryland: $67,173

If the current surge of labor actions persists, educators might successfully shift the lighter shades on such maps toward the deeper blues representing higher wages—a change many would welcome.

There is no shortage of options.
"We have a very good understanding of the needs of our football team," Newsome said. "What we try to do is to match that with the players."
Some things to know about the Ravens' draft:
TIGHT END NEEDED
The leading receiver on the team last season was tight end Benjamin Watson, who joined the Saints as a free agent.
A replacement is sorely needed, and after failing to secure one through free agency, the Ravens will look to snag one in the draft.
"There are some pretty good ones out there. And they're of the athletic variety, pass-catching tight ends that certainly could help impact our offence," said Joe Horitz, director of college scouting.
One of Newsome's best picks was tight end Todd Heap, selected in the first round in 2001 even though the Ravens already had future Hall of Fame star Shannon Sharpe.
TRADE OR NOT?
Newsome cryptically mentioned the possibility of trading the No. 16 pick, but DeCosta likes the idea of drafting in the middle of the round.
"We're in a good spot for a lot of different reasons," DeCosta said. "I think 16 is a good spot to be in this draft. It plays well to our needs and different strategies."
VOLCANO BREWING
Coach John Harbaugh has been in the Ravens draft room since 2008, and when it comes time for Baltimore to make a pick, he just gets out of the way.
"I'll tell you, it's like a volcano, kind of. It's festering, like, 'Is this thing going to blow?' It never quite blows, but there's so much tension," Harbaugh said.
In the end, though, it's Newsome's call.
"Ozzie pulls the trigger and makes a decision," Harbaugh said, "and we all feel good about it."
HITS, MISSES AND BARGAINS
Perriman missed the entire 2015 season with a knee injury, caught 33 passes in 2016 and last season had a mere 10 catches for the league's 29th-ranked passing attack.
Newsome also struck out with safety Matt Elam at No. 32 overall in 2013. But he recently found two fourth-round gems: Defensive end Brent Urban in 2014 and offensive lineman Alex Lewis in 2016.
___
For more NFL coverage: http://www.pro32.ap.org and http://www.twitter.com/AP_NFL
By David Ginsburg, The Associated Press
rewrite:
The Ravens face a wide array of possibilities as they approach the draft. General Manager Ozzie Newsome stated that the organization has a clear grasp of the team's requirements and aims to align those needs with the right athletes.

Key points regarding Baltimore's draft strategy include:

**ADDRESSING THE TIGHT END POSITION**
Last season's top pass-catcher, Benjamin Watson, has departed via free agency, creating a significant void. Having not filled this gap in free agency, the Ravens are expected to target a tight end in the draft. Joe Horitz, the director of college scouting, noted that several promising, athletic prospects are available who specialize in receiving and could bolster the offensive production. Newsome has a history of success at this position, having chosen Todd Heap in the first round years ago despite the presence of an established star.

**EVALUATING DRAFT POSITION**
While Newsome hinted at potentially dealing their first-round selection, assistant general manager Eric DeCosta expressed comfort with picking at the sixteenth spot. He believes that position offers flexibility and aligns well with the team's various objectives and plans.

**THE DRAFT ROOM DYNAMIC**
Head coach John Harbaugh, a fixture in the draft room for a decade, described the atmosphere as intensely pressurized, comparing it to a simmering volcano that never actually erupts. Despite the palpable tension, the final choice rests with Newsome. Harbaugh affirmed that when the general manager makes the selection, the entire staff supports the decision.

**ASSESSING PAST SELECTIONS**
The team's draft history includes both disappointments and successes. For instance, wide receiver Breshad Perriman has struggled with injuries and limited production since being chosen. Similarly, safety Matt Elam, a first-round pick, did not meet expectations. However, Newsome has also uncovered valuable contributors in the middle rounds, such as defensive lineman Brent Urban and offensive lineman Alex Lewis, both selected in the fourth round.

This analysis provides insight into the Ravens' draft considerations and historical patterns as they prepare to make their selections.

Over time, however, Edmonton’s location — and, in particular, the lack of direct flights from New York — came to feel like a plus, rather than a minus.
Advertisement Continue reading the main story
“There was something attractive about doing it in a place where there wouldn’t be a whole set of eyes seeing the work and judging it before it’s fully baked,” Ms. Chavkin, who had never been to Edmonton and had never heard of Citadel, said.
Then there was the money.
The American dollar stretches further in Canada. And Citadel was not asking for much — the theater agreed to spend what it usually spends to stage a musical (about $600,000 Canadian) and also agreed not to seek a royalty from future productions (nonprofits that help develop commercial shows often get a percentage of Broadway profits).
The commercial producers would pay the rest of the costs, and bring their own sound and lighting equipment, a revolving stage, and significant set elements to upgrade what they would find at Citadel.
Photo
“There was no question it was financially in our interest to go to Canada,” said Ms. Isaacs, who is producing the show along with Mr. Kirdahy, Dale Franzen, and Hunter Arnold.
During just three weeks of rehearsal and four previews, Ms. Chavkin restaged the show several times over, with new cast members, including Reeve Carney (“Spider-Man: Turn Off the Dark”), in three of the five main roles. At first, a rail line bisected the stage; the creative team scrapped that design after a single performance. There were several experiments with how best to deploy characters added for the Edmonton production in an effort to bring to life, as it were, those toiling away in hell.
“We’re trying to walk this line between maintaining the metaphorical and poetic world, and also trying to deliver a satisfying story,” Ms. Mitchell said. “The only way we know where it comfortably wants to sit is by going too far in one direction or another.”
The Citadel says that if it worked on a Broadway-aimed show again, it would dedicate a staffer to managing relations with the commercial producers, because immigration and budget issues proved more time-consuming than anticipated.
rewrite:
Edmonton’s geographical situation, especially its absence of nonstop air connections from New York, gradually began to seem like an advantage rather than a drawback. For director Rachel Chavkin, who was unfamiliar with both the city and the Citadel Theatre, there was an appeal in developing a production away from intense scrutiny, where the work could evolve without being prematurely assessed by a broad audience.

Financial considerations also played a key role. The favorable exchange rate increased the purchasing power of the American dollar in Canada. Moreover, the Citadel’s requirements were modest: the theater committed only its standard musical production budget—approximately 600,000 Canadian dollars—and waived any claim to royalties from potential future stagings, a departure from the norm where nonprofit incubators typically share in later commercial earnings. The remaining expenses were covered by the commercial producers, who also supplied their own advanced technical equipment, a rotating stage platform, and major scenic components to enhance the theater’s existing facilities.

Producer Tom Kirdahy, along with co-producers Dale Franzen and Hunter Arnold, affirmed that the economic rationale for choosing Canada was clear and compelling.

The Edmonton run became a period of intensive revision. In a condensed timeline of three weeks of rehearsals and four preview performances, Chavkin repeatedly reworked the staging, integrating new actors into three of the five principal parts. An initial concept featuring a railway track dividing the stage was abandoned after just one show. The creative team also tested various ways to incorporate ensemble members unique to this production, aiming to vividly portray the souls laboring in a hellish realm.

Writer Anaïs Mitchell described the process as navigating a delicate balance: preserving the piece’s allegorical and lyrical essence while crafting a narratively compelling experience. She noted that finding the right equilibrium often required pushing boundaries to extremes in either direction.

Reflecting on the collaboration, the Citadel noted that any future partnership on a production with Broadway aspirations would benefit from assigning a dedicated point person to liaise with commercial producers. The theater found that logistical challenges, particularly concerning cross-border immigration and budget coordination, demanded more time and effort than initially foreseen.

An employee stands outside a Lowe's home improvement chain in Austin, Texas, U.S., February 27, 2017. REUTERS/Mohammad Khursheed
NEW YORK Shares of home improvement retailer Lowe's Companies Inc (LOW.N) could rise by 20 percent or more, helped by better projected earnings growth this year and greater room for margin improvement, Barron's said on Sunday.
Companies such as Lowe's and Home Depot Inc (HD.N) are uniquely positioned due to their strong outlook, as a healthy economy and improving real estate markets in most of the United States encourages homeowners to undertake renovation, Barron's said.
These companies are also "Amazon proof", the report said, noting that home improvement was low on the list of categories the retailer is expected to penetrate.
U.S. retail heavyweights including Target Corp (TGT.N), Wal-Mart Stores Inc (WMT.N) and Kroger Co (KR.N) have been locked in a fierce battle against Amazon Inc (AMZN.O).
While both Home Depot and Lowe's are poised for growth, Lowe's could be more attractive now, due in part to its lower price-to-earnings ratio, the report said.
Lowe's shares trade at $82, or about 18 times projected earnings of $4.63 per share for year ending January 2018, while Home Depot trades at $147, or 20.4 times estimated earnings of $7.19 per share in its current year, Barron's said.
Lowe's same-store sales performance has lagged Home Depot's the past several quarters, mainly due to its focus on do-it-yourself customers who spend less on big-ticket items than professionals.
However, the retailer is taking steps to boost per-store revenue, which would help narrow the valuation gap, Barron's said.
Lowe's offers investors exposure to one of retail's strongest sectors, the potential for 15 percent annual earnings growth and a "shareholder friendly" management, according to the report.
(Reporting by Devika Krishna Kumar in New York; Editing by Meredith Mazzilli)

The publication indicated that home improvement chains like Lowe's and Home Depot Inc benefit from a favorable environment. A robust economy and a recovering housing market across much of the United States are motivating more homeowners to invest in remodeling projects. The report also described these businesses as largely insulated from competition with Amazon, as the home improvement category is not considered a primary target for the online giant's expansion. This stands in contrast to other major retailers, such as Target, Walmart, and Kroger, which are engaged in intense competition with Amazon.

Investors are also attracted to Lowe's for its position in a resilient retail segment, the prospect of around 15 percent yearly profit growth, and a management team committed to returning value to shareholders.

A proposed Snowboard and Freeski Big Air World Cup competition due to take place in Düsseldorf next season has been postponed for a year due to a scheduling conflict.
The event had been scheduled to be held on a temporary ramp in the Espirit Arena in January, the same venue which hosted the World Table Tennis Championships last year.
Organisers have determined, however, that there will be "insufficient time to realise the construction of the competition ramp" in the 54,000 capacity venue due to other events also taking place there.
"Because of this, the decision was made to postpone the event from the 2018/19 season until the 2019/20 World Cup season, where the safety of the athletes can remain paramount and the true vision for the competition can be fully realised," said the International Ski Federation (FIS).
"At this time the proposed schedule for the Düsseldorf Snowboard and Freeski big air World Cup will see the competition held from January 2 to 4, 2020."
The Big Air event in Düsseldorf had been due to take place in the Espirit Arena ©SOP Architekten
The Big Air World Cup season is due to begin in Cardrona in New Zealand in September and continue with events in Milan, Beijing, Canyons in United States, Quebec and Oslo.
"While the cancellation of this season’s Dusseldorf event is disappointing for all parties involved, excitement for the 2020 event is high as the FIS snowboard and freeski tours look forward to bringing World Cup big air action to one of the great cities of Europe," FIS added.
"With Düsseldorf 54,000 seat Espirit Arena - home to the Fortuna [football team who recently earned promotion to the Bundesliga for the 2018/19 season] - lined up to host the competition, the Düsseldorf snowboard and freeski big air competitions are set to be season highlights in January 2020."
rewrite:
An upcoming Big Air World Cup event for snowboarding and freeskiing, planned for Düsseldorf in the coming winter, has been rescheduled to the following year because of a calendar issue. The competition was to be staged on a specially built ramp inside the Espirit Arena this January, the location that previously held the World Table Tennis Championships. According to organizers, overlapping events at the 54,000-seat stadium would not allow adequate time to safely build the necessary ramp structure.

Consequently, the International Ski Federation (FIS) announced the postponement to the 2019/20 World Cup season. This delay will ensure competitor safety is the top priority and will allow the event’s intended scale and quality to be achieved. The rescheduled dates are now set for January 2 through 4, 2020.

The broader Big Air World Cup circuit will still launch this September in Cardrona, New Zealand, with subsequent stops in cities including Milan, Beijing, Canyons in the United States, Quebec City, and Oslo. FIS acknowledged that missing the Düsseldorf event this season is regrettable for everyone, but enthusiasm is building for the 2020 edition. The federation expressed eagerness to stage a World Cup Big Air contest in a major European city.

The venue, the Espirit Arena—which seats 54,000 and is the home stadium of the Fortuna football club, recently promoted to the Bundesliga—is confirmed to host. The Düsseldorf snowboard and freeski big air competitions are anticipated to be standout events in January 2020.

MIAMI (WFLA) – CarePlus Health Plans is notifying customers after a privacy breach that occurred on Jan. 17.
The breach occurred due to a series of programming and printing errors, resulting in Explanation of Benefits letters being mailed to the incorrect CarePlus member.
The EOBs impacted with the errors were mailed out on Jan. 9 and Jan. 16. Roughly 11,200 members’ information as sent to another member.
Personal financial information and Social Security numbers were not contained in the letters.
The information disclosed included:
Member name
CarePlus identification number and plan name
Date(s) of service(s)
Provider of service
Services provided
CarePlus has no information that any data has been inappropriately used.
Anyone who notices any changes in their EOB statement, SmartSummary or medical records that are unfamiliar to them, or customers who have any questions, should contact CarePlus at 1-800-794-5907, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.
WHAT OTHERS ARE CLICKING ON RIGHT NOW:
rewrite: CarePlus Health Plans has alerted its customers to a privacy incident that took place on January 17. The issue stemmed from a combination of programming and printing mistakes, which led to Explanation of Benefits documents being delivered to the wrong individuals. These erroneous mailings were sent on January 9 and 16, affecting approximately 11,200 members by exposing their data to another person. The compromised details consisted of member names, CarePlus ID numbers, plan names, service dates, provider information, and descriptions of services rendered. Importantly, the letters did not include sensitive financial data or Social Security numbers. The company currently has no evidence that any of the information has been misused. Members who observe unfamiliar entries in their EOB statements, SmartSummaries, or health records, or who have general inquiries, are encouraged to call CarePlus at 1-800-794-5907 between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m.

Recently it was reported that the Penn State Outing Club, Nittany Grotto Caving Club and Scuba Club lost their official University recognition. A "risk assessment" deemed the clubs too risky. What a shame! The Caving Club has sponsored regular trips for 70 years; the Outing Club is nearly 100 years old.
What has changed over the past 100 years that would cause Penn State University to take such a drastic step? Lawsuits, lawyers, and a whole lot of money.
According to student leaders of these organizations, losing campus recognition means a club will no longer be covered under the university's $1 million liability insurance policy. I will put it more bluntly: It is too risky for Penn State to continue insuring these clubs because of the constant threat of lawsuits. That pot of a million bucks is just too attractive to plaintiffs' attorneys. The propensity to sue in our overly litigious society puts Penn State and any large organization with deep pockets right in the cross hairs of lawyers.
While some might blame Penn State for being too cautious, the university is not really to blame here. It must make these decisions mindful that attorneys are always looking for the chance to strike. And it's not just "dear old State." Thanks to abusive lawsuits, entire industries have disappeared in Pennsylvania and the cost of goods and services continue to rise as the explosive costs of litigation are factored in. Penn State and its students are just the most recent victims.
It begs the question: Where will the plaintiffs' attorneys strike next? Perhaps the table tennis club?
Curt Schroder
Executive director, Pennsylvania Coalition for Civil Justice Reform
Hatrisburg
rewrite:
A recent announcement revealed that Penn State has withdrawn official status from its Outing Club, Caving Club, and Scuba Club. University officials cited excessive danger following a review process. This is truly regrettable, particularly considering the Caving Club has organized excursions for seven decades and the Outing Club’s century-long history.

What has shifted in the past hundred years to prompt such an extreme action by the university? The driving forces are legal actions, attorneys, and substantial financial stakes.

As explained by the affected student officers, withdrawing university affiliation strips these groups of coverage under the institution’s liability insurance, which provides up to one million dollars in protection. To state it plainly, the university now views insuring these clubs as excessively hazardous due to the ever-present possibility of lawsuits. That substantial insurance pool is a powerful lure for lawyers representing claimants. In our excessively lawsuit-prone culture, a major institution like Penn State, with its considerable resources, becomes a prime target for litigation.

Although some may criticize the university for excessive caution, the true fault lies elsewhere. Penn State must operate under the reality that lawyers are perpetually seeking opportunities to file suits. This problem extends far beyond the university. In Pennsylvania, rampant and frivolous litigation has wiped out some sectors entirely, while the soaring expenses from legal battles drive up prices for products and services for everyone. The university and its students are merely the latest casualties.

This situation raises a pressing concern: which group will be targeted next by lawsuit-happy attorneys? Maybe the ping-pong club is now in jeopardy?

Curt Schroder
Executive Director, Pennsylvania Coalition for Civil Justice Reform
Harrisburg

MELBOURNE Australia pace spearhead Mitchell Starc and batsman Chris Lynn have been named as part of a formidable squad for next month's Champions Trophy in England and Wales despite nursing injuries.
Starc was forced to pull out midway through the India tour last month with a fractured foot while Lynn has been sidelined with a shoulder injury during the Indian Premier League.
Both are expected to be fit for Australia's opener on June 2 against New Zealand.
"Our medical staff will continue to monitor Mitchell and Chris’s recovery from their respective injuries but we are hopeful they will be fit in time for the team’s departure on May 18,” selector Trevor Hohns said in a media release.
James Faulkner, man-of-the-match in the 2015 World Cup final against New Zealand, has been omitted from the 15-man squad named on Thursday, with selectors opting for all-rounders Moises Henriques, Glenn Maxwell and Marcus Stoinis.
Young fast bowler Pat Cummins and James Pattinson, on the comeback trail after suffering stress fractures in his back, were included in an imposing pace battery along with Josh Hazlewood and John Hastings.
"Both James and John have made very good returns from injury and are bowling well for their respective teams in the English county competition as well as both contributing well with the bat," Hohns said.
"When you also add Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins to the fast bowling artillery it becomes a very exciting proposition for Australian cricket."
Legspinner Adam Zampa is the sole specialist spinner in the squad, while batsmen Usman Khawaja, George Bailey and Peter Handscomb have missed out.
World champions Australia, who lost their top ranking to South Africa earlier this year, will bid for their third win in the quadrennial one-day international tournament after back-to-back triumphs in 2006 and 2009.
Squad:
Steve Smith (captain), David Warner, Pat Cummins, Aaron Finch, John Hastings, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Moises Henriques, Chris Lynn, Glenn Maxwell, James Pattinson, Mitchell Starc, Marcus Stoinis, Matthew Wade, Adam Zampa
(Reporting by Ian Ransom; Editing by Amlan Chakraborty/Peter Rutherford)
rewrite:

Starc sustained a foot fracture during the recent tour of India, and Lynn injured his shoulder while playing in the Indian Premier League. Team officials anticipate both players will be ready for Australia’s first match against New Zealand on June 2.

National selector Trevor Hohns stated that medical personnel are overseeing the rehabilitation of Starc and Lynn and expressed confidence they would be available when the squad departs on May 18. Notably absent from the 15-player roster is James Faulkner, who was the standout performer in the 2015 World Cup final. The selection panel has instead chosen all-rounders Moises Henriques, Glenn Maxwell, and Marcus Stoinis.

The pace attack appears particularly strong, featuring Pat Cummins and the returning James Pattinson, who has recovered from a stress fracture in his back. They join Josh Hazlewood and John Hastings to form a formidable fast-bowling unit. Hohns noted that both Pattinson and Hastings have returned effectively from their injuries and are performing well with bat and ball in English county cricket. He added that the combination of Starc, Hazlewood, and Cummins makes the bowling prospects very promising for Australia.

Adam Zampa is the only dedicated spin bowler selected. Several batsmen, including Usman Khawaja, George Bailey, and Peter Handscomb, were not included in the final squad. As the reigning world champions, Australia will aim to secure their third Champions Trophy title, having previously won the tournament in 2006 and 2009, though they recently ceded the top ODI ranking to South Africa.

The full squad consists of Steve Smith as captain, David Warner, Pat Cummins, Aaron Finch, John Hastings, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Moises Henriques, Chris Lynn, Glenn Maxwell, James Pattinson, Mitchell Starc, Marcus Stoinis, Matthew Wade, and Adam Zampa.

MORRIS, Minn. — A 94-year-old Minnesota man whose wife died after battling cancer built a swimming pool in his backyard for children in his neighborhood.
Keith Davison’s wife of 66 years died last year, KARE 11 reports.
“You just can’t imagine what it’s like,” he said. “You cry a lot. That’s just the way it is because she’s not here.”
Davison then decided to do something different to fill his time.
In the spring, the retired judge had an in-ground pool built. In July, the pool, which is 32 feet long and 9 feet deep, opened — and kids from all over the neighborhood came to swim.
“I knew they’d come,” Davison said.
Davison, who has three adult children but no grandchildren, is usually seen sitting in a chair next to the pool, watching the kids swimming, laughing and having fun.
“I’m not sitting by myself looking at the walls,” Davison said. “What else would you think of doing where you could have a whole bunch of kids over every afternoon?”
rewrite:
In Morris, Minnesota, a 94-year-old widower constructed a backyard pool for the local children. Keith Davison lost his spouse of 66 years to cancer last year. He described the profound grief of her absence, noting how tears became a frequent part of his life.

Seeking a meaningful way to occupy his time, the former judge chose to install an in-ground pool this past spring. By July, the 32-foot-long, nine-foot-deep pool was ready, quickly drawing youngsters from throughout the area. Davison had anticipated their joyful arrival.

Though he has three grown children, he has no grandchildren. Now, he often spends afternoons seated beside the pool, observing the children play, swim, and laugh. The project has ended his lonely hours spent staring at empty walls. For him, it is the perfect way to welcome a crowd of cheerful kids each day.

By Liana B. Baker and Olivia Oran
April 12 Morgan Stanley's chief compliance officer Billy Fenrich is leaving the firm just over a year after being named to the position.
Fenrich will be replaced by Raul Yanes, according to an internal Morgan Stanley memo reviewed by Reuters, which was confirmed by a firm spokesman.
Fenrich is joining quantitative hedge fund AQR Capital Management as its chief legal officer, according to an AQR spokeswoman.
Yanes was most recently a litigation partner at the law firm Davis Polk & Wardwell and had also served in a number of senior positions under president George W. Bush, including staff secretary and assistant to the president and senior counselor to the attorney general.
Fenrich joined Morgan Stanley's legal department in 2014 from hedge fund PointState Capital. He was named chief compliance officer in 2016, replacing longtime compliance chief Stuart Breslow. He had also worked at Davis Polk.
Compliance officers have become critical figures on Wall Street since the financial crisis, helping to ensure that bankers and traders stay out of trouble and avoid massive fines. (Reporting by Liana Baker and Olivia Oran in New York; Editing by Tom Brown)
rewrite:
Morgan Stanley's head of compliance, Billy Fenrich, is departing after roughly a year in the role, according to company information verified by Reuters. His successor will be Raul Yanes, as stated in an internal memo. Fenrich's next position will be as the top legal executive at AQR Capital Management, a quantitative hedge fund.

Yanes joins from the law firm Davis Polk & Wardwell, where he was a litigation partner. He previously held several high-level roles during the George W. Bush administration, such as White House staff secretary and a senior advisory position within the Department of Justice.

Fenrich originally came to Morgan Stanley's legal team in 2014 from PointState Capital, another hedge fund. He assumed the compliance leadership role in 2016, taking over from Stuart Breslow. Notably, Fenrich is also a former Davis Polk attorney.

The importance of compliance executives in the financial industry has grown substantially following the 2008 crisis. These officials are essential for guiding firms through regulatory requirements and preventing misconduct that can lead to significant penalties.

HOLLYWOOD stars including Ellen DeGeneres, Paris Hilton, and Chelsea Handler were forced to evacuate their homes as the deadly fire in California continues to burn.
President Donald Trump has declared a state of emergency and ordered federal agencies to help with rescue efforts.
White House spokeswoman Lindsay Walters said Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue briefed Trump and Vice President Mike Pence on a wildfire prevention roundtable today.
Walters said the White House “continues to closely monitor the situation” and is urging “anyone ordered to evacuate during a wildfire, do so immediately and listen to your local and state officials”.
Camera Icon Firefighters monitor a blaze beside Highway 33 near Ojai. Picture: AFP Picture: AFP Camera Icon Firefighters comb through smouldering ash in the remains of dozens of homes destroyed by the Lilac Fire in San Diego. Picture: AFP Picture: AFP
She also said the White House “extends its thoughts and prayers” to everyone affected by the fires that have been tearing through Southern California.
Authorities today issued new alerts about unhealthy air from smoke and ash sent up by the growing wildfire.
Celebrities including former Glee star Lea Michele, talk show host DeGeneres, along with Hilton and Kylie Jenner were forced to flee their homes and, in Jenner’s case, her Kylie Cosmetics headquarters.
Richard Sanchez, a manager at Jeannine’s American Bakery restaurant in the foothill enclave of Montecito, said customers were wearing masks.
Camera Icon Flames erupt on mountainsides in the Los Padres national forest north of Ojai. Picture: AFP Picture: AFP
He said smoke was so thick that visibility was down to a few metres and a layer of ash was coating the streets.
Regulators were warning resident in parts of Santa Barbara, Ventura and Los Angeles counties to stay indoors, avoid vigorous outdoor activities and not do anything to stir up ash.
Even residents of Montecito and neighbouring Carpinteria who weren’t under evacuation orders opted to leave because of the thick blanket of smoke.
rewrite:
Numerous celebrities, such as Ellen DeGeneres, Paris Hilton, and Chelsea Handler, have had to abandon their residences due to the ongoing and destructive wildfires in California. In response, President Donald Trump has issued an emergency declaration, directing federal resources to support relief operations. White House representative Lindsay Walters noted that Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue updated the President and Vice President Mike Pence during a discussion on wildfire mitigation. Walters emphasized that the administration is keeping a watchful eye on developments and strongly advises all individuals under evacuation mandates to comply without delay and follow guidance from local and state authorities.

The White House also expressed its sympathy and support for those impacted by the blazes raging across Southern California. Officials have recently released warnings concerning hazardous air quality caused by smoke and ash from the expanding fires. Notable figures like former Glee actress Lea Michele, along with DeGeneres, Hilton, and Kylie Jenner, were compelled to evacuate; Jenner also left her Kylie Cosmetics corporate office. In Montecito, Richard Sanchez, a manager at Jeannine’s American Bakery, observed patrons wearing protective masks due to the conditions.

He described extremely dense smoke that reduced visibility to just a few meters and left streets covered in ash. Health and safety agencies advised people in areas of Santa Barbara, Ventura, and Los Angeles counties to remain inside, refrain from strenuous outdoor exercise, and avoid actions that might disturb accumulated ash. Many residents in Montecito and nearby Carpinteria, even without formal evacuation orders, chose to depart because of the intense smoke enveloping the region.

A World War One grave in France marked as that of an unknown soldier has been identified as the resting place of an army officer from Scotland.
The headstone at Jonchery-Sur-Vesle, near Reims, was dedicated only to "a major" of the Royal Engineers.
Detective work by David Tattersfield, of the Western Front Association, identified the major to be an Alexander Soutar, a minister's son.
Maj Soutar was born in Cullen and grew up in Glasgow and Thurso.
He fought at the Somme in 1916 and Passchendale in 1917, before being shot and killed by a sniper on 28 May 1918 while helping to defend the village of Hermonville, near Jonchery-Sur-Vesle, from an attack by German soldiers.
One hundred years after his death, Maj Soutar's descendants have gathered at the Commonwealth War Graves Commission Cemetery where he lies to honour him.
A new headstone with his name has been erected.
rewrite: A burial site in France from World War I, previously listed as belonging to an unidentified soldier, has now been recognized as the grave of a Scottish military officer. The original marker at the Jonchery-Sur-Vesle cemetery near Reims referenced only an unnamed major in the Royal Engineers. Research conducted by David Tattersfield of the Western Front Association revealed this officer to be Alexander Soutar, whose father was a clergyman. Born in Cullen, Soutar spent his youth in Glasgow and Thurso. He served in the battles of the Somme and Passchendaele before dying from a sniper's bullet on May 28, 1918, during the defense of Hermonville against German forces. A century later, his family members assembled at the Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery to pay their respects, and a new inscribed headstone has been placed at the site.

ROCHESTER, Mich. — Tai Odiase had 19 points, on 8-for-8 shooting, and three blocks, Godwin Boahen hit four 3-pointers and finished with 16 points and Illinois-Chicago beat Oakland 79-73 on Friday night for its fifth win in a row.
Marcus Ottey added 15 points and Tarkus Ferguson had 13 points, nine rebounds and seven assists for UIC (13-11, 8-3 Horizon League). The Flames have eight conference wins for the first time since finishing the 2007-08 season 9-9 in Horizon League play.
Odiase had a dunk and two layups during a 6-2 spurt that made it 17-14 and UIC led the rest of the way. Ferguson converted a 3-point play to spark a 10-2 run that pushed the lead to 11 points before Boahen's 3-pointer made it 40-30 at the break. Nick Daniels hit a 3 that pulled Oakland (14-10, 6-5) within two points with two minutes to play, but Ottey made two free throws and Odiase hit a jumper to make it 76-69 and UIC made 4 of 6 free throws in the final 32 seconds to seal it.
Martez Walker had 21 points and Jalen Hayes scored 15 for Oakland. Kendrick Nunn added 20, but shot 3 of 22 from the field, including 1 of 10 from 3-point range.
rewrite:
In a Friday night Horizon League matchup in Rochester, Michigan, Illinois-Chicago extended its winning streak to five games by defeating Oakland with a final score of 79-73. Tai Odiase led UIC with a perfect shooting performance, making all eight of his attempts for 19 points, while also recording three blocked shots. Teammate Godwin Boahen contributed 16 points, including four three-pointers. Additional key efforts came from Marcus Ottey with 15 points and Tarkus Ferguson, who neared a triple-double with 13 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists.

This victory improves UIC's record to 13-11 overall and 8-3 in conference play, marking the first time the Flames have achieved eight league wins since the 2007-08 season. The team established an early advantage and maintained the lead throughout the contest. After a surge gave UIC an 11-point cushion, they entered halftime ahead 40-30. Oakland narrowed the gap to just two points in the closing minutes, but timely free throws and a critical jumper from Odiase secured the win for UIC.

For Oakland, now 14-10 and 6-5 in the league, Martez Walker scored a team-high 21 points and Jalen Hayes added 15. Despite a 20-point effort from Kendrick Nunn, he struggled with his shooting, making only 3 of 22 field goal attempts.
