SAN FRANCISCO — A woman who was found dead Wednesday in a stairwell of a power plant at Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital had dementia and vanished from a nearby mental health facility 10 days ago, her daughter said.
A staff member found the body at about 1 p.m. The county medical examiner’s office identified the woman as Ruby Andersen, 75.
An autopsy was pending.
“I don’t know how she died,” her daughter, Charlene Roberts, told KRON-TV . “Did she have a stroke or fell? I don’t know what happened.”
Roberts, who gave her mother’s age as 76, said the woman had dementia and two hearing aids and went missing on May 20 from a mental health facility.
“We almost hired a private investigator” to look for her, Roberts said.
Hospital spokeswoman Rachael Kagan said the woman was not a patient at San Francisco General but noted that there were other facilities on the same campus operated by the San Francisco Department of Public Health. They include the 47-bed Mental Health Rehabilitation Center.
Andersen was found in a stairwell that usually is locked and only accessible to maintenance workers, Kagan said.
“We are very concerned how this could have happened,” she said.
Police, public health and sheriff’s investigators were working on the case.
Five years ago, the body of a missing patient was found in a stairwell at the same hospital, more than two weeks after a patient disappeared from her room.
An autopsy determined that 57-year-old Lynne Spalding had been dead for several days before her body was found in a stairwell that was supposed to be routinely checked by security.
The Sheriff’s Department, which is responsible for the hospital’s security, paid Spalding’s family $3 million to settle a legal claim.
rewrite:
SAN FRANCISCO — According to her daughter, a 75-year-old woman discovered deceased this Wednesday in a hospital power plant stairwell had been missing for ten days after wandering away from a psychiatric care center. She suffered from dementia.

The woman was identified as Ruby Andersen by the medical examiner's office. Her body was located around 1 p.m. by an employee. The cause of death remains undetermined pending an autopsy.

Her daughter, Charlene Roberts, expressed uncertainty about the circumstances, questioning whether her mother had suffered a fall or a medical incident. Roberts stated her mother was 76, lived with dementia, used hearing aids, and had disappeared from the facility on May 20. The family had considered employing a private search party.

A hospital representative clarified that Andersen was not a patient at San Francisco General Hospital itself but noted the campus houses other public health departments, including a mental health rehabilitation facility. The stairwell where she was found is typically locked and restricted to maintenance staff, raising serious concerns about how she accessed it.

Authorities from police, public health, and the sheriff's department are investigating. This incident echoes a similar tragedy at the same hospital five years prior, when a missing patient was found dead in a stairwell over two weeks after vanishing. In that case, a security lapse was determined, as the stairwell was meant to be regularly patrolled. The Sheriff’s Department, which oversees hospital security, later reached a $3 million settlement with that patient's family.

× Thai Prime Minister: cave will become “an important tourist spot”
The Thai cave at the center of an international mission to rescue a soccer team and its coach is likely to become a tourist destination, government officials say.
As rescuers worked around the clock to free the 12 boys and the man who coaches them, Thailand’s Prime Minster Prayut Chan-o-cha said on Tuesday that the cave in the northern province of Chiang Rai was “likely to become famous nationally and worldwide.”
“It will eventually become an important tourist spot,” he said in a Facebook live video stream from his office. “Therefore we have to come up with [safety] measures to accommodate the tourism activities.”
The prime minister added that in the past authorities lacked a good map of the cave, but that following the mammoth rescue operation “we should have a better diagram to create safety.”
The Tham Luang Nang Non cave network made headlines around the world after the boys, aged between 11 and 16, and their 25-year-old coach disappeared on June 23.
The group became stranded in the flooded tunnels after a relentless downpour of rain, until two British divers discovered them perched on a small ledge of dry land nine days later.
Rescue teams are now racing to free the boys before more rain is forecast next week, and are working on solutions ranging from teaching them to dive to drilling an escape route.
Once the mission is complete, authorities plan to repair the damage inflicted on the cave, and upgrade the area to a national park.
The cave network is already well-known by locals. For the first kilometer (0.6 miles) or so inside the cavernous entrance, limestone rock formations hug high ceilings, creating an almost amphitheater-like atmosphere.
Jongklai Worapongsathorn, the deputy director-general of the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, told Thailand’s Public Broadcasting Service (PBS) that the department had set its sights on developing the cave into a tourist destination.
The plan would include signs making it clear to tourists which parts of the cave they should stay clear of, he said.
rewrite:
The site of a dramatic international effort to save a youth soccer team and their coach is expected to be developed into a major attraction, according to Thai officials. During the intense operation to extract the twelve boys and their adult coach, Prime Minister Prayut Chan-o-cha remarked that the cavern in Chiang Rai province would probably gain significant fame both within Thailand and globally. In a live online broadcast, he stated that the location is destined to evolve into a key destination for visitors, necessitating the implementation of appropriate safety protocols for future tourism.

The Prime Minister also noted that prior to this event, detailed layouts of the cave system were insufficient, but the extensive rescue work should yield improved maps to help ensure visitor security. This network of caves, known as Tham Luang Nang Non, captured worldwide attention after the group, consisting of boys aged 11 to 16 and their 25-year-old coach, went missing on June 23. They were trapped by sudden flooding caused by heavy rains and were found alive by two British divers on a narrow dry shelf deep inside after nine days.

Efforts are currently focused on extracting the group before anticipated rainfall next week, with options being considered that include dive training and creating a new exit through drilling. After the rescue concludes, plans are in place to restore any damage to the cave and designate the surrounding region as a national park.

While already familiar to area residents, the cave features expansive entry passages with high ceilings and limestone structures that produce a grand, theater-like effect for approximately the first kilometer inside. Jongklai Worapongsathorn, a senior official with the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, confirmed in a media interview that transforming the cave into a formal tourist site is an objective. This would involve installing clear signage to indicate restricted areas for public safety.

Plans have the old library in Gulfport coming back to life. (Photo source: WLOX)
Ground work on one of the most anticipated projects on the coast is moving right along. The future site of the Mississippi Aquarium in Gulfport is undergoing dirt and drainage work.
There's another project in the works that ties right in to the needs of the big attraction. While technically not a part of the incoming aquarium's property, plans have the old library in Gulfport coming back to life to play a big role in the operations of the attraction.
"We're restoring the library, maintaining the architectural integrity of the building, and re-purposing it to a highly functional, brand new, intermodal center," said Coast Transit Authority Executive Director Kevin Coggin.
Coggin just signed a 40-year lease with the city for the $1.6 million property. Once renovated, Coggin said the bottom floor will be dedicated to CTA business, including a hub for transportation and possibly a food court.
The top 14,000 square feet will be rented out to the aquarium for administrative offices and classrooms. According to Coggin, the only thing standing in the way of construction is an approval by archives and history, which he says is almost there.
"The community will see actual renovation take place on this library this summer," Coggin said.
He hopes to be up and running in the location when the aquarium opens. Then, future plans include a public tram way across Hwy. 90.
"We're going to operate a public tram across to bring people back and forth with a route. You'll be able to bike across and walk across, and there's a lot of good elements to that, too. One of them is safety," said Coggin.
So far, Coggin said work to bring the $8.9 million library renovation to light has been making big strides, and he's looking forward to being a part of the economic boom expected in the city once the attraction opens.
The Gulfport City Council is considering an agreement Tuesday to fund part of $633,000 in improvements near the future CTA center.
Copyright 2017 WLOX. All rights reserved.
rewrite:
A significant revitalization effort is underway for the former library building in Gulfport. (Photo credit: WLOX)
Progress continues steadily on one of the region's most eagerly awaited developments. Preparatory earthmoving and water management activities are currently taking place at the designated location for the forthcoming Mississippi Aquarium in Gulfport.

A complementary initiative is also advancing, designed to support the major attraction's requirements. Although not situated on the aquarium's official grounds, the old library is slated for a revival and will serve an important function for the new facility.

Kevin Coggin, Executive Director of the Coast Transit Authority, explained, "We are rehabilitating the library, preserving its original architectural character, and converting it into a modern, fully-equipped multimodal center." Coggin recently finalized a four-decade lease with the city for the property, valued at $1.6 million. After renovations, the ground level will house CTA operations, potentially featuring a transit hub and dining options.

The upper floor, encompassing 14,000 square feet, will be leased to the aquarium for its administrative and educational spaces. Coggin noted that the final hurdle for starting construction is a pending approval from historical authorities, which is anticipated shortly.

"Visible restoration work on this library will begin this summer," Coggin stated. His goal is to have the center operational in time for the aquarium's debut. Subsequent phases may involve establishing a public tram line over Highway 90.

Coggin described the tram concept: "We plan to run a public tram along a designated route to transport visitors across the highway. The design will also safely accommodate cyclists and pedestrians, enhancing overall safety."

To date, efforts to realize the $8.9 million library renovation have progressed significantly. Coggin expressed enthusiasm about contributing to the anticipated economic surge in Gulfport following the attraction's opening.

In related actions, the Gulfport City Council is reviewing a proposal this Tuesday to allocate funding for approximately $633,000 in infrastructure upgrades around the planned CTA center.

BEIJING May 3 China will further regulate local government debt issuance and financing, six government agencies said in a joint statement on Wednesday, reinforcing recent steps to bolster financial risk controls.
China has taken aim at potential cracks in its financial system, ramping up regulatory checks with various high-flying officials calling for action against an alarming level of leverage.
In the statement, the government agencies, including the National Development and Reform Commission, the finance ministry, the central bank and securities and banking regulators, said China would push for a clearer boundary between local governments and their financing vehicles.
Local governments are strictly prohibited from injecting public assets into local government financing vehicles (LGFVs), or using expected land revenue as debt repayments for LGFVs, the statement said.
It also said LGFVs could not accept guarantees from local governments when thy issue debt, and authorities would strictly prohibit illegal debt issuance by local governments through public-private partnership projects.
The agencies ordered an inspection of local governments' financing and guarantee situation to "fully correct irregularities" by the end of July, the statement, posted on the finance ministry's official website, said.
(Reporting by Yawen Chen and Kevin Yao; Editing by Shri Navaratnam and Nick Macfie)
rewrite:
On Wednesday, six Chinese regulatory bodies jointly announced enhanced measures to oversee the issuance and financing of debt by regional authorities, strengthening ongoing efforts to manage financial risks. The move represents a continued focus on addressing vulnerabilities within the financial framework, with senior officials having recently emphasized the need to curb excessive borrowing.

The statement, issued by agencies such as the National Development and Reform Commission, the Ministry of Finance, the People's Bank of China, and securities and banking regulators, emphasized the need to more clearly separate the roles of local governments from their affiliated financing entities. It explicitly forbids regional authorities from transferring public assets into these local government financing vehicles (LGFVs) or from pledging future land-sale income to back their debts.

Furthermore, LGFVs are barred from obtaining government guarantees when issuing bonds. The regulators also vowed to clamp down on any illicit borrowing by local governments via public-private partnership schemes. An official review of regional financing and guarantee practices has been mandated, with instructions to address all non-compliant activities before July concludes. This notice was published on the finance ministry's website.

This drunk driving suspect says she’s just a follower of Christ.
After allegedly boozing behind the wheel Sunday night, Nicole Ann Mintner defended herself to police by telling arresting officers that “Jesus drank wine and so did I,” The Village News reported.
Deputies said they found the 45-year-old asleep at the wheel inside a silver Dodge with her hazard lights activated and engine running in Sumter County, Fla.
During police interviews, Mintner reportedly refused to take off her sunglasses and slapped an officer twice on the shoulder.
She told officers that she had taken Xanax then later admitted to drinking alcohol after four empty sangria bottles were found in her center console.
Mintner was placed under arrest and into the back of a patrol car where she “continuously” screamed and threatened to urinate while en route to Sumter County Detention Center, according to deputies.
When they arrived at the jail, officers attempted to perform field sobriety tests on Minter but she kept talking over them and began singing “Amazing Grace,” according to the Village News.
She also reportedly threw her socks at a camera recording the tests and exposed herself to the officers.
“The defendant removed her right breast from her shirt and completely revealed it to the camera and jail staff,” according to the police report obtained by the newspaper.
Mintner was booked on charges of driving under the influence, battery on a law enforcement officer and resisting an officer. She was released Monday on $6,000 bond, according to court records.
rewrite:
A woman accused of impaired driving claimed her religious faith as a defense. Following her arrest on Sunday evening, Nicole Ann Mintner reportedly informed officers that since Jesus consumed wine, her own drinking was justified, as detailed by The Village News. Law enforcement discovered the 45-year-old unconscious in the driver's seat of a silver Dodge in Sumter County, Florida, with the vehicle's hazard lights on and the engine still operating.

Authorities stated that during questioning, Mintner declined to remove her sunglasses and struck a deputy on the shoulder two times. She initially stated she had taken Xanax, but later conceded to drinking alcohol after four empty sangria bottles were located in her car. After being arrested and placed in a patrol vehicle, she allegedly screamed nonstop during the trip to the detention center and warned she would urinate.

At the facility, attempts to administer sobriety evaluations were repeatedly interrupted as she talked over deputies and started singing "Amazing Grace." Reports indicate she also threw her socks at a recording camera and bared her breast to both the camera and jail personnel. Mintner faces charges for DUI, battery on a law enforcement officer, and resisting arrest. Court documents show she was released on Monday after posting a $6,000 bond.

Outside view of the plant of gold refiner and bar manufacturer Argor-Heraeus SA in the southern Swiss town of Mendrisio, March 1, 2012. REUTERS/Pascal Lauener
HAMBURG German precious metals group Heraeus [HRHLD.UL] said on Monday it had taken full control of Swiss gold and silver processor Argor-Heraeus.
The German group has raised its shareholding in Argor-Heraeus to 100 percent from about 33 percent previously.
No financial details are being released about the deal, which still requires approval from relevant authorities.
The sellers were Germany's Commerzbank (CBKG.DE), Austrian state mint Muenze Oesterreich and Argor-Heraeus management, Heraeus said.
Argor-Heraeus has around 300 employees with operations in Switzerland, Germany, Italy and South America.
It is involved in refining gold ore, recycling of precious metals and industrial processing of bars, coins, alloys and semi-finished products.
"With the full takeover of the shareholdings, Heraeus is now in the position to fully profit from Argors competence and capacity for gold and silver," Heraeus CEO Jan Rinnert said in a statement.
(Reporting by Michael Hogan; editing by Jason Neely)

On March 1, 2012, the exterior of the Argor-Heraeus SA facility, a refiner and producer of gold bars, is seen in Mendrisio, southern Switzerland. REUTERS/Pascal Lauener

Heraeus has increased its stake in the company from approximately one-third to total ownership. The transaction's financial terms were not disclosed and it remains subject to regulatory consent. According to Heraeus, the divesting parties were Commerzbank (CBKG.DE) of Germany, Austria's state mint Muenze Oesterreich, and Argor-Heraeus management.

Argor-Heraeus employs about 300 people and runs facilities in Switzerland, Germany, Italy, and South America. Its activities include purifying gold ore, recovering precious metals from recycled materials, and industrially producing bars, coins, alloys, and semi-finished goods.

In a statement, Heraeus CEO Jan Rinnert said the total acquisition enables Heraeus to fully leverage Argor's expertise and production capabilities in gold and silver.

Labour MP Chris Hipkins says he didn't know his question to officials about citizenship was in any way linked to questions about Australia's Barnaby Joyce's eligibility for parliament there.
But had he known he might have given it a second thought.
Deputy Prime Minister Joyce's position in Australia's federal parliament is under scrutiny after he revealed the New Zealand High Commission had contacted him last week with the "shocking" information that he could be a New Zealander.
Joyce's father was born in New Zealand and it has been confirmed that he is a citizen by descent. That would rule him ineligible to serve in Australia's Parliament.
Advertisement
Labour leader Jacinda Ardern said today that Hipkins shouldn't have been prioritising questions about citizenship.
"We've had a discussion about [it] and as I said to her, had I known this was where it was going to land up I wouldn't have got involved," Hipkins said.
"I had no intention of getting involved in Australian domestic politics."
Hipkins, who has a keen interest in the rights of Kiwis living in Australia, said he asked the citizenship question out of personal interest.
A spokesman for Internal Affairs Minister Peter Dunne says Australian media had also lodged specific questions about Joyce at or about the same time as Hipkins' general question.
The requests had led to Joyce being informed, he said.
Joyce is the fifth Australian MP to have their citizenship questioned since last month, after senators Scott Ludlam, Larissa Waters, Matthew Canavan and Malcolm Roberts.
- NZN
rewrite:
Labour MP Chris Hipkins has stated he was unaware that his inquiry to authorities concerning citizenship had any connection to the ongoing scrutiny of Australian Deputy Prime Minister Barnaby Joyce's parliamentary eligibility. He added that, had he been aware, he likely would have reconsidered posing the question.

Joyce’s status in Australia’s federal parliament has come under examination following his disclosure that the New Zealand High Commission recently provided him with what he termed surprising information indicating he may hold New Zealand citizenship. Since Joyce’s father was born in New Zealand, it has been established that he qualifies for citizenship by descent, a situation that would disqualify him from serving in the Australian Parliament.

Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern commented that Hipkins should not have focused on such citizenship matters. In response, Hipkins explained, “We discussed the issue, and I conveyed to her that if I had foreseen this outcome, I would not have engaged. I had no desire to involve myself in Australia’s internal political affairs.” He noted that his question stemmed from personal interest, given his concern for the rights of New Zealanders residing in Australia.

A representative for Internal Affairs Minister Peter Dunne mentioned that Australian media had submitted specific questions regarding Joyce around the same period as Hipkins’ more general query. These combined inquiries ultimately led to Joyce being notified of his citizenship status.

Joyce now joins a list of Australian politicians whose citizenship has been disputed recently, following senators Scott Ludlam, Larissa Waters, Matthew Canavan, and Malcolm Roberts.

The number of building permits issued this April compared to last April was up by 14.4%, data released by the Cyprus Statistical Service show. At the same time, an increase of 6.6% is recorded during the first four months of this year.
The number of building permits issued by local authorities this April was 469, compared to 410 in April 2017, recording an increase of 14.4%. The total value of these permits was up by €17 million reaching €105.6 million compared to €89.6 million in April last year.
The total area of the properties reached 101,500 square metres compared to 87,600 square metres last April.
The permits issued this April concern the construction of 418 residential units compared to 289 last April. During the period of January – April 2018, 1,984 building permits were issued compared to 1,861 in the same period of 2017, recording an increase of 6.6%.
The total value of these permits was up by 27.5% and their total area by 24.5%. The number of residential units to be built was up by 22.3%.
Building permits constitute an important indicator for future activity in the building sector, the Statistical Service says.
rewrite:
According to the Cyprus Statistical Service, building permit figures for April show a significant rise compared to the same month last year. The data indicates a 14.4 percent growth in the number of authorizations granted this April relative to April 2017. Specifically, authorities approved 469 permits this year against 410 previously. This expansion is also reflected in financial and spatial terms, with the total permit value climbing to 105.6 million euros from 89.6 million, and the covered area increasing to 101,500 square metres from 87,600.

Furthermore, these April permits authorize the building of 418 new homes, a notable jump from 289 units last year. Examining the first four months of 2018 reveals a broader upward trend, with permits issued rising by 6.6 percent compared to the equivalent span in 2017. The cumulative value and area for these months grew substantially by 27.5 and 24.5 percent, respectively, while planned residential units increased by 22.3 percent. The Statistical Service emphasizes that building permit statistics serve as a crucial gauge for anticipating forthcoming construction activity.

Amazon, which operates Lovefilm By Post, is predictably pushing subscribers in the direction of Prime Video, and is sweetening the deal with £15 off the cost of a Fire TV Stick. DVD and Blu-ray rentals will still be available up until the end of October, though, and Amazon won't be billing subscribers for that final month. The service is also shutting down in Germany, the only other European country it still serves, on the same day.
I guess it's been a long time coming but @lovefilm by post service to close 31st October pic.twitter.com/Vq1rpFX0l1 — Robertie (@Clert) August 14, 2017
In a way, Lovefilm is partly responsible for the demise of its own postal option. Many moons ago, Lovefilm used to run a streaming service in parallel with its rental offering. It became a relatively big player through various acquisitions, even relieving Amazon of its DVD rental arm in 2008. The house that Bezos built returned the favour in 2011, purchasing Lovefilm in its entirety. A few years later, the streaming side of things was absorbed into Amazon Prime Video, making the rental service a separate subscription and the last thing bearing the Lovefilm name.
The idea of getting your movie fix by post might seem seriously old fashioned now, but the demise of Lovefilm actually leaves something of a hole in the market. There's a reason streaming services like Netflix don't carry the latest titles. Studios want to make sure they're squeezing as much money as they can out of new films through purchases and rentals before selling blanket streaming licenses. You can buy digital copies of movies as soon as they are released on DVD/Blu-ray, or pay a couple of quid to rent them for a watch or two.
Lovefilm By Post, however, was an unlimited service. The top, £12 per month tier (£10 for Prime subscribers, naturally) offered unlimited rentals, which is something that simply isn't replicated by streaming services these days -- the way streaming licences work makes this impossible. It was inevitable Lovefilm By Post wasn't going to be viable forever, but come October 31st, we're not just losing a forgotten rental service, but the last unlimited movie subscription of its kind.
rewrite:
Amazon, the company behind Lovefilm By Post, is naturally encouraging its members to transition to Prime Video, offering an incentive of £15 deducted from the price of a Fire TV Stick. However, DVD and Blu-ray rentals will continue until October concludes, and Amazon will not charge users for that final month. The service is also ceasing operations in Germany, the sole other European nation where it remains available, on that same date.

A social media user remarked on the impending closure, noting that while it seemed inevitable, the Lovefilm postal service will officially end on October 31st.

In some respects, Lovefilm itself contributed to the end of its mail-based model. Years ago, Lovefilm operated a streaming platform alongside its physical rental business. It grew significantly through several buyouts, even taking over Amazon's DVD rental division in 2008. Amazon later bought the entire Lovefilm company in 2011. Several years after that, the streaming portion was merged into Amazon Prime Video, leaving the rental side as a standalone subscription and the final remnant of the Lovefilm brand.

Receiving films by mail may appear quite outdated today, yet Lovefilm's closure creates a noticeable gap in the industry. Streaming platforms such as Netflix often lack the most recent releases for a reason. Movie studios aim to maximize revenue from new films via sales and rentals before offering broad streaming rights. Consumers can purchase digital copies once movies are out on DVD or Blu-ray, or spend a small amount to rent them temporarily.

Lovefilm By Post, in contrast, provided an all-you-can-watch model. Its premium plan, priced at £12 monthly (or £10 for Prime members), allowed unlimited rentals—a feature not matched by current streaming services due to the nature of licensing agreements. While it was clear that Lovefilm By Post could not endure indefinitely, its termination on October 31st signifies more than the loss of a niche rental option; it marks the disappearance of the last remaining unlimited movie subscription service of this type.

Unlike the Martian desert in the original Destiny, Helles Basin is an arctic region where players will fight the frozen Hive faction Grasp of Nokris on the way to confront Rasputin, the rogue Warmind. The region will host a new horde-like public event called Escalation Protocol where groups of Guardians face seven waves of Hive capped by a unique boss -- one of five that will rotate every week. The elite foe drops custom gear so folks will have to wait over a month to collect them all; Since players activate the event, at least it won't be random.
PvP is getting two ranked modes, one for casual (Valor) and competitive (Glory), though the latter will move players up and down the rank ladder as they win and lose games. Every season will introduce a new gun exclusive to PvP for players to earn.
Fans already knew that tweaks were coming for their favorite exotic guns, including Sturm/Drang, Graviton Lance, Skyburner's Oath and Rat King, but the stream also showed off changes to Fighting Lion, Riskrunner, Crimson and the infamous Hard Light.
There will be two new strikes, Strange Terrain and Will of the Thousands, and one coming exclusively for PS4 players: The Insight Terminus. The Leviathan raid will get a second lair called Spire of the Stars, which will arrive after Warmind launches. Finally, the prestige version of Curse of Osiris' raid, Eater of Worlds, will arrive when the game's third season starts.
rewrite:
In contrast to the arid Mars setting of the first Destiny, the Helles Basin is a frost-covered zone. Here, Guardians will battle the icy Hive sect known as the Grasp of Nokris as they advance toward the renegade Warmind, Rasputin. This area introduces a fresh public activity, Escalation Protocol, which functions as a survival challenge. Teams must endure seven successive waves of Hive enemies, culminating in a fight against a special boss. With five different bosses cycling weekly, it will take more than a month to obtain all the unique equipment each one provides. Participants initiate the event themselves, ensuring its availability isn't left to chance.

The competitive player-versus-player arena is receiving two distinct ranked playlists: Valor for relaxed matches and Glory for serious competition. The Glory system will adjust a player's standing with each victory or defeat. Each competitive season will also offer a new weapon attainable only through PvP participation.

Adjustments for several exotic weapons, such as Sturm/Drang, Graviton Lance, Skyburner's Oath, and Rat King, were previously announced. The recent presentation further revealed modifications for Fighting Lion, Riskrunner, Crimson, and the notorious Hard Light.

Two new strikes, Strange Terrain and Will of the Thousands, are being added, alongside a PlayStation 4 exclusive mission named The Insight Terminus. The Leviathan raid will gain a new addition called Spire of the Stars, releasing after Warmind. Additionally, a prestigious version of the Curse of Osiris raid, Eater of Worlds, is scheduled to launch with the game's third season.

The current Renault Twingo dates back to 2014, and new spy shots reveal that a styling update is on the way for the little hatchback. The changes appear to maintain the Twingo's cute, friendly aesthetic.
The biggest changes to the front are in the lower fascia. There are new intakes in each corner, which lend a somewhat sporty aesthetic. The center section appears to be a little more rounded, too. There's lots of camouflage, but there don't appear to be major changes elsewhere. The upper grille and headlights appear to have same shapes as on the current Twingo.
At the back, there are revised tailights that appear to have a rounder shape and a different layout with a rectangular white section in the center. The bumper appears to have a completely different shape. It has a new taper that adds some visual interest to the tail, rather than the current design that's fairly flat.
These photos don't provide a look at the cabin but expect Renault to take the opportunity to update things in there. Material changes and infotainment improvements are the most likely tweaks.
This test mule also has an exhaust the pokes out of the rear corner, instead of the semi-hidden layout from most trims of the existing model. This could indicate that Renault is evaluating some powertrain changes for the hatchback.
The existing Twingo is available with a range of tiny, rear-mounted engines. The base unit is a 1.0-liter naturally aspirated three-cylinder with 70 horsepower (52 kilowatts). There's also a turbocharged 900cc three-cylinder with 90 hp (67 kW). The range-topping GT model gets a 110-hp (82 kW) version of this tiny engine.
Source: CarPix

Alterations at the front are most concentrated on the lower bumper. Freshly designed air intakes positioned at either side contribute a slightly more athletic impression. The central area also looks somewhat more curved. Despite extensive camouflage, the main grille and headlamp units above seem largely unchanged from the current car’s familiar silhouette.

The rear features updated light clusters with a more circular form and a new internal arrangement, incorporating a centered rectangular white element. The rear bumper itself is reshaped entirely, introducing a tapered contour that gives the tail a more sculpted appearance compared to the rather simple, vertical design of today’s model.

While the interior is not visible in these shots, Renault will likely refresh the cabin. Anticipated updates include upgraded surface materials and enhancements to the infotainment system.

Notably, this test vehicle sports a visible exhaust tip protruding from the rear corner, deviating from the more concealed setup on most current versions. This detail may suggest the manufacturer is assessing potential modifications to the powertrain lineup.

The present Twingo offers a selection of very small engines mounted at the back. Entry-level power comes from a naturally aspirated 1.0-liter three-cylinder generating 70 horsepower (52 kilowatts). A turbocharged 0.9-liter three-cylinder producing 90 hp (67 kW) is also available. The performance-oriented GT variant uses a higher-output 110-horsepower (82 kW) iteration of this compact engine.

LEGAZPI CITY, Albay: The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) would lower from 3 to 4 the alert level for Mount Mayon in the next few weeks if the volcano’s waning activity continued.
Ed Laguerta, Phivolcs chief volcanologist in the Bicol Region, on Saturday said Mayon was showing low abnormal activity in the last 24 hours but no conclusive proof would support that such activity was weakening.
Thus, according to Laguerta, alert level 4 and the eight-kilometer danger zone stay.
He, however, believes that the volcano may still generate explosions as it did in 1984 when Mayon exploded after being quiet for a week.
“We are closely studying the sudden change and decrease of [sulfur dioxide gas emission]of Mayon to 1,583 tons per day from the more than 3,000 tons two days ago,” Laguerta said in a news briefing.
With Alert Level 4 in place, the public is strongly advised to not enter the eight-kilometer danger zone and to be vigilant against pyroclastic currents, lahars and sediment-laden stream flows.
rewrite:
LEGAZPI CITY, Albay: Officials from the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) indicated that the warning status for Mount Mayon could be reduced from its current level 4 to level 3 in coming weeks, provided the decline in volcanic unrest persists. Ed Laguerta, the agency's lead volcanologist for the Bicol area, stated on Saturday that while the mountain's unusual behavior has been minimal over the past day, this does not definitively confirm a de-escalating trend. Consequently, the highest alert and an eight-kilometer restricted perimeter remain enforced.

Laguerta cautioned that sudden eruptions remain possible, similar to a 1984 event following a quiet period. He noted scientists are analyzing a sharp drop in the volcano's daily sulfur dioxide output, now measured at 1,583 tons compared to over 3,000 tons recently. Under the present Alert Level 4, residents must avoid the designated danger zone and stay alert for hazards like pyroclastic flows, mudslides, and ash-heavy river currents.

New Zealand completed a 240-run thumping of the West Indies in the second test at Seddon Park today.
Spinner Mitchell Santner took the last two wickets on consecutive balls shortly before tea on the fourth day, the West Indies being dismissed for 203.
The result ensured a clean sweep, winning the series 2-0 after their innings and 67-run win at the Basin Reserve in the first test.
Read more:
Who is New Zealand's greatest test batsmen?
Advertisement
The West Indies had started the fourth day at 30 for two, requiring an improbable 444 to win.
They lost stand-in captain Kraigg Brathwaite in the sixth over of the day, caught at gully off Trent Boult, giving the left armer his 200th test wicket, just the fifth such bowler to that mark.
Neil Wagner dismissed Roston Chase for 64. Photo / Photosport
He is also the sixth New Zealand bowler to 200, after Richard Hadlee, Dan Vettori, Chris Martin, Chris Cairns and current team mate Tim Southee.
Shai Hope was struck on an arm by Neil Wagner and hooked the next ball straight to fine leg.
Sunil Ambris took a blow on his left wrist and after battling on a few minutes, retired hurt on five. A check revealed a broken bone and he is out of the ODI squad.
Shane Dowrich was caught by Henry Nicholls. Photo / Photosport
Wicketkeeper Shane Dowrich popped a catch to short leg but Roston Chase and Ray Reifer battled solidly to lunch and well into the second session, before they departed in quick order.
Chase completed his fifth half century, 64, while Reifer made 29 before falling to a fine low catch by captain Kane Williamson at gully.
Wagner finished with three for 42 and there were two wickets apiece for Southee, Boult and Santner.
The three-game ODI series starts in Whangarei next Wednesday, before which the tourists' have a one-day fixture against a New Zealand XI on Saturday.
The squad is significantly different from their test group, with the likes of batting heavyweights Chris Gayle and Marlon Samuels and Evin Lewis arriving this week.
The ODI series continues in Christchurch on December 23 and Boxing Day.
rewrite:
New Zealand secured a decisive victory over the West Indies by 240 runs in the second test match at Seddon Park. The conclusion came on day four just prior to the tea interval, as bowler Mitchell Santner claimed the final two wickets in two successive deliveries, ending the West Indies' second innings at 203 runs. This win completes a 2-0 series whitewash, following a dominant innings victory in the opening test in Wellington.

Beginning the day at 30 for two, the visiting team faced a monumental target of 444. Their hopes diminished early when acting captain Kraigg Brathwaite was caught off Trent Boult, a dismissal that marked Boult's 200th test wicket, placing him among an elite group of New Zealand bowlers. He joins Richard Hadlee, Dan Vettori, Chris Martin, Chris Cairns, and teammate Tim Southee in reaching this milestone.

The West Indies innings was plagued by injuries and steady wicket losses. Batsman Shai Hope was hit on the arm and then caught shortly after. Sunil Ambris sustained a wrist fracture that forced him to retire and will sideline him for the upcoming one-day matches. A partnership between Roston Chase, who scored 64, and Ray Reifer, who made 29, provided some resistance before both fell in quick succession. Chase was dismissed by Neil Wagner, who ended with three wickets for 42 runs. Southee, Boult, and Santner each took two wickets.

Attention now shifts to the limited-overs format. The West Indies will play a warm-up match this Saturday before a three-game ODI series commences next Wednesday in Whangarei. Their squad for these matches will feature several new arrivals, including prominent batsmen Chris Gayle, Marlon Samuels, and Evin Lewis, significantly altering the team's composition from the test series. The ODI fixtures will continue with games in Christchurch on December 23rd and December 26th.

FILE PHOTO: An Apple logo is seen in a store in Los Angeles, California, U.S., March 24, 2017. REUTERS/Lucy Nicholson/File Photo
Apple Inc (AAPL.O) has hired a team of biomedical engineers as part of a secret initiative, initially envisioned by late Apple co-founder Steve Jobs, to develop sensors to treat diabetes, CNBC reported citing three people familiar with the matter.
An Apple spokeswoman declined to comment.
The engineers are expected to work at a nondescript office in Palo Alto, California, close to the corporate headquarters, CNBC said.
The news comes at the time when the line between pharmaceuticals and technology is blurring as companies are joining forces to tackle chronic diseases using high-tech devices that combine biology, software and hardware, thereby jump-starting a novel field of medicine called bioelectronics.
Last year, GlaxoSmithKline Plc (GSK.L) and Google parent Alphabet Inc (GOOGL.O) unveiled a joint company aimed at marketing bioelectronic devices to fight illness by attaching to individual nerves.
U.S. biotech firms Setpoint Medical and EnteroMedics Inc (ETRM.O) have already shown early benefits of bioelectronics in treating rheumatoid arthritis and suppressing appetite in the obese.
Other companies playing around the idea of bioelectronics include Medtronic Plc (MDT.N), Proteus Digital Technology, Sanofi SA (SASY.PA) and Biogen Inc (BIIB.O).
The company's shares were marginally up after the bell on Wednesday.
(Reporting by Divya Grover in Bengaluru; Editing by Sandra Maler and Lisa Shumaker)
rewrite:
A photograph on file depicts the Apple logo displayed at a retail location in Los Angeles, California, dating from March 2017. According to a CNBC report, which referenced three informed sources, Apple has assembled a group of biomedical engineers. This team is part of a confidential project, once a concept of the company's late co-founder Steve Jobs, focused on creating sensors for diabetes management. An Apple representative provided no statement on the report.

CNBC indicated the engineers will be based in an unremarkable office in Palo Alto, California, near Apple's main campus. This development emerges as the distinction between the technology and pharmaceutical sectors becomes increasingly indistinct. Firms are now collaborating to address long-term health conditions by employing advanced instruments that integrate biological, software, and electronic components. This convergence is accelerating the growth of an emerging medical area known as bioelectronics.

For instance, GlaxoSmithKline and Alphabet, Google's parent company, last year formed a joint venture to commercialize bioelectronic devices designed to combat diseases by interfacing with specific nerves. Early promising results in using this technology to manage rheumatoid arthritis and control appetite have been demonstrated by U.S. biotechnology companies Setpoint Medical and EnteroMedics. Additional corporations exploring bioelectronics include Medtronic, Proteus Digital Technology, Sanofi, and Biogen. Following the close of trading on Wednesday, Apple's stock experienced a slight increase.

Veteran fly fishing guide Michael “Rocky” Cox will speak Thursday, Feb. 8, at a free, public meeting of the Clinch River Chapter, Trout Unlimited. His presentation starts at 7 p.m. in the parish hall of St. Francis Episcopal Church, 158 W. Norris Road, Norris.
Cox, owner of Rocky Top Anglers, is a Knoxville native who has guided more than 1,000 fishing trips professionally since he started in 2001. He says his upbringing in East Tennessee “allowed me to grow up with wonderful places to play right in my own back yard. Countless miles of mountain streams and cold tailwaters provided endless playgrounds. I never realized how much those years of playing in the water would influence my adult life.
“I’ve always loved the peaceful excitement of fly fishing and always found myself thinking about that next big trip to the mountains. When my leisure time came, I was fly fishing. I was captivated by the old guides, rowing their anglers downriver and finding those special places only accessible by driftboat. I knew that guiding others and showing them the places I treasure would be a very rewarding career.”
Clinch River Chapter TU works to preserve and protect the Clinch River tailwater and its watershed through conservation projects and through education of children and adults in aquatic natural resources. For more information, visit http://crctu.org.

Norris Road in Norris.

He credits his East Tennessee childhood, with its abundant mountain streams and cold tailwaters, for providing a natural playground that profoundly shaped his future. He did not anticipate how formative those early experiences in the water would become.

Cox describes a lifelong passion for the serene thrill of fly fishing, constantly planning his next mountain adventure and dedicating his free time to the pursuit. He was inspired by veteran guides navigating rivers by driftboat to reach secluded spots, which led him to a fulfilling career sharing his cherished locations with others.

The Clinch River Chapter of Trout Unlimited focuses on conserving the Clinch River tailwater and its surrounding basin. Their efforts include habitat projects and educating people of all ages about water-based ecosystems. Additional details are available on their website.

Wealth and health are definitely connected. But race is also a significant factor, with black residents facing health outcomes that lag behind those of white New Jerseyans — often significantly — over the span a lifetime.
Those are among the conclusions of data released last week as part of the annual County Health Rankings, a national report produced by the New Jersey-based Robert Wood Johnson Foundation and the University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute. The findings compare counties across the nation on measures like low birth-weight babies, poor health days, and early death — as well as factors that impact these outcomes, including smoking, education levels, and obesity.
Racial disparities in health have become a growing focus in recent years, and Dr. Shereef Elnahal, the acting commissioner of the state Department of Health, has made it a priority to reduce these gaps, which he called “embarrassingly high” at a recent hearing. “Needless to say, we have much work ahead to improve New Jersey’s public health,” he told the Senate Judiciary committee earlier this month.
Click here for the full article »
Please enable JavaScript to view the comments powered by Disqus.
rewrite:
There is a clear link between economic status and well-being. However, racial identity also plays a major role, as Black individuals in New Jersey consistently experience poorer health than their white counterparts throughout their lives.

These insights come from the latest County Health Rankings, a nationwide study published annually by the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation and the University of Wisconsin. The report evaluates U.S. counties on various health indicators, such as infant birth weight, self-reported unhealthy days, and premature mortality. It also examines influencing factors like tobacco use, educational attainment, and high body mass index.

Addressing health inequities across racial groups has gained increased attention. New Jersey's Acting Health Commissioner, Dr. Shereef Elnahal, has prioritized narrowing these divides, describing them as unacceptably large during recent legislative testimony. He stated before a state senate committee that substantial effort is still required to enhance the overall health of the state's residents.

Kathrine Herzer has been an actress since she was 10 years old, but her role as Allison McCord on the CBS hit political drama Madam Secretary changed her life. While the California native had small roles in movies such as Mr. and Mrs. Smith and A Lot Like Love, her recurring role alongside stars such as Tea Leoni and Keith Carradine took her career to the next level.
“Madam Secretary is the best,” Herzer told CBS Local in a recent studio interview. “I got the part when I was a junior in high school and I would commute back and forth to New York when we started filming. It’s the best group of people to work with and we have these amazing scripts that create this great energy.”
In addition to her work on Madam Secretary, Herzer is also a full time student at New York University. While her schedule has its challenges, the 20-year-old rising star wouldn’t change anything.
“It’s a lot to balance, but I wouldn’t have it any other way,” Herzer said. “There’s so much that I get from working and going to school at the same time.”
Season Four of the show will be a big one for the McCord family, as Allison is on her way to college. The new season, which premieres Sunday, October 8th at 10pm eastern on CBS, will feature a more mature and empowered Allison McCord.
“Allison is in such a crazy time in her life because she is going to college. She’s venturing into her own world, but the McCord family is so close that it just means that they are all branching out into this new area. I think this bit of independence will give her a lot of power, its an exciting season for her.”

She described the cast and crew as an exceptional team to collaborate with and praised the compelling scripts that foster a dynamic and positive atmosphere on set.

She finds the simultaneous engagement in work and education to be immensely rewarding and enriching.

The upcoming fourth season presents a major transition for her character, as Allison prepares to embark on her college journey. Herzer notes that this period involves navigating newfound independence while maintaining close family bonds, as the entire McCord family explores this fresh chapter together. LAWRENCE, Kan. — Kansas forward Udoka Azubuike withdrew his name from the NBA draft on Wednesday, choosing to return for his junior season after participating in the combine.
The 7-footer from Nigeria started 34 games last season, averaging 13 points and seven rebounds. He shot 77 per cent from the field, a Big 12 record and the best mark in the nation.
Azubuike is a traditional back-to-the-basket big man, and scouts have wondered how his skills would transfer to the NBA. The league's up-tempo pace and the value placed on big men who can shoot from outside go against his strengths, and developing an outside shot will likely be an emphasis at Kansas.
Azubuike said in a statement that he received "good feedback from many sources around the NBA over the last month." He did not hire an agent and had until Wednesday's deadline to withdraw.
rewrite:
LAWRENCE, Kan. — Udoka Azubuike, a forward for Kansas, has decided to return for his third year of college basketball, pulling out of the NBA draft. He made this announcement Wednesday following his involvement in the draft combine.

Standing seven feet tall and hailing from Nigeria, Azubuike was a regular starter last season, posting averages of 13 points and seven rebounds per game. His 77 percent success rate on field goals set a conference record and led the country.

As a classic center who operates near the basket, his fit in the modern NBA is questioned. The league's faster style and preference for centers who can score from distance do not align with his current game, making the development of a perimeter shot a probable focus during his upcoming season.

Azubuike noted he gathered valuable evaluations from NBA figures over recent weeks. By not retaining an agent, he maintained the option to withdraw by the Wednesday cutoff.

Josh Gordon says Packers CB Demarious Randle ‘couldn’t hold my jock strap’
Josh Gordon looked like he could be in for a monster day after he caught two big passes in the first quarter of Sunday’s game, but Green Bay Packers cornerback Demarious Randall did a solid job covering him the rest of the way. Did Randle earn the right to brag about it? That depends on who you ask.
After the game, Randle was asked about his performance against Gordon. He was beaming with confidence.
How well did #Packers CB Damarious Randall cover #Browns WR Josh Gordon? “He had one catch,” Randall said. “Any more questions?” https://t.co/xXwCq9JWOi — Packers News (@PGPackersNews) December 11, 2017
Gordon wasn’t all that impressed. While he complimented the Packers for grinding out an overtime win, he hinted that he would torch Randall if the Cleveland Browns were a better team overall.
Great Win for them but let’s be serious.. Considering several of our disadvantages as a team, this kid couldn’t hold my jock strap on my worst day lol..@RandallTime https://t.co/ennvwjTMUH — Flash Gordon (@JOSH_GORDONXII) December 11, 2017
After seeing Gordon’s tweet, Randall didn’t hold back.
“You must be on that s— again,” he replied.
Gordon ended up with three catches for 69 yards, including one that was an extremely acrobatic touchdown reception early on. Just one of those catches came when Randall was covering him.
Obviously, Gordon would be far more difficult to cover if he had a better quarterback than DeShone Kizer throwing to him. Still, Randall deserves credit for shutting him down in man coverage. Gordon has looked as athletic as ever in his first two games back.
rewrite:
Wide receiver Josh Gordon suggested that Green Bay Packers cornerback Damarious Randall was not in his league following their matchup. Gordon started strong in Sunday's contest, making two significant receptions in the opening quarter. However, Randall effectively contained him for the remainder of the game. Whether this defensive success warranted boasting is a matter of perspective.

Speaking post-game, Randall radiated self-assurance when questioned about covering Gordon, pointedly noting the receiver only managed a single catch against him. Gordon, while acknowledging the Packers' overtime victory, downplayed Randall's individual performance. He implied via social media that, given the Cleveland Browns' overall team shortcomings, Randall would be utterly outmatched against him under different circumstances, using a colorful phrase to question the cornerback's ability.

Randall fired back with a sharp retort to Gordon's post, alluding to the receiver's past off-field issues. Statistically, Gordon finished with three receptions for 69 yards and a spectacular early touchdown, but only one of those catches occurred with Randall in direct coverage. It is reasonable to argue Gordon would pose a greater threat with a more established quarterback, yet Randall's performance in one-on-one situations deserves recognition. Gordon has demonstrated his trademark athleticism since returning to play, making the effective coverage against him more notable.

Cypriot television networks may face fierce competition from a planned new Russian-language channel which could attract a considerable number of advertisers.
Even though no formal complaint has yet been submitted to the Cyprus Broadcasting Authority, there is a lot of behind-the-scenes pressure on authorities to drop the condition of Greek subtitles in Russian-language broadcasts. In this way, they hope to limit the Russian channel’s number of viewers and hence the interest of Cypriot businesses in advertising.
The Russian-language channel has only recently secured a temporary broadcast licence, subject to the rule that its broadcasts will have Greek subtitles. This term was applied because the Cyprus Radio Television Authority needed to be able control the channel’s broadcasts without hiring additional personnel fluent in Russian.
This channel’s licence, as well the licences of all other non-subscription channels in Cyprus, expired on 30 June 2018. The Cyprus Radio Television Authority is currently reviewing applications submitted for new temporary licences which will be valid until 30 June 2019.
Shareholders of the company behind the creation and operation of the Russian-language channel network were willing to abide with the directives of the Cyprus Broadcasting Authority from the start and have already approached companies with relevant experience in subtitling.
According to sources, members of the Board of Directors of Cyprus Broadcasting Authority are considering withdrawing the demand for subtitles. Overall, it appears that the broadcasting Authority is heading towards a partial withdrawal of the term: in particular, it is probable that some of the broadcasts and not all of them will be subtitled.
rewrite:
A new Russian-language television station being planned for Cyprus could draw significant advertising revenue, posing a strong competitive challenge to existing local networks. Although no official grievance has been lodged with the Cyprus Broadcasting Authority, considerable informal pressure is being exerted on regulators to eliminate the mandate for Greek subtitles on Russian-language programming. The aim of this push is to reduce the prospective channel's audience size, thereby making it less appealing to potential advertisers based in Cyprus.

This channel has only obtained a provisional license to operate, contingent on the requirement that its content includes Greek subtitles. This condition was instituted so the Cyprus Radio Television Authority could oversee the broadcasts without needing to employ extra staff proficient in Russian. The licenses for this and all other non-subscription channels in the country lapsed on June 30, 2018. The authority is now in the process of evaluating requests for new provisional licenses, which would remain effective until June 30, 2019.

From the outset, the investors in the company establishing this Russian-language network have expressed readiness to comply with the broadcasting authority's regulations and have already contacted firms specializing in subtitle services. Reports indicate that members of the Cyprus Broadcasting Authority's board are contemplating revoking the subtitle stipulation. In general, the authority seems to be moving toward a moderated stance, likely requiring subtitles for only a portion of the broadcasts rather than for all content.

input: Looks like Mayor Fred Eisenberger's puppy, Dash, will have a new friend to visit when he heads to work with the mayor this summer. Pictured here is Ralph, the creation of the City of Hamilton's horticultural staff. The approximately 15-foot sculpture was developed using Carex buchananii (leatherleaf sedge), a sage grass native to New Zealand and grown in the city greenhouses this spring. The grasses were rooted into a frame created by local metal artist Trevor McInytre with the internal infrastructure designed and implemented by the horticultural staff. This includes soil and a watering system inside the sculpture to keep Ralph's "fur" healthy and growing throughout the hot summer. The whimsical garden's designs were initiated by Marcia Monaghan, superintendent of horticulture for the city. She says her inspiration came from seeing Mosaic Culture, a huge horticultural display in Ottawa last year. Monaghan says that despite all the significant dog references — including the mayor's dog, the OHL-winning Bulldogs and the fact that it is the Year of the Dog in Chinese culture — none of these were actually the inspiration for the sculpture. Monaghan says, "We just thought it would be fun." The gardens, which also include a huge butterfly, will be completed midday Friday.

A metal framework built by local artist Trevor McInytre supports the piece, while city staff engineered its inner structure, incorporating soil and an irrigation network to sustain the grassy “coat” through the warm season.

The playful garden concept originated with Marcia Monaghan, the city’s horticulture superintendent. She drew motivation from Mosaic Culture, a large-scale horticultural exhibition she viewed in Ottawa last year. Monaghan clarifies that, although numerous canine connections exist—from the mayor’s pet to the OHL champion Bulldogs and the Chinese zodiac’s Year of the Dog—none directly inspired Ralph. Her simple explanation: the team believed it would be an enjoyable project. Alongside a large butterfly display, the gardens are scheduled for completion by Friday afternoon.

VICTORIA — Here are questions Attorney General David Eby has recommended to cabinet for a referendum this fall on British Columbia’s electoral system:
1. Which should British Columbia use for elections to the legislative assembly (Vote for only one):
— The current first-past-the post voting system.
— A proportional representation voting system.
2. If British Columbia adopts a proportional representation voting system, which of the following voting systems do you prefer? (Vote for the voting systems you wish to support by ranking them in order of preference. You may choose to support one, two or all three of the systems):
— Dual-member proportional.
— Mixed-member proportional.
— Rural-urban.
——
Here is a look at the three systems of proportional representation that have been recommended:
— Dual-member proportional would take most of the province’s existing single-member electoral districts and amalgamate them with a second neighbouring district to create two-member districts. The largest rural districts could remain unchanged as single-member districts. Parties could nominate up to two candidates in each district. They would appear on the ballot in an order determined by the party. The first seats would be won by the first candidates of the party that received the most votes in each electoral district. The second seats would be allocated based on provincewide voting results and individual district results.
— A mixed-member system would combine single-member electoral districts, where members are elected under first past the post, with seats also allocated on a regional or provincial level and based on a list of candidates running for proportional representation seats prepared by the parties.
— A rural-urban option is also a mixed system that elects members of the legislature two ways. In urban and semi-urban areas, a single transferable vote would be used to rank candidates by preference. In rural areas, single-member electoral districts would elect their representative using the first-past-the-post system, while a small number of proportional representation seats would also be allocated from a list prepared by the parties based on election results.
rewrite:
VICTORIA — The Attorney General, David Eby, has put forward proposed questions for a fall referendum on changing British Columbia’s electoral process. The cabinet will consider these recommendations. Voters would face two key questions:

First, they would be asked to choose one option for electing members to the legislative assembly: keeping the existing first-past-the-post method or switching to a form of proportional representation.

Second, if a move toward proportional representation is approved, voters would then indicate their preferences among three specific systems. They could rank one, two, or all three in order of choice. The options are dual-member proportional, mixed-member proportional, and a rural-urban model.

The three proportional systems under consideration function as follows:

Dual-member proportional would primarily merge two neighboring single-member ridings into larger, two-member districts, though the most expansive rural ridings might stay as they are. Each party could run two candidates per district, listed in a party-determined order on the ballot. The leading party in a district wins the first seat for its top-listed candidate. The second seat is then assigned through a calculation that balances provincial vote totals with local results.

A mixed-member proportional system blends single-member constituencies, elected by first past the post, with additional regional or province-wide seats. These extra seats are filled from party lists to make the overall legislature reflect the popular vote more proportionally.

The rural-urban model is another mixed approach. In cities and suburbs, a single transferable vote system would be used, allowing voters to rank candidates. In predominantly rural areas, representatives would be chosen from single-member districts via first past the post. A limited number of compensatory seats, drawn from party lists, would then be added to enhance proportionality across the final results.

Breaking News Emails Get breaking news alerts and special reports. The news and stories that matter, delivered weekday mornings. SUBSCRIBE
WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court ruled Tuesday that thousands of victims of terrorist attacks overseas cannot sue a foreign bank under a U.S. law dating from the 1700s.
By a 5-4 vote, the court refused to revive lawsuits, dismissed by the lower courts, that sought to hold Arab Bank, which is headquartered in Jordan, responsible for attacks against foreign nationals in the Middle East. More than 6,000 survivors and relatives of those killed in the West Bank and Gaza claimed that officials of the bank were complicit in the attacks.
Beginning in 2004, the victims filed a series of lawsuits accusing the bank of helping to finance Hamas and other terror organizations. The legal action was filed in the U.S. and aimed at Arab Bank through its branch in New York. The lead plaintiff in the case before the Supreme Court, Joseph Jesner, lost his 19-year-old son to a suicide bombing in Tel Aviv.
The lawsuits invoked one of the first laws ever passed by Congress, the Alien Tort Statute of 1789, known as ATS, intended to be a forum for resolving claims of piracy. But Tuesday's ruling said the law did not allow lawsuits of the kind filed by the terror victims.
"Absent further action from Congress, it would be inappropriate for courts to extend ATS liability to foreign corporations," wrote Justice Anthony Kennedy for the court's majority.
"Courts are not well suited to make the required policy judgments that are implicated by corporate liability in cases like this one."

Stay informed with urgent news notifications and exclusive coverage. Essential headlines and narratives are sent directly to you each weekday morning. SUBSCRIBE

WASHINGTON — In a decision issued Tuesday, the Supreme Court determined that U.S. courts cannot be used by thousands of individuals harmed by terrorist acts abroad to pursue legal action against an overseas financial institution under a centuries-old American statute. The ruling was decided by a narrow 5-4 margin.

The court declined to reinstate legal claims that had been thrown out by lower courts. These suits attempted to assign liability to Jordan-based Arab Bank for violent incidents involving non-U.S. citizens in the Middle East. Over 6,000 plaintiffs, including survivors and family members of deceased victims from the West Bank and Gaza, alleged the bank played a supporting role in the attacks.

Legal proceedings began in 2004, with a succession of cases filed in American courts targeting the bank's New York branch. The plaintiffs charged that the institution facilitated funding for Hamas and similar groups. Joseph Jesner, the principal petitioner in this Supreme Court appeal, is the father of a 19-year-old killed in a Tel Aviv suicide bombing.

The litigation relied on the Alien Tort Statute (ATS), an original 1789 congressional act initially created to address claims related to piracy. The Court's majority opinion clarified that this antiquated law does not provide a legal pathway for the claims brought forward by the victims of terrorism.

Writing for the majority, Justice Anthony Kennedy stated that extending ATS responsibilities to international corporations is beyond the judiciary's role without explicit congressional authorization. He added that the courts lack the appropriate capacity to navigate the complex policy decisions inherent in imposing corporate accountability in such international matters.

SYRACUSE, N.Y. – It goes without saying that when you order something custom-made, you expect to receive exactly what you imagine.
However, for Malexa Maeweather, an 18-year-old from Syracuse, New York, a made-to-order prom dress had some unexpected and disastrous results.
According to Seventeen Magazine, Maeweather reached out to a local designer, Kia Wagner, in the hopes that she could create a one-of-a-kind prom dress. Instead, she said she got an absolute dress fail. Even worse, Maeweather didn’t get to see the dress until the night before prom.
Maeweather told WGN, “I was so upset and very aggravated. I didn’t know what I was going to do.”
It wasn’t just Maeweather who was disappointed with the results of the dress. In fact, Maeweather’s mother, Dee Lewis, told Seventeen that Wagner never updated her daughter on the progress of the dress, which left the teen in tears when it finally arrived. Having already put down a $100 downpayment for the dress priced at $300, Lewis took to Facebook to express her discontent.
“So Kia Wagner called my daughter Malexa Maeweather THE NIGHT before prom to pick up her dress which she charges $300 for. Are you serious…was I wrong for wanting my DEPOSIT BACK.”
In response to Lewis, Wagner also posted on Facebook stating, “the reason [Lewis] will not get her $100 deposit back is because I was simply following the instructions she agreed and decided to she had a variety of fabric selections to choose from and as well as several of fittings where i asked her numerous of times if this was the look she was going for…”
Nevertheless, with help from her mother and close friends, Maeweather was able to find and purchase a new dress to salvage her prom day.
rewrite:
In Syracuse, New York, ordering a custom garment typically comes with the anticipation that the final product will match the buyer’s vision. For 18-year-old Malexa Maeweather, however, a specially designed prom gown led to frustration and letdown. As reported by Seventeen Magazine, Maeweather had commissioned local designer Kia Wagner to craft a unique dress for the event, but the outcome was far from what she envisioned. Compounding the issue, she only received the dress the evening before prom.

Maeweather expressed her distress to WGN, stating she felt deeply upset and aggravated, uncertain how to handle the situation. Her mother, Dee Lewis, also spoke to Seventeen, noting that Wagner provided no updates during the dress’s creation, which left her daughter in tears upon its arrival. Lewis had already paid a $100 deposit toward the total $300 cost. She took to Facebook to voice her frustration, questioning the designer’s decision to notify them just a day before the dance and demanding a refund of the deposit.

Wagner responded on Facebook, defending her position by explaining that the deposit was nonrefundable because she had followed the agreed-upon design process. She mentioned offering multiple fabric choices and conducting several fittings where she confirmed the desired look.

Despite the disappointment, Maeweather, with support from her mother and friends, managed to find and buy another dress in time, saving her prom night.

* Stocks lower on signs Fed may cut balance sheet this yr
* Automakers and banks underperform
* Defense firm Ishikawa Seisakusho soars on N.Korea concerns
By Ayai Tomisawa
TOKYO, April 6 Japan's Nikkei share average tumbled to a four-month low on Thursday morning after U.S. shares tumbled overnight on signs the U.S. Federal Reserve may start cutting its king-sized balance sheet earlier than expected.
The Nikkei dropped 1.4 percent to 18,595.12 points by the midday break, the lowest since early December.
Investors were spooked by minutes of the Fed's last meeting, which showed most policymakers thought the U.S. central bank should begin trimming its $4.5 trillion balance sheet this year.
The minutes also showed "some participants viewed equity prices as quite high relative to standard valuation measures."
"We were hit by a bucket of cold water," said Norihiro Fujito, senior investment strategist at Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities.
"Signs that the Fed could pare its balance sheet is shocking enough, but the mood was exacerbated as the Fed touched upon stock valuations, which is very rare," he added.
Automakers, which were already under pressure after weak March U.S. auto sales this week, extended their decline after the dollar fell 0.3 percent at 110.390 yen. Toyota Motor Corp dropped 0.9 percent and Nissan Motor Co Ltd tumbled 1.5 percent.
Banking stocks also lost ground, with Mizuho Financial Group Inc slipping 2.0 percent and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group Inc shedding 1.4 percent.
Investors were also wary ahead of a potentially tense meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, the first between the world's two most powerful leaders.
Meanwhile, defence equipment maker Ishikawa Seisakusho Ltd soared 15 percent to a daily limit high of 1,137 yen, the highest level since July 2015. Investors believe demand for the company's defence equipment could surge as concerns escalate over North Korea.
Regional tensions have risen after North Korea test-fired a ballistic missile on Wednesday, just a day before the Trump-Xi summit, where North Korea's arms development drive will take centre stage.
The broader Topix dropped 1.1 percent to 1,488.39 and the JPX-Nikkei Index 400 declined 1.1 percent to 13,327.02.
(Editing by Randy Fabi)
rewrite:
Japanese equities declined sharply during Thursday's morning session, with the benchmark Nikkei index reaching its lowest point in four months. This followed a substantial overnight drop in U.S. markets, triggered by indications that the Federal Reserve might begin reducing its expansive asset holdings sooner than anticipated.

By midday, the Nikkei had fallen 1.4 percent to 18,595.12, a level not seen since the beginning of December. The sell-off was prompted by the release of minutes from the Fed's most recent policy meeting. These notes revealed that a majority of officials believe the central bank should start shrinking its $4.5 trillion portfolio within the current year. Additionally, the minutes contained observations from certain policymakers that stock prices appeared elevated when judged by traditional metrics.

Market analysts described the impact as a sobering shock. The mere suggestion of the Fed reducing its balance sheet was unsettling, but the rare commentary on equity valuations further worsened investor sentiment, according to a senior strategist at Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities.

Automobile manufacturers, already facing pressure from disappointing U.S. sales figures reported earlier in the week, saw further losses. A slight weakening of the dollar against the yen contributed to the sector's decline, with notable share price decreases for major companies like Toyota and Nissan. The banking sector also retreated, with shares of Mizuho Financial and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group both moving lower.

Investor caution was heightened by the impending first meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping, a potentially high-stakes encounter between the leaders of the world's two largest economies.

In a contrasting move, shares of defense contractor Ishikawa Seisakusho surged by the daily limit of 15 percent. This jump, which pushed the stock to its highest price since mid-2015, was fueled by investor speculation that rising geopolitical concerns over North Korea could increase demand for the company's products. Regional tensions were amplified after North Korea conducted a ballistic missile test on Wednesday, ensuring its weapons program will be a central topic during the upcoming summit.

The broader Topix index and the JPX-Nikkei Index 400 both fell 1.1 percent in tandem with the market's downward trend.
