The Sports Authority of India (SAI) is set for an overhaul with Sports minister Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore announcing change in its name. Now SAI will be called Sports India. The minister also announced some structural changes in the body along with an increase in the daily food expenses of the athletes.
Sports Minister Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore on Wednesday announced that the Sports Authority of India (SAI) will be renamed. While it was not an official announcement, Rathore said that it will be called as Sports India, for the time being.
The minister also announced structural changes in the body along with an increase in the daily food expenses of the athletes.
“It’ll be made leaner, some posts won’t be retained after officers on them retire. Daily expenses of food for athletes are being raised, for which committee is also being formed,” Rathore was quoted by ANI as saying.
Last year in August 2017, the minister had said that the government was planning to change the name of the authority. He had said that there is no need for authority in sports as it’s all about service.
On being asked about the sports quota, Rathore said that the government was in favour for a minimum quota to be fixed for sportspersons. According to reports, he further said that Olympic-winning sports stars should be given reservation in ‘Grade A’ jobs.”
Rathore, who is himself an Olympic medalist, said that Centre was aiming to make the organisation more ‘lean and professional’ by reducing its strength by around 50 percent by 2022. He added that the Centre was also planning to come out with measures to expand its search for talent across the country and government wants to work towards developing a culture of sports among school students.
The SAI was established back in 1984 adn was registered as a Society under Socities Act in pursuance of the Resolution of 1984 of the Departments of Sports with the only objective of promotion of Sports and Games in the country.
SAI comes under the authority of Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. The Ministry was set up as the Department of Sports in 1982 at the time of IX Asian Games in New Delhi.
For all the latest National News, download NewsX App
Read More
rewrite:
India's Sports Minister Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore has declared that the Sports Authority of India (SAI) will undergo a significant transformation, beginning with a new identity. The organization will now be known as Sports India, marking a shift in its official designation. Alongside this rebranding, the minister outlined plans to streamline the institution's framework and enhance the daily nutritional allowances provided to athletes.

Rathore indicated that the body would adopt a more efficient structure, with certain positions being phased out as current officeholders retire. To address the dietary needs of athletes, a dedicated committee will be established to manage the increased food budget. These statements were conveyed through a report by ANI.

The consideration for a name change was initially mentioned by the minister in August 2017, when he expressed the view that sports management should focus on service rather than authority. During recent discussions, Rathore also advocated for establishing a guaranteed quota for athletes in certain sectors, suggesting that Olympic champions should be eligible for top-tier government positions.

An Olympic medalist himself, Rathore emphasized the central government's goal to create a more agile and expert organization by aiming to cut its workforce by half before 2022. Additionally, efforts will be made to broaden the nationwide hunt for athletic potential and to encourage sports participation among schoolchildren.

Originally founded in 1984 under the Societies Act following a government resolution, SAI was created with the sole purpose of advancing sports throughout the nation. It operates under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, which originated as the Department of Sports in 1982 during the IX Asian Games hosted in New Delhi.

TOURISM DOWN: There is trouble brewing for tourism in Agnes Water and Seventeen Seventy.
CONCERNS over a significant drop in tourism numbers at Agnes Water and Seventeen Seventy will be one of the key focuses at Gladstone Regional Council's general meeting today.
Over the last 18 months the two coastal towns have been impacted by a decrease in tourists visiting, with tourism operators holding three interlinked issues responsible:
Sand collecting in Round Hill Creek, reducing access
A lack of marina facilities to facilitate trips to the reef
A lack of reef operators capable of taking passengers
Gladstone Area Promotion and Development Limited CEO Darryl Branthwaite said the issues added up to one major problem.
"The access through Round Hill Creek is very limited for marine operators, and access is 75% of the problem here,” Mr Branthwaite said.
"Agnes Water and Seventeen Seventy have been really affected for a lengthy period of time with less reef operators going to Lady Musgrave,” he said.
Mr Branthwaite said Gladstone Regional Council had to intervene as the access situation "needs to be dramatically improved and quickly”.
A Gladstone Regional Council spokesperson said dredging at Round Hill Creek would be considered at today's council meeting.
Problems with dredging, however, include the expense and the risk the sand builds up when weather conditions change.
Discovery Coast Tourism and Commerce president Amber Rodgers said even if the creek was dredged today, tourist rates would not improve overnight.
"The reality is council are not going to go buy a new boat if access is improved. That's up to investors,” she said.
"The huge investment depends on a lot of people and the fact is, right now, we are seeing how having less seats going to the reef is affecting the rest of our businesses.”
rewrite:
The Agnes Water and Seventeen Seventy region is facing a serious tourism decline, a pressing issue set for discussion at the Gladstone Regional Council's upcoming meeting. Industry representatives point to three connected challenges that have reduced visitor numbers over the past year and a half: sediment accumulation in Round Hill Creek hindering boat access, an absence of marina infrastructure for reef excursions, and a shortage of tour companies offering trips to the reef.

Darryl Branthwaite, CEO of Gladstone Area Promotion and Development Limited, identifies restricted passage through the creek as the primary concern, accounting for the bulk of the difficulty. He notes the prolonged negative effect on both towns due to fewer operators running trips to Lady Musgrave Island. Branthwaite emphasizes the urgency for council action to substantially and swiftly enhance marine access.

A council representative confirmed that dredging the creek is on the meeting's agenda. Nevertheless, such a project faces hurdles, including high costs and the likelihood of sand returning with shifting weather patterns. Amber Rodgers, president of Discovery Coast Tourism and Commerce, cautions that even immediate dredging would not produce a rapid rebound in tourist activity. She explains that improved access alone does not guarantee new investment in vessels, which is left to private investors. The current shortage of reef tour capacity, she states, is having a damaging ripple effect across all local enterprises, underscoring that recovery hinges on a coordinated effort from multiple stakeholders.

HENRICO COUNTY, Va. — Police used a phone left in a stolen car to track down a driver who drove off in a car that was not his.
The car was left running outside a 7-11 on Williamsburg Road around 8 p.m. on New Year’s Eve.
“The victim stated he left his vehicle running, unlocked, and with his phone in it while he ran into 7-Eleven,” a Henrico Police spokesman said. “He was surprised to find his vehicle missing when he came out.”
Using the phone left in the car, police tracked the vehicle to an address on N. 23rd Street in Richmond.
“Officers arrived to find Mr. [Dustin Avory] Swan driving the stolen car,” police said. “During the arrest, Mr. Swan kicked one of the Henrico officers. Once in custody it was determined that Swan was also intoxicated.”
Swan, 44, was charged with Grand Larceny, Disorderly Conduct, and his second DWI in the last five – 10 years.

In Henrico County, Virginia, law enforcement located a stolen vehicle by following a cellphone that had been left inside it. The incident occurred on December 31st when the owner briefly entered a 7-Eleven on Williamsburg Road, leaving his car unlocked and idling with his phone inside. Upon returning, he discovered the car was gone.

Authorities used the phone's location data to find the car at a residence on North 23rd Street in Richmond. There, they encountered Dustin Avory Swan operating the vehicle. During his apprehension, Swan assaulted an officer by kicking him. He was subsequently taken into custody, where it was also found that he was under the influence of alcohol.

Swan, age 44, now faces charges including Grand Larceny and Disorderly Conduct. This arrest also marks his second drunk driving offense within the past decade.

Scientists ID Tiny Prehistoric Sea Worm with 50 Head Spines
Long before dinosaurs roamed the Earth, a bizarre creature with a Venus flytrap-like head swam the seas. Scientists have uncovered fossils of a tiny faceless prehistoric sea worm with 50 spines jutting out of its head. When some unsuspecting critter came too close, its jaw-like spines snapped together and dinner was served.
The discovery reported in Thursday's journal Current Biology offers a glimpse into the Cambrian explosion of life on Earth about 541 million years ago.
The new creature dubbed Capinatator praetermissus is so different that scientists said the fossils represent not only a new species, but a new genus -- a larger grouping of life -- as well.
It was only 4 inches long and its spines were about one-third of an inch long. It feasted on smaller plankton and shrimp-like creatures.
It is an ancestor of a group of marine arrow worms called chaetognatha that are abundant in the world's oceans. The prehistoric version was larger and with far more spines in its facial armory but without the specialized teeth of its descendants, said Derek Briggs of Yale University who led a team that discovered the trove of fossils in two national parks in British Columbia, Canada.
"The spines are like miniature hooks, although more gently curved. They were stiff rather than flexible," Briggs said in an email. "It's hard to say why there are so many spines in the fossil example -- but presumably thus armed it was a successful predator."
Capinatator -- whose name translates to grasping swimmer -- lived 500 million years ago at a time when creatures started getting bigger and more diverse. It's difficult to find complete fossils belonging to the chaetognatha family because they decayed easily, said Briggs. This latest find, however, was so good that even soft tissue was saved, giving scientists a good idea about what Capinatator looked like.
The discovery expands scientists' knowledge of a "pretty enigmatic" group of animals from the Cambrian era, said Smithsonian paleobiologist Doug Erwin, who had no role in the research.

Image credit: Yale Research; Drawing by Marianne Collins. Copyright Royal Ontario Museum.
Read more on: Scientists, Researchers, Fossil, Biology, Discovery, Prehistoric, Dinosaurs
rewrite:
Researchers have identified a minuscule ancient marine worm distinguished by fifty sharp protrusions on its head. This odd animal, which inhabited the oceans long before the age of dinosaurs, possessed a head apparatus reminiscent of a Venus flytrap. Upon examination of fossil remains, experts determined that when potential prey ventured near, these spiny structures would swiftly close like jaws to capture a meal.

Findings published in the journal *Current Biology* provide a window into the Cambrian period, roughly 541 million years ago, when life on Earth underwent a rapid diversification. The organism, named *Capinatator praetermissus*, is considered so unique that it has been classified as both a novel species and a new genus, representing a broader category of life forms.

Measuring about four inches in length, with spines approximately a third of an inch long, it likely preyed upon small plankton and shrimp-like organisms. This creature is an early relative of modern arrow worms, known as chaetognaths, which are common in today's seas. According to Yale University's Derek Briggs, who headed the team that found numerous fossils in Canadian national parks, the ancient form was bigger and bore significantly more head spines than its contemporary descendants, though it lacked their specialized teeth.

Briggs described the spines as resembling small, rigid hooks with a gentle curve. While the exact reason for their great number remains uncertain, this formidable armament probably made it an effective hunter. The name *Capinatator* means "grasping swimmer," and it existed around 500 million years ago, during a phase when ocean life was increasing in both size and variety.

Because such organisms decomposed readily, complete fossils from the chaetognath lineage are rare. However, this particular specimen was exceptionally well-preserved, retaining even soft tissues and offering a clear picture of the animal's appearance. Smithsonian paleobiologist Doug Erwin, who was not involved in the study, noted that the find broadens understanding of a rather mysterious group of Cambrian-era creatures.

Over the weekend, the Alabama Senate race reached its homestretch as national Democrats like Sen. Cory Booker and former Massachusetts governor Deval Patrick traveled south and stumped for former prosecutor Doug Jones while Republicans released a video of alleged pedophile Roy Moore being interviewed by a 12-year-old girl. Democrats are hoping that their strategy will be more effective and are set to unleash a Barack Obama robocall aimed at Alabama voters to head to the polls on Election Day.
“This one’s serious,” Obama says in the call. “You can’t sit it out.”
According to CNN, Obama recorded his message in the last few days as President Trump (who also recorded a robocall) has ratcheted up his endorsements of Roy Moore. Obama does not mention Moore’s name in his call but focuses on Doug Jones’ virtues as a candidate.
“Doug Jones is a fighter for equality, for progress,” Obama says. “Doug will be our champion for justice. So get out and vote, Alabama.”
In November, Obama campaigned for Virginia’s Ralph Northam and New Jersey’s Phil Murphy in their gubernatorial elections, which both Democrats won. While it’s not known how much of an effect either Obama or Trump’s robocalls will have on the election, as the polls show, the involvement of both men is yet another clear indication that the candidates are running neck and neck.

OTTAWA — Only weeks after Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said Canada was prepared to offer helicopters, aircraft and hundreds of troops to peacekeeping, the number of Canadians on UN missions reached a new low, new figures indicate.
Canada had a total of 43 peacekeepers deployed around the world at the end of December, according to the most recent UN numbers, down from 62 in November.
The decline, largely the result of a reduction in the number of Canadian police officers deployed to Haiti, means Canada has fewer peacekeepers in the field than at any point since the 1950s.
That's despite the Liberals having repeatedly promised to ramp up Canada's contributions to UN missions — most recently by pledging equipment, troops and trainers at a peacekeeping summit that Canada hosted in November.
Canadian and UN officials say the two sides are working to identify when and where those pledges will be utilized, but they have declined to provide any timeline for when a decision will come.
Walter Dorn, an expert on peacekeeping at the Canadian Forces College in Toronto who has been tracking the numbers, said the current situation is shameful given the Trudeau government's repeated promises.
"Canada is at its lowest level since Lester B. Pearson proposed the first peacekeeping force in 1956," Dorn said. "This is hypocrisy, coming after the promises and lofty rhetoric of the Vancouver ministerial."
The Liberals promised during the last federal election to renew Canada's commitment to peacekeeping, and pledged in August 2016 to make up to 600 troops and 150 police officers available for future missions.
Canada had 112 peacekeepers in the field at the time of that promise.
Trudeau announced in Vancouver in November that Canada was offering helicopters, a transport aircraft and a 200-member rapid reaction force for use on UN missions, as well as trainers to help other countries with peacekeeping.

OTTAWA — Recent statistics reveal that despite Prime Minister Justin Trudeau’s announcement, made mere weeks earlier, that Canada would commit helicopters, planes, and several hundred soldiers to United Nations peace operations, the nation’s active deployment has fallen to a historic minimum.

According to the latest UN data, Canada had just 43 personnel serving on peacekeeping missions globally by December’s end, a drop from 62 the previous month. This decrease, primarily due to fewer police officers being sent to Haiti, marks the smallest Canadian peacekeeping presence since the 1950s.

This low comes even as the governing Liberal Party has consistently vowed to increase the country’s role in UN operations. Their most recent assurance was given at an international peacekeeping conference hosted by Canada in November, where they promised additional equipment, military personnel, and training support.

Officials from both Canada and the UN state that discussions are ongoing to determine how and where these new commitments will be applied, though no specific dates for decisions have been shared.

Walter Dorn, a peacekeeping specialist at the Canadian Forces College in Toronto who monitors these figures, calls the present circumstances disgraceful in light of the government’s many assurances. He notes that Canada’s contribution is now at its lowest ebb since the concept of peacekeeping was first advanced by Lester B. Pearson in 1956. Dorn describes the gap between the ambitious promises made at the Vancouver ministerial meeting and the current reality as hypocritical.

The Liberals initially vowed to revitalize Canada’s peacekeeping engagement during the previous election campaign, and in August 2016 specifically pledged to ready as many as 600 military members and 150 police officers for UN duties. At the time of that 2016 pledge, Canada had 112 peacekeepers deployed. In November, Trudeau detailed the offer, which included helicopters, a cargo plane, a 200-strong quick-response unit, and instructional personnel for training other nations’ peacekeepers.

JOHNSON CITY, TN (WJHL) – While Wellmont Health System added employees in 2016 compared to 2015, Mountain States Health Alliance reduced its total number of employees by 5%, the equivalent of 470 positions, according to recent tax filings.
A MSHA spokesperson says at the end of 2016, the system employed 8,150 people, which is compared to the 8,620 employees listed on the organization’s most recent tax filing at the end of 2015.
MSHA Chief Financial Officer Lynn Krutak says the organization hasn’t had any reductions in force, but has eliminated non-essential positions, mainly through attrition. Krutak says as the health system is faced with declining reimbursements, management is focused on running a lean organization and eliminating any unnecessary expenses.
“We haven’t reduced any clinical staff,” she said. “We’ve reduced some of the overhead staff, again as we continue to look at every area where we might be able to reduce expenses. There have been some people, but it’s mainly the result of attrition. We haven’t had any reduction in force. We do that through turnover.”
A spokesperson says MSHA has hired 760 people so far this year and currently has 426 open job postings, some of which include multiple positions. MSHA did not release a year-to-date number of employees.
Wellmont reports it employed 6,254 employees at the end of 2016, which was up from 6,106 the year before, according to recent tax filings.

In contrast, Wellmont Health System reported an increase in its number of staff members over the same period.

An MSHA representative stated that the system's employee count was 8,150 at the close of 2016, down from the 8,620 recorded on its prior year's tax filing. Lynn Krutak, the Chief Financial Officer for MSHA, clarified that these cuts did not involve layoffs. Instead, the organization removed non-essential roles, largely through natural attrition as positions were vacated. She attributed this streamlining to pressures from lower reimbursement rates, emphasizing a focus on operational efficiency and cutting superfluous costs. The system did not provide a current total employee figure. Meanwhile, Wellmont's filings show it had 6,254 employees at the end of 2016, a rise from 6,106 in 2015.

Among the applicants is Kevin Greenwood, a familiar presence in civic affairs due to his prior role as Port Director for the Port of Newport. In his submission, Greenwood notes his extensive background in public service, involvement with Waldport Middle School and Crestview Heights Grade School, which his children attend, and participation in the Waldport Jr. League.

Another candidate is Harry Dennis Junior, who holds a university degree in Management and Finance. Dennis points to his significant experience within public works departments. He also serves as the Secretary-Treasurer for the Alsea-Highlands homeowners association. A further applicant is Jerry Phillips, a retiree from Southern California who is currently part of the same homeowners association.

Additional business for the council includes a progress report on a residential project planned for the southern portion of SW Norwood. Tidewater Development, LLC, has proposed constructing 34 new homes at that location.

In staffing news, Dustin Kittel, the city's long-time contract land use planner, is departing. His successor will be Joan Davies, who previously held the position of City Manager in Yachats.

City Manager Kerry Kemp is scheduled to update the council regarding a potential South County Swim Center, an initiative promoted by local advocates. Funding would rely on voters approving a property tax increase to issue construction bonds. Potential sites under consideration are the Commons Ballfields or the Angell Job Corps property. According to Kemp's prepared remarks, even with considerable public backing, the project is estimated to be a minimum of five years from realization, possibly more.

The council session is set for October 12th at 2 p.m. in City Hall, located behind the fire station on Hemlock Street.

Many of the women who once worked as Playboy Bunnies for Hugh Hefner, often perceived simply as servers in revealing outfits, later established notable professional paths after their time in the publisher's clubs.

The iconic rock band Blondie remains a powerhouse in New York City's music scene. Despite the constant shift in musical trends since the 1970s, the group's impact is as potent as ever. These punk icons, whose debut record emerged decades ago, continue to command attention.

Debbie Harry, the lead singer of Blondie, is advocating for government intervention in the music industry's dispute with YouTube. Supported by major record labels, she is adding her voice to a collective effort seeking the White House's support in this conflict.

Giorgio Moroder, the innovative Italian producer whose synthesizer-driven disco anthems defined much of the 1970s and 1980s, is enjoying a resurgence in popularity. His music, famously credited with inspiring romance, is once again in the spotlight.

In a legal matter, Debbie Harry has shown support for the alleged drug supplier of actor Philip Seymour Hoffman. The Blondie musician is backing his efforts to avoid incarceration and seek alternative treatment.

A new posthumous album by Michael Jackson has been released. It is important to note that the late pop star produced only six complete studio albums in his final three decades, a fact highlighting his selective approach to recording.

The story of Blondie, as told by those involved, reflects a history of evolution. Much like their native New York City, the band has continually transformed. Formed in 1974, they initially drew inspiration from the aesthetic of 1960s pop groups before forging their own distinctive path.

NEW YORK With the U.S. economy having now "largely attained" a full recovery from recession, the Federal Reserve can raise interest rates three or more times this year, a centrist Fed policymaker said on Wednesday.
San Francisco Fed President John Williams, who largely repeated his view that the U.S. central bank should continue tightening policy gradually, said the main obstacles to raising economic output are now largely outside of the Fed's realm of influence: the slow growth in new workers in the labor market and in their productivity on the job.
He said such supply-side impediments to pushing overall economic growth above its current 2-percent rate are for lawmakers and business leaders to tackle, not the Federal Reserve.
Lifting rates gradually "prevents the economy from overheating... I would not rule out more than three increases total for this year," Williams told an economists' club in New York.
"With an economy at full employment, inflation nearing the Fed's 2 percent goal, and the expansion now in its eighth year, the data have spoken and the message is clear: We've largely attained the hard-sought recovery we've been after for the past nine years," added Williams, who is close to Fed Chair Janet Yellen and who regains a vote on the Fed's policy committee next year under a rotation.
Earlier this month the Fed lifted rates a notch, its third tightening since the 2007-2009 financial crisis and recession. Forecasts from Fed officials suggest a median of two more hikes are planned before year end.
Williams expects economic growth of around 1.75 percent this year and next, a bit below his colleagues, and for inflation to hit 2 percent in the next year or so.
(Reporting by Jonathan Spicer; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama)
rewrite:
A moderate voice within the Federal Reserve indicated on Wednesday that the U.S. economy has essentially achieved a complete rebound from its downturn, allowing for the possibility of three or greater interest rate increases within the year. John Williams, President of the San Francisco Fed, reiterated his stance that the central bank should persist with a measured approach to policy tightening. He noted that the primary constraints on expanding economic output now lie mostly beyond the Fed's control, stemming from limited growth in the labor force and worker efficiency.

According to Williams, these structural barriers, which are holding overall economic expansion below a pace faster than the current two percent, must be addressed by legislators and the private sector rather than monetary policymakers. A gradual approach to raising rates, he argued, helps avoid excessive economic acceleration. Speaking in New York, he stated that he would consider the potential for more than three total rate hikes this year.

Williams, who is aligned with Fed Chair Janet Yellen and will rejoin the policy committee's voting roster next year, pointed to key economic indicators. With employment at robust levels, inflation approaching the two percent target, and the ongoing recovery in its eighth year, he asserted that the evidence shows the long-sought revival has been largely accomplished over the past nine years.

The Fed recently increased rates slightly, marking only the third such move since the financial crisis and recession a decade ago. Official projections from the Fed indicate a median expectation for two additional increases before the year concludes. Williams anticipates economic growth of approximately 1.75 percent for both this year and the next, slightly under the estimates of some peers, and forecasts inflation will reach its target within about a year.

BERLIN The European Union should try to limit the fallout from Britain's decision to leave the European Union, German Chancellor Angela Merkel said on Monday, conceding that some damage was inevitable.
"This is an incision for the European Union, it's an unfortunate event - Britain's decision," Merkel told a joint news conference with Slovakian Prime Minister Robert Fico and Czech Prime Minister Bohuslav Sobotka in Berlin.
"We want to limit the damage. But there will naturally be some negative impact," Merkel said, adding that it was more important that the remaining 27 EU member states stick together and improve the competitiveness of the bloc.
(Reporting by Joseph Nasr and Paul Carrel)

During the event, Merkel was seen engaging with her counterparts, listening to remarks and speaking to the assembled media.

Addressing the gathered press, Chancellor Merkel focused on the consequences of the United Kingdom's choice to exit the European Union. She characterized the British departure as a significant and regrettable development for the EU. Merkel stated that while the bloc should strive to minimize the adverse effects, some detrimental outcomes were unavoidable. She emphasized that the paramount task for the remaining twenty-seven member nations was to maintain unity and work collaboratively to enhance the Union's overall economic strength and global standing. Her comments underscored a commitment to collective action in navigating the challenges posed by Brexit.

Image copyright Highways England Image caption Six junctions are due for a revamp in the proposals
A consultation into improvements on the A27 has been dubbed "a sham" by council leaders.
Highways England plans to "increase capacity and reduce congestion" between Worthing and Lancing.
But Adur and Worthing councils say the £69m proposal is not fit for purpose and the government body should launch a fresh consultation with updated plans.
Highways England project manager Tom Beasley said the improvements were the "best achievable option".
Large-scale options were considered by Highways England, including dual carriageway schemes with flyovers.
But the consultation focuses a mix of new traffic signalling and road widening on six junctions between Durrington Hill and the Lancing Manor roundabout.
'Best option'
In a joint statement, the leader of Adur District Council, Neil Parkin, and the leader of Worthing Borough Council, Dan Humphreys, said the "modest" plans are not good enough.
Mr Parkin said: "Highways England say they want to consult with us but we say this is a sham. By not allowing the public to weigh up options and see full costings how are we to make any kind of decision?
"All I do know is the current scheme on the table is barely worth the disruption and certainly not worth spending £69m on."
Mr Humphreys added: "Highways England do not seem to be taking us seriously. Our questions were met with an 'experts know best' response."
But Mr Beasley said Highways England think that the proposal "would make a worthwhile improvement to people's journeys and is the best achievable option within the scope and budget available for the project".
"We welcome all views and promise that we will take all responses to the consultation fully into account."
Consultation into the proposal ends on 12 September.
rewrite:
Local authorities have criticized a public feedback process regarding upgrades to the A27, labeling it disingenuous. The highway agency, Highways England, is seeking input on a £69 million initiative aimed at easing traffic and enhancing road capacity along the stretch connecting Worthing and Lancing. However, leaders from both Adur and Worthing councils argue that the suggested plan is inadequate and demand a new consultation with revised proposals.

Tom Beasley, the project manager for Highways England, defended the scheme as the most viable choice given practical constraints. While more extensive solutions, such as constructing dual carriageways with overpasses, were initially reviewed, the current proposal centers on upgrading six intersections from Durrington Hill to Lancing Manor roundabout. These upgrades would involve widening certain road sections and installing modern traffic signals.

In a shared statement, council leaders Neil Parkin and Dan Humphreys dismissed the plans as too limited. Parkin contended that the consultation is flawed because it prevents residents from comparing alternatives or reviewing complete financial details, making informed judgment impossible. He expressed doubt that the proposed changes justify the expected inconvenience or the substantial expenditure.

Humphreys noted that their concerns were dismissed with an appeal to expert authority, suggesting their input was not valued. Beasley responded that the agency believes the plan would meaningfully improve travel and represents the optimal outcome within the project's defined limits and funding. He emphasized that all consultation feedback will be carefully considered. The period for submitting comments closes on September 12.

Doctor-assisted suicide in Canada consists of a lethal injection in hospital or at home (AFP Photo/PATRICK KOVARIK)
Ottawa (AFP) - Nearly 2,000 people with incurable diseases were helped to die by a doctor in the first year since Canada legalized medically-assisted suicide, according to a report published Friday.
From the time Ottawa passed the legislation in June 2016 to June 30, 2017, 1,982 people ended their lives in this way, according to Health Canada.
Most had cancer, the agency said.
Extrapolating from the data collected for the first half of 2017, the number of assisted deaths is expected to rise but remain at less than two percent of all deaths nationwide this year -- "consistent with international experience," it said a statement.
Doctor-assisted suicide in Canada is reserved for adults with serious health problems who want to end their suffering, and consists of a lethal injection in hospital or at home.
Days after the law was changed to allow for the practice, it was challenged in court in an attempt to expand it to include Canadians who suffer from a wasting disease but who are not facing imminent death.
These include people suffering from spinal muscular atrophy, multiple sclerosis, spinal stenosis, locked in syndrome, traumatic spinal injury, Parkinson's disease and Huntington's disease.
Canadian bishops have instructed their clergy to deny religious funerals for deceased persons who chose a doctor-assisted suicide.
rewrite:
In Canada, physician-assisted death involves administering a fatal dose of medication, which can occur either in a medical facility or a private residence (AFP Photo/PATRICK KOVARIK). According to a report released on Friday, almost two thousand individuals with terminal conditions received medical assistance to end their lives during the initial twelve months following the legalization of the practice. Health Canada's data, covering June 2016 through June 2017, indicates that 1,982 people chose this option. The majority of these individuals were cancer patients.

Based on figures from the first half of 2017, projections suggest the annual count will increase, though it will still represent under two percent of total deaths in the country. Officials noted this trend aligns with patterns observed in other nations where similar procedures are permitted. The Canadian law restricts eligibility to adults experiencing severe and irreversible medical conditions who seek relief from their suffering.

Shortly after the legislation took effect, a legal appeal was filed to broaden its scope. The challenge seeks to include individuals with degenerative illnesses, such as multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, or spinal injuries, who are not necessarily near the end of life but endure progressive decline. In response to the law, Canada's Catholic bishops have directed priests to refuse church funeral rites to those who opt for a medically assisted death.

A 68-year-old man who suffered a heart attack at a leisure centre has praised quick-thinking staff and paramedics for saving his life.
Alan Hartley, of Elmswell, was on a treadmill at Everyone Active Leisure Centre, in Stowmarket, on January 23 when he collapsed and went into cardiac arrest.
Gym staff rushed to his rescue with a defibrillator and, together with the East of England Ambulance Service NHS Trust (EEAST), helped revive him. Now recovering well, he reunited with his life-savers on Monday to thank them.
He said: “The gym staff don’t go to work and expect to save a life and for that I owe them so much. It’s amazing to be able to thank them in person.”
When he collapsed, Becky Cruikshank, from Everyone Active, shouted for help, pushed a panic button and, when it became clear Mr Hartley wasn’t breathing, she started chest compressions.
Her colleague Steve Ward brought the gym’s defibrillator and administered the first and most vital shock.
He said: “You just go into auto pilot in those situations. I just saw someone who was very sick and needed our help.”
Medics from the EEAST were dispatched and the air ambulance called.
The ambulance crew shocked him a further two times and resuscitated him.
Mr Hartley was flown to Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital where he remained for three days before being discharged.
He had suffered a total blockage of his anterior lateral artery.
Gym staff have received certificates of thanks from the EEAST.
Paramedic supervisor James Mullett said: “The quick recognition of the severity of the incident by the gym staff as well as early cardio pulmonary resuscitation and the use of a defibrillator ensured Alan had the best chance of survival.”
He added: “I would also like to thank the call handler and dispatcher involved; they deserve credit for delivering excellent instructions over the phone as well as dispatching the appropriate resources Alan needed. Everyone did their part to give Alan his life back to him.”
For more information on how defibrillators work, watch this short video at www.youtube.com
Anyone who is interested in working for the ambulance service should visit www.eastamb.nhs.uk
rewrite:
A man in his late sixties has expressed profound gratitude to the alert employees and emergency medical teams who rescued him after he experienced a cardiac arrest while exercising. Alan Hartley, a resident of Elmswell, was using a treadmill at the Everyone Active Leisure Centre in Stowmarket on January 23rd when he suddenly fell unconscious and entered cardiac arrest.

Personnel at the fitness facility immediately came to his aid, utilizing an on-site defibrillator. Their efforts, combined with the swift response from the East of England Ambulance Service NHS Trust (EEAST), were crucial in restarting his heart. Now on a positive path to recovery, Mr. Hartley met with those who saved him this past Monday to offer his personal thanks.

He stated that the gym employees do not begin their shifts anticipating a life-or-death situation, and for their decisive actions, he is immensely grateful. He found it incredibly moving to be able to express his appreciation to them face-to-face.

When the incident occurred, staff member Becky Cruikshank called for assistance, activated an emergency alarm, and, upon realizing Mr. Hartley had stopped breathing, began performing CPR. Her co-worker, Steve Ward, promptly retrieved the facility's defibrillator and delivered the initial, critical shock to the patient. Mr. Ward reflected that in such moments, instinct takes over; he simply saw an individual in grave condition requiring urgent help.

Emergency medics from EEAST were rapidly sent to the scene, with an air ambulance also requested. The arriving ambulance crew administered two additional shocks and successfully resuscitated him. Mr. Hartley was then airlifted to the Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital, where he received care for three days before being released. His medical event was caused by a complete obstruction of his anterior lateral artery.

In recognition of their vital role, the leisure centre staff have been presented with formal thank-you certificates from the ambulance trust. Paramedic supervisor James Mullett commended the team's rapid assessment of the serious situation, along with their immediate initiation of CPR and use of the defibrillator, which collectively provided Alan with the optimal opportunity to survive.

He further extended thanks to the emergency call handler and dispatcher involved, noting they merit recognition for providing clear telephone guidance and efficiently coordinating all necessary resources. Mr. Mullett emphasized that every person involved played an essential part in returning Alan to his life.

For details on the function of defibrillators, a brief explanatory video can be viewed online. Those interested in pursuing a career with the ambulance service are encouraged to visit the organization's official website.

HOUSTON (AP) — Texans coach Bill O'Brien says he wouldn't have let Tom Savage re-enter Sunday's game after an alarming hit that gave him a concussion and left the quarterback's hands shaking if he had seen the video of the hit.
Savage was injured with about nine minutes remaining in the second quarter of Houston's 26-16 loss to San Francisco when he was driven to the ground on a hit by Elvis Dumervil.
Replays showed Savage looking dazed after his head hit the ground with both of his arms shaking and lifted upward.
He was taken to the medical tent where he stayed for less than three minutes before returning to the bench and going back in for the next series.
Savage threw two incompletions on that drive, and Houston's team doctor approached him after he returned to the sideline at the end of that possession.
He was then evaluated again and taken to the locker room after it was determined that he did have a concussion.
On Monday O'Brien said: "There's no video on the sideline. All there are are tablets. There's no video, there's nothing like that. With benefit of seeing the video ... (and) the care for the player, I would've never let that player back in the game, and I don't believe that (trainer) Geoff Kaplan would've allowed that player back in the game. I don't have benefit of the video. I did not see anything."
Also on Monday an NFL spokesman said the league is looking into whether concussion protocol was properly followed after Savage was injured.
League spokesman Joe Lockhart said the NFL and the players' association "together will conduct a thorough review of the incident focused on whether the protocol was properly followed, but we're also continuing looking at the protocol to look for ways to improve and strengthen it."
___
AP Pro Football Writer Barry Wilner contributed to this report.
___

HOUSTON (AP) — Houston Texans head coach Bill O’Brien stated Monday that, had he viewed footage of the hit that caused quarterback Tom Savage to suffer a concussion during Sunday’s game, he would not have permitted Savage to return to play. The incident occurred with roughly nine minutes left in the second quarter of Houston’s 26-16 defeat to the San Francisco 49ers, when Savage was tackled by Elvis Dumervil and driven forcefully to the turf.

Broadcast replays depicted Savage appearing disoriented after his head struck the ground, his arms trembling and rising involuntarily. Following the hit, he was escorted to the sideline medical tent, where he remained for under three minutes. He then went back to the bench and re-entered the game for the subsequent offensive series. On that drive, Savage threw two incomplete passes. After the possession ended and he returned to the sideline, the team’s physician approached him. He underwent another evaluation, was diagnosed with a concussion, and was subsequently taken to the locker room.

O’Brien explained that sideline access to video is limited. “We don’t have video on the sideline—only tablets. There’s no live video feed available there,” he said. “If I had been able to see the replay and considering player safety, I would never have allowed him back on the field, and I believe our trainer Geoff Kaplan would have made the same decision. Without seeing the video, I wasn’t aware of the severity.”

Also on Monday, an NFL spokesperson confirmed the league is examining whether the concussion protocol was correctly administered after Savage’s injury. League spokesman Joe Lockhart said the NFL and the NFL Players Association will jointly perform a detailed assessment of the event to determine if procedures were followed appropriately. He added that the league is continuously reviewing the protocol to identify potential improvements and enhancements.

___
AP Pro Football Writer Barry Wilner provided reporting for this story.
___
Additional NFL coverage can be found at http://www.pro32.ap.org and http://www.twitter.com/AP_NFL.

Willie Walsh, chief executive of Aer Lingus parent, International Airlines Group (IAG), says the business is happy with the response to its new budget carrier, Level.
IAG launched the new Barcelona-based airline in March and it plans to begin flying to LA, San Francisco, Buenos Aires in Argentine and Punta Cana in the Dominican Republic from June.
The move is designed to combat the launch of cheap transatlantic services by the likes of Norwegian, which will begin services from Ireland to the US in July, and Wow, which offers flights from the Europe to north America via Rekjavik.
Mr Walsh said over the weekend that bookings on its site, flylevel, are strong, with more than 50 per cent of customers in the key 18 to 34 years age bracket. “So it´s an interesting demographic,” he told CNN´s Quest Means Business.
Speaking to the same programme, commentator Ben Schlappig, editor of travel blog, One Mile at a Time, said that it was a case of “monkey see, monkey do”.
He argued that the threat posed by Norwegian and Wow was such that British Airways – one of IAG´s other three airlines – had “no choice” but to follow with a low-cost carrier of its own.
He noted that there were suggestions that British Airways could introduce paid-for meals on its transatlantic economy flights in much the same as Norwegian is already doing.
Shortly after Norwegian announced details of its Irish services, Aer Lingus chief executive, Stephen Kavanagh, indicated that the airline could introduce cheaper no-frills fares on its transatlantic flights, that would exclude elements normally found in ticket prices.

Willie Walsh, who leads International Airlines Group (IAG), the parent company of Aer Lingus, has expressed satisfaction with the early performance of Level, its recently introduced low-cost airline. The carrier, which commenced operations from Barcelona in March, is scheduled to start long-haul routes in June, including destinations such as Los Angeles, San Francisco, Buenos Aires, and Punta Cana. This initiative is a strategic counter to new affordable transatlantic options from competitors like Norwegian, set to begin U.S. flights from Ireland in July, and Wow Air, which connects Europe and North America through Iceland.

Walsh recently noted that bookings through Level's website are robust, particularly with over half originating from passengers aged 18 to 34, a demographic he finds noteworthy. Meanwhile, travel analyst Ben Schlappig, from the blog One Mile at a Time, described the industry dynamic as imitative, suggesting IAG's British Airways felt compelled to respond to the competitive pressure by launching its own budget option. He further observed that British Airways might adopt a paid meal system for economy class on Atlantic routes, mirroring Norwegian's approach. In a related development, Aer Lingus CEO Stephen Kavanagh hinted at potentially offering stripped-down, lower-cost fares on its transatlantic services, removing certain standard inclusions, following Norwegian's expansion announcements.

As noted, Illinois tattoo artist Catherine Alexander recently filed a lawsuit against WWE and 2K Games over the use of Randy Orton's tattoos in the WWE 2K video game series. Alexander, who has done Orton's ink since 2003, claims she owns the copyrights to the designs. She has accused WWE and 2K of copyright infringement because Orton's tats are depicted to a tee in the games. TMZ Sports noted that Alexander claims she brought the issue up with WWE in 2009 and was offered just $450 for the rights to use the designs, which she declined.
The suit was filed on April 17th in the United States District Court of Southern District of Illinois and also names 2K Sports, Take-Two Interactive Software, Visual Concepts Entertainment, Yuke's Co. and Yuke's LA as defendants. PWInsider adds that Alexander has requested a jury trial and is asking the court to rule that the tattoos are her copyrighted works, and that the defendants infringed against her. She is also asking the court to rule that she is owed damages but there's no word yet on how much she's seeking. None of the defendants have responded to the lawsuit as of this week.
Alexander's suit claims that all of her tattoos on Orton are her original designs and that she never gave the defendants permission to recreate them in WWE video games. Alexander says she did the work on Orton between 2003 and 2008, and that the tattoos are "easily recognized by his fans and members of the public."
Alexander submitted applications to register copyrights on each tattoo on March 15th of this year.
The suit also says Orton does not have ownership of the copyrights and has no authority to, and did not grant permission to, the defendants. It should be noted that Orton is not listed as a defendant.

A legal complaint has been initiated by Catherine Alexander, a tattoo artist based in Illinois, targeting World Wrestling Entertainment and the publisher of the WWE 2K video game franchise. Alexander asserts that she holds the copyright to the tattoo artwork she has applied to wrestler Randy Orton since 2003. The lawsuit alleges that the video games reproduce these designs without authorization, constituting copyright infringement. According to reports, Alexander previously raised the matter with WWE in 2009, rejecting a settlement offer of $450 for the rights to utilize her artwork.

The complaint was formally submitted to a federal court in the Southern District of Illinois on April 17th. Additional defendants named include 2K Sports, its parent company Take-Two Interactive, and several affiliated development studios. Alexander has requested a trial by jury, seeking a judicial declaration that her copyrights were violated and an award of monetary damages, the specific amount of which has not been publicly disclosed. The suit emphasizes that these distinctive designs are widely identified by Orton’s fanbase and the general public. Notably, Alexander filed official applications to register the copyrights for each tattoo design in mid-March of this year.

The legal documents further state that Randy Orton himself does not possess copyright ownership of the tattoo artwork, nor did he have the legal right to permit its use by the defendants. It is important to clarify that Orton is not a party to this lawsuit.

By Sarah Stockman

One sunny morning in February I sat in my kitchen waiting for the doorbell to ring. Any minute Palisadian Reed Newman would arrive to tell me about his vegetable garden growing company Revival Roots.
Normally when I interview someone we meet at a neutral location like Starbucks. However, I had taken Newman up on his offer on NextDoor for free garden consultations since I was curious how his company worked.
There was potentially one small hiccup: I live with my parents so I had to ask permission to invite him over. Luckily they didn’t have any problems. “Ask him about replacing sprinklers,” my mom told me. “Tell him to bring us some free plants,” my dad added.
And so I found myself waiting one Tuesday morning for Newman’s arrival.
Newman, 24, grew up in West Los Angeles and Santa Monica Canyon with his twin older siblings and his parents Jeanne and Gary, who are in the entertainment industry.
“We grew up in West Los Angeles and moved to Santa Monica Canyon about six years ago,” Newman said.

U.S. soldiers of the 3rd Battalion, 12th Infantry, 4th Infantry Division take a break during bunker construction on Hill 530 in Vietnam, November 25, 1967. REUTERS/Courtesy U.S. Army
My father had a low draft number and always told me he couldn’t see himself trudging through the jungle with a machete. It was the early ‘70s and Vietnam would be over soon, but young Americans were still dying in Southeast Asia. So dad joined the Navy and served aboard the USS Enterprise. Unlike a lot of the other men of his generation and demographic, dad did his duty.
While dad sweated on the Pacific Ocean and learned the joys of monsoon season, millions of other American men protested the unjust, expensive and bloody war and helped bring it to an end. The popular conception of that period is one of free love and political turmoil. It was an era when old men started unpopular wars and the righteous stayed behind.
But that’s not an accurate picture, according to this week’s War College guest, Bruce Cannon Gibney. He lays out the case against the Boomer’s collective memory in his new book “A Generation of Sociopaths: How the Baby Boomers Betrayed America.”
Gibney shows Boomers overwhelmingly supported the war until they had to serve in it. Worse, most who wanted to avoid the war could seek conscientious objector status but instead abused the deferment system. From dodging down, class privilege to officer bounties, Gibney busts the myths of one of America’s favorite sacred cows.
rewrite:
Members of the 4th Infantry Division's 3rd Battalion, 12th Infantry, pause from building fortifications on Hill 530 in Vietnam on November 25, 1967. My father, facing a high likelihood of being conscripted in the early 1970s, was certain he did not belong in the jungles of Southeast Asia. Although the conflict was winding down, American casualties continued. He chose to enlist in the Navy, serving on the USS Enterprise and fulfilling his service obligation—a path less common among his peers.

As he endured the harsh conditions of the Pacific, including relentless monsoons, vast numbers of his fellow citizens were demonstrating against a war they viewed as immoral, costly, and brutal, ultimately pressuring for its conclusion. The common narrative of that time emphasizes cultural rebellion and social upheaval, often painting a picture of a disillusioned youth resisting conflicts orchestrated by an older generation.

However, this perception is challenged by Bruce Cannon Gibney, a recent guest on the War College. In his work, "A Generation of Sociopaths: How the Baby Boomers Betrayed America," he argues that the collective memory of the Baby Boom generation is deeply flawed. Gibney contends that Boomers largely backed the war until their own personal service became a possibility. He further claims that many who wished to evade combat exploited loopholes for deferrals rather than pursuing official conscientious objector status. Gibney dismantles what he sees as a cherished national myth, detailing how systemic avoidance—through strategies like exploiting educational deferments, class advantages, and incentives for officer commissions—was widespread.

Rio Ferdinand and Steven Gerrard were critical of Lionel Messi's performance in Barcelona's humbling at Paris Saint-Germain as the duo slammed the star's lack of effort in the French capital.
It was a night to forget for Messi and Co. after Barcelona suffered a humiliating 4-0 loss to PSG in the first leg of their Champions League last-16 tie on Tuesday.
Angel Di Maria's brace on his birthday condemned LaLiga champions Barca to an embarrassing defeat in Paris, as five-time Ballon d'Or winner Messi struggled to have any influence on the contest.
1 - Lionel Messi has failed to register a single touch in the opposite box in a #UCL game for the first time this season. Disconnection. pic.twitter.com/zwdduc0T3L — OptaJose (@OptaJose) February 14, 2017
And former Manchester United centre-back Ferdinand criticised Messi's display at the Parc des Princes.
"His reaction there was poor," Ferdinand told BT Sport. "All night he was sloppy.
"He looked dejected and bereft of ideas, [but] he's human."
Former Liverpool captain Gerrard echoed Ferdinand's comments, adding: "He showed zero effort. No reaction all night."
Barca will attempt to salvage the tie in the return fixture at Camp Nou on March 8.
rewrite:
Rio Ferdinand and Steven Gerrard both singled out Lionel Messi for his disappointing display during Barcelona's heavy defeat to Paris Saint-Germain, emphasizing his apparent lack of effort on the pitch. The match, a first-leg Champions League knockout fixture, ended in a 4-0 victory for PSG, marking a particularly forgettable evening for the Spanish side. On his birthday, Angel Di Maria scored twice, contributing to a result that left the Catalan giants thoroughly embarrassed. Messi, a multiple Ballon d'Or recipient, was notably ineffective and failed to make any significant impact on the game.

Statistics highlighted that, for the first time in that season's Champions League, Messi did not manage a single touch inside the opponent's penalty area. Analyzing the performance for BT Sport, Ferdinand described Messi's play as sloppy and his demeanor as dejected and lacking inspiration, though he acknowledged the player's humanity. Gerrard concurred, stating that the Argentine superstar exhibited no effort or positive response throughout the match. Barcelona now faces the daunting task of overturning the substantial deficit when the two teams meet again for the second leg at Camp Nou.

ORLANDO (CBS Local) – Disney World is opening up their theme parks, and their wallet, in a search for thousands of summer workers this year. The Florida resort is looking to fill around 3,500 positions and is reportedly offering signing bonuses of up to $3,000 in order to entice part-time employees.
Disney’s annual hiring blitz is in preparation for the summer vacation season and the company is looking to staff a wide variety of jobs including culinary chefs, lifeguards, bus drivers, and housekeepers. Disney began hosting a series of job fairs for these openings on April 23 at the ESPN Wide World of Sports complex, which focused on staffing the resort’s cooking positions.
A lifeguard job fair is scheduled for May 2 at Disney’s Typhoon Lagoon Water Park in Lake Buena Vista. According to the Orlando Sentinel, full-time and part-time lifeguards can get a $1,000 signing bonus in 2018, double the amount from last year.
Disney’s housekeeping job fair is being held on May 9 at the Walt Disney World Resort Casting Center. The company is also accepting applications for these openings Monday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. Eastern Time through May. Housekeepers are receiving bonuses of $1,250 and an hourly wage of $10.50 according to the Sentinel.
Disney World’s neighbor, Universal Studios, is also stocking up on employees for the summer rush. The theme park and resort also announced that they’ll be hiring 3,000 new workers. The resort said in a press release it will be offering workers “competitive salaries and comprehensive benefits packages” as well as other perks like free admission to their park.

Iraqi Kurds celebrate the results of the independence referendum in the northern city of Arbil, on September 27, 2017 (AFP Photo/SAFIN HAMED)
Paris (AFP) - Iraqi Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi said Thursday he did not want an armed conflict with his country's Kurds, days after the autonomous Kurdistan region voted for independence in a referendum.
"We don't want armed confrontation, we don't want clashes but federal authority must prevail," he said after a meeting in Paris with French President Emmanuel Macron.
"Separatism is unacceptable," Abadi said, reiterating that the non-binding September 25 vote -- in which 92.7 percent of Iraqi Kurds backed independence -- was "illegal".
"Iraq belongs to all Iraqis," he said, appealing to Kurdish Peshmerga forces to work with the Iraqi army "as we have worked together against Daesh (the Islamic State group), to guarantee citizens' safety."
Macron voiced support for Kurds' rights while defending Iraq's territorial unity.
France has "always been sensitive to the situation of Kurds" but is also committed to stability in Iraq, Macron said, calling for dialogue between Baghdad and Iraqi Kurdistan.
"France is ready to contribute actively to the UN's mediation efforts, if Iraqi authorities so wish," he said.
rewrite:
On September 27, 2017, Kurds in Iraq expressed jubilation over the outcome of a recent poll on sovereignty in Arbil, located in the nation's north. In response, Iraqi leader Haider al-Abadi stated on Thursday that he seeks to avoid military hostilities with the Kurdish population, following the autonomous region's decision to pursue statehood through a popular vote. He emphasized that while armed conflict is not desired, the rule of the central government must be upheld. Abadi reaffirmed his position that the September 25 plebiscite, which saw an overwhelming majority of Kurdish voters favor independence, was against the law and that secessionist movements cannot be tolerated. Stressing that Iraq is a nation for all its people, he urged Kurdish military units to cooperate with national forces to ensure public security, just as they had joined efforts against the Islamic State group.

French President Emmanuel Macron, following discussions with Abadi in Paris, balanced his support for Kurdish rights with a firm stance on preserving Iraq's territorial integrity. He noted France's historical concern for the Kurdish people while underscoring a dedication to maintaining stability within Iraq. Macron advocated for ongoing talks between the Iraqi government and the Kurdish regional authority, offering France's willingness to play a significant role in United Nations-led mediation, should Baghdad request such assistance.

BOCA RATON, Fla. — Tyree Griffin scored 21 points, Dominic Magee added 16 more and Southern Miss held off Florida Atlantic in the second half for a 77-66 win Saturday night.
Southern Miss (12-12, 5-6 Conference-USA) closed out the first half with a 22-6 run that included a pair of 3-pointers from D'Angelo Richardson to take a 38-21 advantage into the break, but had to scramble in the second half as Florida Atlantic closed in. The Owls (10-13, 4-7) outscored Southern Miss 45-39 in the final 20 minutes and cut the deficit to 71-66 after a pair of free throws from William Pfister with 37 seconds left.
Cortez Edwards, who finished with 15 points, dropped in a layup at the other end to stretch the Southern Miss advantage back to seven and the Owls were held scoreless the rest of the way as the Golden Eagles sealed it from the free throw line, snapping a two-game skid.
Richardson had 10 points for Southern Miss, which shot 52 per cent from the field, including 8 for 12 from 3-point range.
rewrite: On Saturday evening in Boca Raton, Southern Miss secured a 77-66 victory over Florida Atlantic after maintaining their lead through a competitive second half. Tyree Griffin led the scoring with 21 points, supported by Dominic Magee's 16. A dominant 22-6 surge to conclude the first period, featuring two three-point shots from D'Angelo Richardson, gave Southern Miss a commanding 38-21 halftime edge. However, Florida Atlantic rallied after the break, outscoring their opponents 45-39 in the final half. The Owls narrowed the gap to just five points, at 71-66, following two successful foul shots by William Pfister with 37 seconds remaining. Cortez Edwards, who tallied 15 points, immediately answered with a driving basket to extend the lead back to seven. Florida Atlantic failed to score again as Southern Miss clinched the win with free throws, ending a two-game losing streak. Richardson contributed 10 points to the effort, with the team shooting an efficient 52 percent overall and making 8 of 12 attempts from beyond the arc.

Actor Hugh Grant has spoken out about his appearances in the Bridget Jones franchise – suggesting that he opted out of most recent film Bridget Jones's Baby because his character didn't fit in the narrative.
Grant was at the BAFTA Life in Pictures event last night (December 9), and remarked that in regards to the third Bridget Jones movie, "having easily enough agreed to do it", he ultimately decided to bow out because he "couldn't make the character work in the story".
Reported by Deadline, he went on to say: "I drove them [those making Bridget Jones's Baby] mad for a year. We went back and forth and in the end, I just said 'I don't see how he fits in.'"
View photos Photo credit: Universal More
While at the BAFTA occasion, Hugh also talked candidly about his other work – in particular his recent movie with Meryl Streep, for which he came out of semi-retirement for.
Hugh played St Clair Bayfield alongside Streep in the film Florence Foster Jenkins – receiving BAFTA, Golden Globe, and SAG nominations for his performance.
View photos Photo credit: Pathé More
Of working with Streep, Grant revealed: "[She was] intimidating...She's a genius because she's absolutely dedicated and ruthless. She talks that way about acting: 'I will never do a scene in which I'm not emotionally present'. And I thought, 'Well, f***, I've done thousands.'"
Grant can currently be found on movie screens playing villain Phoenix Buchanan in Paddington 2, which has proved to be a sensational smash hit – which should please the star greatly, seeing as he recently admitted that he took the role as a way of mocking actors.

It should be obvious by now, but Logic cares very deeply about making music with messages (even if his execution often undershoots his ambition). That’s the gist of the new profile mini-documentary about the Everybody rapper from CBS Sunday Morning hosted by Jane Pauley. Of course, the primary focus is the absolutely unreal success of Logic’s “1-800-273-8255” suicide prevention single, which has now gone triple platinum.
Pauley covers the song’s success from the record-setting MTV VMA performance which prompted a 50% traffic increase to the titular hotline and asks Logic whether he had ever experienced suicidal thoughts himself. After he responds in the negative, she wonders why he felt it so important to address the subject. Logic replies that it was prompted by his fans’ messages of support and thanks that propelled him to write “1-800-273-8255.” “They said, ‘you changed my life,'” he shares, “I thought to myself how I wasn’t even trying to do that. If you’re telling me that, could you imagine what I could do if I tried to save somebody’s life.”
Logic’s personal challenge to himself has garnered him a Grammy nomination for Song Of The Year as well as a No. 1 debut for his third studio album, Everybody.

President Donald Trump said he was “disappointed” after K.T. McFarland decided to withdraw from her nomination as Ambassador of Singapore.
“K.T. served my Administration with distinction,” Trump wrote in a statement. “Unfortunately, some Democrats chose to play politics rather than move forward with a qualified nominee for a critically important post.”
McFarland, a Fox News analyst, was first brought into the administration to serve Trump on the National Security Council before she was pressured out by Gen. H.R. McMaster, who replaced National Security Adviser Michael Flynn at the White House.
Trump then nominated her to serve as Ambassador of Singapore, but Senate Democrats froze her confirmation hearings in response to the Russia investigation.
Democrats demanded answers from McFarland about knowledge of conversations with Flynn and former Russian ambassador Sergey Kislyak.
Trump hailed her experience as a commentator on foreign policy in his statement.
“I wish K.T. the best as she uses her considerable wisdom and skill as a commentator to explain to the American people how to make American foreign policy great again,” he said.

BEIJING Beijing has ordered 15 online real estate portals to remove misleading information, false advertising and even advice on feng shui by Wednesday, as part of its campaign to cool a red-hot housing market.
Advertisements on the websites should not promise rising returns on Beijing real estate investment, the official Xinhua news agency reported, as the Chinese capital battles with soaring home prices and property speculators.
While flats in Beijing on average are still cheaper than homes in Tokyo or London, authorities fear surging prices are increasing household debt, heightening banks' credit risks and fanning grassroots resentment as home affordability fades.
The targeted websites, which include popular real estate portals Lianjia and I Love My Home, should also not offer to help prospective buyers handle matters related to local "hukou" residence permits or school enrolment, Xinhua reported late on Tuesday.
They are not allowed to spread rumors or disseminate misleading information such as "limitless potential for price gains."
Content on feng shui or any form of financing advice is also forbidden.
The measures are the latest restrictions to help cool Beijing's fevered real estate sector.
In mid-March, the Beijing government raised the minimum down payment on a second home to 60 percent from 50 percent. On bigger homes, that minimum increased to 80 percent from 70 percent.
They also suspended issuing individual mortgage loans of more than 25 years, effectively forcing borrowers to take on more expensive shorter loans.
Buying a third property has already been banned.
(Reporting by Ryan Woo; Editing by Randy Fabi)
rewrite:
Beijing has instructed fifteen internet-based property platforms to eliminate deceptive content, inaccurate promotions, and guidance on practices like feng shui by a Wednesday deadline. This action supports broader efforts to temper an overheated residential market. According to state media, advertisements on these sites must avoid guaranteeing increased profits from property investments in the city, as officials contend with skyrocketing housing costs and speculative activity.

Although average apartment prices in Beijing remain below those in major global hubs like Tokyo or London, regulators worry that rapid appreciation is driving up personal debt, amplifying financial risks for lenders, and stirring public discontent as housing becomes less attainable. The affected platforms, among them well-known services such as Lianjia and I Love My Home, are also barred from assisting potential buyers with issues linked to local residency permits or school admissions.

These sites must not circulate unfounded rumors or promote misleading claims, such as suggesting prices have boundless room to rise. Prohibited materials additionally include feng shui-related content and any form of financial guidance. These steps mark the newest in a series of controls aimed at calming Beijing's frenzied property sector.

Recently, authorities increased the required down payment for second homes to 60%, up from 50%, and raised it to 80% for larger units. They also halted mortgage loans with terms exceeding 25 years, pushing borrowers toward costlier, shorter-term financing. Purchases of third homes are already prohibited.

LONDON, March 28 (Thomson Reuters Foundation) - British politicians lambasted a popular tabloid for "moronic" sexism on Tuesday after it splashed a photo of Prime Minister Theresa May and Scottish First Minister Nicola Sturgeon's legs across the front page with the headline "Never mind Brexit, who won Legs-it!"
The public also took to social media to denounce the mid-market tabloid for focussing on the two leaders' legs when they met to discuss Britain's departure from the European Union and a potential referendum on Scottish independence.
"The 1950s called and asked for their headline back.#everydaysexism," tweeted Labour parliamentarian Ed Miliband using a hashtag for hightlighting women's experiences of sexism.
Jeremy Corbyn, leader of the opposition Labour Party, tweeted: "It's 2017. This sexism must be consigned to history. Shame on the Daily Mail", while veteran Labour lawmaker Harriet Harman branded the coverage "moronic".
The paper featured more photos of the two leaders inside above another headline: "Finest weapons at their command? Those pins!"
A columnist described Sturgeon's legs as "altogether more flirty, tantalisingly crossed ... a direct attempt at seduction".
The coverage generated a torrent of criticism on Twitter with members of the public branding it as "utterly puerile" and "sexist, derogatory trash journalism".
"Has anyone told the #DailyMail that we put the clocks forward by an hour, not back 3 decades?" one woman tweeted, referring to the country's switch to British Summer Time at the weekend.
The Daily Mail, which has a circulation of 1.45 million and reaches millions more online, backed Brexit in last year's referendum on Britain's EU membership.
Sturgeon, who heads Edinburgh's devolved government, wants Scotland to hold a referendum on independence before Britain leaves the European Union. (Editing by Ros Russell; Please credit the Thomson Reuters Foundation, the charitable arm of Thomson Reuters, which covers humanitarian news, women's rights, trafficking, corruption and climate change. Visit news.trust.org to see more stories.)
rewrite:
On Tuesday, British lawmakers strongly criticized a widely-read tabloid newspaper for what they termed idiotic and sexist coverage. The publication had placed a large image focusing on the legs of Prime Minister Theresa May and Scottish First Minister Nicola Sturgeon on its front page, accompanied by the caption “Never mind Brexit, who won Legs-it!” The two leaders had met to negotiate the terms of Britain’s exit from the European Union and to debate a possible new vote on Scottish independence, making the paper’s emphasis on their appearance a particular focus of outrage.

The response from the public was swift, with many taking to social media to condemn the tabloid’s decision to highlight the politicians’ physical attributes rather than the substantive discussions. Labour Party politician Ed Miliband posted a message on Twitter stating, “The 1950s called and asked for their headline back,” using a hashtag that draws attention to routine gender prejudice. Opposition leader Jeremy Corbyn also tweeted, asserting that such sexist portrayals belong in the past and expressing disapproval toward the Daily Mail. Senior Labour figure Harriet Harman called the article “moronic.”

Inside the newspaper, additional pictures of the two leaders were printed under another headline that made a playful reference to their legs. A columnist offered a description of Sturgeon’s posture as flirtatious and deliberately provocative. This coverage provoked a flood of critical comments online, where readers dismissed it as juvenile and a demeaning example of biased reporting. One woman remarked on the anachronistic nature of the piece, joking that the country had recently moved its clocks forward for daylight saving, not backward by several decades.

The Daily Mail, which has a large print readership and an extensive online audience, supported the campaign for Britain to leave the EU in the previous year’s referendum. Meanwhile, Sturgeon, who leads Scotland’s autonomous government, is seeking to hold an independence vote before the UK completes its departure from the European Union.

* North American pharma customers reluctant to place orders
* 2017 revenue seen at lower end of guidance range
* Shares drop almost 6 percent (Adds details on outlook, shares, analyst comment)
FRANKFURT, April 6 German drugs-packaging firm Gerresheimer on Thursday said its major pharmaceutical customers had been more cautious in placing orders due to uncertainty over the new U.S. administration's policies, sending its shares lower.
Revenues at Gerresheimer's business division that makes glass bottles and vials for drugs fell 2.9 percent in its fiscal first quarter through the end of February as sales in North America slipped.
"Greater uncertainty with regard to the new U.S. government triggered a relatively pronounced reticence among a number of large pharma customers to place orders," Gerresheimer said in a statement, adding that European cosmetic glass sales had risen.
President Donald Trump has promised to increase competition in the pharmaceutical industry without giving details, while promised healthcare reform has been delayed, leaving drugmakers uncertain as to how pricing and demand may be affected.
Overall, Gerresheimer's revenues were down more than 5 percent at 302.8 million euros ($323.1 million) in the quarter, missing analyst consensus of 307 million euros in a Reuters poll.
The group said it expected full-year revenues at the lower end of its forecast range of 1.405 billion to 1.455 billion euros. Analysts on average see 2017 revenues of 1.43 billion euros.
Shares in Gerresheimer fell 5.9 percent in early trading to the bottom of the German mid-cap index, which slipped 0.4 percent.
"The fact that the management currently sees just the lower end of the FY revenue guidance should not come as a major negative surprise after the expected slow start to the year," said DZ Bank analyst Sven Kuerten, reiterating his "buy" rating.
Gerresheimer reiterated that adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) should rise to around 320 million euros this year from 308 million in 2016, after a 6 percent slide in the first quarter. ($1 = 0.9366 euros) (Reporting by Maria Sheahan and Georgina Prodhan; Editing by Victoria Bryan)
rewrite:
German packaging manufacturer Gerresheimer reported on Thursday that hesitation from its key pharmaceutical clients in North America, linked to policy unpredictability under the new U.S. administration, has negatively impacted its performance and stock price.

During the fiscal first quarter ending in February, revenue declined by over five percent, totaling 302.8 million euros, which fell short of market expectations. This was partly due to a nearly three percent drop in sales for the division producing medicinal glass containers, attributed to weaker North American demand. The company noted that several major pharmaceutical customers exhibited marked caution in ordering, citing the uncertain regulatory environment. In contrast, sales of cosmetic glass in Europe saw growth.

The U.S. political landscape has created ambiguity for drugmakers, as proposed healthcare reforms and pledges to foster industry competition remain undefined, clouding the outlook for pricing and future demand.

Consequently, Gerresheimer anticipates its annual revenue will likely reach only the bottom of its projected span, between 1.405 and 1.455 billion euros. Following the announcement, the company's shares dropped approximately six percent, underperforming the broader German mid-cap index.

Analyst Sven Kuerten of DZ Bank commented that the guidance revision was not entirely unexpected given the slow start to the year and maintained a positive "buy" recommendation. Despite the quarterly downturn, the firm reaffirmed its full-year forecast for adjusted EBITDA, expecting an increase to about 320 million euros from 308 million the previous year.
