CNN Money — Amazon says it is taking action against potentially counterfeit solar eclipse glasses.
The company said Sunday that it contacted and issued refunds to some customers who purchased glasses on Amazon that "may not comply with industry standards."
Amazon has also removed a few listings for glasses on its website "out of an abundance of caution." It did not name any of those listings in its statement.
To safely view the solar eclipse August 21, you'll need a special pair of ultra-dark sunglasses. There has been enormous demand for those kinds of glasses, which prevent the permanent eye damage that the sun's rays could cause.
But that demand has been followed by reports that knockoff eclipse glasses — which may not provide adequate protection — have flooded the market.
The American Astronomical Society said last week that it updated its safety advice "in response to alarming reports" of unsafe glasses selling online.
The organization says buyers should be skeptical of glasses even if they're stamped with an ISO seal, which has been used in the past to indicate which glasses comply with standards set by the International Organization for Standardization.
To help tamp down on fraud, the AAS posted a list of verified vendors and websites where those eclipse glasses are sold.

rewrite:
Amazon has announced measures to address concerns over possibly fake solar eclipse viewing glasses sold through its platform. On Sunday, the company stated it reached out to certain buyers and processed refunds for products that might not meet recognized safety specifications. Additionally, Amazon has taken down a small number of product listings from its site as a precaution, though it did not identify those specific items in its announcement.

Viewing the solar eclipse on August 21 safely requires specially designed, extremely dark lenses. Interest in these protective glasses has surged, as they are essential to avoid lasting harm to eyesight from the sun’s intense light. However, this heightened demand has led to widespread accounts of counterfeit glasses entering circulation, which may fail to offer sufficient protection against solar radiation.

Last week, the American Astronomical Society revised its safety recommendations due to disturbing accounts of unsafe glasses being marketed online. The AAS cautions consumers to be wary even if glasses bear an ISO certification mark, as that stamp has historically signaled compliance with International Organization for Standardization guidelines but may now be misused. In an effort to combat deceptive sales, the society has published a list of approved sellers and websites where legitimate eclipse glasses can be purchased.

Nigeria’s Ministry of Mines and Steel Development has accused the management of BUA Group of using armed militia, soldiers and policemen to mine marble and limestone in mining sites allocated to the Dangote Group.
The Ministry, in a statement signed by its Permanent Secretary, Mohammed Abass, also alleged that the company has been using a combination of armed militia, soldiers and policemen to obstruct the ministry’s team from executing the stop work order issued to the company in October.
The ministry’s statement was in response to an open letter to President Muhammadu Buhari by the company alleging that a minister was involved in sabotaging its operations.
Abass said that in the records of the Ministry of Mines and Steel Development and the Nigerian Mining Cadastre Office, the BUA Group did not have a mining lease over the contentious site (No. 2541ML) and was therefore engaged in illegal mining.
He stated, “The ministry stands by the stop work order issued to the BUA Group and signed by the Permanent Secretary dated 17th of October 2017.”
“The letter was issued after thorough investigation confirmed that the BUA Group was indeed engaging in illegal mining of marble/limestone at a mine pit located on geographical coordinates N070 21’ 47.4’ E0060 26’ 51.8’, while the run-of-mine is stockpiled at an area with geographical coordinates N070 21’ 48.4’; E0060 26’37.2’.”
“Clarification provided by the Mining Cadastre Office shows that the coordinates of the mine pit and RoM stockpile area fall wholly within the area of mining Lease No 2541ML belonging to Messrs Dangote Industries Limited.”
Abass added, “The ministry had earlier in 2015 issued a stop work order on this same disputed site but the BUA Group disregarded the order and went ahead with its illegal mining activities, under heavy cover of armed soldiers, policemen and men of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps.”
“The management of BUA also resisted the enforcement of the latest stop work order issued on October 17, 2017 using a combination of armed militia, soldiers and policemen to obstruct the team from the ministry in effecting the stop work order.”
He added that the ministry would not compromise due process in its commitment to promote local and global investments in the Nigerian mining sector.
rewrite:
The Nigerian Ministry of Mines and Steel Development has leveled serious accusations against the BUA Group. According to the Ministry, the company has employed security forces, including military and police personnel, alongside armed militias, to illegally extract marble and limestone from deposits located within a mining lease area legally assigned to the Dangote Group.

These allegations were detailed in an official release from the Ministry's Permanent Secretary, Mohammed Abass. The statement further contends that BUA Group utilized these armed groups to physically block ministry officials from carrying out a suspension order previously served to the company in October. This declaration from the Ministry was issued as a direct rebuttal to a public letter from BUA addressed to the President, which had claimed that a government minister was actively working to undermine the company's operations.

Abass clarified that, according to the official registries maintained by both the Ministry and the Nigerian Mining Cadastre Office, BUA Group holds no valid mining lease for the site in question, identified as No. 2541ML. Consequently, its activities there are deemed unlawful. The Ministry fully affirms the validity of the cessation order issued on October 17, 2017. This directive was enacted following an extensive inquiry which verified that BUA was conducting unauthorized extraction at a specific pit. The investigation confirmed that both the excavation site and the adjacent area used for storing raw, unprocessed material are entirely situated within the boundaries of the mining lease legally owned by Dangote Industries Limited.

The Permanent Secretary also revealed that this is not the first such incident. An initial directive to halt work at this disputed location was issued in 2015, but BUA Group allegedly ignored it. The company is accused of continuing its unauthorized operations under the substantial protection of armed units from the army, police, and the Civil Defence Corps. Similarly, when the most recent order was enforced in late 2017, BUA's management reportedly again mobilized a mixed force of militia, soldiers, and police to obstruct the ministry's enforcement team.

Abass concluded by asserting the Ministry's unwavering dedication to upholding proper legal procedures. This commitment, he stated, is fundamental to fostering a trustworthy environment that encourages both domestic and international investment within the nation's mining industry.

BERLIN — Bayern Munich continued its march to a record-extending sixth consecutive Bundesliga title by beating Mainz 2-0 on Saturday.
Second-placed Bayer Leverkusen was held at Freiburg to 0-0, and Schalke lost at home to relegation-threatened Werder Bremen 2-1, as Bayern increased its already commanding lead to 18 points with 13 games remaining.
"With the large gap and other teams' lack of consistency it really would be a small miracle if we were to let it get exciting again," Bayern defender Mats Hummels said.
Franck Ribery scored with Bayern's first effort on goal after a half-hour when Mats Hummels and Sandro Wagner made way to allow his volley from a half-cleared corner fly inside the post.
The French winger was mobbed by teammates in celebration. Ribery's contract with Bayern is up at the end of the season.
James Rodriguez made it 2-0 before the break, taking Corentin Tolisso's cross on his chest and sending the ball inside the right post with another volley.
Another victory ensured Bayern coach Jupp Heynckes improved his record to 18 wins in 19 games across all competitions since returning for a fourth stint in charge in October.
"The win is deserved. But Mainz fought well and put us under pressure at times after the break, and we were too careless in attack," said Heynckes, who again before the game ruled out extending his contract beyond the end of the season.
SCHALKE STUNNED
Zlatko Junuzovic scored in the third minute of injury time to stun Schalke and boost Bremen's chances of avoiding the drop.
rewrite:
In a Saturday Bundesliga match, Bayern Munich secured a 2-0 victory over Mainz, moving the club closer to a sixth straight league championship, a feat never before achieved. Meanwhile, Bayern's closest competitor, Bayer Leverkusen, drew 0-0 with Freiburg, and Schalke suffered a 2-1 home defeat against a struggling Werder Bremen side. These results expanded Bayern's massive advantage at the top of the table to 18 points, with only 13 matches left in the season.

Defender Mats Hummels remarked that given the enormous lead and the inconsistent performances of rival teams, it would be extraordinary for the title race to become competitive again. The scoring opened after thirty minutes when Franck Ribery, following a partially cleared corner, struck a volley into the net. He was immediately surrounded by celebrating teammates. Ribery's current agreement with Bayern concludes this summer. Before halftime, James Rodriguez doubled the lead, expertly controlling a cross with his chest before volleying home.

This latest win means coach Jupp Heynckes has now guided the team to 18 victories in 19 matches across all tournaments since resuming his role last October. Heynckes stated the result was justified but acknowledged Mainz's resilient second-half pressure and his own squad's occasional attacking lapses. He reiterated pre-game that he will not stay beyond this season.

In a dramatic finish elsewhere, Zlatko Junuzovic's stoppage-time goal sealed a shocking loss for Schalke, providing a vital boost to Bremen's hopes of escaping relegation.

The issue of faith comes into state politics in issues such as abortion and health care. But faith leaders came to the Statehouse today to speak out on another issue that hasn’t seen much action in nearly a decade – payday lending.
A new push for limits on payday lenders
“Lord, we cannot imagine a Heaven where Your will includes poverty profiteering.”
Troy Jackson of Cincinnati’s anti-poverty program the Amos Project led the group in prayer for movement on a bill on payday lenders. The last payday lender crackdown passed in 2008. This bill has bipartisan sponsorship, and would cap interest rates at 28%, and monthly payments at 5% of the borrower’s monthly income. Ohio’s payday lenders charge the highest rates in the nation, and polls show Ohioans want more regulations on them. But payday lenders say they provide a needed service and that their satisfied customers are aware of the costs. The bill’s Republican sponsor says he hopes to bring all interested parties together for a meeting about the bill next week.

The industry defends its role, stating it fulfills a necessary demand and that its clients understand the terms. The Rotary Club of Carpinteria Morning is a vibrant service group of community leaders, business owners and volunteers committed to enhancing the community and building positive international relationships.
Every year, the club produces the Carpinteria Calendar and donates all proceeds from sales to nonprofit organizations in the community. The club has donated more than $80,000 to the community since the Carpinteria Calendar was founded in 2005.
Girls Inc. of Carpinteria was fortunate to be presented with a generous check for $1,000 to support its programs and scholarships for local girls.
“The Rotary Club of Carpinteria Morning is proud to support Girls Inc. and their extensive efforts toward enriching the lives of girls in our community and inspiring them to be strong, smart and bold,” said Rotarian Stefanie Herrington, who also serves on the Girls Inc. of Carpinteria Board of Trustees.
Girls Inc. of Carpinteria serves southern Santa Barbara by providing a variety of quality on-site after-school and summer enrichment programs to girls and young women ages 5 to 18 and their families. It is the only all-girl programming offered in the Carpinteria Valley.
“Girls Inc. is honored to receive funds from this generous group of volunteers and business owners,” Executive Director Victoria Juarez said. “They clearly understand the impact of investing in the future leaders of the Carpinteria.”
— Jill Tyler is the director of development for Girls Inc. of Carpinteria.

Annually, this organization creates and sells the Carpinteria Calendar, channeling every dollar earned directly to area charities. Two men appeared in court today after being charged following a robbery at a business on Wearside.
Investigations led Northumbria Police to Freezemoor Road on New Herrington Industrial Estate at around 9am yesterday after a business premises in Dene Road, Castletown, was robbed at gunpoint earlier in the morning.
Officers, including armed response officers, also carried out a search of a house in Flodden Road on the Ford Estate in connection with the incident.
A spokesman for Northumbria Police said this morning: “Two men have now been charged following a robbery in Sunderland yesterday.
“They are Michael Carty, 45, of Railway Terrace, New Herrington and John Henderson, 50, of Hylton Road, Sunderland.
“A third man was arrested and released without any further action.”
Carty and Henderson appeared before magistrates in South Tyneside this morning, and were remanded in custody.
The police spokesman added: “At around 7.33am yesterday police received a report of a robbery at a premises on Dene Road, Sunderland.
"An offender entered with a firearm and made off with a bag.
“Unarmed and armed officers carried out a search for the offenders and intelligence led them to an industrial estate in New Herrington.
"A vehicle was uplifted and two men arrested.
"Nobody was injured and no firearm was discharged.
“Officers also carried out a search of an address on Flodden Road, Sunderland, in connection with their enquiries.
“Anyone with information is asked to contact police on 101 quoting reference 179 290518 or Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.”

The incident was reported to police yesterday morning shortly after 7:30 a.m., when an assailant entered a building on Dene Road in the Castletown area brandishing a gun and stole a bag before fleeing.

Following investigative leads, law enforcement officials, including both standard and armed units, conducted an operation at the New Herrington Industrial Estate on Freezemoor Road around 9 a.m. A vehicle was seized from that location, and two suspects were taken into custody. LOS ANGELES (CBSLA) — AOL Instant Messenger, the ubiquitous program that gave rise to online chat and countless abbreviations and acronyms, will be discontinued this year, its parent company Oath announced Friday.
Michael Albers, VP of Communications Product at Oath – the new company made up of Verizon, Yahoo and AOL properties – said in his announcement that the program now better known as AIM “tapped into new digital technologies and ignited a cultural shift, but the way in which we communicate with each other has profoundly changed.”
“As a result, we’ve made the decision that we will be discontinuing AIM effective December 15, 2017,” Albers said in his statement.
AIM was launched as a standalone app in 1997 after proving to be wildly popular within the AOL desktop program. Arguably, it was more widely used than competitors like ICQ, and messengers from Yahoo and Microsoft MSN, but usage began to slow when Google launched GChat, which was discontinued earlier this year in favor of Google Hangouts.
Facebook Messenger, and Facebook’s practice of pushing its 2 billion users to download the mobile app, all but guaranteed other chat programs’ demise.
Read more at CBSLA.com.
rewrite:
LOS ANGELES (CBSLA) — The pioneering chat service AOL Instant Messenger, which popularized real-time online conversation and a lexicon of shorthand terms, is set to be retired in 2017, parent firm Oath confirmed this week.

Michael Albers, Vice President of Communications Product at Oath—a consolidation of Verizon, Yahoo, and AOL assets—noted in the announcement that AIM harnessed emerging digital tools and sparked a major social transformation. However, he stated that methods of personal communication have since evolved dramatically.

Consequently, Albers confirmed the decision to end the AIM service as of December 15.

Originally introduced as a separate application in 1997 following its explosive success inside AOL’s desktop software, AIM at one point surpassed rival platforms such as ICQ, Yahoo Messenger, and Microsoft MSN in widespread adoption. Its user engagement started declining notably after Google introduced GChat, a service itself discontinued this year and replaced by Hangouts.

The dominance of Facebook Messenger, coupled with Facebook’s strategy of directing its vast user base to install its mobile app, effectively sealed the fate of many earlier chat programs.

Further details are available on CBSLA.com.

BERLIN (AP) — A Vietnamese man charged with involvement in the kidnapping of a former Vietnamese oil executive in Berlin went on trial Tuesday in the German capital. The case has strained diplomatic ties between Berlin and Hanoi.
The 47-year-old, identified only as Long N.H. because of German privacy rules, is charged with espionage and being an accessory to deprivation of liberty.
German authorities say Trinh Xuan Thanh, the former chairman of PetroVietnam's construction arm, and a woman accompanying him were snatched off the street, bundled into a van and taken to Vietnam in July. Prosecutors say that the kidnapping was carried out by Vietnamese intelligence officials and other employees at the Vietnamese Embassy along with several Vietnamese who live in Europe.
Vietnam claims that Thanh, who was seeking asylum in Germany, returned voluntarily. Thanh was given two life sentences earlier this year for embezzlement.
Advertisement
The suspect who went on trial Tuesday at Berlin's state court is accused of providing logistical support for the operation.
Prosecutors say he rented the van used in the kidnapping in Prague three days before the kidnapping and drove it to Berlin, then drove it back immediately after the kidnapping. In between, he allegedly drove back to Prague another car that had been used to snoop on Thanh.
Prosecutor Lienhard Weiss told the court that the suspect had been aware of the basic details of the plan and approved of it, news agency dpa reported. Defendants don't enter formal pleas in Germany. Defense lawyer Stephan Bonell said he would make a statement at a later stage.
Germany accused Vietnam of breaking international law and last year kicked out the country's intelligence attache. The defendant was arrested in the Czech Republic, where he ran a currency exchange office, in August.
rewrite:
A Vietnamese national faced trial in Berlin on Tuesday over accusations tied to the abduction of a former Vietnamese state oil company executive from the German capital, a case that has heightened tensions between Germany and Vietnam.

The defendant, a 47-year-old man referred to as Long N.H. in accordance with German privacy laws, stands accused of espionage and acting as an accessory to unlawful deprivation of liberty. German prosecutors allege the victim, Trinh Xuan Thanh, who previously led a construction subsidiary of PetroVietnam, was seized from a Berlin street along with a female companion in July. They were reportedly forced into a vehicle and transported to Vietnam. Authorities assert the operation was conducted by Vietnamese state intelligence agents and embassy staff, assisted by several Vietnamese nationals residing in Europe.

Vietnam maintains that Thanh, who had applied for asylum in Germany, returned of his own free will. Thanh was later convicted of embezzlement in Vietnam and sentenced to life imprisonment.

The accused is alleged to have provided logistical aid for the kidnapping. Prosecutors state that three days prior to the incident, he rented a van in Prague, drove it to Berlin, and returned it immediately afterward. He is also accused of driving a separate car used for surveilling Thanh back to Prague following the abduction.

According to news agency reports, the prosecutor informed the court that the suspect was aware of the operation's essential elements and supported it. Under German judicial procedure, defendants do not enter formal pleas. The man's defense attorney indicated he would present a statement later in the proceedings.

Germany has condemned the abduction as a violation of international law and expelled a Vietnamese intelligence attaché last year. The defendant was apprehended in the Czech Republic in August, where he operated a currency exchange business.

U.S. negotiators are at last noticing some progress in trade negotiations with Mexico and Canada after months of work and six rounds of NAFTA talks.
NAFTA Negotiations Update
“We finally began to discuss some of the core issues, so this round was a step forward,” Robert Lighthizer, the U.S. representative, said during remarks after the talks concluded Monday. “But we are progressing very slowly. We owe it to our citizens who are operating in a state of uncertainty to move much faster. We need to modernize and we need to rebalance.”
The Canadian and Mexican officials were also positive about the progress, despite the division still evident over the $1.2 trillion trade pact. “For the next round, we will still have substantial challenges to overcome. Yet the progress made so far puts us on the right track to create landing zones to conclude the negotiation soon,” Mexico’s Economy Minister Ildefonso Guajardo said.
Negotiators still disagree on major parts of the renegotiation proposal, including new rules for car manufacturers, dairy and agriculture, government contracts and a potential five-year sunset clause to terminate NAFTA unless all three countries agree to keep it.
Canadian Minister Chrystia Freeland was hopeful that the talks were on the right track, and that the slow pace is working. “That work, I’m pleased to say, is beginning to bear fruit,” Freeland said.
The three nations promised to renegotiate through March 2018, but some officials are uncertain that the talks will result in an agreement by that deadline, according to Reuters. The three delegations are scheduled to meet in Mexico in February to continue discussions.
Still, some in the U.S. see the latest talks as a good sign. “I am optimistic about the progress made so far in these negotiations and the desire of all three countries to address the outstanding issues,” said Washington Republican Rep. Dave Reichert, chairman of the Trade Subcommittee in the House Committee on Ways and Means.
President Donald Trump promised to address trade issues during the State of the Union address Tuesday, and he has previously commented on the slow progress of the renegotiations. “We have to have reciprocal trade. It’s not a one-way deal anymore,” Trump told reporters on Monday.
Republished by permission. Original here.
rewrite:
After months of effort and six rounds of discussions, American officials are finally observing signs of advancement in trade talks with Mexico and Canada regarding the North American Free Trade Agreement. The U.S. Trade Representative, Robert Lighthizer, noted that the most recent session marked an improvement because it involved deeper engagement with fundamental topics. However, he emphasized that the pace remains sluggish and must accelerate to reduce uncertainty for businesses and citizens, stressing the need to update and recalibrate the agreement.

Officials from Canada and Mexico also expressed cautious optimism about the developments, even as significant disagreements persist over the vast trilateral pact. Mexico's Economy Minister, Ildefonso Guajardo, acknowledged that substantial hurdles remain for future rounds but stated the progress has set a positive direction toward finding common ground and finalizing a deal.

Key areas of contention continue to include proposed regulations for the automotive sector, dairy and agricultural markets, government procurement, and a possible sunset provision that would automatically end the pact after five years unless all nations agree to renew it. Canadian Foreign Minister Chrystia Freeland indicated that the deliberate pace of negotiations is proving effective, with the work starting to yield results.

Although the three countries initially aimed to conclude renegotiations by March 2018, some officials doubt that deadline will be met, according to Reuters reports. The next meeting is planned for February in Mexico.

In the United States, some lawmakers view the latest round as encouraging. Representative Dave Reichert, a Republican from Washington who chairs a key trade subcommittee, said he is hopeful about the trajectory and the shared commitment to resolving remaining issues. President Donald Trump, who has frequently criticized the slow speed of the talks, reiterated his focus on achieving reciprocal trade terms, commenting on the necessity of moving away from what he described as one-sided arrangements. He is expected to touch on trade policy in his upcoming State of the Union address.

Kylie Jenner's daughter has a shoe collection worth $22,000.
The 20-year-old reality star is excited that five-month-old Stormi - who she has with boyfriend Travis Scott - can finally fit into the tiny sneakers that have been filling out her closet since she was born.
In a video shared to Instagram, Kylie said: "Stormi can finally fit into some of her sneakers.
"Her dad gave her loads of vintage shoes so I'm about to see if she likes shoes. Too cute."
Among the dozens of pairs of shoes already in Stormi's collection are $1,000 Giuseppe Zanottis, $275 Gucci flats and several pairs of $50 Nike Air Force 1s.
Meanwhile, the 'Keeping Up With the Kardashians' star has also revealed she's having an air-conditioned dog house built for her beloved pets Norman and Bambi.
Taking to her Snapchat account, Kylie gave fans a quick look at the outside of her dog house, which has been decked and has a white picket fence, and she said: "You guys, my doghouse is almost done! How cute!"
Kylie is known for giving her dogs the life of luxury as Norman and Bambi - which are Italian greyhounds - have their own bedrooms, complete with a plush bed and fancy fireplace, inside her lavish mansion in California.
Taking to her Snapchat last year, Kylie uploaded photo of her furry friends' abode.
She wrote alongside the shot: "Norman & Bambi's room (sic)."
rewrite:
The five-month-old child of Kylie Jenner possesses an assortment of footwear valued at $22,000. The young television personality, aged 20, is delighted that her daughter Stormi—whom she shares with partner Travis Scott—is now big enough to wear the miniature sneakers that have been accumulating since her birth. In a social media clip, Jenner expressed, "Stormi is finally able to wear a few of her little shoes. Her father collected many classic pairs for her, so I'm going to find out if she enjoys them. It's absolutely adorable."

This extensive wardrobe includes numerous items, such as Giuseppe Zanotti designs priced around $1,000, Gucci ballet flats costing $275, and multiple sets of Nike Air Force 1s at $50 per pair. Separately, the famous family member from the reality series 'Keeping Up With the Kardashians' has disclosed that she is constructing a climate-controlled outdoor shelter for her cherished Italian greyhounds, Norman and Bambi. Sharing a glimpse on another social platform, she displayed the nearly finished structure, which features decorative siding and a traditional white fence, commenting on its charming progress.

Jenner is renowned for pampering her pets, who reside in her opulent California home. The dogs have their own dedicated quarters inside the mansion, outfitted with comfortable bedding and an elegant fireplace. Previously, she posted an image of this specialized space, labeling it as belonging to Norman and Bambi.

April 3 The battle to avoid relegation from the Premier League is likely to go down to the final game of the season, Swansea City manager Paul Clement has said after his club were held to a goalless draw by fellow strugglers Middlesbrough on Sunday.
Swansea are one point and one place above the drop zone, with Hull City, Middlesbrough and Sunderland occupying the bottom three spots.
"I think it will go right down to the final games of the season, if not the final game," Clement told British media.
"And we have to be well prepared and give our best in every individual game we have."
The point earned by Middlesbrough was their first in four games and Clement said only time would tell whether Swansea would regret not taking all three points at home.
"I do not know if it will be a decent point, I hope so come the end of the season," he added
Clement is hoping leading scorer Fernando Llorente will recover from an ankle injury before they host second-placed Tottenham Hotspur on Wednesday.
"You do miss him because he's a big focal point," he added.
"He has an ankle issue which I'm hoping won't keep him out for very long so Wednesday is achievable but he's still a doubt for the game."
Spurs, who trail leaders Chelsea by seven points, have won their last four league games, while Swansea are unbeaten at home since a 4-0 defeat to Arsenal in January. (Reporting by Hardik Vyas in Bengaluru; Editing by Peter Rutherford; )
rewrite:
Swansea City manager Paul Clement believes the fight to remain in England's top football division will probably be decided in the last matchday. He made this statement following a Sunday stalemate with Middlesbrough, another club in danger of demotion. The draw leaves Swansea just a single point above the three teams at the foot of the table: Hull City, Middlesbrough, and Sunderland.

Clement told reporters he anticipates the relegation struggle extending to the season's concluding fixtures. He emphasized that his squad must be ready to perform at their maximum in each remaining contest. The result gave Middlesbrough their first point after three consecutive losses, and Clement acknowledged it is too early to know if failing to win at home will prove costly for Swansea. He expressed hope that the drawn match will be viewed favorably when the campaign concludes.

Ahead of a midweek match against Tottenham Hotspur, Clement is optimistic that key striker Fernando Llorente can return from an ankle problem. He noted the player's importance as a central attacking figure and stated a return for Wednesday is possible, though not certain. Swansea will face a formidable challenge from Spurs, who have secured four straight league victories and sit second. The Welsh club, however, has not lost at their home ground since January.

A disproportionate rate of pedestrian tickets were written by the sheriff's department in Jacksonville, causing many people to question the motives of law enforcement.
Having a great discussion about implicit bias and criminal justice here at EWC.#myjaxbar pic.twitter.com/uBrJkzOQ0W — Jacksonville Bar Association (@myjaxbar) March 15, 2018
A Florida sheriff is now admitting that racism may have played a role in his city’s disproportionate citation of pedestrian tickets to people of color.
During a forum on justice bias in Jacksonville, Florida, a number of citizens brought up an observation they have made that suggests racism led to many black individuals getting ticketed more than their white counterparts. Indeed, while blacks make up just 29 percent of Jacksonville’s residents, they account for 55 percent of the city’s pedestrian tickets, according to reporting from ProPublica.
Pressed by members of the audience who observed this incommensurate disparity, Jacksonville Sheriff Mike Williams finally conceded, after months of denying, that racial bias could have had a role in the tickets that were handed out to black individuals versus whites.
After a heated back-and-forth with a community activist, Williams stated racist attitudes could have had an impact.
“Could it have anything to do with implicit bias? Of course it could,” he said.
Williams also stated his belief that other factors were at play — citing structural forces, like the fact that more black citizens use public transportation than whites, that could have explained the disproportionate numbers.
But implicit bias is more real than Williams seems willing to admit. There are several examples of bias resulting in a black person’s arrest throughout the nation that seem to suggest that personal biases, rather than institutional ones, play a larger role.
Law enforcement agencies across the nation need to do more to combat implicit biases of their personnel. The Jacksonville sheriff’s department in particular needs to do more to fix its own problems, which are apparent to many people in the community but only visible to some of the people in charge after much wrangling.
Williams made a good first step in conceding that bias may play a role — but he needs to take many more steps forward and determine a course of action that will remedy the problems in his jurisdiction.
rewrite:
In Jacksonville, the local sheriff's office issued pedestrian citations at a rate that has raised public concern over the intentions behind these enforcement actions. This issue sparked a meaningful conversation about unconscious prejudice and the legal system during a Jacksonville Bar Association event.

A Florida law enforcement official has now acknowledged that racial discrimination might be a factor in why pedestrian tickets in his city are given more frequently to minorities. At a Jacksonville forum addressing prejudice in justice, several community members pointed to patterns indicating that racism led to African Americans receiving these citations more often than white residents. Data from ProPublica highlights this imbalance: although Black people constitute only 29% of Jacksonville's population, they represent 55% of all pedestrian tickets.

Facing questions from attendees who noted this stark inequality, Sheriff Mike Williams eventually agreed, following prolonged refusal, that racial prejudice could have influenced why more tickets were issued to Black individuals compared to white ones. Following a tense exchange with a local advocate, Williams accepted that racist mindsets might have been a contributing factor. He acknowledged, "Could implicit bias be involved? Absolutely, it could."

Williams added that he thought additional elements were also relevant, pointing to broader societal conditions such as higher rates of public transit usage among Black residents, which might partly account for the uneven statistics.

However, unconscious bias is a more significant force than Williams appears ready to fully confront. Numerous instances nationwide where bias led to the arrest of Black individuals imply that personal prejudices often outweigh systemic explanations. Police departments everywhere must increase efforts to address the hidden biases of their officers. Specifically, the Jacksonville sheriff's office must take stronger measures to resolve its clearly perceived issues, which have been evident to many in the public but only reluctantly recognized by some authorities after considerable debate.

While Williams' admission that bias could be a factor is a positive initial move, substantial further progress is required. He must now develop and implement a concrete plan to correct these injustices within his department's purview.

Fleet Street elders are looking on with horror and glee as a slow motion Game of Thrones power battle is played out at The Sun. Anyone who thinks this saga is really about a provocative Kelvin Mackenzie column criticising an Everton footballer is naive. “The New King”, “Joffrey” Gallagher, is caught in the midst of all out war between “The Old King of the North” Kelvin and the fiery “Mother of Dragons”, Queen Rebekah.
The decision by News UK to suspend Old King Kelvin is being widely viewed through the prism of Queen Rebekah loathing him. It has been noted in other realms of the Baby Shard that the statement knifing Kelvin came from a News UK spokesman, not a Sun spokesman.
The emerging narrative is that Gallagher kicked back at the decision and, rightly, defended Kelvin, hence why the statement throwing him under the torrent of outrage did not come from The Sun. It came from News UK, where Queen Rebekah reigns. Last Thursday’s Popbitch reported that “Rebekah is aching to bin his £300,000 a year column, cutting costs and helping to detoxify the Sun’s brand in one easy move”. Kelvin’s column was published on Friday.
The New King Gallagher and The Old King Kelvin also go way back. Gallagher has always owed Kelvin after he helped him secure the Sun throne. Before that, at the Telegraph, Gallagher hired Kelvin as a columnist only to be forced to cancel his column when the Scouse hordes protested.
So far, the views of the One True Sun King of Antipodea remain unclear. Though anyone who has watched the hit HBO series (available through all BSkyB-approved outlets) knows this one is going to end in a bloody mess, with a twist or two along the way…
rewrite:
Veteran figures in the British press are observing the unfolding power struggle at The Sun with a mixture of dread and amusement, akin to a drawn-out episode of a medieval fantasy drama. To believe this conflict stems merely from a contentious column by Kelvin Mackenzie targeting a soccer player is to misunderstand the situation entirely. The editor, dubbed "The New King" or "Joffrey" Gallagher, finds himself at the center of a fierce clash between the veteran "Old King of the North," Mackenzie, and the passionate "Mother of Dragons," Rebekah Brooks.

News UK's choice to suspend Mackenzie is largely interpreted as a direct result of Brooks' well-known animosity toward him. Observers across the media landscape have pointed out that the condemnatory statement originated from a News UK representative, not from The Sun's own spokespeople. This suggests Gallagher resisted the suspension and supported Mackenzie, explaining why the Sun itself did not issue the damning announcement. That came from the parent company, News UK, where Brooks holds significant authority. Industry rumors indicate Brooks is eager to terminate Mackenzie's lucrative contract, seeing it as a chance to reduce expenses and rehabilitate the newspaper's image simultaneously, a desire that preceded the latest controversial column.

The relationship between Gallagher and Mackenzie is long-standing and complex. Gallagher feels a lasting debt to Mackenzie for his past support in securing Gallagher's top position at The Sun. Their history extends further back; at a previous publication, Gallagher initially brought Mackenzie on as a writer but had to swiftly end the arrangement following intense public backlash.

The stance of the prominent Australian media proprietor, the ultimate authority over the newspaper group, remains unknown. However, anyone familiar with the narrative arcs of popular television dramas can predict that this corporate feud is unlikely to conclude neatly, promising further turmoil and unexpected developments before any resolution is reached.

THE figure for overcrowding at University Hospital Limerick has reached the highest in the country this Wednesday – but has actually seen a slight decline in the past 24 hours.
The number of patients on trolleys today is 37, according to figures collated by the Irish Nurses and Midwives Organisation. This breaks down to 23 in A&E and a further 14 on trolleys in wards.
However, the total figure is slightly less than Tuesday’s figure of 40 – which itself was a significant increase on Monday’s total of 16.
UHL has the unwanted honour of being top of the INMO’s trolley and ward watch list for the country this Wednesday, slightly ahead of Cork University Hospital, which has 33 on trolleys.
The overcrowding figure has been consistently high at UHL and the hospital is regularly the most overcrowded nationally.
27 beds that were opened between St John’s Hospital, Ennis and Nenagh hospitals to alleviate overcrowding have now reverted back to their original use.
A state-of-the-art emergency department is expected to open this May, subject to a successful recruitment campaign and HSE funding.
It will be three times the size of the current facility, and is expected to improve the patient and staff experience at the hospital, a spokesperson for the UL Hospitals Group has said.
rewrite:
University Hospital Limerick recorded the most severe overcrowding in Ireland this Wednesday, though the situation improved marginally over the previous day. Data from the Irish Nurses and Midwives Organisation shows 37 individuals awaiting care on trolleys. Of these, 23 are in the emergency department, with an additional 14 placed elsewhere in the hospital.

This total represents a small decrease from the 40 patients counted on Tuesday, which itself was a sharp rise from Monday's figure of 16. The hospital currently leads the national overcrowding list, just above Cork University Hospital, where 33 people are on trolleys. Such congestion is a persistent issue at the Limerick facility, which frequently ranks as the nation's most overcrowded.

Temporary beds opened at nearby hospitals in Ennis and Nenagh to relieve pressure have since been returned to their normal function. A new, advanced emergency department is planned to open in May, contingent on securing adequate funding from the Health Service Executive and hiring sufficient staff. According to the hospital group, this facility will be triple the size of the existing one and is anticipated to significantly enhance conditions for both patients and healthcare workers.

Pimm's, Blazers And Sunshine At Henley Royal Regatta
It's all about the boats, blazers and Pimms in Henley this week.
This year's Henley Regatta is well underway - with thousands of people watching five days of rowing races on the Thames. It runs from Wednesday 4 July until Sunday 8 July.
There are more than 200 races of an international standard, which can include Olympic rowers as well as crews new to the event.
Lots of police are on duty.
Superintendent Sarah Grahame, tactical commander for the Royal Regatta said: "We expect to see an increase in the number of visitors to Henley and the surrounding areas during the five day period.
"My officers and I are working closely with our partners to ensure public safety and to maintain the low levels of crime we have come to expect at this prestigious event.
"I ask people visiting and living in Henley over the Regatta period to be prepared for traffic and some congestion. We ask drivers to be patient and mindful of the increased traffic and pedestrians, to leave plenty of time for their journeys, and to carefully follow the appropriate signs to the allocated car parks.
"As is the case at all major events, there will be a security presence which is there to reassure you rather than alarm you. The public provide our additional eyes and ears on the ground and I ask them to support security staff and my officers by remaining vigilant, keeping their belongings with them and reporting anything suspicious or unusual to staff or by calling 101.
"The Neighbourhood Policing team in Henley will be an integral part of our operation and will ensure the priorities of the local community are acted on, as normal, during this time."
rewrite:
The Henley Royal Regatta is in full swing, offering a classic blend of competitive rowing, traditional attire, and summer refreshments. Throughout this week, the focus is on the river, the stylish jackets, and the iconic British drink enjoyed by spectators. The event spans five days, from July 4th to the 8th, drawing large crowds to the banks of the Thames to witness the contests.

Over two hundred high-caliber races are scheduled, featuring both elite athletes, including those with Olympic experience, and novice teams entering the competition. A significant police deployment is in place to manage the occasion. Sarah Grahame, the tactical commander for the regatta, noted that a rise in visitors to Henley and nearby locales is anticipated during this period. She emphasized that her team is collaborating with partners to uphold public safety and preserve the event's historically low crime rate.

Attendees and residents are advised to expect heavier traffic and some delays. Motorists are encouraged to exercise patience, account for extra pedestrians and vehicles, allow additional travel time, and heed directional signage to designated parking areas. As with any large gathering, security measures will be visible, intended to offer reassurance rather than cause concern. The public plays a key role in safety efforts; visitors are asked to stay alert, secure their personal items, and report any concerning activity to event personnel or by contacting the police non-emergency number.

The local neighborhood policing unit will be central to these efforts, continuing to address community concerns as usual throughout the regatta.

Ireland captain Rory Best was asked after tonight’s game in Paris if he had sought any permission from the IRFU to attend the trial of Paddy Jackson and Stuart Olding last Wednesday.
“We sign out on a Tuesday night and Wednesday is our day off so technically we don’t need permission to do stuff in our own time,” said Best.
“The reason I was there, it’s on the record I was called as a character witness, and I was advised that it is important that I got both sides of the story so I could make an informed decision about that.
“Because it is an ongoing legal matter I will not make any further comment.”
Ireland and Ulster rugby captain Rory Best (right) and club and international team-mate Iain Henderson arrive at Laganside Magistrates’ Court in Belfast on Wednesday, where their team-mates Paddy Jackson and Stuart Olding are on trial for the alleged rape of a woman. Photograph: PACEMAKER
Mr Jackson (26), of Oakleigh Park, Belfast is charged with one count of rape and one count of sexual assault and Mr Olding (24), of Ardenlee Street, Belfast, is charged with one count of rape.
Blane McIlroy (26), of Royal Lodge Road, Ballydollaghan, Belfast, is accused of one count of exposure.
Rory Harrison (25), from Manse Road, Belfast, is charged with perverting the course of justice and withholding information.
They all deny the charges.
rewrite:
Following Ireland's match in Paris, team captain Rory Best was questioned about whether he had received authorization from the Irish Rugby Football Union to be present at the court proceedings involving Paddy Jackson and Stuart Olding the previous Wednesday. Best clarified that the team's weekly schedule concludes on Tuesday evenings, making Wednesday a personal day for players, during which formal approval for personal activities is not required. He explained his attendance by noting he had been formally summoned to provide a character reference. Best added that he had received guidance stating it was crucial to understand the full context of the situation to form a balanced perspective. He declined to elaborate further, citing the active status of the legal case.

Best, who leads both the national team and Ulster Rugby, was seen arriving at Laganside Magistrates’ Court in Belfast alongside provincial and international teammate Iain Henderson. Their fellow players, Jackson and Olding, are facing allegations related to the rape of a woman. Jackson faces charges of rape and sexual assault, while Olding is charged with rape. Two other men, Blane McIlroy and Rory Harrison, are also implicated in the case; McIlroy is accused of exposure, and Harrison is charged with obstructing justice and failing to disclose information. All four individuals have pleaded not guilty to the respective accusations.

President Donald Trump signed a memorandum directing his Trade Representative Robert E. Lighthizer to investigate China for the theft of intellectual property.
“For too long, this wealth has been drained from our country while Washington has done nothing. They have never done anything about it,” Trump said to reporters at the White House. “But Washington will turn a blind eye no longer.”
advertisement
Trump said that combatting piracy and theft of information from American companies was long overdue, blaming the political establishment for looking the other way.
He described his actions as a fulfillment of his campaign promises to defend the American worker.
“We will uphold our values, we will defend our workers, and we will protect the innovations, creations, and inventions that power our magnificent country,” he said.
China protested Trump’s actions through the state-run newspaper, denouncing the president’s attempts to blame them for North Korea’s ongoing hostility to America.
“[I]t is impossible to look at the matter without taking into account his increasing disappointment at what he deems as China’s failure to bring into line the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea,” the editorial read, noting that “exploiting trade as a bargaining chip” would be a “serious mistake.”
Secretary of Commerce Wilbur Ross attended the event as well as Director of Trade and Industrial Policy Peter Navarro, Trade Ambassador Robert Lighthizer, Secretary Steven Mnuchin, and Gary Cohn. Lt. Gen. H.R. McMaster also attended the event.
rewrite:
President Donald Trump issued a directive ordering an inquiry into China's alleged intellectual property violations, tasking Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer with leading the probe. Speaking at the White House, Trump criticized past administrations for inaction, stating that American assets had been unfairly taken for years without a response from Washington, but that such tolerance had now ended. He emphasized that addressing the piracy and data theft affecting U.S. firms was a critical and delayed priority, accusing the political elite of historically ignoring the issue. Trump framed this move as keeping a pledge made during his election campaign to stand up for American laborers. He vowed to maintain national principles, safeguard workers, and secure the innovative outputs that drive the country's success.

China responded critically via its official press, rejecting the allegations and suggesting Trump's motivations were linked to frustration over China's role in managing North Korea's tensions with the United States. An editorial argued that it was a significant error to use trade as a tool for negotiation in this context. The signing ceremony was attended by several high-ranking officials, including Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross, Trade and Industrial Policy Director Peter Navarro, Trade Ambassador Lighthizer, Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin, and Gary Cohn, with National Security Advisor H.R. McMaster also present.

LOS ANGELES (AP) -- Before the game, the UCLA student section serenaded Thomas Welsh with ''Happy Birthday.''
The senior was giving the gift, though.
Welsh hit a go-ahead 3-pointer with 51 seconds left, lifting the Bruins to an 82-79 victory on Saturday and snapping the Trojans' six-game winning streak.
''That's special when you have a seven-footer who can make threes,'' UCLA coach Steve Alford said.
Welsh then calmly sank two free throws with 11 seconds remaining and finished with 21 points on his 22nd birthday to seal a third straight win for the Bruins (16-7, 7-4 Pac-12).
''Just stepping to the line and doing the same repetition,'' Welsh said, describing his mindset with the outcome in doubt. ''Just going through my form and knocking them down, not thinking about it.''
Aaron Holiday led the Bruins with 23 points, including five 3-pointers, and nine assists while playing 40 minutes. They improved to 12-2 at home.
The Trojans (17-7, 8-3) were led by Elijah Stewart with 20 points, nearly double his average. Nick Rakocevic and Shaqquan Aaron added 14 points each.
''Both teams are going to come out fighting and make sure you punch first and keep on punching,'' Welsh said.
After Welsh's go-ahead 3-pointer, Stewart got fouled and made both, leaving USC trailing 80-79.
Aaron missed a jumper for the Trojans and Welsh got fouled while grabbing the rebound. The Bruins ended the game on a 22-10 run.
''It was a really high-intensity game,'' USC coach Andy Enfield said. ''Both teams played great, especially on the offensive end. It really just came down to that last shot at the end.''
Jordan McLaughlin and Jordan Usher each missed 3-pointers for USC in the last four seconds. McLaughlin finished with five points on 2-of-8 shooting, well off his 12.6-point average.
rewrite:
In Los Angeles, as reported by the Associated Press, UCLA fans celebrated Thomas Welsh’s birthday with a cheerful song before the matchup. However, it was Welsh who delivered the real present. With just 51 seconds on the clock, the senior forward sank a crucial three-pointer to put the Bruins ahead, ultimately securing an 82–79 win Saturday and halting USC’s six-game run of victories.

UCLA head coach Steve Alford praised the unique advantage of having a seven-foot player who can reliably score from beyond the arc. Welsh later added two decisive free throws with 11 seconds left, capping a 21-point performance on his 22nd birthday and locking in a third consecutive win for UCLA, now 16–7 overall and 7–4 in the Pac-12. Reflecting on his calm approach at the line with the game in the balance, Welsh said he focused on routine and technique, pushing aside any pressure.

Aaron Holiday topped the Bruins’ scoring with 23 points, hitting five three-pointers, and dished out nine assists while playing the full 40 minutes. The victory improved UCLA’s home record to 12–2. For USC (17–7, 8–3), Elijah Stewart scored 20 points, far above his usual average, supported by Nick Rakocevic and Shaqquan Aaron with 14 apiece.

Welsh emphasized the intense, back-and-forth nature of the contest, noting that both sides came out aggressively. After his go-ahead three, Stewart was fouled and made both free throws, bringing USC within one at 80–79. Aaron then missed a jump shot, and Welsh secured the rebound while drawing a foul. UCLA closed the game on a 22–10 surge.

USC coach Andy Enfield described the matchup as highly intense, with both teams performing well offensively, and acknowledged that the final shot proved decisive. In the last four seconds, Jordan McLaughlin and Jordan Usher each missed three-point attempts for the Trojans. McLaughlin ended with only five points, shooting 2-for-8, well below his 12.6-point average.

A Vernon orchard has a unique way of keeping the birds away from its bumper cherry crop. (Submitted Photo)
VERNON, B.C. — You usually see them on the side of the road, wiggly arms and tube body bouncing around trying to attract people to a sale.
But a B.C. farmer has found a great use for the air dancers (or air rangers), which have protected his crop from pesky birds.
Peter’s U-Pick Orchard has rescued a bumper crop in large part thanks to the fun inflatables he used to protect his cherries.
“They are working great compared to previous years where we would have flocks of birds on the early cherries now we just barely see a Jay or two in there compared to flocks of 20-40 at a time,” said owner Peter Sidorczuk.
“I got the idea from our neighbour, the Krugers, they tried one last year in their grapes and she said it is working. So I did a bit of research online and bought three of them to try this year and am impressed.
“It is a great idea.”
See related: Cherry grower hopes to avoid helicopter use
The BX orchard, which opened for the season Saturday, also used a device called bird guard to protect the early cherries. Designed in Australia, the bird guard randomly emits bird distress calls.
Combined with the air dancers, there’s plenty of cherries available at the farm this year. Plus the devices have helped keep pesky birds from the Peter’s peaches and apricots.
Peter’s U-Pick, on Rimer Road, is open seven days a week from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.
@VernonNews
jennifer@vernonmorningstar.com
Like us on Facebook and follow us on Twitter.
rewrite:
A fruit farm in Vernon has discovered an unusual method to prevent birds from eating its abundant cherry harvest. Typically, air dancers—those tall, waving inflatable figures often seen advertising sales—are found near roadsides. However, a British Columbia grower has repurposed them as effective guardians for his fruit.

At Peter’s U-Pick Orchard, these playful inflatables have played a key role in safeguarding the season’s plentiful yield. The owner, Peter Sidorczuk, notes a significant reduction in bird activity compared to earlier seasons, when large groups would descend on the early-ripening cherries. Now, only an occasional jay is spotted, rather than dozens at once.

Sidorczuk took inspiration from neighboring growers, the Krugers, who successfully tested an air dancer in their grape vineyard last year. After some online research, he purchased three to try this season and has been pleased with the results.

In addition to the air dancers, the orchard, located in the BX area and opened for the season last Saturday, uses a tool named “bird guard.” This Australian invention broadcasts random recordings of bird distress signals. Together, these strategies have not only protected the cherry crop but also kept birds away from the farm’s peaches and apricots.

Peter’s U-Pick on Rimer Road operates daily from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., offering plenty of fruit for visitors to harvest this year.

It isn’t difficult to remember when buyers, hats in hand, were making offers on homes that tried every possible way to win over the sellers’ favor.
“We promise to take good care of the vegetable garden you put so much work into,” one potential buyer might write. Or, “We love great novels as much as you do, and we’ll get a lot of profound enjoyment from the library remodel you put into the fourth bedroom.”
That was a seller’s market. Buyers found themselves competing with other buyers who, with offers in hand, wanted to win the right to purchase the home. Today, though, we’re still in the midst of a buyer’s market in which sellers will often go to unusual lengths to accommodate the needs and wishes of buyers.
Is one market better than another? It depends on what you need to accomplish.
If you simply need to sell your home and move into a cave in the Himalayas, you’re probably worse off in a buyer’s market than you would be in a seller’s market. But if you need to sell your home to buy a replacement home, the market may balance the good with the bad. It may be somewhat difficult in a buyer’s market to get your home sold, but it will be that much easier — and less costly — to buy your next home in this buyer’s market.
It is a matter of knowing how best to approach the market, just as it is a matter of knowing the best things to say to buyers and to sellers. Those statements change, as you can see.
What doesn’t change, though, is your need for able guidance from your real estate professional, who represents buyers and sellers week in and week out and is aware of how best to approach each market — and each individual offer situation.
— Paul Suding, a real estate agent with Cool Santa Barbara Homes and Village Properties, is president of the Santa Barbara Association of Realtors. He can be contacted at .(JavaScript must be enabled to view this email address) or 805.455.8055.
rewrite:
Recalling a time not long ago when prospective home purchasers would eagerly court sellers with personalized appeals is easy. Hopeful buyers might pen heartfelt notes pledging to nurture a beloved garden or expressing shared appreciation for a custom-built library, all in hopes of standing out among competing bids. That period was a definitive seller's market, characterized by multiple buyers vying for a single property.

Currently, the dynamics have shifted to a buyer's market. In this environment, sellers frequently find themselves making extra concessions and adapting their strategies to meet buyer demands. Determining which market condition is superior isn't straightforward; the answer hinges entirely on one's specific circumstances and goals.

For someone aiming solely to sell a property, perhaps to relocate far away, a seller's market is undoubtedly more advantageous. Conversely, for an individual selling one home to purchase another, the buyer's market presents a mixed outcome. While selling might prove more challenging, acquiring the next home becomes significantly easier and often more affordable within the same market climate. The key lies in understanding how to strategically navigate the prevailing conditions, including tailoring communication effectively—whether addressing buyers or sellers—as these approaches continually evolve.

Amidst these shifting tides, one constant remains: the critical importance of skilled advice from a seasoned real estate professional. An agent who consistently works with both parties possesses the nuanced insight needed to optimally handle each market phase and negotiate individual offers successfully.

— Paul Suding, a real estate agent with Cool Santa Barbara Homes and Village Properties, serves as president of the Santa Barbara Association of Realtors. He is available at .(JavaScript must be enabled to view this email address) or by phone at 805.455.8055.

FILE PHOTO: Senator Alejandro Guillier is pictured at the Chilean congress in Valparaiso, Chile January 10, 2017. REUTERS/Rodrigo Garrido
SANTIAGO Chilean presidential candidate Alejandro Guillier would, if elected, aim to shift the country toward public transport networks that run on electricity, he told a gathering of journalists on Thursday.
The independent leftist senator also pledged to support renewable energy generation in the South American nation, which has experienced a boom in wind and solar power in recent years.
The country is beginning a major infrastructure build-out, and the two trends have begun showing some synergies. The metropolitan rail system of the capital, Santiago, for instance, is the first in the world to run primarily on solar power.
As well as electric public transport, Guillier said he plans to push for an electric vehicle charging park in his first year in office, and build up the country's minimal inter-urban rail links to cut reliance on fossil fuels.
Polls show the 63-year-old senator in second place in voting intentions to win November's presidential election, after conservative ex-president Sebastian Pinera.
Chile, which has essentially no local hydrocarbons, has shifted heavily toward renewable energy in recent years. In August, a slew of European renewable generators won the majority of contracts in a massive auction to supply the public power grid from the 2020s.
Energy developers will be watching the election keenly for clues as to the future direction of policy, such as the changing structure of the nation's public power auctions, and whether clean energy subsidies might be introduced.
(Reporting by Antonio de la Jara; Writing by Gram Slattery; Editing by James Dalgleish)
rewrite:
Chilean presidential hopeful Alejandro Guillier outlined his energy and transportation priorities to reporters on Thursday. The independent left-leaning senator stated that, should he win the presidency, he would work to transition the nation's public transit systems to electric power.

Guillier further committed to backing the expansion of renewable energy sources. Chile has seen significant growth in its wind and solar sectors lately. This development aligns with ongoing large-scale infrastructure projects, creating combined benefits. A leading example is the Santiago metro, which is now predominantly powered by solar energy, a global first.

In addition to electrifying public transportation, the candidate proposed establishing a network of electric vehicle charging stations within his initial year as president. He also aims to enhance the country's limited regional rail connections to decrease dependence on oil and gas.

Current surveys indicate the 63-year-old senator is trailing only former conservative president Sebastian Pinera in voter preference for the November election.

Lacking substantial domestic fossil fuel reserves, Chile has moved aggressively toward renewables. This past August, numerous European renewable energy firms secured most of the contracts in a major bidding process to provide electricity to the national grid starting in the next decade.

Energy companies are monitoring the electoral race closely for insights into future government policies. Key areas of interest include potential modifications to the national power auction system and the possibility of new subsidies for clean energy projects.

In American League action, Toronto fell to Boston with a final score of 6-4. The Blue Jays scored two runs in both the sixth and ninth innings, but the Red Sox built their lead with single runs in the third and fifth, two in the sixth, and another pair in the eighth. Sam Gaviglio took the loss for Toronto, while Eduardo Rodriguez earned the win. Craig Kimbrel secured the save. Teoscar Hernandez homered for the Jays, with Eduardo Nunez and J.D. Martinez going deep for Boston.

Cleveland dominated Chicago, winning 9-1. The Indians established a commanding lead early, scoring two in the first, five in the second, and two more in the fourth. The White Sox managed only a single run in the ninth. Corey Kluber pitched effectively for the win, while Reynaldo Lopez was charged with the loss. Home runs came from Yolmer Sanchez for Chicago, and Jose Ramirez and Edwin Encarnacion for Cleveland.

Houston scored two in the fifth and one in the ninth. Luis Severino recorded the victory, with Dallas Keuchel taking the loss. Aroldis Chapman closed the game for a save. Max Stassi hit a home run for the Astros.

In interleague play, the Washington Nationals shut out the Baltimore Orioles 2-0. Washington scored single runs in the third and seventh innings. Max Scherzer was brilliant on the mound for the win, and Sean Doolittle finished for the save. David Hess was the losing pitcher. Bryce Harper provided the game's only homer.

A National League contest saw Milwaukee edge St. Louis 3-2. The Brewers broke a scoreless tie with a run in the fifth, and after the Cardinals tied it with two in the seventh, Milwaukee responded with two of their own in the bottom of that inning. Jeremy Jeffress got the win in relief, while Sam Tuivailala took the loss. Corey Knebel earned the save. Harrison Bader homered for St. Louis, and Christian Yelich for Milwaukee.

Scott Schebler and Adam Duvall homered for Cincinnati, with Paul Goldschmidt and John Ryan Murphy connecting for Arizona.

Joe Musgrove earned the win for Pittsburgh, with Kyle Hendricks suffering the loss. Felipe Vazquez recorded the save. Josh Harrison's home run provided the decisive run for the Pirates.

NEW YORK (AP) — Roseanne Barr is partly blaming Ambien for the tweet that led to her show’s cancellation, but the maker of the insomnia drug quickly retorted that “racism is not a known side effect.”
Hours after ABC axed her show for her offensive tweet about former Obama adviser Valerie Jarrett — and quickly breaking a promise to stay off Twitter — the comedian was back on the social media platform.
She urged people not to defend her and said of her Jarrett tweet that she was “ambien tweeting” at 2 a.m.
That led to the response on Twitter by the drug maker Sanofi.
People of all races, religions and nationalities work at Sanofi every day to improve the lives of people around the world. While all pharmaceutical treatments have side effects, racism is not a known side effect of any Sanofi medication. — Sanofi US (@SanofiUS) May 30, 2018

rewrite:
Comedian Roseanne Barr has attributed her controversial social media post, which resulted in ABC canceling her program, in part to the sleep aid Ambien. Shortly after the network terminated her show due to the offensive remark about former Obama aide Valerie Jarrett, Barr returned to Twitter, despite a prior vow to leave the platform. She asked supporters not to justify her actions, explaining she composed the post about Jarrett in the early morning hours while under the influence of the medication.

The pharmaceutical company Sanofi promptly answered this claim on Twitter. They stated that their employees, who come from diverse backgrounds, are dedicated to enhancing global welfare. The company's official response clarified that although their medicines can have adverse reactions, racism is not documented as one for any product they manufacture.

After reporting a bigger than expected jump in new orders for U.S. manufactured goods in the previous month, the Commerce Department released a report on Friday showing factory orders once again increased by more than expected in December.
The Commerce Department said factory orders surged up by 1.7 percent in December, matching the upwardly revised jump seen in November.
Economists had expected factory orders to climb by 1.5 percent compared to the 1.3 percent increase originally reported for the previous month.
The bigger than expected increase in factory orders was partly due to a spike in durable goods orders, which shot up by 2.8 percent in December after jumping by 1.7 percent in November.
Orders for non-durable goods also climbed by 0.7 percent in December after soaring by 1.6 percent in the previous month.
The report also said shipments of manufactured goods rose by 0.6 percent, while inventories of manufactured goods increased by 0.5 percent.
The inventories-to-shipments ratio subsequently came in at 1.35 in December, unchanged from the previous month.
by RTT Staff Writer
For comments and feedback: editorial@rttnews.com
Economic News

On Friday, the Commerce Department announced that orders for manufactured goods in the U.S. rose more than anticipated in December. This follows a report from the prior month that also showed a stronger-than-forecast increase. Specifically, factory orders advanced by 1.7 percent in December, equaling an upwardly adjusted gain from November. Analysts had projected a 1.5 percent rise, compared to an initially reported 1.3 percent increase for November.

A significant contributor to this larger-than-expected result was a sharp 2.8 percent rise in orders for durable goods, building on a 1.7 percent gain in November. Orders for non-durable goods also increased, climbing 0.7 percent after a 1.6 percent surge the month before. Additionally, the data indicated that shipments of manufactured goods grew by 0.6 percent, while inventories saw a 0.5 percent increase. Consequently, the ratio of inventories to shipments held steady at 1.35 in December, unchanged from November.

A Dublin mother who told gardaí ­ she had a gun for self protection because of a threat on her life has been sentenced to five years, with two years suspended.
Garda Michelle Fitzpatrick told a sentence hearing last month that colleagues had served Niamh Fitzpatrick (39) GIM forms, which are Garda forms to notify a person of a threat on their life.
The garda then agreed with Keith Spencer BL, defending, that there had been a threat against Fitzpatrick but that had expired.
Mr Spencer submitted to Judge Melanie Greally that his client had been abducted from her flat and suffered a violent attack from a person who is since deceased. Counsel said Fitzpatrick suffered from “profound Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder” as a result of this violence.
Fitzpatrick, a mother-of-one from O’Rahilly House, Ringsend, Dublin pleaded guilty at Dublin Circuit Criminal Court to possessing a Smith & Wesson revolver in an air vent at her home on February 23rd, 2017.
She has 21 previous convictions, mostly for minor road traffic offences.
Judge Greally said she did not think Fitzpatrick’s explanation for how she came into possession of the gun was credible and said it “did not stand up to scrutiny”.
She said a number of reports set out in “considerable detail” the many aspects of Fitzpatrick’s history, “the traumatic incidents which have shaped her life and the damaging alliances which she had formed over her adult life”.
The judge said she was taking into account the fact that Fitzpatrick had “taken steps” over the years to address her heroin addiction and the fact that she had a number of mental health issues.
Judge Greally sentenced Fitzpatrick to five years in prison and suspended the final two years on condition that she remain under 18 months of probation supervision on her ultimate release from prison.

A woman from Dublin has received a five-year prison term, with two years suspended, after admitting to gardaí that she kept a firearm for personal safety due to a perceived threat against her. During last month's sentencing hearing, Garda Michelle Fitzpatrick informed the court that official notifications regarding a threat to the defendant's life had been issued to Niamh Fitzpatrick (39). The garda acknowledged under questioning from defense barrister Keith Spencer that while such a threat had existed, it was no longer active.

Representing the accused, Mr. Spencer explained to Judge Melanie Greally that his client had previously been taken from her apartment and violently assaulted by an individual who has since died. He stated this experience left Fitzpatrick with severe Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder. The defendant, a resident of O’Rahilly House in Ringsend and a mother to one child, admitted guilt to the charge of having a Smith & Wesson revolver concealed within a ventilation unit at her residence on February 23rd, 2017. Her prior criminal record consists of 21 convictions, largely for minor traffic violations.

Judge Greally expressed skepticism regarding the defendant's account of how she acquired the weapon, finding it unconvincing upon examination. She noted that several reports thoroughly documented Fitzpatrick's background, including traumatic life events and harmful relationships developed during her adulthood. The judge stated she considered mitigating factors, such as the defendant's efforts to combat her heroin dependency and her ongoing mental health struggles.

Ultimately, Judge Greally imposed a sentence of five years' imprisonment, suspending the final two years contingent upon the defendant completing an 18-month probationary supervision period following her release.

Nu Couche (Sur Le Cote Gauche) is said by Sotheby's to be the greatest painting from the artist's series of once-controversial nudes.
A Modigliani nude has a 150 million dollar (£107 million) price tag – the highest estimate ever placed on a work of art at auction.
Nu Couche (Sur Le Cote Gauche) is said by Sotheby’s to be the greatest painting from Modigliani’s series of once-controversial nudes.
Completed in 1917, it was also the largest painting of his career.
The record for a work actually sold at auction still stands with Leonardo da Vinci’s Salvator Mundi, which went under the hammer for 450 million US dollars (then £341 million) in 2017.
But the Modigliani painting breaks the 140 million dollars record for an estimate, previously held by Picasso’s Les Femmes d’Alger (Version ‘O’), from 2015.
Simon Shaw, co-head worldwide of Sotheby’s impressionist and modern art department, said: “This painting reimagines the nude for the modern era.
“Modigliani depicted his models as confident and self-possessed in their sexuality.
“Nu Couche is an incredibly sensual image, with the sitter’s gaze meeting the viewer’s head-on in truly mesmerising fashion.
“While situating itself within a classical canon of nude painting, the work is radically innovative in style.”
He said of Modigliani’s paintings: “Together these pictures signal a watershed in perhaps the greatest tradition in art – there is the nude before Modigliani, and there is the nude after Modigliani.”
The painting featured at Tate Modern’s recent show on the Italian-born artist, who “scandalised” society with his paintings depicting body hair.
It will lead Sotheby’s Evening Sale of Impressionist and Modern Art in New York on May 14.
© Press Association 2018
rewrite:
According to Sotheby's, *Nu Couche (Sur Le Cote Gauche)* represents the most exceptional work within Modigliani's famed series of nudes, which initially provoked public outcry. This piece carries an estimated value of $150 million, or approximately £107 million, marking the highest pre-sale valuation ever assigned to an artwork at auction. Painted in 1917, it also holds the distinction of being the largest canvas the artist ever produced.

The current auction record for a sold artwork remains with Leonardo da Vinci's *Salvator Mundi*, which fetched $450 million in 2017. However, Modigliani's work surpasses the previous highest estimate of $140 million, set by Picasso's *Les Femmes d’Alger* in 2015. Simon Shaw, a co-leader of Sotheby's impressionist and modern art division, remarked that this painting redefines the nude for contemporary times. He noted that Modigliani portrayed his subjects with a sense of assurance and comfort in their own sensuality. Shaw described *Nu Couche* as a profoundly sensual image, captivating viewers through the model's direct and engaging gaze. While rooted in the historic tradition of nude painting, he emphasized that the work is strikingly original in its execution.

Shaw further commented that Modigliani's nudes collectively mark a pivotal moment in one of art's most significant genres, effectively dividing the tradition into periods before and after his influence. This particular painting was recently displayed in a Tate Modern exhibition focusing on the Italian-born artist, whose inclusion of body hair in his nudes once scandalized audiences. It is scheduled to be the highlight of Sotheby's Evening Sale of Impressionist and Modern Art in New York on May 14th.
