SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — Puerto Rico’s new governor has been sworn in as the U.S. territory prepares for what many believe will be new austerity measures and a renewed push for statehood to haul the island out of a deep economic crisis.
Ricardo Rossello was sworn in Monday and proposed several measures aimed at alleviating the crisis. Among them is a proposal to hold a referendum that would ask voters whether they prefer statehood or independence.
“The United States cannot pretend to be a model of democracy for the world while it discriminates against 3.5 million of its citizens in Puerto Rico, depriving them of their right to political, social and economic equality under the U.S. flag,” Rossello said in his inaugural speech, delivered in Spanish. “There is no way to overcome Puerto Rico’s crisis given its colonial condition.”
The new governor said he would hold elections to choose two senators and five representatives and send them to Washington to demand statehood, similar to what Tennessee did in the 1790s in its push for statehood.
Rossello also aims to boost public-private partnerships and use that revenue to save a retirement system that faces a $40 billion deficit. Rossello has pledged to work closely with a federal control board that U.S. Congress created to oversee Puerto Rico’s finances. He said he supports negotiations with creditors to help restructure a nearly $70 billion public debt.
Rossello announced that he has already signed six executive orders, among them are efforts to promote bilingual education and to eliminate the wage gap for female government employees.
Supporters rallied outside the Capitol on Monday cheering the new governor, many waving U.S. flags.
rewrite:
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — Ricardo Rossello has officially assumed the role of governor in Puerto Rico, commencing his term as the island confronts a severe financial downturn. Expectations are widespread that his administration will introduce strict economic cuts and intensify efforts to achieve U.S. statehood as a pathway to recovery.

During his inauguration on Monday, conducted in Spanish, Rossello outlined multiple initiatives to address the crisis. A central proposal is a planned vote allowing residents to express their preference between becoming a state or gaining full independence. In his address, he criticized the United States, arguing that it cannot claim democratic leadership while denying equal political, social, and economic rights to Puerto Rico's 3.5 million residents. He firmly stated that the territory's colonial status is an insurmountable barrier to resolving its difficulties.

Echoing a historical strategy used by Tennessee in the 1790s, Rossello plans to organize an election to select two senators and five representatives. These officials would then advocate in Washington, D.C., for Puerto Rico's admission as a state. Additionally, his economic strategy includes fostering collaborations between the government and private enterprises. The income generated would help rescue the island's pension system, which is currently burdened by a $40 billion shortfall.

Rossello committed to cooperating with the federal oversight board established by Congress to manage Puerto Rico's fiscal affairs. He also expressed support for discussions with lenders to reorganize the island's approximately $70 billion public debt. Already, the new governor has enacted six executive orders, which include measures to advance bilingual education and to close the pay disparity for women working in government positions.

Outside the Capitol building, enthusiastic supporters gathered on Monday to celebrate the inauguration, many displaying American flags in a show of solidarity.

By Eamon Quinn
Eir has told its investors its next big decision on its future plans won’t be revealed until later this spring when the deal involving its new French owners is expected to be completed.
It comes as another business group, Isme characterised the telecom firm’s plan announced this week to pull out of the Government’s National Broadband Plan as disastrous and which will likely delay the introduction to 2023. It said it has serious reservations about the contract process run by the Department of Communications after what Isme said was Eir securing “low hanging fruit” in its existing installation of broadband.
Outgoing Eir chief Richard Moat in its latest quarterly report blamed the complexity of the National Broadband Plan contract and identified pricing issues “outside of the National Broadband Plan process” for it quitting the tender.
Underlying earnings of €125m in the three months to end December were up 4% from a year earlier on reduced costs, even as revenues fell 2% to €322m, leaving it on target to hit full-year earnings growth targets, it said. Storm- related costs came to €3m in the quarter. Mr Moat had no other news on the company’s strategy. Eir has changed hands more times than any other European national telecom. It is being bought by French entrepreneur Xavier Niel via NJJ and Iliad.
He will buy a 64.5% stake in Eir for an estimated €1bn, while two US hedge funds remain as minority shareholders. The firm has net debts of €2.16bn. Fitch Ratings analyst Damien Chew said Eir’s latest earnings were “broadly in line with what we expected”. He said the effects of the change of ownership won’t be known until the deal is completed, probably in April.

Don't Miss
rewrite:
Eamon Quinn reports that Eir has informed its stakeholders that any significant updates regarding its strategic direction will be postponed until later this spring. This delay coincides with the anticipated finalization of an acquisition by new French investors.

Separately, the business organization Isme has strongly criticized the telecom operator's recent choice to withdraw from the state's National Broadband Plan, labeling the move catastrophic. Isme predicts this decision will push the rollout timeline to 2023 and has expressed deep concerns about the procurement procedures managed by the Department of Communications. The group alleges that Eir benefited by initially targeting easier, more profitable areas in its existing network deployment.

In the company's most recent quarterly update, departing CEO Richard Moat cited the intricate nature of the broadband contract and separate pricing concerns unrelated to the official plan as reasons for exiting the bidding process. For the quarter ending in December, Eir posted core earnings of €125 million, a 4% annual increase achieved through cost reductions, despite a 2% decline in revenue to €322 million. The company stated it remains on track to meet its annual profit goals, even after accounting for €3 million in expenses related to storm damage. Moat offered no further details on corporate strategy.

Eir, which has undergone more ownership changes than any other major European telecom, is in the process of being purchased by French businessman Xavier Niel through his holdings NJJ and Iliad. The deal, valued at approximately €1 billion, will give Niel a 64.5% controlling interest, while two U.S. hedge funds retain minority stakes. The firm carries a net debt burden of €2.16 billion.

According to Fitch Ratings analyst Damien Chew, Eir's recent financial performance largely matched projections. He noted that the full impact of the ownership transition will remain unclear until the transaction closes, likely in April.

GM Extends Summer Shutdown at Two Car Plants as Demand Falls
by Darryl Hood
General Motors is extending the normal two-week summer shutdown at two U.S. car factories because of slumping demand.
Union officials say the Lordstown, Ohio, plant near Cleveland and the Fairfax plant in Kansas City, Kansas, will close for as long as five weeks in June and July. The summer shutdown normally lasts two weeks.
Lordstown makes the Chevrolet Cruze compact while Fairfax builds the Chevrolet Malibu midsize car.
Cruze sales are up 36 percent due largely to fleet sales. Sales to individual buyers are down 3 percent. Malibu sales are down 30 percent through May.
Spokesman Jim Cain confirms that some car plants will see more down weeks but wouldn’t give specifics. He says GM is adjusting as the market shifts from cars to trucks and SUVs.
(Copyright 2017 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten or redistributed.)
rewrite:
General Motors is prolonging the typical summer pause at two American assembly facilities in response to declining consumer interest. According to union representatives, the locations in Lordstown, Ohio, and Fairfax, Kansas, will be idled for up to five weeks during June and July, far exceeding the usual two-week halt. The Lordstown factory produces the Chevrolet Cruze compact, and the Fairfax site manufactures the midsize Chevrolet Malibu.

While Cruze transactions have risen 36 percent, primarily driven by bulk fleet purchases, retail sales to individual customers have dipped 3 percent. Malibu sales have fallen 30 percent through May. Company spokesperson Jim Cain acknowledged that certain plants will experience additional idle periods, without providing details. He stated GM is adapting its operations as market preferences move away from passenger cars toward trucks and sport utility vehicles.

The selection of Brussels as a base fulfills key requirements by offering a stable regulatory environment in a central European hub. Such an agreement is vital to permit commerce to proceed under optimal terms after the formal exit. She expressed that achieving a mutually advantageous deal is critical not only for London's financial district but for Europe as a whole.

WACO, Texas (AP) -- Terry Maston scored a career-high 23 points and Baylor ended a four-game losing streak with an 81-67 victory over Iowa State on Saturday night.
The lead changed hands eight times before the Bears went on a 15-0 run over a 2:12 span early in the second half. Baylor had three 3-point plays during the spurt, including one that resulted in a five-point trip after Iowa State coach Steve Prohm was hit with a technical foul.
''We wanted to come out and you want to get the crowd going, and we wanted to get some momentum,'' Baylor coach Scott Drew said. ''We were able to get some separation and get the crowd into the game. That really helps, especially with the zone and different things like that, because now they're trying to score quicker and it's harder to score quicker against (the zone).''
Baylor (13-10, 3-7 Big 12 Conference) led 51-38 at that point and the Cyclones never got closer than eight the rest of the way.
''When we went into halftime they told us to be very aggressive and take the ball to the basket,'' said Maston, who was 9-of-11 shooting. ''I know I was shooting a couple of fadeaway jumpers, and they told me to get in there and basically force my will into the paint and get easy buckets. So that's what I did, and it ended up working out great.''
Manu Lecomte added 14 points for the Bears, who won despite shooting 2 for 14 from 3-point range. Baylor made up for that with a 43-35 edge in rebounds and 52-28 in points in the paint. The Bears shot 62 percent in the second half and 50 percent for the game.
Jo Lual-Acuil Jr. added 10 points and 14 rebounds for Baylor.
''I think it was just determination. We knew coming into the game we had to win,'' Lual-Acuil said. ''T.J. (Maston) did a great job playing with energy and we didn't want to leave here without a win.''
rewrite:
WACO, Texas (AP) -- Baylor snapped a four-game skid by defeating Iowa State 81-67 on Saturday, fueled by a career-best 23 points from Terry Maston. The contest saw eight lead changes before Baylor seized control with a decisive 15-0 surge early in the second half, a run lasting just over two minutes. That stretch featured three three-point plays for the Bears, one of which became a five-point opportunity following a technical foul called on Cyclones coach Steve Prohm.

Baylor coach Scott Drew emphasized the importance of energizing the home crowd. "Our aim was to start strong, build momentum, and get the fans involved," Drew said. "Creating that gap allowed the crowd to become a factor. That support is crucial, particularly when we use defensive schemes like the zone, as it pressures the opponent to hurry their offense, which is difficult against that setup."

After that run, Baylor (13-10, 3-7 in the Big 12) held a 51-38 advantage, and Iowa State could not narrow the deficit to fewer than eight points thereafter. Maston, who made 9 of 11 shot attempts, credited halftime instructions for his success. "At halftime, the coaches urged us to attack the basket aggressively," Maston said. "I had taken some fadeaway jumpers, but they told me to impose myself in the paint and finish at the rim. I followed that plan, and it paid off."

Manu Lecomte contributed 14 points for Baylor. The Bears overcame a poor 2-for-14 performance from beyond the arc by dominating rebounds 43-35 and outscoring Iowa State 52-28 in the paint. Baylor shot 62 percent after halftime and 50 percent overall. Jo Lual-Acuil Jr. posted a double-double with 10 points and 14 rebounds.

Lual-Acuil pointed to the team's resolve as the key. "It came down to sheer determination. We entered this game knowing we needed a victory," he said. "T.J. (Maston) brought tremendous energy, and we were all committed to leaving with a win."

SAN FRANCISCO — Tesla dropped a standard new-car braking test it saw as unnecessary as it pushed to make an elusive production target for its Model 3 sedans last week.
The so-called "brake and roll" test was halted early on June 26, according to Business Insider.
"I can't even figure out a good reason to ever bypass this," Dave Sullivan, manager of product analysis for AutoPacific, said in an email to USA Today. "For a company that is under such immense scrutiny for safety, there is zero reason to bypass anything related to brakes now."
Tesla, based south of San Francisco in Palo Alto, Calif., has faced scrutiny for a series of accidents involving its Autopilot system, which handles some of the driving chores but requires driver oversight.
Tesla spokesperson Dave Arnold said that the test was redundant because the company drives every Model 3 on its test track, where it checks brakes, alignment and other aspects of the car that would impact its overall safety.
"Every car we build goes through rigorous quality checks and must meet exacting specifications, including brake tests," Arnold said in a statement. "There are no exceptions."
Investors were buoyed by the news earlier in the week that CEO Elon Musk had hit his long-promised output of 5,000 Model E's — the $35,000-and-up Model 3 is considered critical to the company's financial success — by Musk's second quarter deadline. But some analysts warned that the level, which included Tesla setting up a tent for additional production, wasn't sustainable.
CFRA Research downgraded Tesla stock to "sell."
In a note Tuesday, GBH Insights analyst Daniel Ives called the "brake and roll" news "a potential gut punch to the bulls that now worry about sustainability and speed bumps ahead on the Model 3 front."
Ives still rates the stock a buy with a $375 target due largely to the recent positive news about Model 3. But, he said, "the knee jerk reaction from the Street's perspective is clearly a concern that neutralizes some of the long awaited good news from reaching the key 5,000 per week goal."
rewrite:
In San Francisco, Tesla eliminated a routine brake inspection for new vehicles, deeming it superfluous, during its drive to achieve a challenging production milestone for its Model 3 sedans last week.

Business Insider reported that this "brake and roll" assessment was discontinued on June 26. Dave Sullivan, AutoPacific's product analysis manager, expressed strong concern in correspondence with USA Today, stating he could not identify any valid justification for omitting such a procedure. He emphasized that for a company already facing intense safety examination, bypassing any brake-related check is indefensible.

The Palo Alto-based automaker has been under watch due to multiple incidents involving its Autopilot feature, a system that assists with driving but still necessitates active driver supervision.

Tesla representative Dave Arnold defended the move, explaining the test was duplicative. He noted that each Model 3 undergoes evaluation on the company's test track, where braking, wheel alignment, and other safety-critical systems are verified. Arnold affirmed that all vehicles are subject to strict quality controls and must satisfy precise standards, with brake inspections being a mandatory part of the process.

Earlier in the week, investors were encouraged by CEO Elon Musk's announcement that the company had finally met its pledged output of 5,000 Model 3 units by the end of the second quarter. This affordable model is seen as vital for Tesla's economic viability. However, several observers cautioned that this output level, achieved partly by erecting a temporary assembly tent, may not be maintainable. Following the developments, CFRA Research lowered its rating on Tesla's shares to "sell."

Daniel Ives, an analyst at GBH Insights, described the brake test news as a significant setback for optimistic investors, who are now apprehensive about production stability and future obstacles for the Model 3. While Ives maintains a "buy" rating with a $375 price target, largely due to the recent production achievement, he acknowledged that the immediate market reaction reflects worry, which dampens the positive impact of reaching the long-sought weekly production goal.

It’s been seven years since Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore ended their marriage — and by default — broke up their landmark noise rock band Sonic Youth. The dissolution of alt rock’s only surviving power couple came as a blow to anyone who thought there was something special about the healing and sustaining power of experimental noise rock. Now, as if to underline and punctuate the finality of the break, former drummer Steve Shelley is selling off some of the band’s effects pedals on eBay.
Sonic Youth was known for anarchic, dissonant soundscapes and their heavy reliance on particular effects pedals and customized instruments in order to achieve their aesthetic. They famously had to cancel a tour once after their custom gear had been stolen because it was impossible to re-create their sound live with factory instruments. Clearly, these pedals represent more than your usual stompbox. And by all indications, the band is on board with this sale. Their still active official twitter account actually tweeted out a link to the sale. So it’s safe to assume this sale is sanctioned by the band or at least whoever runs their social.
You can peruse the items and bid on them for yourself over on eBay, but bear in mind that they come with a disclaimer on the listings themselves:
“It cannot be said with certainty when or by whom each particular pedal was used.”
There are currently only four items up and the prices are already in the hundreds of dollars. Expect to pay a high price for an authentic lo-fi sound.
rewrite:
Seven years have passed since the marriage between Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore dissolved, leading inevitably to the disbandment of their influential noise rock group, Sonic Youth. For fans who believed in the unique, restorative force of avant-garde rock music, the split of alternative rock's last enduring artistic partnership felt like a significant loss. As if to emphasize the permanence of this separation, ex-drummer Steve Shelley is currently auctioning several of the group's guitar pedals via eBay.

The band was celebrated for crafting chaotic and discordant audio textures, relying extensively on specific effects pedals and modified equipment to realize their distinctive style. On one notable occasion, they were forced to abandon a tour after their customized gear was stolen, as standard instruments could not replicate their live sonic experience. These devices are evidently far more than ordinary foot pedals. All signs suggest the group approves of this auction; their still-operational official Twitter account shared a link to the sale, indicating it is likely authorized by the band or its representatives.

Interested buyers can browse and bid on the listings, though a note attached to them offers a caveat: “It cannot be confirmed exactly when or by which musician each individual pedal was employed.” Only four items are currently available, with bids already reaching several hundred dollars. Acquiring one of these pedals will likely require a substantial investment for those seeking a genuine piece of the band’s raw, experimental sound.

input: Clouds have been stubborn lately across south Florida and the region. On Monday they persisted much of the day although only a few favored locations actually received rain from them. The wettest, by far, was the Lower and Middle Florida Keys. Looking ahead, brief rain showers will remain possible as we tap into some moisture off the ocean. High pressure is at the heart of our weather pattern. It’s anchored south of Bermuda in the western Atlantic (and likely to stay stationary into the middle of the week). For us, that means a continued onshore flow with comfortable temperatures and a nice breeze. Later in the week, the high should weaken further and ease southward. Local winds, in turn, will probably start veering more out of the south by the upcoming weekend. Expect a rise in temperature, into the middle 80’s with higher levels of humidity. Early next week looks a bit more interesting, by the way. Long range forecast maps show a cold front crossing the Gulf of Mexico and moving our way by late Sunday or Monday. Rain and thunderstorm chances will likely increase ahead of the boundary… if the front holds together. Right now, it’s too far off to say with any confidence (and fronts this time of the year can be especially weak, if not fickle).
rewrite:
South Florida has experienced persistent cloud cover recently. While Monday saw overcast skies for most of the day, rainfall was limited to only a few specific areas. The Lower and Middle Florida Keys recorded the most significant precipitation by a wide margin. In the near term, passing showers remain a possibility as some oceanic moisture drifts inland. Our current conditions are dominated by a high-pressure system situated south of Bermuda in the western Atlantic, which is expected to remain fixed through midweek. This setup maintains a pleasant onshore breeze and mild temperatures.

Later, this high will likely diminish and shift southward. Consequently, local winds are forecast to become more southerly by the weekend, bringing warmer conditions with highs reaching the mid-80s and increased humidity. The outlook for early next week appears more dynamic. Extended models indicate a cold front may traverse the Gulf of Mexico, approaching our region by Sunday night or Monday. This could elevate the potential for rain and thunderstorms ahead of its arrival, provided the front remains intact. However, given the considerable lead time and the typically unstable nature of frontal systems during this season, confidence in this scenario remains low.

Chris Christie chowed down with President Trump at the White House Tuesday amid speculation that the New Jersey governor might join the administration as it grapples with growing pains.
Christie and wife Mary Pat had a Valentine’s Day’s lunch with the commander in chief the day after Trump ousted his national security adviser, Michael Flynn, and amid chatter among Trump allies that more shakeups are coming.
A source close to Christie told The Post that possible ­administration positions were discussed.
“I heard it was about chief of staff,” the source said.
But the White House said the conversation was about curbing opioid abuse, a major priority for the governor, and the chief-of-staff issue “didn’t even come up.”
“They talked about combating drugs briefly,” White House Press Secretary Sean Spicer told The Post.
Spicer pushed back on speculation that Christie would be drafted to beef up the White house staff.
“I think Governor Christie said he has a year left of his administration and he intends to fully serve it out,” Spicer said.
“So we’re not discussing one month in what we intend to do in a year and a half. Let’s get there first.”
Christie, an early and effective surrogate for Trump during the election race, was previously passed up for vice president and was also replaced by VP Mike Pence to head up the White House transition team.
But Christie remained a loyal friend to Trump and blamed early White House problems, such as the botched immigration executive-order rollout, on staff that ­“ill-served” the president.
Christie’s office didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
The closed-door meeting occurred as Trump allies were openly questioning Reince Priebus’ ability to serve as chief of staff.
The public complaints started Sunday when Christopher Ruddy, CEO of Newsmax Media, said Priebus was “in way over his head” and should be canned. Ruddy later softened his tone after talking with Priebus and reported that the White House has full confidence in the chief of staff.
rewrite:
Amid ongoing discussions about potential changes within the administration, New Jersey Governor Chris Christie and his wife dined with President Trump at the White House on Valentine's Day. This private lunch took place shortly after the dismissal of National Security Advisor Michael Flynn and as rumors circulated about further possible staff reorganizations.

An individual familiar with Christie's situation mentioned to The Post that roles within the administration were considered during the meeting, specifically noting the chief of staff position as a topic. However, White House Press Secretary Sean Spicer offered a different account, stating the discussion centered on addressing opioid addiction—a key issue for Christie—and that the chief of staff subject was not raised. Spicer further downplayed the idea of Christie joining the White House staff, referencing the governor's commitment to completing his final year in office.

Christie, who was a prominent supporter of Trump's campaign, was not selected as the vice presidential candidate and was later succeeded by Vice President Mike Pence in leading the transition team. Despite this, he has maintained his allegiance to the President, attributing early missteps, like the troubled implementation of the immigration order, to advisors who did not perform adequately.

The gathering happened concurrently with public doubts from some Trump supporters regarding Chief of Staff Reince Priebus's performance. Criticism emerged publicly when Newsmax Media's Christopher Ruddy commented that Priebus was unqualified and should be replaced, though he later revised his stance after conversations with Priebus, affirming the White House's support for him. Christie's representatives did not provide an immediate comment on the meeting.

Apple likes to add new features and data points into Maps, the latest of which is the addition of bike sharing data for more than 175 cities across 36 countries.
You can search for the specific bike share system in your city in the search field in Apple Maps, search for “bike sharing”, or ask Siri.
Apple has partnered with Ito World to provide the bike data; this is the first bike-sharing dataset provided as a single feed.
The schemes have a total of more than 12,810 "points of interest", each one a place where you can pick up or drop off a cycle.
Cities and services added in the UK are:
Bath (nextbike Bath)
Belfast (Coca-Cola Zero Belfast Bikes)
Exeter (co bikes)
Glasgow (nextbike Glasgow)
London (Santander Cycles/Boris Bikes)
Milton Keynes (Santander Cycles MK)
Stirling (nextbike Stirling)
University of Warwick (UniCycles)
Apple’s original woes with Apple Maps are well documented, but the company has improved the app phenomenally over the last few years, adding in much more accurate detail.
Public transport information continues to be extended as well, while lane guidance for navigation has also recently launched in Canada, Australia, Switzerland, Austria, South Africa and Poland.
Apple Maps recently added more than 30 detailed indoor airport maps for major international airports including London Heathrow, JFK, LaGuardia, LAX, Hong Kong International, Chicago O’Hare, Amsterdam, Schiphol, Geneva, Toronto Pearson, and the remarkably-still-open Berlin Tegel.
Check out Indoor Maps for Apple Maps: What are they and how can you use them?
rewrite:

The underlying data is supplied through a collaboration with Ito World, marking the first instance such bike-sharing information is delivered as a unified stream. This system encompasses more than 12,810 distinct stations, each designated as a location where bicycles can be rented or returned.

In the United Kingdom, the newly included cities and their respective services are: Bath (nextbike Bath), Belfast (Coca-Cola Zero Belfast Bikes), Exeter (co bikes), Glasgow (nextbike Glasgow), London (Santander Cycles), Milton Keynes (Santander Cycles MK), Stirling (nextbike Stirling), and the University of Warwick (UniCycles).

While Apple Maps faced significant initial challenges and criticism, the application has seen substantial improvements in recent years, achieving far greater precision and detail. The service is also broadening its public transit directions. Additionally, features like lane guidance for drivers have recently become active in several countries, including Canada, Australia, Switzerland, Austria, South Africa, and Poland.

Furthermore, the app now provides detailed interior layouts for more than 30 major international airports. These include terminals at London Heathrow, New York's JFK and LaGuardia, Los Angeles International, Hong Kong International, Chicago O’Hare, Amsterdam Schiphol, Geneva, Toronto Pearson, and Berlin Tegel. (CBS Local) – Gun owners around the country are blowing up expensive coolers after the NRA accused outdoor lifestyle company Yeti of joining a nationwide boycott of the gun-rights organization.
According to a letter from Marion P. Hammer of the NRA’s Institute for Legislative Action, Yeti has cut ties with the NRA and is refusing to do business with the NRA Foundation or offer discounts to members. “YETI should be ashamed. They have declined to continue helping America’s young people enjoy outdoor recreational activities,” Hammer claims in the April 20 statement.
In response to the news, NRA members and supporters have begun taking their frustrations out on the company’s hottest item: outdoor coolers. In a number of online videos boycotting Yeti, gun owners are seen destroying the expensive containers by loading them with explosives and shooting them. “This Yeti ain’t ready,” South Carolina resident Bryan Atkinson declared before obliterating his cooler.
The pricey coolers reportedly cost anywhere between $250 and $1,300; making a discount on Yeti camping and hunting gear very helpful to consumers. “If Yeti can’t stand behind the NRA, I ain’t standing behind Yeti no more,” Atkinson added in a Facebook post.
Yeti is disputing the NRA’s claims that they’ve joined a boycott against pro-gun Americans. “Yeti notified the NRA Foundation, as well as a number of other organizations, that we were eliminating a group of outdated discounting programs,” the company wrote in a statement posted to Facebook. The outdoor lifestyle supplier added that they’re offering business partners like the NRA alternative programs and called claims that Yeti was turning their backs on young gun owners untrue.
Several organizations including airlines and rental car companies have cut ties with the National Rifle Association in the wake of the deadly Parkland, Florida school shooting which killed 17 people in February. Since the shooting, many Americans have lashed out at the NRA for their stance on assault rifles and lobbying efforts against tighter gun laws.
Although Yeti says that their policy change on discounts is not related to the boycott, the decision was made less than two months after groups began to cut ties with the pro-gun group. Bank of America joined the movement in mid-April when the company announced that it would no longer lend money to companies which produce assault-style weapons for civilians.

In a letter from the NRA’s legislative arm, representative Marion P. Hammer stated that Yeti has discontinued its association with the organization and will no longer provide discounts to its members or conduct business with the NRA Foundation. Hammer’s statement criticized the company, asserting, “YETI should be ashamed. They have declined to continue helping America’s young people enjoy outdoor recreational activities.”

This announcement has prompted a retaliatory boycott from NRA supporters, who are targeting Yeti’s popular coolers. Numerous videos circulating online show individuals using firearms and explosives to demolish the costly containers. For instance, Bank of America recently declared it would cease financing manufacturers of military-style firearms for civilian use.

Sleaford First XI came agonisingly close to winning at second-placed Grantham on Saturday, eventually losing the Lincs ECB Premier League fixture by just a single run.
Grantham batted first after winning the toss but after a solid start, some determined bowling saw the innings interestingly poised at 126-5 with Andrew Jones and Adi Sreedharan each claiming two victims.
Home captain Daniel Webb helped his side post a competitive total, supervising the rest of the innings with an important knock of 66 to take the hosts to 224 from their allotted overs.
At 90-4 in Sleaford’s reply the game was in the balance, but a stand between Andy Hibberd and Shaun Morris swung the game in favour of the visitors who took themselves to within 18 runs of victory with five wickets in hand.
But Sleaford finished just short of the target despite Hibberd’s contribution of 93.
* In the South Lincs and Border League Premier, Sleaford Seconds took maximum points against Frieston to stay top.
Batting first, Sleaford posted 201-7 with Charlie Roberts (67) the principal contributor. The visitors never threatened in reply and were all out for 74, with spinners Angus Youles, Sumit Puri and Ben Hutson claiming eight wickets between them.
Sunday’s game for Sleaford Academy, sponsored by Turnbulls, brought a comprehensive 10-wicket win against Boston who were dismissed for only 39.
* Sleaford Firsts, sponsored by Baker Plant Hire, host Market Deeping on Saturday, while on Sunday, Revesby visit London Road in the Lincoln Sunday League Premier. Matchball sponsor is Michael Shaw.

The Obama administration policy protecting the children of undocumented immigrants who were brought to the United States in their youth may face its first test under the Trump administration when Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents arrested a Mexican migrant in Washington state last week.
The arrest of Daniel Ramirez, 23, first reported by Reuters Tuesday evening, is possibly the first of an immigrant protected by the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program during the presidency of Donald Trump.
Trump campaigned on the progress to halt undocumented immigration, particularly from Mexico, and to roll back Obama-era programs that provide amnesty to immigrants already living in the country.
ICE said in a statement Ramirez is a "self-admitted gang member" arrested on Feb. 10 "during an operation targeting a prior-deported felon."
"ICE officers took Mr. Ramirez into custody based on his admitted gang affiliation and risk to public safety," the statement said.
According to the government, gang membership can be an indicator that an immigrant poses a public safety threat.
Ramirez's attorney, Theodore Boutrous Jr., said: “The government offered no explanation of why Mr. Ramirez was initially taken into custody and why he is still being held" and said his client "had documentation that clearly indicated he had DACA( Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals) status, allowing him to live and work in the United States."
rewrite:
A key immigration policy from the Obama era, which shields certain undocumented immigrants who arrived in the U.S. as minors, could encounter an early challenge under the new presidential administration. This follows the detention of a young Mexican man in Washington state by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers last week.

The case involves 23-year-old Daniel Ramirez, whose apprehension might represent the first instance of an individual protected under the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program being taken into custody since Donald Trump assumed office. During his campaign, President Trump pledged to curb illegal immigration, with a focus on arrivals from Mexico, and to dismantle earlier initiatives that offered protection to undocumented immigrants residing in the nation.

ICE asserted in a release that Ramirez was detained on February 10th during an action focused on a felon who had been previously deported. The agency labeled him a "self-admitted gang member," stating the arrest was due to this admitted affiliation and the associated potential danger to community safety. Federal guidelines note that gang ties can signal a public safety risk from an immigrant.

Ramirez's legal representative, Theodore Boutrous Jr., countered that authorities have provided no justification for his client's initial arrest or continued detention. He emphasized that Ramirez possessed official proof of his active DACA status, which grants him permission to reside and be employed in the United States.

Leeds United head coach Garry Monk has revealed that he always expected a goalkeeper of Rob Green’s quality to pull off important saves last night against Bristol City.
Chris Wood and Pablo Hernandez scored on either side of the break to provide a solid two goal cushion to Leeds at Elland Road and while Bristol City did pull one back in the sixth minute of stoppage time, it was nothing more than a consolation goal.
However, Leeds were under pressure after the break despite being two goals ahead and Green had to make some smart saves to keep the away side at bay in the second half.
There was an argument that the goalkeeper could have been rewarded with the Man of the Match accolade, but Monk feels the saves Green made were regulation for a goalkeeper of his quality.
Asked if Green could have deserved the Man of the Match award, the Leeds boss told BBC Radio Leeds: “I guess so, in terms of the actual saves that he made.
“But I think they are saves you expect Green, of his quality, to make them; it was important.”
Leeds remain in fifth in the league table on 57 points, six clear of seventh placed Norwich City at the moment.

Although Bristol City managed a late goal deep into added time, it served merely as a minor consolation.

Despite the lead, Leeds faced sustained pressure in the second period, requiring Green to produce several sharp interventions to preserve their advantage. Some observers believed the goalkeeper's performance warranted the Man of the Match honor, but Monk considered the stops to be standard for a player of Green's ability. When questioned if Green deserved the award, Monk responded to BBC Radio Leeds that while the saves were significant, they were precisely what is expected from a goalkeeper of his quality.

With this result, Leeds maintains its fifth-place standing in the league, accumulating 57 points and currently holding a six-point buffer over Norwich City in seventh.

Since 2013, I have primarily covered the Anoka-Hennepin and Spring Lake Park school districts as well as the city of Spring Lake Park for ABC Newspapers.
Both women charged in the assault of a 15-year-old St. Francis girl this summer were ordered to write her an apology letter and pay restitution.
In August, the women were arrested after allegedly hitting and kicking 15-year-old Sydney DeTenancour and cutting off some of her hair in a wooded area near The Ponds Golf Course in St. Francis June 17.
A video of the attack has been viewed on Facebook more than 500,000 times.
Cassandra Teal Borden, 19, of Cedar, hit and kicked the victim nearly 50 times. She was convicted of fifth-degree misdemeanor assault Nov. 14, and as part of a plea agreement, she had a fourth-degree property damage misdemeanor charge for allegedly breaking the victim’s cellphone dismissed at sentencing.
Alexis Sue Nelson, 20, of Zimmerman, was also charged with fifth-degree misdemeanor assault after allegedly cutting off several inches of the victim’s hair.
Nelson received a stay of adjudication Dec. 19. The case will be dismissed after one year if she completes conditions set forth by the judge, including writing a letter of apology to DeTenancour, taking medications as directed, continuing counseling with a psychiatrist, paying $80 in restitution and more.
At sentencing last month, Borden was also ordered to write a letter of apology. She had a 90-day jail sentence stayed for one year during which time she will be on probation. In addition, Borden was ordered to pay $669 in restitution, attend anger management, complete 40 hours of community service and earn her GED certificate.

The incident occurred in mid-June near The Ponds Golf Course in St. Francis, where the teenager, Sydney DeTenancour, was reportedly beaten and had a portion of her hair cut off. Following their arrest in August, footage of the altercation circulated widely on social media, accumulating over half a million views.

Cassandra Teal Borden, a 19-year-old from Cedar, was found guilty of a misdemeanor assault charge in mid-November for striking the girl approximately fifty times. As part of a negotiated plea, a separate property damage charge related to the victim’s broken cellphone was dropped at her sentencing. The court required her to write an apology, imposed a suspended 90-day jail term with a year of probation, and ordered her to pay $669, complete anger management classes, perform 40 hours of community service, and obtain a GED.

Alexis Sue Nelson, 20, of Zimmerman, faced a similar assault charge for cutting the victim’s hair. In late December, she was granted a stay of adjudication; her case will be closed after one year provided she meets judicial requirements. These include writing an apology, following prescribed medications, continuing psychiatric counseling, and paying $80 in restitution.

"The king represents the whole nation and they are insulting the king, which is like they are insulting the whole nation," spokesman for the country's Ministry of Interior General Khieu Sopheak said as he confirmed an investigation had been launched.
"We have got orders to arrest them," he said. "If we don't take action against them, more people might follow their act," he explained, according to AFP.
The offending image of King Norodom Sihamoni, 63, was first shared on social media accounts December 25. It was captioned "Cambodian king is gay," the BBC reports.
While in neighboring Thailand, even sharing such an image could lead to arrest, Cambodia is much more relaxed when it comes to discussing its monarchy. But it seems there are some lines that mustn't be crossed.
Cambodia's police plan to arrest the three suspects, one of whom they believe to be in Thailand, Sopheak said. Cambodia may ask Thailand for assistance in tracking down the rogue Photoshopper.
AFP observes that Sihamoni, who took the throne somewhat reluctantly in 2004 after the abdication of his father, fulfills the symbolic role of head of state but stays well away from domestic politics. Sihamoni, who speaks several langauges, spent much of his adult life overseas, where he worked in the arts, even establishing his own ballet company. The king is unmarried and has no children.
Legal expert Sok Sam Oeun told the Phnom Penh Post that while Article 502 of Cambodia's criminal code provides for the punishment of those who insult civil servants and public elected officials, there is no such protection for the king.
"If there's no punishment in the law, we cannot punish anybody," he said. "Legally, we cannot extend the definition [to include] another crime. The law should be clear."
Cambodia's constitution describes the king as "inviolable."
rewrite:
A spokesperson for Cambodia's Interior Ministry, General Khieu Sopheak, stated that an inquiry is now underway regarding an incident perceived as an affront to the monarch. He conveyed that disrespecting the king equates to disrespecting the entire country. The general confirmed instructions to detain the individuals responsible, warning that failure to act could encourage others to imitate the behavior, as reported by AFP.

The contentious post, which labeled the 63-year-old King Norodom Sihamoni as homosexual, initially appeared on social media on December 25, according to the BBC. Compared to the strict laws of neighboring Thailand, where similar content could result in detention, Cambodia typically allows more open discourse about the royal family. However, certain boundaries are still deemed unacceptable to breach.

Authorities intend to apprehend three people linked to the case, with one suspect thought to be residing in Thailand. General Sopheak indicated that Cambodian officials might seek cooperation from Thailand to locate this individual. AFP notes that King Sihamoni assumed the throne in 2004 following his father's stepping down, though he was not eager for the position. He serves as a ceremonial head of state and deliberately avoids involvement in political matters. Fluent in multiple languages, Sihamoni lived abroad for many years, dedicating himself to artistic pursuits, including founding a ballet company. The king is not married and has no heirs.

Legal analyst Sok Sam Oeun informed the Phnom Penh Post that Cambodia's criminal code, under Article 502, outlines penalties for insulting government officials and elected representatives, but does not explicitly shield the king from such offenses. He emphasized that without a specific legal provision, no one can be prosecuted, arguing that legal definitions cannot be arbitrarily broadened and that statutes must be precise. The Cambodian constitution refers to the king as a figure who is "inviolable."

The Brooklyn woman who allegedly started a massive blaze that killed two people in Dyker Heights has been indicted on two counts of second-degree murder and two of first-degree arson.
see also Angry tenant sparked fatal fire by torching trash in hallway A Brooklyn woman was so angry that garbage was piling...
Joanna Mei, 22, was ordered held without bail after pleading not guilty Monday to setting a fire in a trash can Nov. 9 in a first-floor staircase of the apartment building where she lived.
She appeared emotionless in Kings County Supreme Court and made no statement.
“The alleged actions of this defendant displayed a complete and callous disregard for human life, and caused two tragic but avoidable deaths,” said Acting Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez “We will now seek justice for the victims and their loved ones for the heartbreaking loss that they suffered.”
Mei allegedly told police she lit the fire because she was angry that trash had been piling up in the hallways, sources said. The fire turned into an inferno that killed a couple on the third floor, Xi Huang, 58, and his wife, Feng Xu, 56.
Mei’s next court date is Feb. 6, 2018. She faces a maximum sentence of 25 years to life in prison.
rewrite:

The woman, identified as 22-year-old Joanna Mei, entered a plea of not guilty on Monday and was subsequently detained without the possibility of bail. Prosecutors allege that on November 9th, she intentionally ignited refuse within a first-floor stairwell of her apartment building. According to sources, she confessed to authorities that this act was motivated by frustration over accumulated garbage in the hallways.

The resulting blaze escalated rapidly, claiming the lives of a married couple residing on the third floor, 58-year-old Xi Huang and 56-year-old Feng Xu. In a Kings County Supreme Court appearance described as devoid of emotion, Mei offered no verbal statement. Acting Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez stated that the accused's purported conduct demonstrated a profound and reckless indifference toward others, directly causing two needless fatalities. He affirmed the office's commitment to pursuing justice for the victims and their grieving families. Joanna Mei is scheduled to return to court on February 6, 2018, and could receive a prison term ranging from 25 years to life if convicted.

CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — Want the world’s best, up-close view of a rocket launch without being right there at the pad?
For the first time, cameras will provide live 360-degree video of a rocket heading toward space.
NASA will provide the 360 stream Tuesday as an unmanned Atlas rocket blasts off from Cape Canaveral, Florida, with a capsule full of space station supplies. The stream will begin 10 minutes before the scheduled 11:11 a.m. liftoff and continue until the rocket is out of sight.
The four fisheye-lens cameras are located at the pad, about 300 feet (100 meters) from the rocket. A computer in a blast-proof box will stitch together the images for a full, in-the-round view. There will be about a minute lag time.
It will be shown on NASA’s YouTube channel.

ROME (Reuters) - Alessandro Zanni will win his 100th cap for Italy on Sunday after being drafted into the team following a two-year absence for their Six Nations opener against England in Rome.
The 34-year-old, who was named at lock, last played against Wales in the Six Nations in March 2016 and has been out injured for much of the time since. He has spent most of his career as a loose forward.
He is among seven changes in the team named by coach Conor O’Shea on Friday from their 35-6 defeat to South Africa in Padua last November.
Tommaso Allan returns at flyhalf after injury kept him out of the last three internationals against Fiji, Argentina and the Springboks and there are starting berths for veterans Tommaso Benvenuti at wing and hooker Leonardo Ghiraldini.
Sunday’s team includes seven players who will be making their first Six Nations appearance, including Matteo Minozzi at fullback, the centre pairing of Tommaso Boni and Tommaso Castello, youthful flankers Renato Giammarioli and Sebastian Negri, New Zealand-born lock Dean Budd and Simone Ferrari in the front row.
Six Nations title holders England have won all 23 of their previous meetings with Italy, averaging 40 points a game.
They had something of a scare at Twickenham last year, however, when they struggled to deal with the Italians’ surprise “no ruck” tactics before coming from behind at halftime to emerge 36-15 winners.
Italy have finished last and picked up the “wooden spoon” 12 times in the 18 years since the tournament was expanded to become the Six Nations.

PITTSBURGH (AP) - The Pittsburgh Steelers have signed inside linebacker Jon Bostic to a two-year contract.
Details of the deal were not disclosed and it will not be finalized until after Bostic undergoes a physical on Monday.
The 26-year-old Bostic played 14 games for Indianapolis last season, getting 97 tackles and one sack. Bostic injured his right knee against Denver in December and finished the season on injured reserve. Pittsburgh is Bostic's fifth stop.
Bostic began his career with Chicago after being taken in the second round of the 2013 draft. He played two seasons in Chicago then one in New England before the Patriots traded him to Detroit in 2016. He missed the entire season in Detroit with a foot injury before joining the Colts.
The Steelers are in need of depth at inside linebacker with Ryan Shazier already ruled out for 2018 because of a spinal injury suffered in Cincinnati in December.

Jessa Duggar Seewald and husband Ben show off their second son, Henry, just days after his birth and talk about their plan for more children. Subscribe now for this Duggar exclusive – only in PEOPLE!
Although the Seewalds are still learning to juggle parenting their newborn son and 15-month-old toddler, their hearts are wide open to welcoming more children in the future.
“I take one. He takes the other,” Jessa (Duggar) Seewald, 24, says in this week’s issue of PEOPLE of her co-parenting strategy with husband Ben Seewald.
“Right now we have two kids and there’s two of us, so it’s man-to-man coverage,” adds Ben. “When we have more, we’ll have to switch it up to a zone defense!”
Just over a week ago, the couple exclusively told PEOPLE that they welcomed their second son — Henry Wilberforce — on Feb. 6, revealing that he was born at 4:26 a.m., weighing 8 lbs. and 11 oz. and measuring 21¾ in. long.
While the couple, who wed on Nov. 1, 2014, may be busy at home with their two little boys — Spurgeon Elliot, 1, and 1-week-old Henry Wilberforce — they are excited about the possibility of growing their brood.
“It will be a little while since we just had a baby, but adopting and fostering to adopt is very much in our hearts,” Jessa says.
For much more about the Seewalds’ new world as a family of four, pick up this week’s issue of PEOPLE, on newsstands Friday
Though the Counting On star — the fourth of 19 children born to Jim Bob and Michelle Duggar — is excited about the possibility of more little footsteps in her Arkansas home, there’s one thing she and her husband need more of before their family grows — square footage!
“We just need a little more space,” Jessa says with a laugh. “We’re always checking the market!”
With plans to expand her own family, Jessa — who comes from a megafamily herself — credits her mother, Michelle, for teaching her an invaluable lesson that she now implements into her home: the power love.
“My mom always says, ‘Love doesn’t divide, it multiplies,’ ” Jessa tells PEOPLE. “It’s so true.”
Counting On airs Mondays (9 p.m. ET) on TLC.
—With NATALIE STONE

A rapist who fled the UK has been jailed after he walked into a Birmingham police station.
Jabar Ababakr, of no fixed address, entered the station in Sutton Coldfield in February and said he been in Iraq visiting his dying mother.
The 33-year-old left the country after he raped a woman in Burton-upon-Trent in 2014.

INDIANAPOLIS (AP) - The NCAA's playing rules oversight panel will give college basketball coaches more room to roam next season after approving an extension of the coaches' boxes from 28 to 38 feet.
Other men's basketball rules changes include finding more consistent spots for inbound passes.
The shot clock will be reset to 20 seconds when the offensive team draws a foul in the frontcourt. If more than 20 seconds remain there will be no change.
Referees can use instant replay in the final two minutes of the game or overtime to determine whether a secondary defender was inside or outside the restricted-arc area.
A legal screen will require players to keep their feet no wider than their shoulders. And a minimum of 0.3 seconds will be taken off the game clock when the ball is legally touched.
Defenders who straddle an offensive player's leg and prohibit him from making a normal basketball move, including pivoting, will be assessed a personal foul.
Women's basketball rule changes included moving the restricted-area arc in the lane to 4 feet. The arc previously had been 3 feet in front of the basket. A secondary defender must be outside the arc and in legal guarding position to draw a charge.
Also in women's basketball, coaches will be allowed to carry over all timeouts to the second half rather than having one "use it or lose it" first-half timeout. The 10-second backcourt count won't be reset when a women's basketball team on offense calls time out. Women's basketball also approved the same rule change the men adopted in extending the coaches' boxes from 28 feet to 38 feet.
Women's basketball officials also will be allowed to use replay to determine if the ball was released on made baskets before the shot clock expired.

rewrite:
The NCAA's rules oversight committee has sanctioned several adjustments for the upcoming college basketball season. A key modification grants coaches expanded sideline movement, widening the designated coaching area from 28 to 38 feet. Additional men's game alterations involve standardizing locations for throwing the ball in from out of bounds.

Specific timing rules have been adjusted. When the offensive team is fouled in its frontcourt, the shot clock will now revert to 20 seconds, but only if fewer than 20 seconds were remaining. Otherwise, the clock continues from its current time. In the last two minutes of regulation or during overtime, officials may consult video review to judge a secondary defender's position relative to the restricted arc under the basket.

Regulations concerning player contact have also been clarified. Setting a legal screen now necessitates that a player's feet remain within the width of their shoulders. Furthermore, a defender who places a leg between an opponent's legs, hindering a standard move like a pivot, will be called for a personal foul. A minimum of three-tenths of a second will also be deducted from the game clock whenever the ball is legally contacted.

For women's basketball, the restricted arc has been moved to four feet from the basket, extending it from the previous three-foot distance. A secondary defender must now be outside this arc and properly positioned to legally draw an offensive charge. Timeout rules are revised, permitting coaches to retain all unused first-half timeouts for the second half, eliminating a previously forfeited timeout. Calling a timeout will no longer reset the 10-second count to advance the ball past midcourt. The women's game will also adopt the same expanded coaches' box as the men. Officials may also employ replay to verify whether a successful shot was released before the expiration of the shot clock.

There are plenty of stories about artificial intelligence ending the world as we know it (see 2001: A Space Odyssey, The Terminator, certain Elon Musk tweets). There are fewer about how AI could save the world, but believers are out there. At a gathering Monday for the two-year anniversary of the Paris climate accord, Microsoft announced a $50 million investment in its AI for Earth project that it believes can be a “game-changer for our planet.”
Microsoft launched AI for Earth over the summer with an initial $2 million, hiring Lucas Joppa to run it as the company’s chief environmental scientist—a role that, as far as Joppa knows, doesn’t exist at any other technology company. Since the launch, the company has given out 35 grants to groups in 10 countries. The new investment will support and expand upon the current projects as well as new ventures over the next five years.
“We’re impatient and a lot of partners are too,” Joppa told MIT Technology Review. “There isn’t enough money and resources for people doubling down on these issues.”
AI for Earth grants give groups access and training to use the Azure platform and other Microsoft AI products. The projects so far include producing a more precise land cover map of the Chesapeake Bay watershed for conservation work, a mosquito tracking program that lets researchers learn about wildlife populations through blood analysis (it also functions as an early-warning system for Zika outbreaks), and getting farmers more data to increase crop yields with fewer resources.
AI for Earth is, of course, good for Microsoft’s bottom line as well. Joppa said that if the technology works for small, cash-strapped groups often working in tough conditions in the field, Microsoft gets feedback for their products and clients can be assured that the system will work for them.
“Anytime we can stress-test the technology, the better,” he said.
And of course, AI talent retention and recruiting is a huge concern for the tech industry. Joppa said that AI for Earth and its mission are a draw for researchers and developers.
“Yes, you need to pay them,” he said. “But you need to give them meaningful things to work on.”
rewrite:
While many narratives imagine artificial intelligence leading to global catastrophe—a theme echoed in films like *2001: A Space Odyssey* and *The Terminator*, as well as in various social media pronouncements—there is a less prominent yet equally passionate perspective that AI could rescue our planet. Advocates for this view found a platform during a recent event marking the Paris climate agreement's second anniversary, where Microsoft revealed a substantial $50 million commitment to its AI for Earth initiative, described as a potential transformative force for the environment.

Originally introduced earlier this year with a $2 million seed fund, the program is led by Lucas Joppa, who holds the unique position of chief environmental scientist at Microsoft—a title he believes is unmatched in the tech sector. To date, the initiative has awarded 35 grants across ten nations. The fresh infusion of capital will bolster these ongoing efforts and fund new undertakings over the coming half-decade. Joppa, in remarks to MIT Technology Review, emphasized a shared sense of urgency, noting that financial and material support for critical environmental challenges remains insufficient.

Through the program, recipients gain training and access to Microsoft’s Azure cloud platform and AI tools. Current projects range from creating detailed land cover maps to aid conservation in the Chesapeake Bay area, to a mosquito surveillance effort that analyzes blood samples to monitor wildlife and detect Zika virus threats, and initiatives providing farmers with data-driven insights to boost harvests while conserving resources.

The endeavor also aligns with Microsoft’s commercial interests. As Joppa explained, deploying technology with organizations operating under constrained budgets and difficult field conditions serves as a rigorous real-world test, yielding valuable product feedback and demonstrating reliability to potential clients. He stressed that such stress-testing ultimately strengthens their offerings.

Additionally, in a competitive industry where attracting and keeping AI expertise is paramount, Joppa highlighted that the project’s purposeful mission acts as a magnet for researchers and engineers. While competitive compensation is essential, he noted that offering meaningful, impactful work is equally crucial to engaging top talent.

HOUSTON - Harris County leaders will announce plans Wednesday for a proposed bond aimed at paying for flood control measures.
County Judge Ed Emmett and Russ Poppe, the county’s flood czar, scheduled a 2:30 p.m. news conference to discuss their plan for the proposed bond, including the types of projects it would pay for, the costs of those projects and a series of community meetings about the issue.
Emmett floated the idea of a bond measure in the aftermath of Hurricane Harvey last year.
Earlier this month, Emmett said that while the amount of the proposed bond is not final, it could be upward of $2.5 billion. It would pay for existing flood control projects on Brays, White Oak and Hunting bayous and on Clear Creek, and it could include money for a third reservoir to be built in the county.
Voters will ultimately decide the issue during a special election on Aug. 25 -- the one-year anniversary of Harvey's landfall.
Click2Houston.com plans to offer a live stream of Wednesday’s news conference.

The concept for this bond was introduced by Emmett following Hurricane Harvey in 2017. The Legislature has gone past the deadline set under state law to finish the annual session – and there are few signs that they’ll be finishing their work soon.
Monday was the 91st day of the session, which is scheduled to last 90 days, although the state constitution allows for 121 days.
The Senate and House haven’t yet named the six members of conference committees to resolve differences over the operating budget and a plan to draw money from Permanent Fund earnings to pay for state government.
Instead of making announcements on major bills, the two chambers passed smaller legislation.
One example is Senate Bill 80, which allows state regulators to charge cellphone owners a new monthly fee.
The money would be used to pay for communication devices and software for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, or who have a speech disability.
Anchorage Sen. Mia Costello said the bill is a consequence of many residents moving to mobile phones, including her own family.
“We hardly use our landline, and many families in Alaska now solely use a cellphone,” she said.
Currently, residents’ landlines are charged 9 cents per month to fund services for those with disabilities, while business lines are charged 18 cents per month.
The Regulatory Commission of Alaska expects to charge cellphone users 5 cents a month if the bill is enacted, Costello said.
Costello said the number of Alaskans who have landlines is only 47 percent of what it was when the fees were started. She said the bill expands the number of people who will benefit from the program, while costing cellphone users only 60 cents a year.
“This is an important bill because it looks to the 21st century, and updating the type of the type of technology that hearing impaired Alaskans will be able to use,” she said.
All 19 senators who were present on Monday voted for the bill. It now heads to the House.
rewrite:
The state's legislative body has continued its work beyond the statutory deadline for concluding its yearly session, with little indication that adjournment is imminent. Monday marked the 91st day of the proceedings, exceeding the planned 90-day period, though the constitution permits an extension up to 121 days.

Key negotiations remain stalled, as neither the Senate nor the House has appointed members to the conference committees needed to reconcile disagreements on the main state budget and a proposal to utilize Permanent Fund earnings for government funding. Rather than advancing these significant measures, both chambers focused on passing minor legislation.

One such piece is Senate Bill 80, which would authorize state regulators to impose a new monthly charge on cellular phone subscribers. The revenue generated is intended to fund communication tools and programs for individuals with hearing loss or speech disabilities. According to Anchorage Senator Mia Costello, the legislation responds to the widespread shift toward mobile phones, a trend she noted in her own household. "We rarely use our landline, and many Alaska families now rely exclusively on cellphones," she stated.

Presently, a monthly fee of nine cents on residential landlines and eighteen cents on business lines supports these disability services. Costello explained that if the bill becomes law, the Regulatory Commission of Alaska anticipates setting the cellphone fee at five cents per month. She highlighted that landline subscriptions in Alaska have declined to 47% of their number when the original fees were established. The proposal, she said, would broaden the pool of beneficiaries while costing cellphone users just sixty cents annually.

"This is significant legislation because it modernizes our approach for the 21st century, updating the technological resources available to hearing-impaired residents," Costello remarked. The bill received unanimous support from all nineteen senators present and now moves to the House for consideration.

Cliqz, developer of a privacy-focused browser, has acquired the Ghostery browser extension and the team behind it
Cliqz, the German developer of the privacy-focused browser of the same name, has acquired the tracker-blocking browser extension Ghostery and its development team from its creator, Evidon.
Partly owned by Mozilla, Cliqz will combine Ghostery's technology with similar functions in its browser, but plans to continue development of the extension for other browsers too, it said Wednesday.
The sale will resolve an apparent conflict of interest for Evidon, which on the one hand provided the Ghostery extension to enhance privacy, and on the other sold aggregate information to businesses regarding which trackers users blocked. It will still obtain that aggregate information from Cliqz, but one step removed.
Sharing of aggregate data and the creation of user accounts are optional features of the extension.
The Ghostery antitracking tool has about 10 million active users worldwide, the companies said. One advantage of the acquisition that Cliqz touted is that it is based in Germany, a country with some of the strictest privacy laws in the world, which it said should provide better privacy protection for any data the company holds about its users.
While Cliqz sets about integrating Ghostery's functions into its browser, it recommends adding the Ghostery extension to the Cliqz browser, or using the Ghostery and Cliqz extensions for Mozilla's Firefox together. Cliqz offers beta versions of its browser for Windows, Mac, Linux, Android and iOS. The Ghostery extension is available for Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Internet Explorer, Safari and Opera, with some functions available in mobile apps for iOS and Android.
rewrite:
The German software firm Cliqz, known for its privacy-centric web browser, has purchased the Ghostery add-on along with its technical staff from Evidon, the original maker. Cliqz, which counts Mozilla among its investors, announced it will merge Ghostery's tracker-blocking capabilities with its own browser's existing privacy tools. However, the company also intends to keep supporting and updating the Ghostery extension for use on other popular browsers.

This transaction addresses a prior conflict for Evidon. While its Ghostery product helped users block online trackers to protect their privacy, Evidon simultaneously sold summarized, anonymized data to companies about which trackers were being blocked. Under the new arrangement, Evidon will still receive this aggregated data, but indirectly through Cliqz, creating a degree of separation. It is important to note that both the data-sharing and any user account creation within Ghostery remain optional features controlled by the individual user.

Ghostery is widely used, with an estimated 10 million active global users. Cliqz highlighted that being headquartered in Germany, a nation with rigorous data protection regulations, offers an additional privacy safeguard for any user information the company manages. During the integration phase, Cliqz suggests that users of its browser also install the Ghostery extension for maximum effect, or pair the Ghostery and Cliqz add-ons in Firefox. The Cliqz browser is available in beta for Windows, Mac, Linux, Android, and iOS. The Ghostery extension supports Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Internet Explorer, Safari, and Opera, with certain features also accessible in its mobile apps for iOS and Android.

The Crown says it has filed an appeal after charges were stayed against Jamie Bacon in relation to the Surrey Six killings. (File photo)
B.C.’s prosecution is appealing after charges were stayed in the Surrey Six massacre against Red Scorpions gang leader Jamie Bacon.
On Dec. 1, a BC Supreme Court decision was released that said a judge had granted Bacon’s application for a stay of proceedings in his trial on charges of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder.
The hearing occurred in closed court, and the judge’s reasons for granting the application are sealed.
On Monday, the prosecution service said it has reviewed the abbreviated ruling, saying it reveals “errors of law” and that “the public interest requires an appeal.”
The service said it anticipates that further court filings, as well as some or all of the appeal proceedings, will be sealed or closed to the public.
Six men, including two innocent bystanders, were shot dead at the Balmoral Tower on Oct. 19, 2007. Cody Haevischer and Matthew Johnston were convicted in 2014 of six counts of first-degree murder and one count of conspiracy.
rewrite:
British Columbia's prosecution service is appealing a recent court decision to stay charges against Jamie Bacon, an alleged leader of the Red Scorpions gang, connected to the Surrey Six murders. The stay was issued by a BC Supreme Court judge on December 1, halting proceedings on counts of first-degree murder and conspiracy. This hearing was conducted privately, and the judge's rationale remains confidential under seal.

After reviewing the abbreviated ruling, prosecutors stated they have identified legal errors and believe an appeal is necessary in the public interest. They further anticipate that upcoming court documents and potentially the entire appeal process may also be sealed or held away from public view.

The case stems from the 2007 shooting deaths of six individuals at the Balmoral Tower in Surrey. Two of the victims were uninvolved bystanders. Other individuals, Cody Haevischer and Matthew Johnston, were convicted in 2014 for their roles in the killings.

PALMERTON -- A music store owner in Carbon County has a message for would-be vandals: smile for the camera!
Security video shows the vandal struggle to flip the heavy concrete bench in front of Prodigy Studios in Palmerton.
The bench is toppled and cracked.
"It's not just a park bench to me," owner Tony Oriolo said.
He says vandals went on an early morning tear along Delaware Avenue, knocking over signs and seating at places including Halls of Horror.
"It gets me annoyed. We work hard for all this stuff and it does get me annoyed," said Charles Knight with Halls of Horror.
In less than 24 hours, Tony Oriolo used a combination of his security footage and Facebook to figure out who broke his bench.
"I recognized his friends and through the power of Facebook, you can figure out who is connected at any given time if you are a good enough detective," Oriolo said.
Then he sent the man a message, and he heard back.
"He fessed up to it."
The guy in the video turned out to be a customer.
The story has another twist. Oriolo says not only did someone donate new concrete bench ends, the vandal volunteered to bring them to the store himself.
"He even offered to work here in the music store to make amends."
Detectives with Palmerton police told Oriolo if that works out, they may not file charges.
"He is not a bad guy. He just probably made some bad choices last night."
This modern-day music man figures his tale is a lesson to aspiring criminals, with cameras everywhere, your cover can get blown.
rewrite:
To view this video, Javascript must be activated.

In Palmerton, located in Carbon County, the proprietor of a music shop has a warning for anyone considering property damage: you are being recorded. Surveillance footage captures an individual attempting to overturn a substantial concrete bench situated outside Prodigy Studios. The bench was ultimately pushed over and damaged.

For the owner, Tony Oriolo, this object holds greater significance than mere public seating. He reports that vandals caused a series of disturbances in the early hours along Delaware Avenue, damaging signs and fixtures at several businesses, among them Halls of Horror. Charles Knight of Halls of Horror expressed his frustration, stating that such destruction is aggravating given the hard work invested in these establishments.

Within a day, Oriolo managed to identify the person responsible for breaking his bench by reviewing his security recordings and conducting research on social media. He explained that by recognizing the individual's associates online, he was able to trace connections and determine his identity. After Oriolo contacted him, the individual admitted to the act.

Interestingly, the vandal was actually a patron of the store. The situation took an unexpected turn when a donor provided new bench supports, and the person who caused the damage offered to deliver them personally. He also proposed working at the music store to rectify his mistake.

According to Oriolo, local police detectives indicated that if these reparations are completed, they might not pursue legal action. Oriolo believes the individual is not inherently malicious but likely exercised poor judgment that evening.

This contemporary music store owner concludes that his experience serves as a cautionary note for would-be offenders: in an age of pervasive surveillance, anonymity is difficult to maintain.
