Cleveland Fed President Loretta Mester takes part in a panel convened to speak about the health of the U.S. economy in New York November 18, 2015. REUTERS/Lucas Jackson
A Federal Reserve policymaker on Thursday repeated her call for further rate hikes and a trimming of the central bank's balance sheet later this year, as the U.S. economy is expected to rebound from what looks like a weak first quarter.
"If economic conditions evolve as anticipated, I believe further removal of accommodation via increases in the fed funds rate will be needed," said Cleveland Fed President Loretta Mester, a hawkish policymaker who regains a vote on interest rates next year. "I would (also) be comfortable changing our reinvestment policy this year."
The Fed raised rates in mid-March, its second policy tightening in three months. The central bank has also been topping up a $4.5 trillion portfolio of bonds amassed in the wake of the financial crisis, but plans to eventually begin shrinking it by letting the assets mature.
While the economy has been expanding at a 2-percent rate over the last few years, the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow forecast predicts it dipped to 1 percent in the first three months of the year.
Yet the "underlying fundamentals supporting the economic expansion are sound," Mester added in prepared remarks to a financial risk conference in Chicago. "While growth in the first quarter may come in on the weak side, I think this largely reflects transitory factors and residual seasonality in the data."
(Reporting by Jonathan Spicer; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama)

This perspective is based on expectations that the economy will recover after a sluggish start to the year. She also expressed openness to adjusting the Fed’s reinvestment strategy within the year.

In mid-March, the Fed increased rates for the second time in three months. Additionally, while maintaining a large balance sheet of bonds accumulated post-financial crisis, the central bank intends to start decreasing its size by ceasing to reinvest the proceeds from maturing securities. Although economic growth has averaged around two percent in recent years, current tracking estimates suggest it slowed significantly in the first quarter. Mester, speaking at a Chicago conference on financial risk, noted that the foundational elements of the expansion remain strong. She attributed any first-quarter weakness largely to temporary influences and ongoing seasonal adjustments in economic measurements.

New Zealand's Regan Ware in action against France on day one of the Hamilton Sevens. Source: Photosport
It was all looking a bit grim for the Kiwis heading into the dying moments of their Waikato showdown until Ravouvou broke down the right to crash over.
They had been trailing 12-5 after first-half Luciano Gonzalez and Felipe del Mestre tries handed a valiant Argentinian side the ascendancy.
But tries to Vilimoni Koroi and Ravouvou turned it around late on.
Undefeated across Saturday's pool play, the All Blacks Sevens will now go on to face England in Sunday's quarter-final after the latter's loss to South Africa.

Scotland eventually beat out Argentina and France to a quarter-final berth via head-to-head after all three sides finished pool play on five points.
They'll play the fearsome Blitzbokke, who made light work of the English in Pool B's afternoon crunch match with a 28-7 triumph.

[India], Mar. 20 (ANI): The fear of failure is so high among students taking the Uttar Pradesh Board examinations that some of them turned to desperate measures like attaching notes on their answer sheets.
Currency notes of Rs 100, Rs 50 and Rs 500 were found in answer sheets during the checking of 12th board examination papers in Firozabad district.
The teachers said, "Students, whose exams did not go well, are attaching currency notes in the examination papers to bribe us. We are giving marks only on merit. None of us are accepting the money found in the answer sheets."
Another thing that came to light was that the CCTV cameras that were installed inside the examination centres were not working as their connection wires were damaged. When teachers were asked about the same, they refused to comment on it. Recently, in a related but different episode, a video went viral, wherein a miscreant brandishing gun can be seen inside an examination hall for facilitating the students to cheat. The incident took place at Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar University in Agra. Vice-Chancellor Dr Arvind Kumar Dixit said that the matter would be probed with the help of administration and police force. (ANI)

Furniture and household items are being moved out from the Estates at Acqualina, a Sunny Isles Beach resort undergoing a massive renovation, and donated to two Florida foundations.
Laura and Jorge Posada’s foundation for Puerto Rico have joined Derek Jeter’s Turn2 foundation to get the donated household items to hurricane victims in Puerto Rico, Miami and Key West.

“Now I can also say that I am Derek Jeter’s teammate because we are working together to benefit all those who were affected by the natural disasters,” Laura said.

More than 125 pieces are being donated by the estates at Acqualina.

WASHINGTON — The Environmental Protection Agency plans to restrict research used in developing regulations, the agency said Tuesday, a change that could affect rules governing everything from household products to power-plant emissions.
The proposal follows years of complaints by conservatives that regulations such as emissions restrictions under the Obama administration sometimes went beyond what science could prove. The new proposal would exclude the many research studies that don’t make their raw data public and limit the use of findings that can’t be reproduced by others. The EPA said this would boost transparency.
“When you have studies that you actually publish from third parties, but you don’t publish the methodology, and you don’t publish the data, you only publish the conclusions, that presents problems to those that want to offer comment on the veracity, the authenticity, the ability to assess and evaluate the conclusions that have been drawn,” Administrator Scott Pruitt said before signing the proposed rule.
The proposal is subject to a public-comment period of at least 30 days and is likely to see legal challenges, which could delay or prevent its implementation. The move prompted an uproar from scientists who say it would exclude so much research that the resulting rules would endanger Americans’ health. Ahead of the announcement, a coalition of 985 scientists issued a statement decrying the plan.
An expanded version of this report appears on WSJ.com.
Also popular on WSJ.com:
Amazon to start offering in-car deliveries.
How to dress like a billionaire.
rewrite:
The Environmental Protection Agency announced on Tuesday its intention to impose new limits on the scientific studies that can inform its rulemaking process. This shift could influence future regulations covering a wide array of areas, including consumer goods and industrial pollution.

This initiative responds to long-standing criticisms, primarily from conservative circles, that certain past regulations—like those on emissions during the previous administration—were at times based on insufficient scientific evidence. Under the planned policy, the EPA would generally disregard studies that do not publicly share their underlying data. It would also place greater emphasis on research that other scientists can independently replicate. The agency contends these steps will increase transparency in regulatory science.

Administrator Scott Pruitt, speaking before signing the draft rule, argued that using studies which disclose only their conclusions, and not their methods or raw data, creates difficulties for the public and experts attempting to scrutinize those findings.

The proposal will now enter a public feedback period lasting no less than 30 days and is expected to face legal opposition, potentially hindering its enactment. Many scientists have reacted with alarm, warning that disqualifying vast amounts of existing research would lead to weaker public health protections. Just before the announcement, a group of 985 scientists released a statement condemning the plan.

A more detailed account of this story is available on WSJ.com.

Puebla, Mexico, October 6, 2017 ( venezuelanalysis.com ) – Venezuelan electoral authorities completed Friday an audit of voting infrastructure, ahead of elections later this month.
According to state media outlet AVN, the National Electoral Council was set to complete its checks of Venezuela’s voting booths and other voting equipment, as the October 15 regional vote draws closer. The previous day, the CNE said it had audited their software, along with servers used by the country’s electronic voting system.
The final preparations were being made amid an ongoing controversy over last minute changes to ballots. The opposition has accused the CNE of failing to remove candidates who lost their primaries last month. Critics have warned that if the candidates remain on the ballots, opposition supporters could cast votes for candidates that aren’t technically in the race anymore, leaving their ballots null.
The controversy has even pulled in Canada, which issued a statement demanding the CNE scrub the null candidates from ballots.
“All political parties must be allowed to replace candidates according to the law ... Canada calls on the CNE to make decisions in full respect of the electoral law,” Canada’s embassy said.
On Wednesday the Supreme Court's Electoral Tribunal ruled that the CNE should accept candidate changes and modifications up to ten days before the elections. However, the decision has been criticised by opposition spokespeople as too little too late. They say that there is no longer time to make the substitutions, while the CNE has yet to officially comment.
But the candidate replacement issue isn’t the only controversy. The opposition has also accused the CNE of quietly shuttering 77 voting stations. Opposition leaders claim the closures were concentrated in areas that typically vote against the government.
Thought the CNE has not responded to the allegations, the President of the Council of Electoral Experts [CEELA] Nicanor Moscoso said Thursday that Venezuela’s voting system remains one of the best in the world.
“It is the safest method, and nobody can manipulate the information given by the voting machine,” he said.
According to teleSUR, Moscoso also praised the automated system as “extraordinary”.
The CNE signed an agreement with CEELA Thursday, and confirmed that the body will formally observe the country's upcoming elections.
The vote will take place on October 15, and will see the election of new governors and state legislators.
rewrite:

The country’s state-run news agency, AVN, indicated that the National Electoral Council (CNE) had concluded its review of voting booths and associated hardware. This followed an audit conducted the prior day on the software and servers integral to Venezuela’s electronic voting process.

These concluding steps occurred against a backdrop of dispute concerning late alterations to the candidate lists. Opposition groups have alleged that the CNE neglected to exclude candidates who were defeated in primary elections held the previous month. Analysts have expressed concern that if these individuals remain listed, supporters might inadvertently select them, rendering those votes invalid.

The matter has attracted international attention, including from Canada, which released a communiqué urging the CNE to remove such ineligible candidates from all ballots. The Canadian embassy stated that all parties should be permitted to substitute candidates in accordance with legal statutes and called upon the electoral authority to adhere strictly to the law.

In a related development, Venezuela’s Supreme Court Electoral Tribunal decided on Wednesday that the CNE must permit candidate changes up to ten days prior to the election. Opposition representatives have dismissed this ruling as insufficient and untimely, arguing that the window for implementing such substitutions has effectively closed. The CNE has not provided an official statement on this criticism.

Beyond candidate eligibility, further contention arose from opposition accusations that the CNE discreetly closed 77 polling locations, allegedly in regions historically unfavorable to the governing party. The electoral council has not publicly addressed these claims.

Conversely, Nicanor Moscoso, President of the Council of Electoral Experts of Latin America (CEELA), remarked on Thursday that Venezuela’s electoral mechanism remains among the most robust globally. He described the automated system as exceptionally secure and resistant to manipulation. International broadcaster teleSUR quoted Moscoso lauding the system as “extraordinary.”

The CNE formalized an agreement with CEELA on Thursday, confirming that the organization will serve as an official observer for the impending elections. On October 15, Venezuelans will cast ballots to select new governors and state legislative representatives.

Crane said they are now actively looking at different properties and pursuing new locations. They hope to be out of the temporary location by next Easter.

Shocking pictures reveal the devastating effect prosecco can have on your teeth.
Everyone’s favorite fizz turns teeth into a “chalk like powder” according to an alarming new study.
Dental scientists from the Oral Health Foundation left healthy human molars and incisors in the Italian sparkling wine for 14 days.
Prosecco is known for having a triple threat to your pearly whites for acidic bubbles, alcohol and a high sugar content.
And as we enter the party season more and more people will be knocking back the fizz.
But the study might make drinkers think again after the tooth was completely destroyed after being immersed in prosecco for a fortnight.
Dr. Ben Atkins told the Daily Mail: “If I were to pick the tooth up, it would likely turn to a chalk-like powder in my hand.”
“This could be extremely painful, leading to a need for extensive restoration or extraction.”
“Prosecco’s high sugar [and acid] content hits drinkers with a double whammy of erosion and decay. At Christmas, if we are sipping a drink throughout the day, our teeth are under constant attack.”
Cola was also tested in the study and was shown to have an “extreme” and “shocking” effect on teeth.
Worries over the soft beverage lead to it being banned from school vending machines and cafeterias in a bid to keep kids’ teeth healthy.
Atkins said: “Apart from the extensive staining, turning the tooth brown after only two days, it has also completely cracked in half owing to the huge extent of demineralization which has made it weak.
“The effects on young teeth can very quickly become extreme, devastating future oral health. With 12 spoons of sugar in a typical can of a cola-like drink, the decay potential is almost off the scale.”
Back in August the worries of the “prosecco smile” were revealed by a top London dentist.
Dr. Mervyn Druian said: “It is acidic and it has sugar in it so, while a few glasses are fine, if you drink too much of it you are going to have a problem. The signs of prosecco smile are where the teeth come out of the gum.”
“It starts with a white line just below the gum, which if you probe it is a little bit soft and that is the beginning of tooth decay which can lead to fillings and dental work.”

Prosecco presents a triple danger to dental health due to its combination of acidity, alcohol, and significant sugar levels. As Dr. Ben Atkins explained to the Daily Mail, handling the affected tooth would likely cause it to crumble into a chalky dust. He warned that such damage could result in serious pain, necessitating major dental repairs or even removal of the tooth. The drink's potent mix of sugar and acid delivers a dual blow, simultaneously eroding and decaying enamel. During extended holiday celebrations, where one might sip continuously, teeth face relentless assault.

The same research also examined cola, observing similarly severe and alarming effects on dental material. Concerns over such soft drinks have previously prompted bans in school vending machines and cafeterias to protect children's oral health. Dr. Atkins noted that cola not only caused deep staining, turning the tooth brown within two days, but also led it to split in half. This fracture resulted from profound demineralization, which critically weakened the structure. He emphasized that for younger teeth, the impact can be rapid and severe, compromising long-term dental wellness. Given that a typical can of cola contains about twelve teaspoons of sugar, its capacity to cause decay is exceptionally high.

The telltale signs emerge near the gum line, starting as a soft, white mark just below the gums. This softness indicates the onset of decay, which can progress to require fillings and other dental treatments.

LAGOS, April 13 Nigerian interbank lending rates rose sharply by around 100 percentage points on Thursday, as commercial lenders scrambled for cash to pay for bond purchases and cover their positions, traders said.
Overnight lending rates rose to around 300 percent from 200 percent at the end of Wednesday, as naira liquidity dried up in the banking system and some banks were forced to borrow from the central bank.
Nigeria raised 105.32 billion naira ($345 million) from bond sales this week, and payment for the debt sale was due on Thursday, draining liquidity in the market and pushing further up the cost of money in the market.
"The market is currently short of funds with major placers asking for a higher rate on their money as a result of pressure from those who need cash to cover their positions," one trader said.
The central bank has consistently sold dollars at both the spot and forward markets, and required banks to pay for the purchase. This has drained liquidity in the market.
The bank said authorised dealers bought $45 million out of $100 million it made available on the spot market.
"There are strong indications that the demand for foreign exchange by authorized dealers has slumped," it said in a statement.
Nigeria's financial markets will be closed until April 18 for a public holiday. ($1 = 305.1000 naira) (Reporting by Oludare Mayowa; Writing by Oludare Mayowa and Alexis Akwagyiram; Editing by Toby Chopra)
rewrite:
LAGOS, April 13 — According to traders, interest rates for short-term loans between Nigerian banks surged dramatically on Thursday, increasing by approximately one hundred percentage points. This spike occurred as financial institutions urgently sought funds to settle recent government bond acquisitions and manage their financial balances.

The rate for one-day loans jumped to roughly 300 percent, up from 200 percent the prior day. This severe tightening was caused by a shortage of the local naira currency within the banking sector, compelling several banks to seek emergency loans from the country's central bank.

A government bond auction this week successfully raised 105.32 billion naira ($345 million), with settlement required on Thursday. This large cash outflow significantly reduced available funds in the financial system, driving borrowing costs higher. One trader noted the system was critically low on cash, with institutions holding surplus funds demanding much higher interest rates due to intense demand from those needing to cover obligations.

Furthermore, the central bank's ongoing sales of U.S. dollars, for which commercial banks must provide immediate naira payment, has also withdrawn substantial liquidity from the market. The bank reported that authorized dealers purchased $45 million of the $100 million it offered in its latest spot market auction. It added in a statement that demand for foreign currency from these dealers appears to have weakened considerably.

Nigerian financial markets are scheduled to remain closed until April 18 for a public holiday. ($1 = 305.1000 naira)

OCEAN SHORES, Wash. — Police are searching for a Utah woman who stayed at an Ocean Shores hotel and then disappeared.
Police say 31-year-old Tracy Ann Lewis of Eden, Utah was last seen at the Morning Glory Hotel on March 9.
“She checked out of the motel in the morning and was last seen walking northbound on Ocean Shores Blvd. NW. Her vehicle, containing all of her belongings, was left in the hotel parking lot.”
Officers said she went on a family vacation to Disneyland before driving up the coast. She was expected to visit San Francisco and Portland.
Her family said they don’t know why she would have gone to Ocean Shores.

She checked out in the AM and was last seen walking NB on Ocean Shores Blvd. NW. @catchwmw #Q13FOX pic.twitter.com/hUkp2SxmGj — David Rose (@DavidRoseQ13FOX) March 19, 2018
Police searched the sand dunes in the area with police officers, a dozen volunteers and three search dogs.
Anyone with information is asked to call 360-289-3331.
rewrite:
Authorities in Ocean Shores, Washington, are seeking the public's assistance in locating a missing woman from Utah. Tracy Ann Lewis, aged 31 and from Eden, Utah, was last spotted on March 9 at the Morning Glory Hotel. After checking out that morning, she was observed traveling on foot in a northerly direction along Ocean Shores Boulevard Northwest. Her car, which held all her personal items, remained parked at the hotel.

Lewis had been on a family trip to Disneyland prior to driving north along the coastline, with plans to stop in San Francisco and Portland. Her relatives have expressed confusion over her presence in Ocean Shores. An organized search of the nearby dunes has been conducted, involving officers, volunteer personnel, and canine units. Individuals with any relevant details are urged to contact the police at 360-289-3331.

President Donald Trump recorded a robocall encouraging Alabama voters to back Republican Roy Moore in Tuesday’s special election to fill a vacant U.S. Senate seat representing Alabama.
Politico first reported on Saturday that Trump would record a message, and CNN obtained audio of the call on Sunday.
“We need Roy voting for us. I am stopping illegal immigration and crime. We’re building a stronger military and protecting the Second Amendment and our pro-life values,” Trump says in the robocall supporting Moore, per CNN. “But if Alabama elects liberal Democrat Doug Jones, all of our progress will be stopped cold. We already know Democrat Doug Jones is a puppet of Nancy Pelosi and Chuck Schumer, and he will vote with the Washington liberals every single time.”
Moore faces allegations from several women that he inappropriately pursued a sexual or romantic relationship with them when they were teenagers and he was in his 30s. Despite the sexual misconduct allegations, Moore has pressed on in the race. Although Republican leaders urged Moore to leave the race when the allegations first surfaced, GOP leaders have since softened on Moore and pushed to keep the seat in Republican control.
rewrite:
In a prerecorded phone message, former President Donald Trump urged Alabama residents to support Republican candidate Roy Moore in a special Senate election. The call was aimed at filling an empty seat representing the state. Initial reports from Politico on Saturday indicated Trump would record such an endorsement, with CNN acquiring the actual audio the following day.

According to CNN's reporting, Trump states in the call that Moore's vote is needed to advance his agenda, which includes curbing illegal immigration, reducing crime, strengthening the military, and upholding gun rights and anti-abortion values. He warns that electing his Democratic opponent, Doug Jones, would halt this progress. Trump characterizes Jones as being controlled by Democratic figures Nancy Pelosi and Chuck Schumer, claiming he would consistently side with liberal lawmakers in Washington.

Moore's campaign has persisted despite multiple accusations of inappropriate sexual advances toward teenage girls when he was in his thirties. After initially calling for Moore to withdraw following these allegations, many Republican officials have moderated their stance, prioritizing retaining the Senate seat for their party.

Photo: Scott Kirkland / PictureGroup / Sipa / USA Today
By Scott T. Sterling
Lin-Manuel Miranda and Ben Platt have teamed up for a cause.
The Broadway stars have united to create “Found/Tonight,” a mashup of “You Will Be Found” from Dear Evan Hanson and “The Story of Tonight” from Hamilton.
Related: Lin-Manuel Miranda Shares ‘Almost Like Praying ft Artists for Puerto Rico (Salsa Remix)’
The song comes with a new music video. Watch it below. Sheet music for “Found/Tonight” is made available for free here.
The song was inspired by the thousands of students across the country who mobilized following the Stoneman Douglas High School shooting in Parkland, FL just last month. A portion of all proceeds will go towards the March For Our Lives Initiative. Platt and Miranda are also united in encouraging other artists to help spark a viral campaign by explaining why they march using the hashtag #IWillMarch.
“In the wake of Parkland, I was awestruck by the strength and leadership of the students and their ability to speak truth to power,” Miranda explained in a press statement. “In the midst of their grief, they mobilized the youth of our nation and created a movement. This is their moment. Not just for themselves, but for all of us. This song is my way of helping to raise funds and awareness for their efforts, and to say Thank You, and that we are with you so let’s keep fighting, together.”
“When Lin called me to be a part of this mashup, I couldn’t say no,” Platt added. “Better gun control is something that all Americans should be passionate about. These students are paving the way for future generations and it’s so inspiring to see young people standing up for what is probably the most important cause right now in this country, and demanding action. I hope that this song can play some small part in bringing about real change.”
Find more information about the March For Our Lives Initiative here.

The inspiration for this project stems from the widespread student activism that emerged across the United States after last month’s tragic shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida. A share of the revenue generated will be donated to support the March For Our Lives campaign. Both artists are urging their fellow creators to participate in a social media effort, using the tag #IWillMarch to share their personal reasons for supporting the movement.
Miranda expressed his admiration in a released comment, stating he was deeply moved by the resolve and moral clarity shown by the students following the Parkland tragedy. He noted that, despite their profound sorrow, they have activated young people nationwide to build a powerful force for change. Miranda emphasized that this is a pivotal time for them and for society as a whole, and that the song aims to generate both financial support and public attention for their work, serving as a gesture of gratitude and solidarity in the ongoing struggle.
Platt remarked that he immediately agreed when Miranda invited him to contribute to the mashup. He believes advocating for more effective firearm regulations is a vital issue for every citizen. Platt finds it motivating to witness these young individuals championing such a critical national cause and calling for concrete measures, setting a precedent for those to come. He expressed a hope that their musical effort might contribute in some modest way to achieving meaningful progress.

April 12 Mediatel SA:
* Said on Tuesday that it has convened extraordinary general meeting of shareholders for May 8 to vote on lowering the company's share capital by 65.4 million zlotys ($16.32 million) in order to compensate for losses incurred by the company from previous years
* Plans to lower nominal value of each share to 0.5 zloty per share from 1 zloty per share
* At the same time, the company plans to increase its share capital via issue of 130.8 million series C shares of nominal value 0.5 zloty each
* Series C shares to be offered via private subscription without pre-emptive right
* The company intends also to issue up to 138.3 million series D shares of nominal value of 0.5 zloty per share
* Series D shares to be offered via private placement without pre-emptive rights
* Says that the resolutions are aimed at defending Hawe group, and in particular Hawe Telekom, from an attempt of a hostile takeover by Hawe Telekom's main creditor, Agencja Rozwoju Przemysłu SA
Source text for Eikon:
Further company coverage: ($1 = 4.0065 zlotys) (Gdynia Newsroom)
rewrite:
Mediatel SA announced on Tuesday that it will hold a special shareholder meeting on May 8. The agenda includes a vote to reduce the company's share capital by 65.4 million zlotys (equivalent to $16.32 million) to cover accumulated losses from prior periods. As part of this move, the par value of each existing share will be halved, dropping from 1 zloty to 0.5 zloty.

Concurrently, the firm plans a capital increase through two private offerings. It will issue 130.8 million new Series C shares, each with a face value of 0.5 zloty, available by private subscription without granting existing shareholders pre-emptive rights. Additionally, up to 138.3 million Series D shares, also with a nominal value of 0.5 zloty per share, will be offered in a private placement, again excluding pre-emptive rights.

The company stated these measures are designed to protect the Hawe group, specifically Hawe Telekom, against a hostile takeover attempt by its primary creditor, Agencja Rozwoju Przemysłu SA.

Medal of Honor recipient humbled by appreciation in Illinois
hello
SPRINGFIELD, Ill. -- A Medal of Honor recipient says he's humbled by the appreciation he's been shown by the people in Illinois.
The State Journal-Register reports 71-year-old James McCloughan (mih-KLOO'-uhn) of South Haven, Michigan was the keynote speaker during the main program of the Veterans and Gold Star Family Day Event at the Illinois State Fair on Sunday.
McCloughan, who was accompanied on stage by Gov. Bruce Rauner and Springfield Mayor Jim Langfelder, called all of the veterans and current service members his heroes.
McCloughan received the Medal of Honor from President Donald Trump at the White House on July 31. He's the first Medal of Honor recipient under Trump.
McCloughan, a combat medic, is credited with saving the lives of 10 members of his company during a Vietnam War battle despite his own serious wounds.
___
Information from: The State Journal-Register, http://www.sj-r.com
rewrite:
A Medal of Honor recipient expressed deep gratitude for the warm reception he received in Illinois. James McCloughan, age 71 and from South Haven, Michigan, delivered the featured address at the Veterans and Gold Star Family Day gathering during the state fair in Springfield. He was joined by Governor Bruce Rauner and Mayor Jim Langfelder. McCloughan told the audience he views all veterans and active military personnel as heroes.

President Donald Trump presented him with the nation's highest military award at a White House ceremony on July 31, making McCloughan the first person to receive the Medal of Honor during this administration. His recognition stems from actions as an army medic in the Vietnam War, where he rescued ten fellow soldiers from his company while injured himself.

CAIRO — Two passenger trains collided on Friday just outside Egypt's Mediterranean port city of Alexandria, killing at least 36 people and injuring about 123, according to two medical officials.
A statement by the Egyptian Railways Authority said a train traveling to Alexandria from Cairo, Egypt's capital, crashed into the back of another train, which was waiting at a small station in the district of Khorshid, just east of Alexandria.
A general view of people by the wreckage after two passenger trains collided in Alexandria, Egypt, on Friday. Hazem Gouda / EPA
The stationary train had just arrived from Port Said, a Mediterranean city on the northern tip of the Suez Canal, when it was hit, according to the statement.
The statement did not say what caused the accident, saying only that the authority's experts would be investigating.
Associated Press video footage from the scene showed mangled train coaches on the tracks as hundreds of onlookers and victims' relatives gathered around on both sides of the tracks.
Ambulances were standing by and riot police were deployed to keep the onlookers away from the scene of the disaster.
Egypt's railway system has a poor safety record, mostly blamed on decades of badly maintained equipment and poor management.
Friday's collision was the latest in a series of deadly accidents that have claimed hundreds of lives over the years. Figures recently released by the state's statistics agency show that 1,249 train accidents took place last year, the highest number since 2009 when the number reached 1,577.
Friday's accident was the deadliest rail accident since 2006, when at least 51 people were killed when two commuter trains collided near Cairo.
Two trains are seen after they collided just outside Egypt's Mediterranean port city of Alexandria, Friday. Ravy shaker / AP
And earlier, in 2002, a massive fire engulfed a train filled with local holiday travelers. The train sped for miles, with flames engulfing one carriage after another, killing more than 370 people.
In November 2012, a speeding train crashed into a bus carrying Egyptian children to their kindergarten in the country's south, killing more than 50 — mostly children between the ages of four and six. Two months later, at least 19 people died and more than 100 were injured in a train derailment south of Cairo.
rewrite:
On Friday, a severe collision involving two passenger trains occurred near Alexandria, Egypt's Mediterranean port, resulting in a minimum of 36 fatalities and approximately 123 injuries, as confirmed by medical sources.

According to Egypt's Railways Authority, the incident involved a train traveling from the capital, Cairo, to Alexandria, which struck the rear of another train. The stationary train, having recently arrived from Port Said—a city at the Suez Canal's northern entrance—was waiting at Khorshid station, located east of Alexandria, when the impact happened. The authority's announcement did not specify a cause for the crash, noting only that its specialists would conduct an inquiry.

Video from the site depicted severely damaged train carriages on the rails, with crowds of bystanders and family members of those affected assembled along the tracks. Emergency medical vehicles were present, and security forces were tasked with controlling the gathering crowds.

Egypt's rail network is known for its inadequate safety standards, often attributed to long-term neglect of infrastructure and administrative failures. This recent crash adds to a history of fatal incidents on the system. Official data indicates that 1,249 train accidents occurred in the previous year, the highest annual count since 2009. The event marks the most severe rail disaster since 2006, when a collision of commuter trains close to Cairo led to at least 51 deaths.

Other major tragedies in recent decades include a 2002 fire that swept through a holiday train, claiming over 370 lives as it traveled, and a 2012 collision where a train hit a kindergarten bus in southern Egypt, killing more than 50, most of whom were young children. Another derailment south of Cairo early the following year caused at least 19 deaths and over 100 injuries.

TOKYO, April 6 JERA Co said on Thursday that it had struck a memorandum of understanding with Dubai Supply Authority (DUSUP) on cooperation in the liquefied natural gas (LNG) business.
JERA, the world's top LNG importer, has been forming alliances with other big LNG buyers to secure more flexible supply contracts in a move which shifts power to importers from producers as oversupply grows.
JERA, a fuel joint venture between Tokyo Electric Power and Chubu Electric Power, said it and DUSUP would discuss opportunities for mutual collaboration in the LNG business, including joint procurement of LNG and opportunities for cooperation related to LNG shipping and storage capacity.
DUSUP procures natural gas through national and international pipelines and through the development of an LNG import facility called a floating storage regasification unit (FSRU) in Jebel Ali.
"JERA believes that strengthening its relationship with DUSUP will contribute to expanding business opportunities for both companies," JERA said in a statement.
The Tokyo-based firm last month signed a similar agreement with two of the world's biggest LNG buyers, Korea Gas Corp (KOGAS) and China National Offshore Oil Corp (CNOOC) to exchange information and cooperate in the joint procurement of LNG. (Reporting by Osamu Tsukimori. Editing by Jane Merriman)
rewrite:
On Thursday, JERA Co., based in Tokyo, announced it had entered into a preliminary agreement with Dubai's Supply Authority (DUSUP) to explore collaborative efforts within the liquefied natural gas sector. As the globe's leading LNG importer, JERA has been actively building partnerships with other major purchasers. This strategy aims to obtain more adaptable supply terms, a trend that increases the leverage of buyers relative to suppliers amid a growing market surplus.

A joint fuel venture between Tokyo Electric Power and Chubu Electric Power, JERA stated that the two entities will consider areas for mutual cooperation. These may include combined purchasing of LNG, as well as potential joint efforts involving shipping and storage infrastructure for the fuel. DUSUP secures natural gas via domestic and cross-border pipelines and is developing an LNG import terminal, known as a floating storage and regasification unit, located in Jebel Ali.

JERA expressed in a release that deepening its ties with DUSUP is expected to create broader commercial prospects for both organizations. This follows a comparable pact signed by the Japanese company last month with two other leading LNG importers, Korea Gas Corp and China National Offshore Oil Corp, focusing on information sharing and coordinated procurement activities.

Image caption The 1983 film made the phone box in the Aberdeenshire village of Pennan famous
A musical based on the classic 1983 film Local Hero will have its world premiere in Edinburgh next year.
The Royal Lyceum will be the first to perform the musical, which has been adapted by the theatre's artistic director David Greig and Bill Forsyth.
The Scottish filmmaker wrote and directed the original movie.
International music star Mark Knopfler has written the music and lyrics for the new production, which will open in Spring 2019.
Knopfler, who rose to fame in multi-million selling band Dire Straits, wrote the score for the 1983 film.
It tells the story of an American oil company representative who is sent to the fictional Ferness on the west coast of Scotland to buy the village and its land in order to build a refinery.
Image caption The inn in the village of Pennan was the setting for many scenes in the film
However, "Mac" MacIntyre adapts to Scottish village life and becomes worried the deal will ruin the place he has come to love.
It was made in several locations around Scotland but most of the Ferness village scenes were filmed in Pennan on the Aberdeenshire coast.
The red phone box on the village's main street where Mac makes phone calls to his boss in Texas, played by Burt Lancaster, became one of the most famous images of Scottish cinema.
Image copyright Mihaela Bodlovic Image caption Bill Forsyth and David Greig at the Royal Lyceum Theatre in Edinburgh
Glasgow writer and director Forsyth's other films include Gregory's Girl and Comfort and Joy.
David Greig, an acclaimed playwright as well as theatre director, said: "Local Hero is one of those great Scottish stories that has captured the imaginations of people across the world, it has been one of my favourite films since I first saw it as a teenager.
Local Hero is due to open at The Lyceum in Spring 2019 before transferring to The Old Vic in London.
rewrite:
The iconic red telephone booth located in Pennan, a coastal settlement in Aberdeenshire, gained widespread recognition after being featured in the 1983 movie *Local Hero*. A stage adaptation of this beloved film will debut for the first time globally in Edinburgh during the upcoming year. This musical presentation will be staged initially at the Royal Lyceum Theatre. The theatrical version has been crafted by David Greig, who serves as the artistic director for the venue, in collaboration with Bill Forsyth, the Scottish writer and director responsible for the original cinematic work.

For this new production, the musical compositions and song lyrics have been created by internationally renowned artist Mark Knopfler. Knopfler, originally achieving fame with the hugely successful group Dire Straits, also provided the soundtrack for the 1983 film. The narrative follows an emissary from an American petroleum corporation who travels to the invented Scottish Highland community of Ferness. His assignment is to purchase the entire village and surrounding territory to facilitate the construction of an oil refinery. As the story progresses, the representative, known as "Mac" MacIntyre, finds himself embracing the local way of life and grows concerned that the proposed development will destroy the cherished environment he has come to admire.

Although shooting occurred in various parts of Scotland, the majority of scenes depicting the village of Ferness were captured in Pennan. A central visual symbol from the film is the red phone box situated on the village's primary road, where Mac places calls to his superior in Texas, a role performed by Burt Lancaster. This image remains one of the most memorable in Scotland's film history. Bill Forsyth, from Glasgow, has additional notable works such as *Gregory's Girl* and *Comfort and Joy*. David Greig, a respected playwright and director, expressed that *Local Hero* is a quintessential Scottish tale that has engaged audiences worldwide, remaining a personal favorite since his teenage years. Following its spring 2019 premiere at The Lyceum, the production is scheduled to move to The Old Vic in London.

LSU head coach Ed Orgeron celebrates with his players after a win over Texas A&M in an NCAA football game at Kyle Field on Thursday, Nov. 24, 2016, in College Station, Texas. LSU won the game 54-39. (Smiley N. Pool/The Dallas Morning News)
Texas coach Tom Herman has desperately tried to find a way into Louisiana for a satellite camp this summer.
And on three different occasions, Herman and his staff were told that plans changed and the Longhorns were no longer welcomed at the host college, according to Sports Illustrated.
Why? LSU doesn't want Herman -- or really any Power Five peer, for that matter -- snooping around Louisiana for young talent at satellite camps. According to SI's Pete Thamel, Arkansas, Texas A&M and Houston were all disinvited to a camp at Southeastern Louisiana this summer.
While recent news of a Texas-Belhaven camp fallout made waves Tuesday, LSU's mindset isn't a new one under Ed Orgeron, who was promoted from interim coach to head coach at the end of last season.
Last year, former LSU coach Les Miles was incredibly upset with Tulane for its camp agreement with Texas A&M. When LSU hosted satellite camps this summer, the Tigers invited essentially everybody but Tulane.
rewrite: Following a 54-39 victory over Texas A&M in a November 2016 NCAA football matchup at Kyle Field in College Station, LSU head coach Ed Orgeron joined his team in celebration. Texas coach Tom Herman has repeatedly sought to establish a satellite camp presence in Louisiana this offseason. However, as reported by Sports Illustrated, Herman and his staff have been informed on three separate instances that previously arranged camps at local colleges were canceled, leaving the Longhorns without a venue. The underlying reason is LSU's firm opposition to allowing prominent programs from other major conferences to evaluate and recruit prospects within its home state. This stance has led to schools like Arkansas, Texas A&M, and Houston being uninvited from a planned camp at Southeastern Louisiana. Although a recent canceled camp involving Texas and Belhaven College drew attention, this protective strategy predates Coach Orgeron's permanent appointment last season. His predecessor, Les Miles, also strongly objected when Tulane partnered with Texas A&M for a camp, leading LSU to exclude Tulane when hosting its own camps this summer.

“So, they convinced him to come out, but it’s not in his heart. It’s not in his heart and you could see that,” she said.
Waters added that if Trump should have initially come out without prepared remarks and denounced such groups explicitly.
“It would have been easy for him to do, but he didn’t do it because it’s not in his heart,” she said.
Waters strongly rebuked the president, calling Trump a “dishonorable human being who does not deserve to be president of the United States of America.”
White House aides came to Trump’s defense following his Saturday remarks, with Vice President Mike Pence initially pinning blame on the media for not focusing more on the violence.
And on Sunday, the White House had put out a statement further clarifying Trump’s comments, saying: “The President said very strongly in his statement yesterday that he condemns all forms of violence, bigotry and hatred and of course that includes white Supremacists, KKK, neo-Nazi and all extremist groups. He called for national unity and bringing all Americans together.”
rewrite:
During a January 31 press conference in Washington, D.C., Representative Maxine Waters (D-CA) addressed recent events. She expressed the view that although the individual was persuaded to make a public statement, his convictions were not genuinely aligned with its message. Waters contended that a more immediate and direct condemnation of specific extremist factions would have been appropriate and straightforward, but that the failure to do so revealed a lack of sincere belief.

She issued a severe condemnation, labeling the former president as unfit for office due to what she described as a profound lack of honor. In response to the initial remarks, several administration officials offered support. The Vice President initially suggested media coverage was disproportionately focused, rather than addressing the underlying issues. Subsequently, an official statement was released to elaborate, asserting that the earlier comments had unequivocally denounced all violent bigotry and hatred, explicitly naming white supremacist and neo-Nazi groups, while advocating for national solidarity.

The Santa Barbara County Sheriff’s Office has detained two men suspected in the Thursday night burglary of a home in Montecito.
Franke James Showell, 25, of Lancaster and Donyae Lamonte Dixon, 29, of Los Angeles are in custody at Santa Barbara County Jail on suspicion of burglary and conspiracy, with Showell also suspected of false impersonation. Both men are being held on $50,000 bail.
Just after 9 p.m. Thursday, a resident in the 200 block of Gould Lane, in Montecito, said he heard “strange noises coming from a child’s bedroom inside his residence,” according to the sheriff’s office.
The man, a father of two young children, investigated and “upon entering a hallway between bedrooms, he immediately saw a male suspect dressed in dark clothing.”

The sheriff’s office said the man yelled at the suspect, who fled back into the bedroom and out the window, which allegedly was used to enter the home.
“The suspect was last seen fleeing down an embankment to a wooded area,” according to the sheriff’s office.
In the wake of the Montecito mudslide, deputies have conducted increased patrols in the area. Within minutes of the 911 call, deputies located Showell, one of the suspected intruders, fleeing in a vehicle. Dixon, the other suspected intruder, was found “hiding in the bushes alongside the roadway.”
The sheriff’s office said a K-9 team tracked the scent from the window of the home to the patrol car where Showell was detained.
rewrite:
Two individuals have been arrested in connection with a residential break-in that occurred on Thursday evening in Montecito, as announced by the Santa Barbara County Sheriff’s Office. The suspects, identified as 25-year-old Franke James Showell from Lancaster and 29-year-old Donyae Lamonte Dixon from Los Angeles, are currently incarcerated at the county jail. They face allegations of burglary and conspiracy, with Showell additionally accused of assuming a false identity. Bail for each has been set at $50,000.

Authorities report that the incident unfolded shortly after 9 p.m. when a homeowner on Gould Lane heard unusual sounds emanating from a child’s bedroom. The resident, who has two small children, went to investigate and encountered an intruder wearing dark clothes in a hallway. After being confronted, the individual retreated into the bedroom and exited through a window that had apparently been used to gain entry. The suspect then ran down a slope toward a forested section of the property.

Due to heightened patrols implemented following the recent mudslides in Montecito, deputies responded swiftly to the emergency call. Showell was apprehended minutes later while attempting to flee in a vehicle. Dixon was discovered concealed in roadside vegetation. A police dog assisted in the investigation by tracing a scent from the point of entry to the patrol car where Showell was being held.

KANSAS CITY, Kan. — Tensions between the KCK Fire Department and the city’s former mayor are flaring once again.
An investigation by the KCK Fire Department determined some firefighters set of a firetruck siren early Tuesday morning near former mayor Mark Holland’s house. The department said the firefighters were returning to the station from a medical call when they set off the siren.
After they had passed his home, Holland said they turned the siren off. The former mayor posted surveillance video of the firefighters’ actions, which he called harassment, on his Facebook page.
The department said in a statement the firefighters involved “will be dealt with as necessary to ensure that activation of sirens and lights will only be done in compliance with current policies.”
The former mayor and KCK firefighters have a contentious relationship. The firefighters’ union, which backed David Alvey for mayor in last year’s election, fell into a back-and-forth mud slinging with Holland that ended with the resignation of the KCK fire chief and Holland’s accusations of corruption in the fire department.
rewrite:
In Kansas City, Kansas, a recent incident has reignited friction between the local fire department and the city's prior mayor. An inquiry by the department found that firefighters activated a siren on their vehicle early Tuesday morning while near the residence of ex-mayor Mark Holland. According to officials, this occurred as the crew was heading back to the station following a medical response.

Holland stated the siren was switched off after the truck moved past his home. He later shared security footage of the event on social media, labeling it a form of targeted harassment.

The fire department issued a response, indicating the personnel involved would face appropriate measures to guarantee that sirens and emergency lights are used strictly according to established rules.

This episode is part of a longstanding adversarial history. The firefighters' union, which supported David Alvey in the most recent mayoral race, previously engaged in a bitter public dispute with Holland. That conflict culminated in the fire chief stepping down and Holland alleging misconduct within the department.

[India], December 11 (ANI): India's first Electronic Manufacturing Cluster (EMC) will be coming to Andhra Pradesh.
The Government of India, through the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeiTY), had announced in 2012 about setting up an EMC in India, with grant-in-aid for establishing such clusters.
An EMC is designed and developed for providing facilities and amenities for manufacturing mobiles and allied products.
In 2015, the Andhra Pradesh government announced the first exclusive mobile and electronic manufacturing cluster in the new capital, Amaravati.
A Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) called Sri Venkateswara Mobiles and Electronics Manufacturing Hub Private Limited was formed. The foundation stone was laid by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the same year. The SPV Company has applied for the final approval of the project. Three major Indian mobile manufacturers - Celkon, Karbonn and Lava have come forward to establish their units in the EMC. An anchor unit has been formed in the name of Seven Hills Digital Park Private Limited for the three companies. It will be involved in manufacturing of accessories to mobile phones and other related electronic equipment. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has allotted 113.27 acres of land for the new cluster, through Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (APIIC). Nara Lokesh, Minister of Information Technology and Communications, had said that the new EMC is being developed at the cost of Rs 104 crore. Around 50,000 jobs will be created every year in the cluster. (ANI)
rewrite:
On December 11, the news agency ANI reported that the inaugural Electronic Manufacturing Cluster (EMC) in India is slated for development in Andhra Pradesh. This initiative follows a 2012 declaration by India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, which proposed establishing such clusters nationwide with financial support. An EMC is a specialized zone created to offer comprehensive infrastructure and services for producing mobile devices and associated components.

In 2015, authorities in Andhra Pradesh designated the new capital region of Amaravati as the site for the country's premier dedicated cluster focused on mobile and electronics production. A dedicated entity, Sri Venkateswara Mobiles and Electronics Manufacturing Hub Private Limited, was incorporated as a Special Purpose Vehicle to oversee the project. Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone that same year. This SPV has now sought the last stage of official authorization for the venture. Three prominent domestic handset brands—Celkon, Karbonn, and Lava—have committed to setting up factories within the cluster. A central anchor entity, named Seven Hills Digital Park Private Limited, has been formed to support these three firms and will focus on producing mobile phone accessories and other electronic items.

The state's Chief Minister, N Chandrababu Naidu, has allocated 113.27 acres of land for the complex through the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation. According to IT and Communications Minister Nara Lokesh, the development cost for the new EMC is approximately 104 crore rupees. It is projected that the cluster will generate about 50,000 employment opportunities annually.

What do you do when you need to get in some last-minute preparation for the U.S. Women’s Open but the U.S. Women’s Open course is closed? You improvise.
With the remnants of subtropical storm Alberto dumping more than four inches of rain the last two days at Shoal Creek Golf Club, USGA officials kept players and spectators off the Birmingham, Ala., course on Tuesday . So reigning U.S. Women’s Open champion Sung Hyun Park sought out another place to practice, and showed up early Tuesday afternoon at the Topgolf Birmingham.
Chris Stevenson, a writer for The Athletic Ottawa, happened to go to the facility as well to pass the time, and stumbled upon Park hitting balls in a bay. He then shared Park’s swing on his Twitter account.
“People here and there were stopping to watch her,” Stevenson told GolfChannel.com. “I would hit two balls and turn around and watch her hit two. I asked her if I could take a video. She was gracious enough to say yes.”
With Shoal Creek still closed through Wednesday morning, fans might want to head to Topgolf to see who else shows up.
RELATED: U.S. Women's Open officials trying to sort things out as wet weather soaks Shoal Creek
rewrite:
How do you manage some final practice for the U.S. Women’s Open when the actual tournament venue is unavailable? You adapt creatively.

After subtropical storm Alberto left over four inches of rain at Shoal Creek Golf Club in Birmingham, Alabama, across two days, officials from the USGA prohibited access to the course for players and fans on Tuesday. This led the current champion, Sung Hyun Park, to find an alternative location for her training session. She arrived at Topgolf Birmingham shortly after noon that day.

By chance, Chris Stevenson, a journalist with The Athletic Ottawa, also visited the entertainment complex to occupy his time. He discovered Park practicing her shots in one of the bays and later posted a clip of her swing on Twitter.

Stevenson mentioned to GolfChannel.com that several individuals paused to observe her play. He described his own routine of hitting a couple of balls and then turning to watch her do the same. After requesting permission to record, Park kindly agreed.

Given that Shoal Creek remained shut through Wednesday morning, spectators might consider visiting Topgolf to spot other competitors who could appear for impromptu practice.

It will be a feast for both the ears and the eyes on Sunday in New Hampton, as the Carnegie Cultural Center will host “A Day of Art,” starting at noon with a performance by the University of Iowa College of Music piano students at Trinity Lutheran Church in New Hampton. Dr. Ksenia Nosikova and her students will perform masterpieces for your enjoyment.
Then Ann Bishop McGregor will be at the Carnegie Center at 3 p.m. to discuss her process and inspiration, as she captures the beauty of Northeast Iowa landscapes. McGregor’s work is currently on display in the CCC until Nov. 5. The exhibit is a pastel show entitled “Seeking the Sublime.” There will be an open house Sunday — a gallery talk and public reception at the Carnegie Center with McGregor — from 3-5 p.m. McGregor will be talking from 3-3:30 p.m.
For more of this article, see Friday's New Hampton Tribune.
rewrite:
This Sunday in New Hampton promises a rich sensory experience with "A Day of Art," hosted by the Carnegie Cultural Center. The event begins at twelve o'clock at Trinity Lutheran Church, where piano students from the University of Iowa's College of Music, under the guidance of Dr. Ksenia Nosikova, will present a concert of classic works.

Later, at 3 p.m., the focus shifts to the Carnegie Center for an open house featuring artist Ann Bishop McGregor. She will share insights into her creative methods and the influences behind her pastel depictions of Northeast Iowa's scenery. Her exhibition, "Seeking the Sublime," remains on view through November fifth. From three to five o'clock, a public reception will include a gallery talk, with McGregor speaking about her work from 3:00 until 3:30.

Further details can be found in the most recent edition of the New Hampton Tribune.

WASHINGTON (AP) — A chartered train carrying dozens of GOP lawmakers to a Republican retreat in West Virginia struck a garbage truck south of Charlottesville, Virginia, on Wednesday. No lawmakers were believed injured, but it at least one person in the truck was said to be seriously injured.
"We're fine, but our train hit a garbage truck. Members with medical training are assisting the drivers of the truck," Rep. Greg Walden, R-Ore., wrote on Twitter.
A GOP aide said the train is partially derailed.
Oklahoma GOP Rep. Tom Cole says a person on the truck may have been seriously injured.
Cole said he's not aware of any injuries on the train. A GOP aide speaking on condition of anonymity says no lawmakers were injured.
Cole said he believes the accident occurred south of Charlottesville, Virginia. The train was en route to the Greenbrier resort in White Sulfur Springs for a three-day issues retreat featuring appearances by President Donald Trump and Vice President Mike Pence.
Rep. Bradley Byrne, R-Ala., tweeted: "The train carrying GOP members to our retreat had a collision, but Rebecca and I are both okay. Security and doctors on board are helping secure the scene and treat injuries."
Cole said he felt "a tremendous jolt" when the accident occurred at about 11:15 a.m. EST, nearly two hours after it left Washington headed to the Greenbrier resort in White Sulphur Springs, W.Va.
He said the train stopped quickly after impact. He said several GOP lawmakers who are doctors got off the train to assist, including Rep. Brad Wenstrup, R-Ohio, who was also at last June's shooting of Republicans at a baseball practice in nearby Alexandria, Virginia, and treated some of the victims.
Other doctor-lawmakers who helped included Reps. Michael Burgess, R-Texas, Phil Roe, R-Tenn., and Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La.
Cole said the front of the train hit a vehicle that appeared to be a trash truck, which he said was torn in half. He said the accident apparently occurred at or near a crossing because he could see railroad crossing gates.
He said lawmakers had not been told when they would resume their trip to their retreat.
rewrite:
A train chartered for Republican members of Congress collided with a garbage truck in Virginia on Wednesday morning while traveling to a party gathering in West Virginia. While none of the legislators aboard are thought to be hurt, initial reports indicate at least one individual in the truck sustained serious injuries.

The incident occurred around 11:15 a.m. Eastern time, south of Charlottesville. The train was transporting lawmakers to a three-day policy retreat at the Greenbrier resort in White Sulphur Springs, an event scheduled to include addresses from President Donald Trump and Vice President Mike Pence. Representative Tom Cole, a Republican from Oklahoma, described feeling a powerful jolt upon impact, after which the train came to a swift stop.

According to a Republican aide, the train was partially derailed. Cole stated the front of the train struck a vehicle that looked like a trash truck, severing it in two, and noted the presence of railroad crossing gates, suggesting the accident happened at or near a crossing.

Several lawmakers with medical expertise immediately went to assist. Representative Greg Walden, an Oregon Republican, posted on social media that members possessing medical training were aiding the truck's drivers. Among those who provided help were Representatives Brad Wenstrup of Ohio, Michael Burgess of Texas, Phil Roe of Tennessee, and Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana. Notably, Wenstrup had also aided victims during the shooting at a congressional baseball practice last June.

Alabama Representative Bradley Byrne confirmed the collision in a post, stating he and his wife were unharmed and that security and medical personnel from the train were responding. Officials speaking anonymously confirmed no legislators were injured. There was no immediate information regarding when the journey to the retreat would continue.

NEW YORK Two Russian nationals arrested in the United States last October on charges of conspiring to export sensitive military technology from the United States to Russia were sentenced to time served on Friday, a spokesman for U.S. prosecutors said.
Dmitrii Aleksandrovich Karpenko, 33, and Alexey Krutilin, 27, both pleaded guilty on March 8 and were sentenced by U.S. District Judge Leo Glasser in Brooklyn. They have agreed to immediate deportation to Russia, where both live, the spokesman said.
U.S. prosecutors said the men planned to obtain microelectronics from manufacturers and suppliers in the United States and export them to Russia while evading government controls on high-tech exports.
The technology at issue included devices used in radar and missile guidance systems, prosecutors said. The United States restricts the export of items it believes could contribute to weapons proliferation and undermine U.S. national security.
Karpenko and Krutilin were arrested in Denver on Oct. 5 in a sting operation arranged by U.S. Department of Homeland Security agents posing as sellers, according to court filings.
In briefs filed in the Brooklyn court, lawyers for Karpenko and Krutilin said while the two men knew the purpose of their trip was illegal, they had been sent by their employer, a Russian company called Aelek, and did not plan the purchases themselves.
"We're grateful that Judge Glasser recognised the limited role that Mr. Karpenko and Mr. Krutilin played in the conspiracy," said Richard Levitt, a lawyer for Karpenko.
Raymond Granger, a lawyer for Krutilin, said his client was "extremely gratified" by the decision.
Prosecutors said last October that Karpenko and Krutilin conspired with Alexey Barysheff, a U.S. citizen living in Brooklyn who was also arrested. Prosecutors say Barysheff set up front companies to buy and export electronics.
Barysheff also has pleaded guilty and is scheduled to be sentenced on June 17, court records show.
(Reporting by Brendan Pierson in New York; Editing by Jonathan Oatis and Bill Trott)
rewrite:
In New York, two Russian citizens who were taken into custody last fall for allegedly plotting to smuggle advanced American military equipment to Russia received sentences equivalent to their time already spent in detention this past Friday, according to a representative from the U.S. attorney’s office.

Dmitrii Aleksandrovich Karpenko, age 33, and Alexey Krutilin, 27, each admitted guilt on March 8. Their sentencing was carried out by Judge Leo Glasser in a Brooklyn federal court. The spokesperson noted that both individuals have consented to be promptly deported back to their home country of Russia.

Authorities stated that the pair intended to acquire sophisticated microelectronics from American sources and illegally ship them to Russia, thereby bypassing strict controls on the export of sensitive technology. These components are applicable in systems such as radar and missile targeting, which are subject to U.S. trade restrictions due to potential risks to national security and arms control.

Their arrest occurred on October 5 in Denver following an undercover operation conducted by Homeland Security agents who acted as suppliers. Legal documents submitted in the case indicated that the defendants acknowledged the illicit nature of their activities but claimed they were acting under instructions from their employer, a Russian firm named Aelek, and were not the architects of the procurement scheme.

Attorneys for the men expressed appreciation for the court’s recognition of their clients’ minor roles in the operation. Karpenko’s lawyer, Richard Levitt, and Krutilin’s attorney, Raymond Granger, both conveyed their clients’ satisfaction with the judicial outcome.

The prosecution had previously alleged that Karpenko and Krutilin collaborated with Alexey Barysheff, a Brooklyn resident and U.S. citizen who was also apprehended. Barysheff is accused of establishing shell corporations to facilitate the purchases and exports. He has likewise entered a guilty plea and is awaiting sentencing scheduled for mid-June.

Saudi Arabia’s powerful heir apparent, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, is visiting Washington and other American cities this week promoting his image as an enlightened reformer out to modernize his conservative country and encourage foreign investment.
That image is stained by his chief foreign policy initiative, the humanitarian catastrophe that is the war in Yemen, in which at least 10,000 civilians have been killed, many as a result of indiscriminate airstrikes by the Saudis and their Persian Gulf partners. The United States has been Saudi Arabia’s main enabler, supplying weapons and other military aid.
President Trump is unlikely to use his meeting with the crown prince at the White House on Tuesday to try to persuade him to halt the war. Fortunately, some members of Congress want to exercise their constitutional responsibilities over how and when the United States wages war. A bipartisan resolution, ending American military involvement in Yemen within 30 days unless Congress formally authorizes it, could face a Senate vote as early as Tuesday. Other legislative efforts would block military aid to Saudi Arabia, including millions of dollars in arms sales.
These are sensible ways to help end the attacks, as the need for a political solution in Yemen, one of the poorest countries in the Arab world, grows more urgent by the day.

It has been wracked by civil war since 2014, when Houthi rebels allied with Iran, and forces loyal to former President Ali Abdullah Saleh, took control of the capital, Sana, and much of the rest of the country.
rewrite:
Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman of Saudi Arabia is touring the United States this week, aiming to bolster his reputation as a progressive leader dedicated to updating his nation's traditional society and attracting international capital. However, this portrayal is heavily marred by his primary international undertaking: the devastating conflict in Yemen. This war has led to a severe humanitarian crisis, with a minimum of 10,000 non-combatant deaths, numerous casualties stemming from reckless aerial bombardments conducted by Saudi Arabia and its allies from the Persian Gulf. The U.S. has played a key supporting role in this conflict by providing armaments and various forms of military assistance.

President Trump is not expected to pressure the Crown Prince during their White House meeting to cease hostilities. However, certain lawmakers are seeking to reclaim their mandated authority concerning American military engagements. A cross-party proposal, which would terminate U.S. military action in Yemen within a month absent formal congressional approval, may be voted on in the Senate soon. Additional proposed laws aim to cut off defense support to Saudi Arabia, halting substantial arms transactions.

Such measures represent prudent steps toward stopping the assault, as the necessity for a diplomatic resolution becomes increasingly critical in Yemen, among the Arab world's most impoverished nations. Since 2014, the country has been torn apart by internal strife, initiated when Houthi insurgents, supported by Iran, joined with troops following ex-President Ali Abdullah Saleh to seize the capital city of Sana and extensive other territories.

Legislators plan to introduce legislation on Wednesday that would require the Department of Transportation to implement a residential parking permit system in designated parts of the city — including much of northern Manhattan.
One proposed bill would cover all areas between 60th Street and Inwood and would allow the DOT to reserve as many as 80 percent of the parking spaces in certain areas for local residents.
Manhattan City Council members Mark Levine, Helen Rosenthal and Keith Powers said the measure is needed because so many park-and-ride commuters from outside the borough take up spots in residential neighborhoods and then hop on the subway.
“For too long suburban commuters have taken advantage of free street parking in Northern Manhattan and crowded out the people who actually live in our neighborhoods,” said Levine, a co-chair of the Manhattan delegation.
“Whether you live in Washington Heights or the Upper East Side, parking in our borough is an incredible challenge for so many who live here,” he added. “We can’t afford to continue as one of the only big cities in America that doesn’t have a residential parking permit system–this policy is long overdue.”
The legislation would limit permits to those with a New York State driver’s license, one permit per driver, and would be attached to a specific license plate.
Another bill, by Council Transportation Committee Chair Ydanis Rodriguez (D- Upper Manhattan), would seek a citywide residential permit parking system. It would require permit holders to pay yet-to-be-determined fees to park in their designated areas.
Rodriguez did not immediately return messages.
Both bills leave the determination of the parking hours and locations where parking would be reserved for permit-holders to the DOT, which in the past has expressed resistance to such programs.
A spokesperson for Council Speaker Corey Johnson said he’s reviewing the bills.
Reps for DOT and Mayor de Blasio’s office said they would review the legislation when introduced.
The bills faces at least one major hurdle — by some officials’ reckoning, Albany would have to give its permission to implement the program.
City DOT officials say they believe residential permit parking would require state approval.
Additional reporting by Danielle Furfaro
rewrite:
On Wednesday, lawmakers are set to propose new bills aimed at establishing a residential parking permit program in specified city zones, particularly across northern Manhattan. One legislative proposal would apply to neighborhoods from 60th Street up to Inwood, granting the Department of Transportation authority to designate up to 80% of on-street spaces in certain sections for community residents.

Manhattan City Council representatives Mark Levine, Helen Rosenthal, and Keith Powers argue the action is necessary due to an influx of commuters from outside the borough who occupy neighborhood parking before using public transit. Levine, who co-leads the Manhattan delegation, stated that suburban drivers have long used northern Manhattan’s free curbside parking, displacing local residents. He emphasized that securing parking anywhere in the borough, from Washington Heights to the Upper East Side, remains extremely difficult for inhabitants. Levine further noted that New York cannot remain an exception among major American cities without a residential permit system, calling the policy urgently needed.

Under the proposed law, permits would be issued only to individuals holding a New York State driver’s license, limited to one per driver and linked to a specific vehicle plate. A separate bill from Council Transportation Committee Chair Ydanis Rodriguez, representing Upper Manhattan, would pursue a permit system across the entire city. This version would involve fees for permit holders, though the amounts have not been set. Rodriguez was not available for immediate comment.

Both proposals would allow the DOT to decide the specific hours and locations where reserved parking would be enforced, despite the agency’s historical reluctance toward such programs. Council Speaker Corey Johnson’s office indicated he is evaluating the legislation, while representatives from the DOT and the mayor’s office said they will review the bills once formally introduced.

A significant obstacle remains: according to several officials, authorization from Albany would likely be required to enact any permit program. City DOT officials share the view that state approval is necessary. Reporting contributions were provided by Danielle Furfaro.

SEOUL, South Korea (AP) " South Korea has called up English Premier League stars Son Heung-min and Ki Sung-yeung for vital 2018 World Cup qualifiers against Iran and Uzbekistan.
South Korea needs at least four points from matches against Iran in Seoul on Aug. 31 and Uzbekistan in Tashkent five days later to be sure of heading to Russia next summer.
There have been injury concerns over both players. Son, who scored 21 goals last season for Tottenham Hotspur, fractured his arm for his country in a 3-2 loss in Qatar in June. Ki, the national team's captain, picked up a knee injury in the same game.
"There is more possibility of Ki playing in the second game," recently-appointed head coach Shin Tae-yong told a news conference Monday. "I have been in regular contact with him and with some new players in the squad, we need players like Ki."
Advertisement
Ki did not feature for Swansea City in its opening league 0-0 draw at Southampton on Saturday.
There was better news regarding Son, who appeared as a second-half substitute for Spurs in an opening day 2-0 win at Newcastle, wearing a bandage on his arm.
Shin, in charge for his first game after Uli Stielike was fired in June following a third loss in five qualifying matches, also recalled 38-year-old striker Lee Dong-gook in his 26-man roster.
South Korea sits second in Group A in the third round of Asian qualifying, seven points behind the already-qualified Iran and just a point ahead of Uzbekistan.
Only the top two in both six-team groups progress automatically to Russia. The third-place teams from Groups A and B will meet in an October two-match Asian elimination game for the right to enter a final play-off against CONCAFAF's fourth-placed team.
rewrite:
South Korea's national soccer team has selected two prominent players from England's top football division for crucial upcoming matches in the quest to reach the 2018 World Cup. Son Heung-min and Ki Sung-yeung are included in the squad for the important qualifying games against Iran and Uzbekistan.

To secure a place in next year's tournament in Russia, the team must earn a minimum of four points from these two fixtures. They will first host Iran in Seoul, followed by an away match against Uzbekistan in Tashkent.

Both athletes have been dealing with physical issues. Son sustained an arm fracture while playing for his national team in June. Ki, who serves as team captain, injured his knee during the same contest.

The newly appointed head coach, Shin Tae-yong, indicated that Ki is more likely to be available for the second match. He emphasized the veteran's importance to the team, especially with newer players in the lineup. Ki was absent from his club's first league match of the season over the weekend.

There is encouraging progress regarding Son's recovery. He recently played in his club's season opener, entering the game in the second half while wearing protective arm support.

Coach Shin, leading the team for the first time after the previous manager was dismissed, has also called up experienced forward Lee Dong-gook, aged 38, in his selection of 26 players.

In the current Asian qualifying stage, South Korea holds the second position in its group. It trails Iran, which has already secured its World Cup spot, by seven points and leads Uzbekistan by a single point.

Only the top two finishers from each six-team group will advance directly to the World Cup. The teams that finish third will compete in a subsequent Asian playoff in October. The winner of that playoff will then face the fourth-place team from the CONCACAF region for a final chance to qualify.
