The Baker Spartans were plagued by penalties and fell to the Huntley Project Red Devils 37-0 last Friday night.
By Cameron MacKay & Aaron Smith
The Baker Spartans were plagued by penalties and fell to the Huntley Project Red Devils 37-0 last Friday night. This loss takes the Spartans to 3-2 on the year with both losses being conference games. Keenan Reynolds, Lane Sumner and Tylan Croy were among the Red Devils that gave the Spartans trouble. In the first quarter, Huntley found the end zone by way of Keenan reception from Tylan, PAT no good. The Spartans were stood up inside the 10 yard line of Huntley late in the second quarter and turned the ball over on downs. The Red Devils capitalized on the turnover and scored along TO run by Lane, PAT no good, making it 12-0 at half.
In the second half, the scoreboard again was ruled by Huntley Project. Tylan not only threw a touchdown to Keenan, PAT good by Croy, but also recovered an unlucky snap that went over the punter’s head from the Spartans for a touchdown, PAT no good. Lane then had another rushing touchdown with the PAT no good. The last score of the game was a pass from Tylan to Keenan with another failed PAT.
The Spartans rushed well with their leading rusher being Dalton Herbst-Holestine on 35 carries for 116 yards, with Morgan Rising behind him with 13 carries for 71 yards. The Spartans were led in tackles by Dalton with 8, along with Andrew Craft and Trevor Lingle both with 6 tackles. Javon DeGrand had a blocked extra point attempt. The Spartans travel to Shepherd to take on the Mustangs on Oct. 6 at 7 p.m.
rewrite:
In a Friday night matchup, the Baker Spartans were defeated by the Huntley Project Red Devils with a final score of 37-0, a performance hindered by numerous penalties. This outcome brings Baker's season record to three wins and two losses, with both defeats occurring in conference play. Key players for Huntley Project, including Keenan Reynolds, Lane Sumner, and Tylan Croy, posed significant challenges for the Spartans throughout the contest.

The Red Devils opened the scoring in the initial quarter when Tylan Croy connected with Keenan Reynolds for a touchdown; the point-after attempt was unsuccessful. Baker advanced deep into Huntley Project territory late in the second period but was stopped short on fourth down, turning possession over. The Red Devils promptly converted this opportunity into points, with Lane Sumner breaking free for a touchdown run. Another missed extra point left the halftime score at 12-0.

Huntley Project continued to dominate after the break. Tylan Croy threw his second touchdown pass to Keenan Reynolds, and this time the point-after by Croy was successful. Croy also scored on a special teams play, recovering a wayward snap on a Spartan punt attempt and returning it for a touchdown, though the extra point failed. Lane Sumner added another rushing touchdown, again with a missed PAT. The final points came from another Croy-to-Reynolds passing touchdown, with the extra point attempt once more unsuccessful.

For the Spartans, Dalton Herbst-Holestine led the ground attack, accumulating 116 yards on 35 carries, followed by Morgan Rising with 71 yards on 13 attempts. Defensively, Dalton Herbst-Holestine recorded eight tackles, while Andrew Craft and Trevor Lingle each made six. Javon DeGrand contributed by blocking an extra point. Baker looks ahead to its next game, an October 6th road contest against the Shepherd Mustangs scheduled for 7 p.m.

Democratic Sen. Tammy Duckworth expressed concern Sunday about the way the executive branch is handling the immigration crisis, but stopped short of joining her liberal colleagues in the Senate calling to abolish US Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
"I think there's a lot of other things we can do before we get to that point," Duckworth told CNN's "State of the Union" anchor Jake Tapper. "First of which, which is, you've got somebody in the White House who has these policies which are horrendous, which he still hasn't fixed. Families are still separated. Children are still in cages. Nursing babies are still separated from their moms."
The Illinois senator's comments come after some of her Democratic colleagues, including New York Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand and Massachusetts Sen. Elizabeth Warren, called for ICE to be abolished during protests over the weekend.
Duckworth said that the crisis of undocumented immigrant children being separated from their families is rooted in policies enacted by President Donald Trump's administration.
"I think if you abolish ICE as it is as an executive agency, it reflects the policies of the White House, of the President," she said. "You abolish ICE now, you still have the same President with the same failed policies, whatever you replace it with is just still (going to) reflect what this President wants to do."
Duckworth wasn't the only Midwestern Democratic lawmaker who stopped short of calling for ICE to be eliminated. Minnesota Sen. Amy Klobuchar also said on ABC's "This Week" Sunday that the crisis was rooted in poor policies.
"I think what has to change are the policies, and the people that are making these policies are making horrendous decisions like separating kids from their parents," Klobuchar said. "We are always going to need immigration enforcement. ... So to me, the issue is what are those policies, and please let's get comprehensive immigration reform, something I've strongly supported for years."
Duckworth also told CNN that she has not received a response from the White House to a letter asking how the administration plans to reunite immigrant children with their families.
"(My concern is) that they don't have a plan. That's my suspicion," Duckworth said. "I don't think they even really know where all of the children are and who these children belong to."
rewrite:
On Sunday, Senator Tammy Duckworth, a Democrat, voiced her unease regarding the executive branch's management of the immigration situation. However, she did not align herself with fellow progressive senators who are advocating for the dissolution of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. During an interview on CNN's "State of the Union" with host Jake Tapper, Duckworth suggested there are numerous alternative steps to consider prior to taking such a drastic measure. She emphasized that the current administration's approach remains deeply problematic, noting that family separations persist, children are still detained in inadequate facilities, and infants are being taken from their mothers.

These remarks follow calls from other Democratic senators, such as Kirsten Gillibrand of New York and Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, to dismantle ICE amid recent demonstrations. Duckworth, representing Illinois, traced the core of the issue to the policies implemented under President Donald Trump. She argued that simply eliminating ICE in its current form would be insufficient, as the agency merely carries out directives from the White House. Without a change in leadership and its underlying agenda, any replacement organization would likely continue to enforce the same objectionable practices, she contended.

Duckworth was not alone among Democrats from the Midwest in hesitating to endorse the abolition of ICE. Senator Amy Klobuchar of Minnesota, appearing on ABC's "This Week," similarly attributed the crisis to flawed policy decisions rather than the agency itself. Klobuchar stressed that the nation will always require mechanisms for immigration enforcement, but the critical focus must be on altering the specific policies that lead to harmful outcomes, such as separating families. She reiterated her long-standing support for a broad overhaul of immigration laws as the necessary solution.

Additionally, Duckworth revealed that she has yet to receive a reply from the White House concerning a letter she sent inquiring about plans to reunite separated immigrant children with their families. She expressed her apprehension that the administration may lack a coherent strategy, suspecting that officials might not even have full knowledge of the whereabouts of all the children or their familial connections.

* NORBORD REPORTS RECORD 2017 EARNINGS; DECLARES QUARTERLY DIVIDEND
* Q4 ADJUSTED EARNINGS PER SHARE $1.41
* “DEMAND IN ALL OUR CORE MARKETS REMAINS STRONG”
* IN NORTH AMERICA, EXPECT NEW HOME CONSTRUCTION ACTIVITY AND OTHER OSB END USES TO SUPPORT FURTHER DEMAND GROWTH
* ‍ FUNDAMENTALS IN KEY MARKETS REMAIN FAVOURABLE AND LOOK FORWARD TO FURTHER GROWTH FROM ALL SEGMENTS OF BUSINESS​
* REPORTED Q4 AND FULL-YEAR 2017 INCOME TAX EXPENSE INCLUDES NON-RECURRING $35 MILLION NET RECOVERY
* EUROPEAN BUSINESS IS “POISED FOR IMPROVED EARNINGS” NEXT YEAR AS OSB SUBSTITUTION FOR PLYWOOD DRIVES ACCELERATED DEMAND GROWTH
* ‍ PRODUCTION FROM EXPANDED INVERNESS MILL WILL NOT INCREASE MARKEDLY FROM 2017​
* NORBORD‘S 2018 CAPITAL EXPENDITURE BUDGET IS $175 MILLION FOR PROJECTS
* Q4 EARNINGS PER SHARE VIEW $1.26, REVENUE VIEW $617.7 MILLION -- THOMSON REUTERS I/B/E/S
* ‍ BELIEVE WILL SEE FURTHER PRICE MOMENTUM IN 2018 IN RELATION TO EXPANDED INVERNESS MILL​ Source text for Eikon: Further company coverage:
rewrite:
On February 2nd, Reuters reported on Norbord Inc.'s financial results. The company announced its highest annual earnings to date for 2017 and issued a dividend for the quarter. For the final quarter, adjusted earnings reached $1.41 per share. Management expressed that robust demand continues across all primary markets. In North America, they anticipate that new residential building and other applications for oriented strand board (OSB) will lead to increased demand. The outlook for major markets is positive, with expectations for expansion in every business division.

The income tax figures for both the fourth quarter and the entire year include a one-time net benefit of $35 million. The European division is expected to achieve better profitability in the coming year, as OSB continues to replace plywood, speeding up demand growth. Output from the enlarged Inverness facility is not projected to rise significantly compared to 2017 levels. Norbord has allocated $175 million for capital projects in 2018. Analyst estimates, according to Thomson Reuters I/B/E/S, projected fourth-quarter earnings at $1.26 per share and revenue at $617.7 million. The company also forecasts continued positive price trends for 2018 linked to the Inverness mill expansion.

Officials in Van Zandt County are searching for three missing teens.
The Edgewood Police Department and surrounding local agencies are looking for what they are calling 3 runaways between the ages of 13 and 16 years old.
Cheyenne Andrews, Bryan Nyman, and Steven Shumate reportedly went missing from their residence in the 2400 block of Van Zandt County Road 3504 near Wills Point. All three kids were living in the same foster home for about 4 years. They are not related. According to the Van Zandt County Sheriff's Office, none have a prior history of running away.
Officials say they are reaching out to the biological families but so far this is not being treated as an abduction.
The Sheriff's Office says to their knowledge, two of the children have an intellectual disability.
The City of Edgewood confirms currently, a ground and air search are being conducted with the Sheriff's Department, local agencies, and the Van Zandt County Game Warden.
The city says if you are interested in volunteering you can call the Sheriff's department at 903-567-4133 and add your name to a list. Coordination of volunteers will begin this afternoon after 1:00 p.m. All civilian volunteers should to report to the Edgewood fire station
The City of Edgewood posted to their Facebook page that there are 2 males, wearing white t-shirts, and one female who is wearing a pink backpack who are currently missing.
If you know of their whereabouts you are asked to contact officials immediately.
Copyright 2017 KLTV. All rights reserved.
rewrite:
Authorities in Van Zandt County are actively seeking three adolescents who have disappeared. The Edgewood Police, along with other area law enforcement, are attempting to locate these individuals, described as runaways aged 13 to 16. The missing youths—Cheyenne Andrews, Bryan Nyman, and Steven Shumate—were last seen at their foster home on Van Zandt County Road 3504, close to Wills Point. Having resided together in that foster placement for approximately four years, the trio are not biologically related. The Van Zandt County Sheriff's Office notes there is no record of any previous runaway incidents involving them.

Investigators have been in contact with the teens' birth families; however, the situation is not presently considered an abduction. According to the Sheriff's Office, two of the juveniles are believed to have an intellectual disability.

A coordinated search effort, involving both ground teams and aerial assets, is underway with participation from the Sheriff's Department, local agencies, and the county Game Warden. Community members wishing to assist may volunteer by calling the Sheriff's Office at 903-567-4133 to be placed on a list. Volunteer coordination is scheduled to commence after 1:00 p.m. today, with all civilians asked to gather at the Edgewood fire station.

An official social media update describes the missing persons as two males in white t-shirts and one female carrying a pink backpack. Anyone with information on their location is urged to contact authorities without delay.

Copyright 2017 KLTV. All rights reserved.

Puertolas defeated Westrick, 6-2, 6-2, at No. 4, while Lucich recorded a 6-4, 6-2, win at No. 5 over Schille and Ortega Vela finished off the match with a 6-1, 7-5, victory against Sivam at No. 6.

SEATTLE (KGTV) -- Newly released body camera footage shows the moment police officers nabbed a pair of thieves trying to walk out of a Seattle-area Costco carrying $2,200 worth of laptops and vacuums.
On March 14, South Precinct officers responded to a call at about 5:30 p.m. of a shoplift in progress at the Costco, police said. Loss Prevention officers inside the store recognized one of the suspects inside and said he had previously stolen items in the past and run out the fire exit.
Responding Seattle Police Department officers spotted a female driver inside a black Toyota that was backed up to the store's emergency exit doors. The officers pulled their patrol vehicle in front of the Toyota to prevent it from leaving and contacted the 18-year-old woman, police said.
As police were talking with the woman, they could hear someone attempting to open the doors.
"Moments later, two suspects, a 30-year-old man and a 21-year-old woman opened the emergency doors and attempted to walk out of the store carrying stolen computers and vacuum cleaners," police said.
Officers located a 7″ fixed blade from the male suspect. According to the security personnel, the suspect had carried a large knife in past incidents.
The male suspect was later booked into the King County Jail for investigation of robbery, while the two women were booked for investigation of theft, police said.
rewrite:
Recently unveiled police body camera video captures the apprehension of two individuals attempting to leave a Costco near Seattle with stolen electronics and cleaning appliances valued at approximately $2,200. According to authorities, South Precinct officers were dispatched to the warehouse store on the evening of March 14 following reports of an active shoplifting incident. Store security personnel identified one of the alleged thieves, noting he had a history of stealing merchandise and escaping via the fire exit.

Upon arrival, officers observed a black Toyota sedan positioned near the store's emergency doors with a young woman inside. To block a potential getaway, the police car was moved to obstruct the Toyota, and officers made contact with the 18-year-old driver. While speaking with her, the officers heard noises from someone trying to open the emergency doors from within.

Shortly after, a man and a woman, aged 30 and 21 respectively, emerged through those doors carrying the purportedly stolen laptops and vacuums. Police discovered a fixed-blade knife on the male suspect. Security staff reported that this individual had been armed with a large knife during previous thefts. The man was subsequently arrested on suspicion of robbery, while both women were taken into custody for alleged theft. All three were processed at the King County Jail.

Sligo Rovers boss Gerard Lyttle described his side's FAI Cup loss to Longford Town as "upsetting, embarrassing and hurtful" as he vowed to repay the fans with a big performance.
Sligo host Bray Wanderers on Tuesday night in the SSE Airtricity Premier Division in desperate need of three points.
They're second bottom, three points off ninth-placed Finn Harps having played a game more, and the 4-2 extra-time defeat to First Division Longford was another big blow to morale.
Lyttle admitted the performance was way off what's expected, but is confident his team will respond.
"It was disappointing, upsetting, embarrassing, hurtful," he said.
"We weren’t good enough and everybody knows what. We spoke for an hour in the dressing-room after the game and the players were more vocal then they’ve been before.
"I believe in our players. We are sticking together and as a club we need to stick together. It’s a big job ahead and there’s no shying away from that.
"The players played with fear last Saturday and I don’t want my team to play like that. I’ve told them to go out and express themselves, believe more in themselves, to focus and show they are better that what we saw."
Sligo are without Jamie McDonagh due to suspension but otherwise have a clean bill of health.
Lyttle is now hoping a big effort at the Showgrounds can get the fans back on side and earn a crucial victory.
"The supporters were unhappy last Saturday and rightfully so," he added. "I know what they are feeling. They are right to voice it.
"On Tuesday night we play this game against a difficult opponent but we have to keep positive. It’s what we’ve tried to do for our players and when the game starts on Tuesday I want our supporters to do what they’ve done all season and get behind us once more.
"It’s going to take a huge effort but this club is capable of it. We’ve done well at home, it’s a hard place for teams to come and we can make it even harder by uniting behind the cause and do all we can to get three points."
rewrite:
Gerard Lyttle, the manager of Sligo Rovers, characterized his team's FAI Cup elimination at the hands of Longford Town as a profoundly negative experience, using terms like "distressing, humiliating, and painful." He committed to making amends to the club's supporters with a significantly improved display. The focus now shifts to a critical league encounter this Tuesday, as Sligo welcomes Bray Wanderers to the Showgrounds in urgent pursuit of a win.

The club's position is precarious, sitting just above the relegation zone and trailing the team directly above them, while also having contested an additional match. The recent cup defeat, a 4-2 loss after extra time against a side from the lower division, has further damaged team spirit. Lyttle acknowledged the display fell far short of acceptable standards but expressed faith in his squad's ability to react positively.

He elaborated on the post-match atmosphere, noting an extended and unusually candid discussion in the locker room where players were particularly vocal. Lyttle emphasized his continued belief in the group, the necessity for unity within the entire club, and the scale of the challenge ahead. He identified fear as a factor in the previous performance, instructing his team to play with greater freedom, self-confidence, and concentration to demonstrate their true quality.

With Jamie McDonagh unavailable through suspension, the squad is otherwise at full strength. Lyttle's aim is for a determined performance to regain fan support and secure a vital result. He understood and validated the supporters' frustration, acknowledging their right to express it. While recognizing the difficulty of the upcoming fixture, he called for maintained positivity, urging the fans to replicate their season-long backing and create a united front.

He concluded by stressing that a monumental collective effort is required, but one within the team's capability. Highlighting their strong home record as a formidable venue for visitors, Lyttle believes that by rallying together, they can enhance that advantage and do everything possible to secure the three points.

By Udeme Akpan
Nigeria’s youth unemployment, estimated at 40 million youths would soon drop as the Federal Government has short listed 300,000 youths for immediate training and engagement.
The youths, drawn from the 36 States of the federation were short listed from a total of 2.5 million who applied for the programme this year.
The Senior Special Adviser to the Presidency on Jobs Creation and Youths Empowerment, Afolabi Imokhuede, who confirmed the development, said the youths would be attached to reputable organisations with capacity to train them in areas such as renewable energy, oil and gas, construction and agriculture.
According to him, the training would last for three months while attachment to organisations would last for about one year.
He said that such organisations may grant some of them permanent employment, while others would have to form clusters to enable them offer professional services to operators in different sectors of the nation’s economy.
The management of Lagos Deep Offshore Logistics Base (LADOL) also disclosed that it would assist to train and build the capacity of youths in many areas, including oil and gas, fabrication and welding.
The company disclosed this when the United State Trade and Development Agency (USTDA) its premises noted that has commended the Lagos Deep Offshore Logistics Base (LADOL) as a safe haven for investment and having great capacity for job creation in the African sub-region.
Investigations showed that the action of the government would go a long way towards complementing the efforts of the private sector to enhance capacity building and employment in the nation.
It showed that many stakeholders have started to show interest in tackling the issues as a result of its negative impact on the nation’s economy.
rewrite:
By Udeme Akpan  
The high level of joblessness among young Nigerians, which currently affects an estimated 40 million individuals, is expected to decline in the near future. This follows the federal government’s selection of 300,000 young people for rapid skills development and placement. These candidates were chosen from across all 36 states, out of a pool of 2.5 million applicants this year.

Afolabi Imokhuede, the Senior Special Adviser to the Presidency on Job Creation and Youth Empowerment, verified the initiative. He explained that participants will be assigned to established organizations capable of providing instruction in fields like renewable energy, oil and gas, construction, and agriculture. The formal training phase is set to last three months, followed by a placement period of approximately one year with these organizations.

Imokhuede added that some participants may secure permanent roles with these companies, while others will be encouraged to form cooperative groups. These clusters would then provide specialized services to businesses across various economic sectors.

In a related development, the management of the Lagos Deep Offshore Logistics Base (LADOL) announced its commitment to developing youth skills in areas such as oil and gas, fabrication, and welding. This pledge was made during a visit by the United States Trade and Development Agency (USTDA), which recognized LADOL as a secure investment destination with significant potential for generating employment in the region.

Analysis indicates that this government effort will substantially support private sector actions aimed at improving skills development and job availability in the country. The severe economic consequences of youth unemployment have prompted a growing number of stakeholders to engage with the problem.

A Florida couple was found dead next to their vehicle on a highway Saturday morning, while their three young children were discovered in the backseat unharmed, police said.
According to the Orlando Sentinel, Volusia County Sheriff’s Office spokesman Andrew Gant said that a state trooper found the vehicle at around 2:08 a.m. It was parked on the eastbound side of Interstate 4 near DeLand with its hazard lights on.
Authorities found Daniel Kelsey, 32, and Heather Kelsey, 30, unconscious outside the SUV with their three young sons – ages ranging between eight months and four years – sitting in the backseat, Gant said. The parents were pronounced dead at the scene,
The children were transferred to Halifax Health Medical Center in Daytona Beach as a precautionary measure, according to the Sentinel. Family services is expected to meet with the children in an effort to assist with the investigation.
Gant said police were still investigating the incident. There were no signs of foul play.
Click for more from the Orlando Sentinel.

Officials identified the couple as Daniel Kelsey, 32, and Heather Kelsey, 30. They were found unresponsive outside the vehicle. Their three boys, the youngest eight months old and the oldest four years, were unhurt in the back. The parents were declared dead at the location.

As a precaution, the children were taken to a hospital in Daytona Beach. Child welfare services will connect with them to aid the ongoing inquiry. Police indicated the case remains under investigation, with no current evidence suggesting criminal activity.

The Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association (TSSAA) Board of Control approved the addition of a Unified Track & Field event at their recent meeting on Monday, August 14, 2017. This competition, which will initially begin as an Invitational Championship, is to be first implemented during the 2018 Spring Fling Championships. The decision marks the beginning of a partnership between TSSAA and Special Olympics Tennessee in Unified Sports.
Dedicated to promoting social inclusion through shared sports training and competition experiences, Unified Sports joins students with and without intellectual disabilities on the same team. It was inspired by the principle that practicing and competing together promotes inclusion and understanding to help break down stereotypes.
TSSAA member schools with existing Unified Track & Field programs will have until October 1 to notify Special Olympics Tennessee of their desire to participate. For the inaugural year, eight teams will be invited by Special Olympics Tennessee to take part in the event. The TSSAA desires to officially sanction the sport of Unified Track & Field in subsequent years, involving more schools and implementing qualifying sectionals.
Bernard Childress, Executive Director of the TSSAA, expressed excitement over the partnership with Special Olympics Tennessee. “Special Olympics Tennessee has done amazing work in our state for a long time and we are thrilled to be working with them to enhance our State Championship experience. The addition of Unified Sports and the relationship we have begun with Special Olympics will have an extremely positive impact on athletics and student-athletes across our state. Whenever we can make a decision that provides opportunities for more student-athletes, that is a direction we want to go.”
Alan Bolick, President of Special Olympics Tennessee, stated his appreciation to the Board of Control and staff of TSSAA and echoed similar sentiments. “The establishment of this unique partnership will no doubt have a positive influence on creating more inclusive environments in our public and private schools as well as the communities in Tennessee where these athletes live.”
Events included in the inaugural TSSAA Unified Track & Field Invitational will be the 100 meter Dash, 400 meter Run, 4×100 meter Relay, Shot Put, and Long Jump. The Unified Track & Field events will be incorporated into the existing Spring Fling Track & Field schedule, with individual medals awarded and a Unified Track & Field Champion and Runner-up team decided.

Unified Sports is designed to foster social inclusion by uniting students with and without intellectual disabilities on athletic teams. The foundation of this initiative is the belief that shared training and competition build mutual respect and dismantle prejudices, thereby cultivating greater acceptance.

Schools under the TSSAA umbrella that already run Unified Track & Field programs must inform Special Olympics Tennessee of their intent to compete by October 1. For the first year, Special Olympics Tennessee will extend invitations to eight teams. The TSSAA aims to grant full sanctioning to Unified Track & Field in future seasons, which would expand participation to additional schools and introduce preliminary sectional qualifying meets.

Bernard Childress, the TSSAA Executive Director, shared his enthusiasm for the new alliance. These events will be integrated into the current Spring Fling Track & Field program. The competition will recognize individual medalists and will also crown an overall Unified Track & Field Champion team and a Runner-up team.

A white elephant gift exchange is a holiday tradition where a group of friends, family members or coworkers exchange useless and wacky gifts during a holiday party.
You can either play by Secret Santa rules or each person draws a number to determine who goes first. The person who draws number one chooses a gift and opens it for everyone to see. Each person after that can either steal an already opened gift from someone before them or he/she can choose an unopened gift.

A white elephant gift swap is a festive custom in which participants gather to trade impractical and humorous presents. This activity typically follows one of two formats: either adopting a Secret Santa approach or having each individual select a number to establish the order of turns. The participant with the first pick selects a wrapped gift and reveals it to the group. Subsequent players then decide whether to take an already revealed item from a previous person or to choose a new, unopened package.

When an item is claimed by another player, the person who lost it then selects a fresh gift from the remaining unopened ones. This sequence proceeds until everyone has had a turn. RICHMOND HEIGHTS, Ohio (KRON/CNN) — A nurse in Ohio is now out of a job after deciding she was too sick to work.
She says the hospital she worked for fired her after she got the flu.
We know this flu season is worse than normal, and when one “fill-in” nurse at University Hospitals said she was too sick to work two times over the course of a few days, it violated hospital policy.
Just after Christmas Theresa Puckett was hardly a picture of good health.
She called out sick once at the end of 2017, and when she came back, a superior sent her home early because she was still fighting off the flu.
“I was putting in my cough drops, I was drinking my water, I was putting in my Mucinex,” Puckett said. “I mean, the whole nine yards just to patch myself up enough to go to work.”
That led to another sick day, opening her up to being fired because of UH’s policy that temporary nurses called PRNs, like Theresa, may be dismissed after two non-approved absences over 60-days.
Theresa says it speaks to the nursing and hospital culture, keeping hospitals staffed no matter what the consequences.
“But when it happened to me, and I really truly was too sick to go to work, I was punished for that,” Puckett said. “I was punished for staying home with a doctor’s note.”
UH has a “no-fault” attendance policy, where the hospital says “notes from a physician do not ‘excuse’ an occurrence of absence.”
The policy says only approved leaves of absence, workplace illnesses or injuries, scheduled paid time off–like vacation time or doctors appointments–or jury duty or bereavement leave are considered excused.
That means even Theresa’s note from her own doctor saying she shouldn’t interact with people who are already sick wasn’t enough.
rewrite:
An Ohio nurse has been dismissed from her position after reporting she was too ill to report for duty, stating the termination followed a bout of influenza. This occurs during a notably severe flu season. The nurse, employed as a per diem or PRN staff member at University Hospitals, missed work twice within a short span, which constituted an infraction of the institution's attendance guidelines.

Theresa Puckett was unwell shortly after the Christmas holiday. She initially called in sick near the end of 2017. Upon returning, a supervisor directed her to leave early as she was still exhibiting flu symptoms. Puckett describes attempting to manage her condition with various remedies just to be able to work. This subsequent absence, following closely on the first, made her subject to dismissal under a policy stating that temporary nursing staff can be terminated after two unexcused absences within a sixty-day period.

Puckett believes this reflects a broader institutional mindset that prioritizes maintaining staffing levels above all else. She feels penalized for being genuinely ill and for heeding medical advice to stay home, even with a physician's documentation. The hospital enforces a "no-fault" attendance system where a doctor's note does not automatically justify an absence. According to the policy, only pre-approved time off, scheduled paid leave, certain workplace incidents, or specific civic obligations are considered excused. Consequently, Puckett's medical note advising her to avoid contact with vulnerable patients was deemed insufficient, leading to her job loss.

Related Coverage Brewin’ up with Coal Yard Coffee
INDIANAPOLIS (WISH) — We’re talking this java morning.
24-Hour News 8’s Dick Wolfsie is on a tour of local coffee shops.
First up, he headed down to the south side to check out Strange Brew Coffee in Greenwood.
The locally-owned shop has been open for about 14 years. Owner Daniel Carr says it is the oldest coffee shop in Greenwood and is all about creating a community feel.
“We have local artists that we give space to,” Carr said. “We don’t take profits from their sales. What they sell is what they get. And we rotate them out every once and a while. So, we like to support the local art community.”
What do customers think of the shop?
“People from all sorts of walks of life come in here, they enjoy their products,” said Andrew Dills. “It’s just wonderful place for drinks and gathering and a sense of oneness.”
Next up, Dick popped up to Rabble Coffee on the east side just near 10th and Rural streets.
General Manager Josie Hunckler highlighted what the shop is doing for the community.
“We have a pay-it-forward system,” Hunckler said. “There’s a lot of scarcity in our neighborhood and we’re just trying to, like, help feed people and get people coffees. So what you can do here is you can buy a burrito or a medium coffee for someone else.”
The company has a token system to help with their pay-it-forward system.

The establishment supports area artists by providing display space without taking any commission; the artists keep all earnings from their sold work. These exhibits are changed periodically to feature new creators.

Customer Andrew Dills shared his perspective, noting the diverse clientele and praising the spot as an excellent location for beverages, socializing, and community.

The tour then moved to Rabble Coffee on the east side, near the intersection of 10th and Rural streets. General Manager Josie Hunckler explained their community outreach effort: a pay-it-forward initiative. Recognizing local needs, the cafe allows patrons to purchase a medium coffee or a burrito for someone in need. To facilitate this, the shop uses a token system to manage the charitable donations.

The unprecedented flow of leaks coming out of the American intelligence community about President Donald Trump and members of his inner circle does not appear to be stemming anytime soon. Tonight, the New York Times published a report based on the account of anonymous U.S. intelligence officials detailing how “phone records and intercepted calls show that members of Donald J. Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign and other Trump associates had repeated contacts with senior Russian intelligence officials in the year before the election.” The Times notes that U.S. intelligence “intercepted the communications around the same time that they were discovering evidence that Russia was trying to disrupt the presidential election by hacking into the Democratic National Committee.”
The National Security Agency, which monitors the communications of foreign intelligence services, initially captured the communications between Mr. Trump’s associates and Russians as part of routine foreign surveillance. After that, the F.B.I. asked the N.S.A. to collect as much information as possible about the Russian operatives on the phone calls, and to search through troves of previous intercepted communications that had not been analyzed.
…
But the intercepts alarmed American intelligence and law enforcement agencies, in part because of the amount of contact that was occurring while Mr. Trump was speaking glowingly about the Russian president, Vladimir V. Putin. At one point last summer, Mr. Trump said at a campaign event that he hoped Russian intelligence services had stolen Hillary Clinton’s emails and would make them public.
The officials said the intercepted communications were not limited to Trump campaign officials, and included other associates of Mr. Trump. On the Russian side, the contacts also included members of the Russian government outside of the intelligence services, the officials said. All of the current and former officials spoke on the condition of anonymity because the continuing investigation is classified.
rewrite:
The steady stream of confidential disclosures from U.S. intelligence agencies concerning former President Donald Trump and his close allies shows no signs of abating. In a recent article, the New York Times cited unnamed intelligence sources who revealed that communications records and monitored calls indicate frequent interactions between individuals affiliated with Trump's 2016 campaign and high-level Russian intelligence operatives during the period leading up to the election. According to the report, these intercepts occurred as agencies were also uncovering Russian efforts to interfere in the electoral process through cyber intrusions targeting the Democratic National Committee.

Routine surveillance of foreign intelligence channels by the National Security Agency first recorded these exchanges between Trump connections and Russian officials. Subsequently, the Federal Bureau of Investigation requested the NSA to gather extensive data on the Russian individuals involved and to examine previously collected but unexamined communications archives.

These intercepted discussions raised significant concerns within American intelligence and law enforcement circles. This was partly due to the frequency of the contacts, which coincided with Trump publicly praising Russian President Vladimir Putin. During the campaign, Trump once expressed hope that Russian intelligence had obtained Hillary Clinton's emails and would release them.

The sources indicated that the monitored interactions extended beyond Trump campaign staff to include other figures in his orbit. On the Russian end, participants also involved government officials not directly part of intelligence services. All officials providing this information requested anonymity due to the classified nature of the ongoing investigation.

Portia Woodman scored eight tries as New Zealand hammered Hong Kong 121-0, while there were also wins for Canada, England, USA, Ireland and France on day two of the Women’s World Cup in Dublin.
Playing with pace and power, the Blacks Ferns steamrolled Hong Kong, with Woodman at the centre of the 19-try rout. New Zealand ran in nine first-half tries for a commanding 57-0 lead at the break and they more than doubled that tally with 10 tries in the second stanza. The bonus-point victory takes New Zealand top of the log in Pool A.
Canada ground out 15-0 win against Wales with Lori Josephson and Magali Harvey dotting down. The result means Canada are now one point behind New Zealand in the standings.
In Pool B, England registered a comfortable 56-13 bonus-point win over Italy. Danielle Waterman, Lydia Thompson and Emily Scarratt scored two tries each.
The USA also collected maximum log points with a 43-0 triumph against Spain. The bonus-point win puts the USA and England are level on 10 points apiece and means the forthcoming match between the sides will be a straight shootout for a spot in the semi-finals.
Ireland needed a strong second half performance to beat a gallant Japan outfit 24-14. Japan led 14-0 at half time, but the hosts came to life in the last 25 minutes to the win.
France lashed Australia 48-0 in the last game of the day. The win takes the French two points clear of Ireland at the summit of the Pool C standings.
Photo: World Rugby
rewrite:
On the second day of the Women's Rugby World Cup in Dublin, New Zealand delivered a dominant performance, overwhelming Hong Kong with a score of 121-0. Portia Woodman was the standout, crossing the line for eight of her team's nineteen tries. Demonstrating speed and strength, the Black Ferns built a 57-0 halftime lead from nine tries and added ten more after the interval. This decisive bonus-point win placed them at the top of Pool A.

Canada secured a 15-0 victory over Wales, with tries from Lori Josephson and Magali Harvey, moving them to within a point of New Zealand. In Pool B, England earned a bonus point with a 56-13 win against Italy, featuring two tries each from Danielle Waterman, Lydia Thompson, and Emily Scarratt.

The United States also claimed maximum points, defeating Spain 43-0. This result leaves the USA and England tied at ten points, setting up their next encounter as a direct decider for a semi-final berth. Ireland mounted a second-half comeback to overcome a resilient Japan team 24-14, after trailing 14-0 at halftime. Concluding the day, France powered past Australia 48-0, giving them a two-point advantage over Ireland at the top of Pool C.

Newlywed actress Jessica Chastain is in talks to take on a villain role in the next X-Men film.
Producer/screenwriter Simon Kinberg will make his directorial debut on X-Men: Dark Phoenix, and according to Deadline.com, Chastain has been tapped to tackle the character Shi’ar Empress Lilandra.
Franchise stars Jennifer Lawrence, Michael Fassbender, James McAvoy, and Nicholas Hoult will all return for the next movie, as will Sophie Turner, Tye Sheridan, and Kodi Smit-McPhee, who joined the cast for 2016’s X-Men: Apocalypse.
Kinberg is also producing the project, alongside Hutch Parker and Lauren Shuler Donner. He has long been involved with the X-Men franchise and wrote 2006’s X: Men: The Last Stand, in addition to writing and producing X-Men: Days of Future Past and X-Men: Apocalypse. He also produced X-Men: First Class and Deadpool, while he is involved in its upcoming sequel, and is working on X-Men: The New Mutants, which comes out next year.
X-Men: Dark Phoenix will focus on Game of Thrones’ Turner as powerful young mutant Jean Grey, also known as Dark Phoenix. It is set for release in November, 2018.
Lawrence previously ruled herself out of returning to the X-Men franchise, but admitted she would reconsider if she was allowed to play Mystique alongside Chris Pratt’s Star-Lord in a Guardians of the Galaxy film.
“I won’t be Mystique in the X-Men movies, but I would love to be Mystique in Guardians Of The Galaxy,” she said. “I wonder if I could do that?”
Meanwhile, one person who will not be returning to the franchise is Hugh Jackman. The actor recently completed his last run as Wolverine in spin-off film Logan.

Reports indicate Chastain is being considered for the part of Lilandra, the empress of the Shi’ar. They will be joined by Sophie Turner, Tye Sheridan, and Kodi Smit-McPhee, who were introduced in *X-Men: Apocalypse* in 2016.

The narrative of *Dark Phoenix* will center on Sophie Turner's character, Jean Grey, a formidable mutant who transforms into the Dark Phoenix. Its premiere is scheduled for November 2018. Conversely, Hugh Jackman has definitively concluded his tenure as Wolverine, following his final performance in the standalone feature *Logan*.

PINELLAS COUNTY, Fla. (WFLA) — On Saturday, U.S. Representative Charlie Crist (D – St. Petersburg) will meet with community leaders, parents and teenagers to try and find a solution for the growing problem of teens stealing cars in Pinellas County.
The Pinellas County Sheriff has called this issue an epidemic.
Crist will also sit down with non-profit and community leaders for a panel discussion on how to get young people more engaged.
This comes after local, county and state leaders met over the summer with parents and teens to try and identify why this is happening.
“The takeaway from our meeting last summer was that kids are hungry for programs aimed at their interests. It was also clear we need to do a better job letting them know what’s currently available. With that in mind, our office will be hosting a local youth program expo this Saturday,” said Crist. “It will bring together non-profits working with at-risk youth, so they can share information on what’s being offered to children, their parents, and community leaders. I’m hopeful it might also lead to some synergy and partnerships between the organizations participating.”
The event Saturday is free and open to the public. It will be held at the Childs Park Recreation and Fitness Center in St. Petersburg from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m.
Teen vehicle thefts have been a problem in Pinellas County for months now.
On Feb. 1, four teenagers were arrested after police say they tried to hit officers with a minivan they had stolen in St. Petersburg.
Last August, three teens with lengthy criminal records died in a crash in Palm Harbor while playing a game of “cat and mouse” in two stolen vehicles. In a news conference after the crash, Pinellas County Sheriff Bob Gualtieri described the incident as “an unfortunate continuation of the epidemic of juveniles engaging in the deadly game of auto burglary and auto thefts.”
Back in March of 2016, three teenage girls were found dead inside a car that drove into a St. Pete pond. All three girls had criminal histories which included grand theft auto.
rewrite:
In Florida's Pinellas County, U.S. Congressman Charlie Crist, a Democrat representing St. Petersburg, has scheduled a meeting for this Saturday with local parents, youths, and community figures. The goal is to address the escalating issue of juvenile auto theft, which the Pinellas County Sheriff has termed an epidemic. Crist will further participate in a forum with leaders from non-profit and community groups to explore ways of increasing youth involvement.

This gathering follows discussions held earlier in the summer among municipal, county, and state officials, along with families and adolescents, which sought to understand the root causes of this trend. Crist noted that the summer meeting revealed a strong desire among young people for activities aligned with their passions, alongside a need to improve communication about existing opportunities. In response, his office is organizing a public youth program exposition this Saturday. The expo will convene non-profits that serve vulnerable young people, providing a venue to inform children, their parents, and community leaders about available resources. Crist expressed optimism that the event could also foster collaboration and new alliances among the attending organizations.

The free community event will take place from 10 a.m. until noon at the Childs Park Recreation and Fitness Center in St. Petersburg.

For several months, Pinellas County has struggled with a pattern of vehicle thefts committed by teenagers. In early February, four adolescents were taken into custody after allegedly attempting to strike police officers with a stolen minivan in St. Petersburg. A tragic incident last August in Palm Harbor claimed the lives of three teens with extensive criminal histories; they crashed two stolen cars while reportedly playing a reckless "cat and mouse" pursuit. Following that crash, Pinellas County Sheriff Bob Gualtieri stated it represented a sad extension of the widespread problem of minors participating in the dangerous pursuits of car burglary and theft. In a separate 2016 event, three teenage girls, all with prior records that included auto theft, were discovered deceased in a vehicle that had submerged in a St. Petersburg pond.

LIVERPOOL, England (Reuters) - Everton manager Ronald Koeman said Wayne Rooney, who scored on his return to the club in the 1-0 win over Stoke on Saturday, was far from a spent force and showed exactly why he was the right signing for the club.
Rooney's move back to his boyhood club, after 13 successful years at Manchester United, divided opinion between those who viewed it as a welcome romantic return and those who felt he was not the right player for Koeman's new-look side.
But in his first Premier League outing Rooney not only scored the winner with a beautifully executed header from a Dominic Calvert-Lewin cross, but he also exuded quality and composure throughout.
"There was one player in an Everton shirt today who was, from the first second to the last, comfortable on the pitch," said the Dutch manager.
"He made every decision the right one and he scored a great goal from a great cross from Dominic.
"In difficult moments, he showed his experience. That is why we signed Wayne -- expecting to show his team-mates all that experience, and it was really important," he said.
Rooney last scored a goal for Everton at Goodison on March 13, 2004 when he claimed the winner against Portsmouth.
That gap of 4,869 days is the longest between goals for the same club in the Premier League. The header was his 300th involvement in a goal in the Premier League, with 101 assists to add to his 199 goals. Only Alan Shearer, with 324, has more.
And he joined Shearer and Frank Lampard with the most goals on the league's opening day - eight.
Koeman not only believes that Rooney fits perfectly into his plans at Everton, but he also thinks he is far from the faded force that many felt he was becoming at United.
"Wayne showed he is still one of the best players in his position and he showed today the player that we expected," said Koeman.
"A lot of cleverness on the pitch and a great goal and a great header. We can't ask for more than he showed today."
rewrite:
LIVERPOOL, England (Reuters) – Following a 1-0 victory against Stoke, Everton's head coach Ronald Koeman stated that Wayne Rooney’s performance in his first match back for the club demonstrated he remains a potent player and was an ideal acquisition.

Rooney’s transfer to his original team, following a lengthy and trophy-filled spell with Manchester United, sparked debate. Some saw it as a sentimental homecoming, while others questioned his suitability for Koeman’s evolving squad.

However, in his initial league appearance, Rooney did more than just net the decisive goal with a superb header from a Dominic Calvert-Lewin delivery. He displayed consistent class and calm control during the entire game.

Koeman noted that a single Everton player appeared completely at ease from start to finish. He stated that this player made consistently correct choices and converted an excellent chance from a fine cross. During challenging phases of play, his veteran savvy was evident, which Koeman identified as a key reason for bringing him to the club: to guide his teammates with that know-how.

Rooney’s previous goal for Everton at Goodison Park was a match-winning strike against Portsmouth on March 13, 2004. The interval of 4,869 days between those goals sets a Premier League record for the longest time between scoring for the same club. This header also marked his 300th direct goal contribution in the competition, combining 199 goals with 101 assists. Only Alan Shearer, with 324, has a higher total.

Additionally, Rooney equaled the record shared by Shearer and Frank Lampard for the most goals scored on the Premier League’s opening day, with eight.

Koeman is convinced that Rooney aligns well with his vision for Everton and rejects the notion that the player’s abilities had significantly diminished during his later period at United. He affirmed that Rooney proved he remains among the top talents in his role, exhibiting the intelligence and quality anticipated. Scoring a magnificent header and contributing so effectively, according to Koeman, meant Rooney delivered everything that could be asked for in the match.

By Eric Heinz
A 27-year-old man died after crashing his vehicle while traveling at a “high speed” on Pacific Coast Highway at Doheny Park Plaza in Dana Point on Sunday morning, Jan. 1, according to Orange County Sheriff’s Department Officials.
Pacific Coast Highway at the area was closed off until 7:30 a.m. Sunday morning and lanes in both directions were open as of 9:30 a.m., officials said.
Lt. Lloyd Downing, the department commander handling public relations for the case, said the man was driving in rainy conditions at 2:30 a.m. near Doheny Park Plaza when he lost control of his vehicle, struck a pole, was ejected from his car and subsequently run over by an oncoming motorist.
Downing said the other motorist who struck the ejected man was not cited in the incident. Downing also said the speed of the driver hasn’t been determined.
A name of the man has not yet been released. No other factors were listed as contributing to the incident. The Orange County Coroner’s Office will make the final determination on factors that contributed to the death.
If you have any information regarding the incident, call the Orange County Sheriff’s Department at 949.770.6011.
Editor’s note: This is a developing story. More information will be provided when it is available.
rewrite:
A man aged 27 lost his life in a single-vehicle collision early on New Year's Day in Dana Point. The crash occurred along Pacific Coast Highway near Doheny Park Plaza, as confirmed by the Orange County Sheriff’s Department. Authorities reported that the driver was moving at a significant rate of speed amidst rainy weather around 2:30 a.m., which led to a loss of control. The vehicle then hit a pole, causing the driver to be thrown from the car. Tragically, he was then struck by another vehicle passing through the area.

The roadway in both directions was shut down until approximately 7:30 a.m. and had fully reopened by 9:30 a.m. that Sunday morning. Lieutenant Lloyd Downing, the department's spokesperson for this case, indicated that the other driver involved was not issued a citation. The exact speed of the deceased driver remains undetermined at this time.

The identity of the man has not been disclosed, and no additional contributing circumstances have been identified. The Orange County Coroner’s Office will ultimately establish the official cause of death. Anyone with details about this event is asked to contact the Orange County Sheriff’s Department at 949.770.6011. This report is being updated as further information emerges.

MANILA, Philippines – The Department of Justice (DOJ) will begin its preliminary investigation into the criminal charges filed against 6 suspects involved in a major drug bust operations in San Juan City on Tuesday, January 3.
The suspects – Chinese nationals Shi Gui Xiong alias "Xiong," Che Wen De aka "Jacky Tan," and Wu Li Yong alias David Go, as well as their alleged Filipino cohorts Abdullah Mahmod Jahmal, Salim Cocodao Arafat, and Basher Tawaki Jama – will be facing prosecutors at 10:30 am for violation of the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002.
The 6 suspects were arrested following several raids in houses in Mangga Street, Barangay Little Baguio and Bonifacio Street in San Juan.
Charges were filed against them before the DOJ for the manufacture and sale of illegal drugs on December 27. Inquest proceedings were conducted before Assistant State Prosecutors Mary Jane Sytat and Ethel Rhea Suril.
The drug busts in San Juan City were part of a 4-month long operation led by the National Bureau of Investigation.
The operation, considered as the biggest so far under President Rodrigo Duterte’s term, led authorities to recover 890 kilos of shabu with a street valued pegged at around P3 million.
Assisted by their legal counsels, the suspects have all agreed to file their counter-affidavits during the prelimineray investigation. They, however, have waived their right to immediate resolution of charges for their immediate release. – Rappler.com

The group, comprising three Chinese citizens identified as Shi Gui Xiong (also known as "Xiong"), Che Wen De (referred to as "Jacky Tan"), and Wu Li Yong (alias David Go), along with three Filipino associates named Abdullah Mahmod Jahmal, Salim Cocodao Arafat, and Basher Tawaki Jama, will appear before prosecutors. They are accused of breaching the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002.

Represented by their attorneys, all accused have consented to submit rebuttal affidavits in the preliminary phase. Nonetheless, they have relinquished their entitlement to a prompt resolution of the charges, which would have allowed for quicker release from custody.

The Borussia Dortmund team bus is seen after an explosion near their hotel before their Champions League quarter-final first leg game against AS Monaco in Dortmund, Germany. REUTERS/Kai Pfaffenbach/Livepic
BERLIN German prosecutors have doubts about the authenticity of letters that suggested Islamist militants attacked soccer team Borussia Dortmund's bus and a newspaper cited an investigator as saying right-wing extremists were probably behind the bomb attack.
Three identical letters printed in German found near the scene of Tuesday's attack in Dortmund had stated it was carried out "in the name of Allah", broadcaster ARD reported, citing other media. The letters referred to the use of Tornado reconnaissance planes in Syria, which Germany has deployed as part of the military campaign against Islamic State.
But a report commissioned by investigators said there were "significant doubts" about the letters and suggested they had been written to trick people into thinking there was an Islamist militant motive, ARD added.
"That's accurate," Frauke Koehler, a spokeswoman for the federal public prosecutor's office, said when asked to comment on the ARD report.
"It is indeed doubtful," she said of the letters.
Asked why there were doubts, she said she could not give any more information as the investigation was ongoing.
Bild newspaper cited an investigator as saying: "The overall circumstances lead us to believe it's most likely that the perpetrators have a right-wing background."
Koehler declined to comment on that report.
German newspaper Tagesspiegel said on its website on Friday it had received an anonymous far-right email claiming responsibility for Tuesday's attack. It said the email referred to Adolf Hitler, railed against multiculturalism and suggested another attack might occur on April 22.
Koehler said prosecutors had received a copy of the letter but she could not comment further.
The Borussia Dortmund players' bus was heading to their stadium for a Champions League match against AS Monaco on Tuesday when three explosions occurred, injuring Spanish defender Marc Bartra.
Experts have been expressing scepticism for days about the origins of the letters claiming responsibility. Security sources have said investigators are looking at whether left or right-wing extremists may have carried out the attack.
A day after the attack, the interior minister of the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia described the letters as "unusual".
(Reporting by Michelle Martin; Editing by Alison Williams)
rewrite:
Following an explosion near their hotel prior to a Champions League match in Dortmund, the Borussia Dortmund team bus was photographed. German authorities are now questioning the legitimacy of letters that initially pointed to an Islamist militant involvement in the bombing. According to media reports, three similar documents recovered near the site referenced Germany's military role in Syria and claimed the act was committed for religious reasons.

However, a forensic analysis ordered by officials indicates serious reasons to question the letters' genuineness, proposing they may have been planted to mislead the inquiry by suggesting a false terrorist motive. A spokesperson for the federal prosecutor's office confirmed these doubts exist, though she could not elaborate due to the active investigation.

In contrast, one newspaper has quoted an investigator stating that evidence currently points toward a right-wing extremist origin for the attack. Separately, a different German publication reported receiving an anonymous far-right message claiming responsibility; this communication contained historical references and anti-immigrant rhetoric, along with a threat of future violence. Prosecutors acknowledged receiving this message but offered no additional details.

The explosion occurred as the team traveled to face AS Monaco, resulting in an injury to one player. For several days, specialists have been cautious about attributing the attack based on the initial letters. Security personnel are examining possibilities across the political spectrum, including both left-wing and right-wing extremism. The day after the incident, a regional interior minister characterized the discovered letters as atypical.

March 31 Royal Dutch Shell Plc plans to double the capacity of its liquefied natural gas import facility at Hazira on India's west coast to 10 million tonnes a year, a top company executive said on Friday.
Shell Gas B.V, a unit of Royal Dutch Shell Plc, owns a 74 percent stake in Hazira LNG Ltd, while Total Gaz Electricite France, a unit of France's Total SA, holds the rest.
"We've done all the work, now it's sort of taking a look at when is the right timing in terms of demand that's available," Nitin Prasad, chairman of Shell Companies in India, told Reuters, without giving a timeline for the expansion.
A government panel said in a report in April 2015 that Hazira LNG will look to expand the capacity of its LNG terminal in the western state of Gujarat by 50 percent to 7.5 million tonnes per annum in the fiscal year to March 2017.
Shell on Friday opened a new technology centre in Bengaluru, the capital of the southern state Karnataka. The technology hub, Shell's third in the world, is aimed at expanding the company's research and development activities in Asia.
India aims to raise the share of natural gas in its energy mix to 15 percent in the next three years from about 6.5 percent at present, as it attempts to achieve energy security while keeping pollution levels down.
India's gas imports in April 2016-February 2017 rose 16.4 percent to 22.53 billion cubic metres, according to government data. (Reporting by Arathy S Nair and Tanvi Mehta in Bengaluru; Editing by Subhranshu Sahu)
rewrite:
On Friday, a senior official from Royal Dutch Shell announced the company's intention to expand its liquefied natural gas terminal in Hazira, India. The planned upgrade will increase the facility's annual capacity to 10 million tonnes, which is double its current volume. Shell Gas B.V., a subsidiary of Royal Dutch Shell, holds a 74% interest in the Hazira LNG venture, with the remaining 26% owned by Total Gaz Electricite France, a part of France's Total SA.

Nitin Prasad, who chairs Shell's operations in India, informed Reuters that the necessary preparatory work for the expansion is complete. He stated the company is now evaluating the optimal timing for the project based on future market demand, though he did not provide a specific schedule. This follows a 2015 government report which indicated that the Hazira terminal was expected to increase its capacity to 7.5 million tonnes annually by March 2017.

In a related development, Shell inaugurated a new global technology center in Bengaluru, Karnataka, on the same day. This facility, the company's third worldwide, is designed to bolster its research and development efforts across Asia. The expansion aligns with India's national goal to significantly increase the proportion of natural gas in its energy consumption. The country aims to boost gas usage from the current 6.5% to 15% within three years, seeking to enhance energy independence and reduce environmental pollution. Government figures show that India's gas imports for the period from April 2016 to February 2017 grew by 16.4%, reaching 22.53 billion cubic metres.

Scrooge is transported to Kelowna in New Vintage Theatre’s new holiday play, opening Wednesday
Head to the Rotary Centre For The Arts this week for a classic Christmas play with a promised Kelowna twist.
New Vintage Theatre’s new holiday play brings the holiday’s infamous Scrooge to the streets of Kelowna.
Adapted for the stage by Artistic Director Bonnie Gratz, A Kelowna Christmas Carol incorporates the beloved elements of Dickens’s original story; Scrooge, the Cratchits and an adorable Tiny Tim, and places them in Kelowna at a pivotal period of the city’s history.
“Our play looks at the character of Scrooge in a very unique way. I have incorporated stories of Kelowna historical figures such as one of the city’s first doctors Dr. Benjamin Boyce and his wife, Mary; Countess Bubna, the exotic first owner of The Eldorado, then called The Eldorado Arms Hotel; Frank and Nell DeHart and Mar Jok. Arthur Knox, the land magnet that owned almost all of Kelowna from Water Street to The Mission, plays an important role, too,” said Gratz.
Another surprising element of this production will be the community members that are set to take part in the play as hosts.
Those hotsts include: Dom Rampone, Mayor Colin Basran, Councillor Maxine DeHart, Marianna DeHart and Linda Digby of Kelowna Museums, who assisted New Vintage in the research stage of play development.
Gratz said the play has already received a huge response from the community and there are just a few tickets remaining for evening and matinee shows.
Tickets are available from www.rotarycentreforthearts.com or The Rotary Centre For The Arts Box Office.
A Kelowna Christmas Carol by Bonnie Gratz runs Dec.13-21 at The Rotary Centre For The Arts.
Public shows are at 7 p.m. on Dec.14, 15, 16 and 21 with a matinee on Dec.17 at 2 p.m.
For more about New Vintage, check out their website at www.newvintage.ca.
To report a typo, email:
newstips@kelownacapnews.com.
@carmenweld
carmen.weld@bpdigital.ca
Like us on Facebook and follow us on Twitter.
Graham Daley and Vince Walzak in A Kelowna Christmas Carol. Photo Credit: Alison Beaumont
rewrite:
This holiday season, New Vintage Theatre presents a fresh seasonal production that reimagines a timeless tale with local flair. Opening this Wednesday, the play transports the iconic character of Scrooge to the setting of Kelowna. Audiences can experience this novel adaptation at the Rotary Centre for the Arts.

Artistic Director Bonnie Gratz has penned this adaptation, titled *A Kelowna Christmas Carol*. It retains the core characters from Charles Dickens’s classic—including Scrooge, the Cratchit family, and the endearing Tiny Tim—but situates their narrative within a significant era of Kelowna’s own past.

Gratz describes a distinctive approach to the well-known story, weaving in accounts of actual local historical personalities. These figures include Dr. Benjamin Boyce, among the city's inaugural physicians, and his wife Mary; the distinctive Countess Bubna, original proprietor of the establishment known then as The Eldorado Arms Hotel; and community members Frank and Nell DeHart alongside Mar Jok. The influential landowner Arthur Knox, who once possessed much of the area from Water Street to The Mission, also features prominently in the plot.

Adding to the local engagement, several notable community members will participate in the production as special hosts. Among them are Dom Rampone, Mayor Colin Basran, Councillor Maxine DeHart, Marianna DeHart, and Linda Digby from Kelowna Museums, who provided research support during the play's development.

Gratz notes that community interest has been exceptionally high, with limited seating still available for both evening and afternoon performances. Tickets can be purchased via the Rotary Centre for the Arts website or directly at their box office.

*Bonnie Gratz's A Kelowna Christmas Carol* will be staged from December 13th through the 21st. Evening performances are scheduled for 7 p.m. on December 14th, 15th, 16th, and 21st, with a 2 p.m. matinee on December 17th.

Further information about New Vintage Theatre is available on their official website.

Manta rays are some of the sea’s most graceful creatures, capable of gliding almost effortlessly and able to swim efficiently even in turbulent water. Now, researchers at the National University of Singapore have created a robot that mimics the manta.
Dubbed “MantaDroid,” the cute little bot is about 14 inches long and 25 inches wide and weighs 1.5 pounds. Using its pair of flexible pectoral fins, each powered by a single electric motor, it’s able to swim for up to 10 hours.
“Manta rays are known to be extremely efficient swimmers,” Chew Chee Meng, an associate professor in the university’s department of mechanical engineering, told NBC News MACH in an email. “We wanted to explore an alternative solution to traditional propeller-based thrusters that are used by most autonomous underwater vehicles.”
The robot could be used for search and rescue operations, as well as to perform underwater surveys and inspections, like those conducted by environmental groups. It could even be deployed in swarms for faster, more efficient searches and surveys, according to the researchers.
The engineers spent two years testing 40 different fin designs, aiming to recreate how real-life manta rays thrust forward by flapping their fins to drive water backwards. They say the MantaDroid achieved “good maneuverability” when tested in a pool. The bot was able to swim at a top speed of 2.3 feet per second — equivalent to almost 1.6 miles per hour.
Like its real-life counterpart, the MantaDroid has a wide, flat body, which means it could be equipped with multiple sensors on its “belly.” And the fins seem to have big benefits over propellers, Meng said. In addition to being less likely to get tangled in aquatic plants, they cause less turbulence than props.
“As a whole, MantaDroid tends to have less environmental impacts on marine ecosystems,” Meng said.
Meng and his colleagues want to test the MantaDroid in a marine environment to study its swimming ability at various depths, and to gauge its ability to handle currents.
The engineers are also working to make the bot autonomous.
“We plan to incorporate sensors and implement perception algorithms on the current prototype to make MantaDroid autonomous after we have completed the maneuverability study and design optimization,” Meng said.
rewrite:
In the ocean, manta rays are among the most elegant swimmers, moving with minimal effort and maintaining efficiency even in rough waters. Inspired by this natural design, scientists from the National University of Singapore have developed a robotic imitation.

This small robot, named MantaDroid, measures roughly 14 inches in length and 25 inches in width, weighing just 1.5 pounds. It employs two pliable pectoral fins, each driven by one motor, allowing it to operate underwater for as long as ten hours.

Chew Chee Meng, an associate professor of mechanical engineering at the university, explained via email that manta rays exhibit remarkable swimming efficiency. The research team aimed to move beyond conventional propeller systems, commonly found in autonomous underwater vehicles, by exploring this bio-inspired approach.

Potential applications include search and rescue missions, along with underwater monitoring and inspection tasks, such as those carried out by ecological organizations. The researchers note that groups of these robots could work together to accelerate and improve the effectiveness of such operations.

Over two years, the engineering team experimented with 40 distinct fin shapes to replicate the natural manta ray motion, which involves flapping fins to push water backward. Pool tests demonstrated that MantaDroid possesses strong maneuvering capabilities, reaching a maximum velocity of 2.3 feet per second, or nearly 1.6 miles per hour.

Similar to an actual manta, the robot has a broad, flat underside, providing ample space to mount various sensing devices. Meng highlighted that the fins offer significant advantages compared to propellers. They are less prone to entanglement in seaweed and generate reduced water disturbance.

Overall, MantaDroid is designed to minimize disruption to delicate ocean habitats, according to Meng.

Future plans involve sea trials to evaluate the robot’s performance at different ocean depths and its capacity to navigate currents. Additionally, the team is focused on achieving full autonomy for the device.

Meng stated that once studies on maneuverability and design improvements are finished, the intention is to integrate sensors and perception software into the existing model, enabling MantaDroid to operate independently.

The man, who lived in the area, suffered cuts, bruises and other possible injuries, but his actual condition was not available.
The accident happened at 12:18 p.m. Wednesday at the intersection of 14th and Brush streets.
Police said the man was in a marked crosswalk in his scooter going east across Brush Street when he was hit by a tractor rig pulling an end-dump trailer.

A safety warning has been voiced by police after a rise in incidents involving drones.
Northumbria Police are issuing a safety message to all drone users after an increase in popularity.
Superintendent Sarah Pitt.
Officers say they are causing concerns and could cause hold ups and risks to plane journeys of they are flown close.
They have also warned about the legality of using them in crowded areas.
Superintendent Sarah Pitt, Northumbria Police’s operations department, said: “The public need to be aware that if we identify them as flying in restricted areas then they could be prosecuted.
“Some users don’t realise these types of aircraft are subject to rules and legislation.
"We need to ensure we do our part to keep the public safe and informed.
“You should always keep your drone within your line of sight and always fly your drone away from helicopters, aircrafts, airports and airfields; those found violating these rules could face prosecution.
“Flying these types of aircraft within 150 metres of a crowded area is a criminal offence and may infringe air safety legislation.
“Not only could flying drones in the flight paths of aircrafts cause major delays, some of which come at a great cost, but it could also put members of the public at risk and it will not be tolerated.”

Authorities additionally highlighted the illegal nature of operating drones in populated spaces.

Superintendent Pitt, from the force's operations department, emphasized that the public must understand that flying in prohibited zones could lead to legal action. Ducati MotoGP rider Andrea Dovizioso of Italy rides during the Japanese Grand Prix at the Twin Ring Motegi circuit in Motegi, north of Tokyo, Japan, October 11, 2015.
(Reuters) - Ducati's Andrea Dovizioso held off MotoGP points leader Marc Marquez to claim his third victory of the season at the Austrian Grand Prix on Sunday.
Italian Dovizioso, who started on a soft rear tyre, took the lead with seven laps to the finish line and maintained a slender advantage over Honda riders Marquez and Dani Pedrosa, who completed the podium.
Dovizioso's team mate Jorge Lorenzo finished fourth despite taking an early lead in dry conditions at the Red Bull Ring, while Johann Zarco finished fifth.
Yamaha endured a disappointing afternoon with Maverick Vinales and Valentino Rossi taking the sixth and seventh spot, respectively.
Alvaro Bautista secured an eighth-placed finish for Aspar Ducati, with Avintia Ducati's Loris Baz ended ninth.
KTM wildcard Mika Kallio beat last year's winner Andrea Iannone to the 10th spot.
Marquez leads the championship standings with 174 points, 16 ahead of second-placed Dovizioso. Vinales slipped to third spot with 150 points, followed by Rossi on 141.
rewrite:
At the Austrian Grand Prix on Sunday, Ducati competitor Andrea Dovizioso secured his third win of the MotoGP season, narrowly defeating current championship leader Marc Marquez. The Italian rider, beginning the race with a soft compound rear tire, moved into first position with seven laps remaining. He then managed to keep a slight edge over Honda's Marquez and Dani Pedrosa, who joined him on the podium.

Dovizioso's teammate, Jorge Lorenzo, initially led in the dry conditions at the Red Bull Ring but ultimately finished in fourth. Johann Zarco took fifth place. It was a difficult day for Yamaha, as Maverick Vinales and Valentino Rossi could only achieve sixth and seventh positions. Alvaro Bautista came eighth for Aspar Ducati, while Loris Baz of Avintia Ducati was ninth. Mika Kallio, riding as a wildcard entry for KTM, claimed tenth, finishing ahead of the previous year's victor, Andrea Iannone.

In the overall standings, Marquez remains in front with 174 points, holding a 16-point advantage over Dovizioso in second. Vinales is now third with 150 points, followed closely by Rossi with 141.
