The Supreme Court (SC) on Tuesday halted the Quezon City government from implementing a resolution that increases the city’s real property tax rates from 100 percent to 500 percent.
During an en banc session in Baguio City, the high court issued a temporary restraining order halting the implementation of Ordinance No. 2556 (Series of 2016).
The Alliance of Quezon City Homeowners’ Association questioned the ordinance that adjusts the fair market value of lands, houses and other structures.
Named respondents were Quezon City Mayor Herbert Bautista, the City Assessor’s Office and City Treasurer’s Office.
The SC ordered the Quezon City government to file its comment within 10 days from the receipt of the order.
Mayor Herbert Bautista welcomed the court’s ruling but he urged the SC to resolve the case “the soonest possible time.”
“We have yet to receive an official copy of the decision but the Quezon City government welcomes the development. We pray that the SC will resolve the matter the soonest possible time to ensure the smooth operations of the delivery of basic services to its constituents,” he said.
In a separate statement, the city’s Public Affairs’ office said that the city was “compelled” to adjust the fair market values of real properties after the Department of Finance and the Commission on Audit directed the city government to implement the “long-delayed” adjustment as mandated by Section 219 of Republic Act 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991. Jomar Canlas and Dempsey Reyes
rewrite:
On Tuesday, the Supreme Court intervened to stop the Quezon City administration from enforcing a measure that would raise real estate tax rates by up to fivefold. The high court, meeting in Baguio City, granted a temporary restraining order against Ordinance No. 2556 from 2016. This ordinance, which revises the assessed market value of land and buildings, was challenged by the Alliance of Quezon City Homeowners’ Association. The case lists Mayor Herbert Bautista, along with the City Assessor’s and Treasurer’s Offices, as respondents. The Court has directed the city to submit its response within ten days of receiving the order.

Mayor Bautista expressed approval of the ruling while asking for an expedited resolution. He stated that although an official copy is pending, the city views the development positively and hopes for a swift decision to maintain uninterrupted public services. Separately, the city’s Public Affairs office explained that the tax adjustment was undertaken in response to directives from the Department of Finance and the Commission on Audit. These agencies instructed the city to proceed with the update, which had been postponed for some time, as required by the Local Government Code of 1991.

SUNRISE, Fla. — Jonathan Huberdeau scored with 7.7 seconds left in the third period to lift the Florida Panthers to a 3-2 victory over the Detroit Red Wings on Saturday night.
Aleksander Barkov and Aaron Ekblad also scored for the Panthers. Harri Sateri made 26 saves for his third straight NHL win. Keith Yandle had two assists.
Danny DeKeyser scored both goals for Detroit and Petr Mrazek stopped 30 shots in his third straight start.
With the score tied at 2, Huberdeau slid a rebound under Mrazek’s pad from inside the crease. The goal was challenged for goalie interference by Detroit but the call stood.
Barkov broke a 1-1 tie with his goal with 6:22 left in the second period. Evgenii Dadanov passed to Barkov in the high slot and Barkov skated in and beat Mrazek on the glove side.
DeKeyser tied it with his second of the game. Sateri blocked a shot and the bouncing puck went off DeKeyser’s skate as he crashed the net and went across the goal line at 3:00 of the third period.
Ekblad’s goal gave the Panthers a 1-0 lead at 3:14 of the first. Ekblad took a pass from Huberdeau in the slot and backhanded the puck off the post and into the net.
DeKeyser tied the score when his shot from the slot went over Sateri’s shoulder on the stick side at 8:51 of the second.
NOTES: Panthers D Alex Petrovic played his 200th NHL game. … Florida F Jamie McGinn returned after missing two games with an upper-body injury. … The Red Wings played their third game in four days. … DeKeyser played his 350th NHL game.
UP NEXT:
Red Wings: Host the Boston Bruins on Tuesday
Panthers: Host the Vancouver Canucks on Tuesday.
rewrite:
In a Saturday night matchup in Sunrise, Florida, the Panthers secured a dramatic 3-2 win against the Red Wings thanks to a last-minute goal by Jonathan Huberdeau. The decisive play occurred with just 7.7 seconds remaining in regulation. Huberdeau capitalized on a loose puck in front of the net, slipping it past Detroit goaltender Petr Mrazek. The Red Wings contested the score, alleging interference with their goalie, but officials upheld the call after review.

Florida’s other goals came from Aleksander Barkov and Aaron Ekblad. Barkov broke a deadlock in the second period, taking a feed from Evgenii Dadanov and firing a shot past Mrazek’s glove. Ekblad opened the scoring early in the first, finishing a backhand chance off the post following a pass from Huberdeau. Panthers netminder Harri Sateri earned his third consecutive victory with 26 saves, while defenseman Keith Yandle contributed two assists.

Detroit’s offense was powered solely by Danny DeKeyser, who recorded both of his team’s goals. His first tied the game in the second period, beating Sateri high from a central position. He later knotted the score again in the third, when a blocked shot deflected off his skate and into the net. Mrazek made 30 stops in the loss.

Additional notes from the game included Panthers defenseman Alex Petrovic appearing in his 200th NHL contest, and forward Jamie McGinn returning from a two-game absence. Detroit was playing its third contest in four days, and DeKeyser skated in his 350th career game.

Looking ahead, the Red Wings will welcome the Boston Bruins on Tuesday, while the Panthers are set to host the Vancouver Canucks the same evening.

rewrite:
On May 2, First Solar Inc. disclosed its financial performance for the opening quarter of 2017. The company reported a non-GAAP profit of $0.25 per share, while its GAAP earnings stood at $0.09 per share. Quarterly revenue reached $892 million, surpassing the Thomson Reuters I/B/E/S projection of $667.8 million. Earnings per share also exceeded the anticipated loss of $0.13.

For the entire year, First Solar provided updated forecasts, now expecting a range from a loss of $0.30 to a profit of $0.40 per share. The company raised its outlook for annual revenue, earnings per share, operating cash flow, and net cash position. It anticipates GAAP net sales between $2.85 billion and $2.95 billion, with shipments projected from 2.4 to 2.6 gigawatts. The non-GAAP earnings per share forecast is set from $0.25 to $0.75, and the GAAP gross margin is expected to be 12.5% to 14.5%. These figures compare to analyst estimates of $2.78 billion in revenue and $0.32 per share for the full year.

The rise in quarterly net sales was mainly attributed to the divestment of the Moapa project, which helped counterbalance a decline in module sales to external clients. The company noted that its shift to the Series 6 product line is advancing well in terms of both technology and market readiness.

Qantas has no plans to alter its flight schedule to Exmouth, despite mounting evidence planes have been filling up all year, resulting in higher prices and limited travel options for residents and tourists.
The Shire of Exmouth and Exmouth Chamber of Commerce and Industry has been lobbying the national carrier to boost capacity, with chamber president Barry Sullivan stating evidence suggested current services were above 80 per cent capacity.
Shire president Matthew Niikkula said long-term commitment to increased flight capacity would support investment and jobs growth in Exmouth.
“Qantas and Tourism Australia are using the Ningaloo Reef experience to support the campaign to attract visitors to Australia,” he said.
“Providing additional ongoing seating capacity to Exmouth will make sure people can access that experience they are being promised.
“The first step is to have a commitment to additional flights, and to date that has not happened outside ad hoc, short-term measures such as one-off increases during the coming school holidays.”
Mr Niikkula said bigger planes, additional flights or provision of an Exmouth to Broome link would be beneficial.
QANTAS has slashed airfares from Perth to Broome in a bid to get more people heading to WA's north instead of Bali. The West Australian Video QANTAS has slashed airfares from Perth to Broome in a bid to get more people heading to WA's north instead of Bali.
Qantas refused to confirm the capacity of flights to and from Exmouth, claiming the average amount of people on a plane was commercially sensitive information.
“We currently have no plans to change our schedule for flights to Learmonth, however we are always reviewing our network to ensure that we have the right aircraft on the right route to match demand,” a spokeswoman said.
North West Central MLA Vince Catania said the State Government needed to push airlines to be more honest with the public.
“The Government should be demanding Qantas puts on extra flights as a requirement of their licence,” he said.
“Airlines look at load factor and how they can maximise profits to benefit them, rather than looking at capacity for the community.
“This is not just about reducing airfares, it is about the company being open and transparent on how they come up with their ticket price.”
Mr Catania said Exmouth fares should be capped at $150.
rewrite:
Qantas is not intending to adjust its flight operations to Exmouth, even as data indicates that aircraft have consistently been operating at high occupancy throughout the year. This situation has led to elevated ticket costs and fewer choices for both local inhabitants and visitors. Local advocacy groups, including the Exmouth Shire and the Exmouth Chamber of Commerce and Industry, have been urging the airline to expand its available seats. Barry Sullivan, who leads the chamber, points to information showing existing flights are consistently operating above 80 percent capacity.

Matthew Niikkula, the Shire President, emphasized that a sustained pledge to enhance flight availability would encourage economic investment and job creation in the region. He noted that Qantas, in partnership with Tourism Australia, is promoting the Ningaloo Reef to attract international tourists to the country. Ensuring reliable, increased seating to Exmouth, he argued, is essential for delivering the experience being advertised to potential travelers. He stated that a firm commitment to more frequent flights is needed, something that has so far been absent beyond temporary, limited actions like occasional extra services during peak holiday periods. According to Mr. Niikkula, solutions could involve larger aircraft, additional flight frequencies, or even establishing a direct air link between Exmouth and Broome.

This occurs alongside Qantas reducing fares on the Perth to Broome route, an initiative aimed at diverting travel interest toward Western Australia's north rather than overseas destinations like Bali. The airline has declined to disclose specific load factors for Exmouth services, stating that average passenger numbers are confidential business data. A spokesperson commented that while there are no current plans to alter the schedule to Learmonth (the airport for Exmouth), the network is continually assessed to align aircraft supply with route demand.

Vince Catania, the Member for North West Central, contends that the state government should compel airlines to be more forthright with the public. He believes the government should mandate additional flights as a condition of Qantas's operating license. Mr. Catania argues that airlines prioritize load factors and profit maximization over serving community capacity needs. The issue, in his view, extends beyond lowering prices to include corporate transparency about how airfares are determined. He has proposed that fares to Exmouth should have a maximum price set at $150.

The iconic “Hollywood” sign got a New Year’s Day makeover from an unknown vandal who used a black tarp to transform the letters into a message celebrating marijuana.
Multiple social media images showed the new “Hollyweed” sign on Mount Lee overlooking Los Angeles. One of the black tarps appeared to have an image of a peace symbol and the other a heart.
Cops have surveillance video of the suspect, TMZ reported. The vandal, dressed in all black, could face a misdemeanor trespassing charge, said Sgt. Robert Payan. The person scaled a protective fence surrounding the sign and then clambered up each giant letter to drape the coverings, Payan said.
California in November passed a measure legalizing marijuana for recreational use.
Though the Prop 64 vote may have been an impetus to change the sign, it wouldn’t be the first time someone has taken to the hills to alter the letters in honor of cannabis. A vandal also changed the sign to read “Hollyweed” on New Year’s Day 1976, TMZ reported.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
rewrite:
On the first day of the new year, the famous "Hollywood" sign was altered by an unidentified individual, who covered parts of it with dark fabric to display a pro-marijuana statement. Photographs shared online depicted the modified landmark, now reading "Hollyweed," situated on Mount Lee above Los Angeles. The coverings included designs resembling a peace sign and a heart shape.

Law enforcement possesses camera footage of the person responsible, according to TMZ. Sergeant Robert Payan stated the individual, wearing black clothing, may be charged with trespassing, a minor offense. The suspect reportedly climbed over a security barrier and then ascended each large letter to attach the materials.

This incident follows California's recent ballot initiative approving recreational cannabis. While this new law might have inspired the act, it is not unprecedented; a similar alteration to spell "Hollyweed" occurred on New Year's Day in 1976. This account includes information from The Associated Press.

Rep. Tim Murphy (R-PA), who announced his resignation from Congress Thursday, reportedly ran a office rife with the mistreatment of staffers.
Before his resignation, the vocally pro-life Pennsylvania Republican was revealed to have asked a mistress to get an abortion.
Politico reported the behavior on Thursday, following Murphy’s announcement of his resignation. The outlet reported that a potential investigation into Murphy’s treatment of his employees by the House Ethics Committee motivated his resignation as much as the revelations about his mistress.
Multiple unnamed former Murphy staffers told Politico that the behavior of the congressman’s chief of staff, Susan Mosychuk, had moved them to quit.
“It was one of the worst places I have ever worked in my life. There was screaming. Intimidation. Nothing you ever did was right,” a former Murphy district director, Nick Rodondo, told Pittsburgh radio station KDKA, Politico noted.
Every other source was unnamed: Politico reported that Mosychuk called staffers “worthless” and their work “garbage.”
“It’s not like a private company where you have an HR department,” one former staffer told Politico. “It was a culture of abuse and a culture of corruption. There really is no oversight.”
“Screaming was an everyday thing,” said another unnamed former staffer. “The manipulation and the mind games. … Everybody in that office was depressed.”
Multiple unnamed ex-staffers told the publication the chief of staff used white noise machines placed around the congressman’s office in order to mask the sound of her screaming. Staffers were told to take the stairs instead of the elevator as a punishment, according to one former employee, and bathroom breaks were cut short in order to administer verbal disciplining.
Politico also reported that a leaked June 2017 memo by Mosychuk, called “Office Conduct and Behavior: Harassment/Legal Compliance” and outlining supposed abusive behavior by the congressman, more accurately described Mosychuk’s own behavior.
“She was the one who would verbally abuse staff,” one unnamed ex-staffer said. “He was bad, but you can deal with a tough member. She was literally terrorizing people.”
Read Politico’s full story here.
rewrite:
Congressman Tim Murphy, a Republican from Pennsylvania, stepped down from his position on Thursday. His departure followed reports of a hostile workplace environment within his office, where employees faced regular mistreatment. Additionally, despite his public stance against abortion, Murphy was revealed to have urged a woman with whom he was having an affair to terminate a pregnancy.

According to a Politico report published the same day as his resignation announcement, Murphy’s decision was driven not only by the scandal involving his personal life but also by the prospect of a House Ethics Committee inquiry into how he managed his staff. Several former employees, who chose to remain anonymous, cited the conduct of Murphy’s chief of staff, Susan Mosychuk, as their reason for leaving.

One former district director, Nick Rodondo, described the office to a Pittsburgh radio station as among the worst workplaces he had ever experienced, characterizing it by frequent yelling, intimidation, and a pervasive sense that no work was ever deemed satisfactory. Other unnamed sources recounted to Politico that Mosychuk routinely belittled staff, labeling them “worthless” and dismissing their efforts as “garbage.” They described an atmosphere of abuse and corruption, noting the lack of a human resources department to provide recourse or oversight.

Former aides stated that shouting was a daily occurrence, accompanied by psychological manipulation and mind games that contributed to widespread depression among the team. To conceal the noise of her outbursts, Mosychuk allegedly positioned white noise machines throughout the office. Punitive measures included forcing staff to use stairs instead of elevators and interrupting bathroom breaks to deliver verbal reprimands.

Politico further noted that a memo written by Mosychuk in June 2017, titled “Office Conduct and Behavior: Harassment/Legal Compliance,” detailed abusive conduct that ironically mirrored her own behavior more than that of the congressman. One former staffer observed that while Murphy could be difficult, Mosychuk was the true source of terror, systematically verbally abusing and intimidating those in the office.

MOSCOW (Sputnik) — In January, New Zealand's media reported that interviews of refugees ahead of their resettlement would start in February.
The team of contractors arrived in the detention center and had already arranged the list of interviews with the migrants detained in the Australian facility, the ABC Online news outlet reported Tuesday.
The media outlet added that there would be about 20 interviews per day during a month.
Australia detains refugees who come to the country to seek asylum in offshore detention camps, while their application is being processed by the authorities. Such measures have been repeatedly criticized by different rights groups.
In November 2016, then-US President Barack Obama and Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull concluded a one-time deal to resettle refugees, currently detained in Australian processing centers on the Manus Island and Nauru in the South Pacific.
However the agreement had been reportedly criticized by the incumbent US President Donald Trump and several media suggested that the deal could be terminated.

According to reports from New Zealand's press in January, screenings of refugees prior to their relocation were scheduled to commence in February. A contracted group has reached the detention site and finalized a schedule for questioning the individuals held at the Australian camp, as stated by ABC Online on Tuesday. The outlet further noted the process would involve approximately 20 screenings daily over one month.

Australia holds asylum seekers in offshore facilities while their claims are reviewed, a practice frequently denounced by various human rights organizations. A singular arrangement to relocate these individuals, who are presently held at Australian centers on Manus Island and Nauru in the South Pacific, was agreed upon in November 2016 by then-U.S. President Barack Obama and Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull. Nevertheless, this pact has reportedly faced criticism from President Donald Trump, leading to media speculation that it might be dissolved.

Lucy Durack on set, on her first day of filming Lift
Lucy Durack on set, on her first day of filming Lift Picture: Ian Munro
It was an odd encounter in the lift at her daughter’s day care that led Lucy Durack home to Perth — and to her debut as a screenwriter.
Durack, an acclaimed theatre actress, will spend much of this week inside a makeshift wooden elevator inside a small film studio in Maylands, shooting Lift, a romantic comedy web series she created and wrote.
Sydney-based Durack, best known for her award-winning turns as Glinda the Good Witch in Wicked and Elle Woods in Legally Blonde: The Musical, said seeing her script come to life was “incredibly, overwhelmingly fun”.
Durack penned five comedies with her writing partners, brother and sister duo Jess and Leon Murray, but they settled on Lift partly because of its format of seven four-minute episodes.
The story follows Olivia (Durack) on her way to a job interview and Simon (theatre actor Duncan Ragg), who is about to propose to his girlfriend, and their fateful meeting in an elevator.
“I love a romantic comedy ... and this one came out of a fairly awkward conversation I had with a stranger in a lift at my daughter’s day care,” Durack laughed.
Actress and singer Lucy Durack is back home in Perth visiting her family for a week. She is also appearing in new Nine series Doctor Doctor. Picture: Ian Munro
“We wanted something we could make on a small budget, before we got funding from Screenwest.
“The rules were each episode was one lift ride and there was one location, so we had to stretch the boundaries to make it into a real romantic comedy, just in microscopic form.”
And when Lift goes online midyear, it will be the culmination of tireless work by “an incredible team of up-and-coming WA crew and volunteers”, according to producer Lauren Elliott.
WA’s Zoe Pepper is directing and Chloe Rickard is executive producer. As Durack points out, it is an all-female line-up at the helm. “It’s just cool to be on a set with so many women,” she said. “It’s really inspiring and exciting.”
rewrite:
During the initial day of shooting for *Lift*, Lucy Durack found herself on set. An unexpected conversation in an elevator at her child's preschool ultimately guided the well-known stage performer back to her hometown of Perth and marked her first venture into writing for the screen.

Primarily recognized for her celebrated theatrical roles, such as Glinda in *Wicked* and Elle Woods in *Legally Blonde: The Musical*, Durack is now dedicating her week within a constructed elevator set in a Maylands studio. Here, she is filming *Lift*, a romantic comedy series she authored. The experience of witnessing her written words transform into a production has been, in her words, tremendously enjoyable.

The concept originated from a genuinely uncomfortable exchange with an unfamiliar person in a daycare lift. Durack developed the script alongside writing collaborators Jess and Leon Murray. Among several comedy drafts, they selected *Lift* for its structure, consisting of seven brief episodes. The narrative centers on two characters, Olivia and Simon, whose paths cross in an elevator during pivotal moments in their lives, leading to a significant encounter.

Durack, who is also in Perth for family reasons and appears in another television series, explained the project's practical origins. The goal was to create a viable production with minimal resources before pursuing formal financing. The creative challenge involved confining each episode to a single elevator journey and one setting, thereby expanding the possibilities of the genre within a tightly focused framework.

Producer Lauren Elliott notes that the series' online release later this year will represent the dedicated efforts of a promising team from Western Australia, comprising both crew and volunteers. The project is led by director Zoe Pepper and executive producer Chloe Rickard. Durack highlights the significance of the entirely female leadership team, describing the atmosphere on set as uniquely motivating and exhilarating.

CHARLOTTE, North Carolina, Aug 12 (Reuters) - Hideki Matsuyama has broad shoulders but is not finding it easy to carry the weight of an entire nation as he seeks to become the first Japanese man to win a major.
Matsuyama started the third round of the PGA Championship tied for the lead with Kevin Kisner but never got into gear, a bogey at the first setting the table for a pedestrian one-over-par 72.
That was still good enough to remain in contention, a stroke behind Kisner, who dropped three shots in the final three holes.
"Probably the pressure had something to do with it, being in the last group in a major tournament," said Matsuyama.
"But I haven't been spot-on all week, and the worries I had about my swing showed up today in the way I played.
"I'm disappointed the way I played today, however I'm happy to be one stroke back and still have a chance and looking forward to tomorrow."
Matsuyama is coming off a closing 61 that clinched a runaway victory at last week's WGC-Bridgestone Invitational. He said at the time he had shot the stunning score despite being uncomfortable with his swing, words he repeated pre-tournament here.
Despite his struggles, the 25-year-old played the difficult final three holes better than his rivals, parring them all to finish the day much closer than he expected an hour previously.
rewrite:
CHARLOTTE, North Carolina, Aug 12 (Reuters) - While possessing the physical stature for a heavy burden, Hideki Matsuyama is grappling with the immense expectation of securing a historic major victory for Japan.

Entering Saturday's play at the PGA Championship as a co-leader with Kevin Kisner, Matsuyama stumbled early with an opening bogey and never found his rhythm, ultimately carding a mediocre 72. This kept him in the hunt, however, just one shot behind Kisner, who faltered late with three bogeys on the final three holes.

Matsuyama acknowledged the strain of competing in a major's final pairing likely affected him. He admitted his game had felt imperfect all week, and his lingering doubts about his swing manifested in his performance. Despite his disappointment, he expressed satisfaction at remaining within a single stroke and retaining an opportunity for Sunday.

This follows a dominant win at the prior week's WGC-Bridgestone Invitational, sealed with a final-round 61. He had noted then, and reiterated this week, that even that spectacular score came while he felt uneasy with his swing. Demonstrating resilience, the 25-year-old navigated the challenging closing trio of holes more steadily than his competitors, securing pars on each to end the day in a stronger position than anticipated.

During CBS’ coverage of the shooting at a Congressional baseball practice, anchor Charlie Rose stated, “people talk about things like ‘lock her up,’ and we saw some of the most crude political language that we’d heard. … This has been a season of sort of coarse political rhetoric.”
Rose said, “[W]e saw during the time that members went back home, because of some of the debates in Congress, they were particularly raucous town meetings, not about threats to their lives, but clearly, the level in combativeness was more apparent than ever.”
He later added, after Congressional Correspondent Nancy Cordes said that it can be difficult for members of Congress to tell who is merely exercising their free speech rights and someone who has the intent of committing violence, “Clearly, we saw that during the campaign, which people talk about things like ‘lock her up,’ and we saw some of the most crude political language that we’d heard, even though there’s a long history of political attacks in American politics since the Founding Fathers. We did see expressions that we had not heard before. This has been a season of sort of coarse political rhetoric.”
Follow Ian Hanchett on Twitter @IanHanchett
rewrite:
While reporting on the shooting at a Congressional baseball practice for CBS, anchor Charlie Rose commented on the harsh tone of recent political discourse. He noted that chants such as "lock her up" exemplified some of the most vulgar political language heard in recent memory. Rose described this period as one marked by unusually coarse rhetoric.

He reflected on the contentious town hall meetings lawmakers faced after returning to their districts, pointing out that these events were notably raucous. The hostility displayed, he suggested, was more intense than ever, even if direct threats were not always explicit.

Rose later agreed with Congressional Correspondent Nancy Cordes, who observed that it can be hard for legislators to distinguish between protected free speech and genuinely threatening intent. He reiterated that the recent campaign season featured unprecedented expressions of crude language, despite America's long history of political attacks dating to the Founding Fathers. This era, he concluded, has been characterized by a particularly rough and unrefined political dialogue.

PRINCETON, N.J. — Jerome Desrosiers’ 3-pointer with 36 seconds left in overtime provided the winning points in Princeton’s 76-73 victory over Yale on Friday.
After Desrosiers’ trey, Yale missed consecutive 3-point shots and fouled Amir Bell, who missed the front end of a one-and-one. The teams exchanged turnovers before a desperation 3-point try by Yale missed.
Yale took possession after a tie-up in regulation but Trey Phills was unable to connect on a 3-pointer as the game went to overtime.
Myles Stephens scored 18 points and Devin Cannady and Bell 16 apiece for the Tigers (11-8, 3-1 Ivy), who have won three straight, with Bell collecting a career-high 11 rebounds for his first career double-double.
Alex Copeland scored 18 points, Phills had 17 points and a career-high 14 rebounds for his first career double-double while Blake Reynolds added 15 points for the Bulldogs (9-12, 2-3).
rewrite:
In a Friday matchup that went to an extra period, Princeton secured a 76-73 win over Yale. Jerome Desrosiers hit a crucial three-pointer with 36 seconds remaining in overtime to put his team ahead for good. Yale then failed to score on two three-point attempts and committed a foul. After Princeton missed a free throw, both teams turned the ball over before a final, unsuccessful long-range heave by Yale as time expired.

The game had reached overtime after Yale held the ball following a tied score in regulation, but Trey Phills missed a three-point shot at the buzzer.

For Princeton (11-8, 3-1 Ivy), now on a three-game streak, Myles Stephens led with 18 points. Devin Cannady and Amir Bell each contributed 16 points, with Bell also grabbing a personal-best 11 rebounds to record his first double-double.

Yale (9-12, 2-3) was paced by Alex Copeland's 18 points. Phills scored 17 points and collected a career-high 14 rebounds for his own first double-double, while Blake Reynolds added 15 points.

Talk about living up to your name.
A Florida woman named Crystal Methvin was arrested Saturday in St. Johns County on drug possession charges after being caught with crystal meth, jail records show.
Methvin, 40, of St. Augustine, was busted after an anonymous caller tipped off cops who found her inside a car with two other people in a parking lot on South Dixie Highway, WJXT reports.
Police searched the car and found drug paraphernalia and a substance that tested positive for crystal meth.
Methvin was taken into custody with a man identified as Douglas Nickerson, WJXT reports.
Methvin has arrests in the county dating back to 1998 when she was booked into the St. Johns County Jail for driving under the influence. Most recently, she was arrested in January on 14 felony counts of drug possession and misdemeanor possession of drug equipment, jail records show.
Methvin remains in custody on $5,000 bond, according to jail records. It’s unclear if she’s hired an attorney.
rewrite: This incident presents a striking alignment of name and circumstance. A Florida resident, Crystal Methvin, age 40, was taken into custody in St. Johns County over the weekend. Her arrest followed a police search prompted by an anonymous tip, which located her in a vehicle with two other individuals. During the search, officers discovered paraphernalia and a substance later confirmed to be crystal methamphetamine. She was arrested alongside a man identified as Douglas Nickerson. Methvin's criminal history in the county extends back to 1998, beginning with a DUI charge. More recently, she faced multiple felony drug possession charges earlier this year. She is currently being held with bail set at five thousand dollars, and her legal representation status is unknown.

The main TAIEX index fell 0.4 percent to 9,793.12 points as of 0141 GMT, after closing at 9,832.42 points.

The Taiwan dollar firmed T$0.008 to T$30.642 per U.S. dollar on Wednesday. (Reporting by Faith Hung; Editing by Amrutha Gayathri)

JOSE MOURINHO WAS spotted at a friendly between Austria and Russia on Wednesday, as rumours swirl he is targeting a move for Austrian forward Marko Arnautovic.
The West Ham star has been linked with a big money move to the north of England as Mourinho looks to bring in reinforcements for Manchester United behind Romelu Lukaku.
The pair previously worked together in 2009-10 at Inter, when Arnautovic was on loan from Twente, but the move did not work out.
The forward only appeared in three Serie A contests as a substitute, with Mourinho saying the striker had “the mentality of a child” and claimed he was “unmanageable”.
However, that was eight years ago, and the 29-year-old Arnautovic has displayed quality since then, scoring 11 goals last season for West Ham after making a £20 million move from Stoke City, where he had spent the previous four seasons. He also added six assists in his 31 Premier League appearances
It was the second time in three seasons Arnautovic had scored 11 goals and added six assists, having managed it with Stoke in 2015-16.
Those numbers have led to speculation Mourinho could seek to add him to play with or beside Lukaku after the Red Devils’ depth behind the Belgian was proven wanting in the 1-0 FA Cup loss to Chelsea .
And Mourinho’s presence at a friendly in which Arnautovic started is only likely to pour more fuel on the rumour fire despite Mourinho reportedly claiming he was only “on holiday” when asked why he was in attendance at Innsbruck
However, if Mourinho was there to have a look at the forward, he was treated to Arnautovic making an impact for his national side as he laid on the assist for Alessandro Schopf’s 28th minute opener.
That proved to be the winner as Arnautovic played 83 minutes of the victory over the World Cup hosts.

rewrite:
Amid ongoing speculation that he is interested in acquiring Austrian striker Marko Arnautovic, Jose Mourinho was seen observing an international exhibition match between Austria and Russia this past Wednesday. The Manchester United manager is reportedly aiming to strengthen his squad's attacking options to support Romelu Lukaku, with the West Ham United forward being considered for a costly transfer to a club in northern England.

Mourinho and Arnautovic have a shared history from the 2009-10 campaign at Inter Milan, during which the Austrian was on a temporary arrangement from FC Twente. That stint, however, was unsuccessful. Arnautovic made merely three brief appearances in Italy's top division, prompting Mourinho to criticize his immature attitude and suggest he was difficult to coach.

Now 29, Arnautovic has significantly developed since that period eight years ago. After a four-year spell at Stoke City, he transferred to West Ham for £20 million and proceeded to net 11 goals while providing six assists in 31 league matches last season. Notably, this replicated his output from the 2015-16 season with Stoke, where he also recorded 11 goals and six assists.

This consistent performance has fueled talk that Mourinho might pursue him to bolster United's offensive ranks, especially following a lackluster showing from the substitutes in a recent narrow cup defeat to Chelsea. Mourinho's appearance at the friendly, where Arnautovic was in the starting lineup, intensifies these rumors, even though the manager has dismissed his presence as merely a holiday activity.

Should his purpose have been to scout the player, Mourinho witnessed a productive outing from Arnautovic, who contributed an assist for Austria's first-half goal in a victory over Russia. The forward featured for most of the match, further showcasing the form that has made him a subject of transfer speculation.

DAYTON, Ohio (WDTN) – A local attorney is warning that we could begin to see more violent crimes taking place on social media.
Following Sunday’s live broadcast on Facebook of a deadly shooting in Cleveland he’s concerned about the direction social media is headed.
Cyberspace attorney, Andrew Rossow says social media plays a major role in how suspects are traced and prosecuted. He says what happened on Facebook Live in Cleveland is disturbing, but may just be the beginning.
“People are starting to live through their devices and online technology. Hiding behind their Facebook user names or Twitter handles, thinking people can’t find them,” said Rossow with the Gregory M. Gantt Co., L.P.A law firm.
He says if you see a crime on social media, call law enforcement immediately. Also, if you think what you’re posting is private, it’s not. He says Facebook’s policy allows posts to be traced if requested through the legal system.
“You hope people understand right from wrong, but some people don’t and unfortunately, the next thing is going to be what is the next thing that’s going to happen,” he said.
rewrite:
An Ohio-based lawyer has expressed concern that social media platforms may increasingly be used to broadcast acts of violence. This warning comes after a fatal shooting was streamed live from Cleveland on Facebook this past Sunday. Attorney Andrew Rossow, who specializes in internet-related legal matters, emphasizes that these platforms are crucial tools for identifying and charging those who commit crimes. He finds the Cleveland incident alarming and fears it could signal a trend.

Rossow, of the Gregory M. Gantt Co., L.P.A., notes that individuals often immerse themselves in digital worlds, believing the anonymity of usernames offers protection from consequences. He strongly advises anyone witnessing illegal activity online to contact the police without delay. He also cautions users that content is never truly private, as Facebook can provide data to authorities under proper legal request.

While hoping most people possess an inherent moral compass, Rossow worries that some do not, leading him to question what disturbing event might occur next in the digital space.

Students take part in a protest to demand the appearance of three missing film students alive, in Guadalajara, Jalisco state, Mexico, on March 24, 2018. Three film students from the University of Audiovisual Media of Jalisco state went missing March 19.
Authorities said Monday that three Mexican film students who went missing in March in Guadalajara were kidnapped, tortured and killed, and their bodies were dissolved in acid, NBC News reported.
Javier Salomón Aceves Gastélum, Daniel Díaz, and Marco Ávalo were last seen on March 19 in the municipality of Tonala, in the state of Jalisco, filming a class project during their Spring Break. The three aspiring filmmakers were students at the Universidad de Medios Audiovisuales.
According to state prosecutors, their car broke down during the trip and they were later kidnapped by gunmen from the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), who confused them for members of a rival gang.
Academy Award winning director Guillermo del Toro, who is a native of Guadalajara, expressed outrage on social media in response to the killings.
"Words can't explain the dimension of this madness. 3 students are killed and dissolved in acid. The "why" is unthinkable, the "how" is terrifying,” the "Shape of Water" director tweeted.
rewrite:
On March 24, 2018, demonstrators gathered in Guadalajara, located in Mexico’s Jalisco state, calling for the safe return of three university film students who had disappeared. The three had gone missing on March 19. According to an NBC News report, officials stated on a Monday that the students, after being abducted in Guadalajara that March, were subjected to torture and murder, with their remains subsequently dissolved using acid.

The missing individuals were identified as Javier Salomón Aceves Gastélum, Daniel Díaz, and Marco Ávalo. They were last observed in Tonalá, Jalisco, where they were working on a school assignment over their spring holiday. All three attended the University of Audiovisual Media.

State investigators reported that after their vehicle experienced mechanical failure, armed members of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel seized them, mistakenly believing they were affiliated with a competing criminal group.

Guillermo del Toro, the Oscar-winning filmmaker originally from Guadalajara, publicly voiced his anger regarding the murders on social media. In a tweet, the director of "The Shape of Water" stated that language fails to capture the enormity of such insanity, expressing that the reason behind the killings is beyond comprehension and the method used is horrifying.

OAKLAND, Calif. (AP) — Golden State forward Andre Iguodala will be out for Game 1 of the NBA Finals on Thursday night as he recovers from a bone bruise in his left knee that cost him the final four games of the Western Conference finals.
The Warriors said Iguodala, who was injured in Game 3 against the Rockets on May 20, was evaluated Tuesday and is making progress but still has the bruise and inflammation of the nerve surrounding his knee. Kevin Love’s status for Cleveland remained unclear as he went through the concussion protocol after he was injured in Game 6 of the Eastern Conference finals against Boston. He wasn’t scheduled to attend media day Wednesday at Oracle Arena, where the Warriors host the series opener.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) – A research team from Taipei City University of Science and Technology won one gold award and three special prizes for their smart baby carrier at a trade show in Goyang, South Korea from June 27-July 1, reported CNA.
The smart baby carrier has self-regulated heating, sensors to ensure the baby is strapped in safely and Bluetooth functionality to help caregivers take better care of the child.
The research team attended the Korea International Women's Invention Exposition 2018 and walked away with multiple awards.
The successful research team is an interdisciplinary group of computer scientists and communications engineers, and was comprised of both students and teachers.
Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer and Communication Engineering, Taipei City University of Science and Technology Tsai Yao-pin (蔡耀斌) said baby carriers are a very important product and none available to buy have heating capability.
This gap in the market led the research team to develop their award winning invention, Tsai said.
Research team member and third year student Chen Wei-hung (陳威宏) said the team added a warming pouch to keep the baby's bottle warm at about 45 degrees Celsius.
An infant is unlikely to drink cold milk, he added.
The baby carrier has Bluetooth functionality, allowing it to link to a smart phone to display temperature information to help caregivers to take better care of child, Chen said.
Tsai said that most parents fret about whether the baby carrier is buckled and fastened correctly. In response, their invention had a sensor installed which illuminates if the baby carrier is fastened incorrectly.
The research team is currently in discussions with manufacturers from Hong Kong and Taiwan about bringing the award-winning invention to market.
rewrite:
A team from Taipei City University of Science and Technology earned significant recognition at a trade exhibition held in Goyang, South Korea, between late June and early July, as covered by CNA. Their innovative infant carrier received a gold medal along with three distinct honors.

This intelligent carrier incorporates several advanced features designed to assist caregivers. It includes an automatic warming system, safety sensors to confirm proper securement of the child, and Bluetooth connectivity for enhanced monitoring.

The group presented their creation at the 2018 Korea International Women's Invention Exposition, where it garnered multiple accolades. The team itself is a collaborative effort, blending expertise from computing and communications fields, and includes both faculty members and students.

Tsai Yao-pin, an assistant professor in the university's Department of Computer and Communication Engineering, noted that while baby carriers are essential, existing models lack integrated heating. This identified market need inspired the project that ultimately achieved award-winning success.

Chen Wei-hung, a third-year student and team contributor, explained that a dedicated warming compartment maintains a baby's bottle at approximately 45 degrees Celsius, addressing an infant's typical refusal of cold milk. Furthermore, via a Bluetooth link to a smartphone, the carrier relays temperature data to help adults oversee the child's comfort more effectively.

Tsai added that a common parental concern involves ensuring the carrier is properly fastened. To resolve this, the design integrates a sensor that activates a light if the buckles are incorrectly engaged.

The researchers are now engaged in talks with potential producers in both Hong Kong and Taiwan to explore commercial production and distribution of their honored device.

BELGRADE Germany supports Serbia on its path to the European Union membership but the Balkan country must work on reforms and sort out ties with its former province Kosovo, German Foreign Minister Sigmar Gabriel said on Wednesday .
Speaking before a meeting with Serbian president-elect Aleksandar Vucic, Gabriel said: "You have a responsibility to continue reforms and to continue to develop better relations with Kosovo. That is an essential precondition for accession to the European Union."
Gabriel said he could not give a precise date when Serbia could enter EU.
Earlier on Wednesday, Gabriel who will visit Kosovo on Thursday and Albania on Monday on his Balkan tour, urged Balkan states to overcome their divisions to integrate into the European Union.
Six countries in the Western Balkan region, which is still recovering from a decade of wars and economic turmoil in the 1990s, aim to join the European Union - Serbia, Montenegro, Macedonia, Bosnia, Kosovo and Albania.
Gabriel said Serbia, the biggest market, has "a good bit of work" to do to meet the requirements for EU membership, including improving transparency, governance and rule of law, and fighting corruption.
Those steps were also important for Serbia to be able to attract small- and medium-sized businesses, who needed stable conditions, he said.
He said it was good that daily protests by thousands of people after Vucic's election on April 2 had been allowed to proceed without government intervention.
"If you want to get into the EU, you must know that demonstrations and protests against democratically elected governments and president are possible, permitted and within the EU, quite common," Gabriel said.
Vucic, who won a presidential election on April 2 in a landslide, said: "As far as we are concerned we are on the European Union path and whether it will happen or not it does not only depend on us."
Gabriel said he remained concerned about developments elsewhere in the region, where "demons of the past" were arising once again.
Tensions have flared in recent months between Kosovo and Serbia, as well as between three ethnics groups in Bosnia, as nationalist sentiment grows across the region.
(Reporting by Andrea Shalal)
rewrite:
Germany has expressed its endorsement of Serbia's aspirations to join the European Union, while also emphasizing the necessity for the Balkan nation to implement reforms and normalize relations with Kosovo. This statement was made by German Foreign Minister Sigmar Gabriel during a visit to Belgrade. Ahead of discussions with Serbia's president-elect, Aleksandar Vucic, Gabriel highlighted that advancing reforms and fostering improved ties with Kosovo are fundamental requirements for EU accession.

Gabriel refrained from specifying any timeline for Serbia's potential entry into the bloc. As part of a regional tour that includes upcoming stops in Kosovo and Albania, he called on all Western Balkan states to resolve their differences to facilitate European integration. Several nations in the area—Serbia, Montenegro, Macedonia, Bosnia, Kosovo, and Albania—seek EU membership, despite the lingering effects of the conflicts and economic instability of the 1990s.

The German minister noted that Serbia, as the region's largest economy, still has considerable progress to make in areas such as enhancing transparency, strengthening governance and legal frameworks, and combating corruption. These measures, he added, are crucial not only for EU candidacy but also for attracting small and medium-sized enterprises, which depend on a stable environment.

Gabriel viewed positively the fact that ongoing public demonstrations following the April 2 election have occurred without state interference. He stressed that within the EU, the right to protest against elected leaders is both protected and commonplace.

In response, Vucic, who secured a decisive victory in the presidential poll, affirmed Serbia's commitment to a European path while acknowledging that the outcome depends on more than just domestic efforts.

Gabriel also voiced apprehension about rising tensions in other parts of the Western Balkans, where historical animosities are resurfacing. Recent months have seen increased strain between Serbia and Kosovo, as well as among ethnic factions in Bosnia, amid a broader surge in nationalist rhetoric across the region.

ABC News(NEW YORK) — A fresh round of cold and snow headed toward the Midwest and Northeast on Monday.
The National Weather Service has issued winter storm watches and warnings for nine states from Indiana to Maine as an Alberta Clipper storm system moves through Monday into Tuesday.
The system is just moving into the northern Plains from the Dakotas to Minnesota and Wisconsin, with snow from Minneapolis to Chicago.
The storm system is forecast to move east into the Great Lakes by Monday evening, bringing snow from Detroit to Cleveland.
The clipper system is expected to touch down in the Northeast by Tuesday morning, with snow mostly inland and rain showers from Boston south to Washington, D.C.
Most of the snow will fall in the Midwest and Northeast just north of major metropolitan areas. Some parts of inland Maine could get as much as 10 inches.
Behind the storm system, the coldest air of the season is forecast for the Northeast by Wednesday morning.

× Cheap Wine Is About to Get a Lot More Expensive
The price of wine is going up.
Global wine production slumped to its lowest level in 60 years in 2017, according to data from the International Organisation of Vine and Wine.
The most recent harvest produced 25 billion liters of wine, a decrease from 26.7 billion in 2016 and 27.6 billion in 2015. The decline was driven by weak harvests in key markets including Europe and South Africa.
The shortage has caused the wholesale price of basic wine in Italy to skyrocket 74% over the previous year, according to the European Commission. Prices are up 45% in Spain and over 10% in France.
Analysts said that producers, dealers and retailers will absorb some of the price hikes, but consumers will end up paying more — especially for cheaper bottles.
“The wine companies that are targeting very low prices … will be hit the worst, because their margins are very low,” said Stephen Rannekleiv, a global beverages strategist at Rabobank. “When prices go up, it puts a lot of strain on them.”
Reduced supply will also hurt quality.
“There will be, in some cases, lower quality wines getting blended into slightly higher value products, so everyone kind of goes down a tier in quality,” said Rannekleiv.
Related: Forget craft beer. The next craze is non-alcoholic brew
Producers were hardest hit in Europe, where heavy hailstorms and harsh frosts damaged vineyards in early 2017 before a summer drought took its toll. The continent accounts for 65% of global wine production, and 57% of consumption.
European production dropped 15% in 2017. Production fell 21% in Italy, 18% in France and 15% in Spain, according to the Commission.
Other regions had problems, too.
Wildfires destroyed or tainted some of the harvest in California, and drought harmed vineyards in South Africa. Warm weather can cause grapes to ripen early and be smaller in size.
Rannekleiv said the result was a global harvest that was even worse than analysts had feared.
Related: Coke is launching an alcoholic drink in Japan
The pain could spread to other industries.
Rannekleiv said the slump in production means there will be less wine to divert for use in other products. Brandy and vinegar makers could be hurt, for example.
rewrite:
The cost of affordable wine is poised to rise significantly. Global output reached a six-decade low in 2017, as reported by the International Organisation of Vine and Wine. The annual yield fell to 25 billion liters, down from 26.7 billion the prior year and 27.6 billion in 2015. This drop stemmed largely from poor harvests across major producing nations in Europe and South Africa.

Wholesale prices for basic wines have surged as a result. In Italy, costs have jumped 74% year-over-year, while Spain saw a 45% increase and France over 10%, according to European Commission figures. Industry experts note that while producers, distributors, and sellers will cushion part of the increase, shoppers will ultimately face higher prices, particularly on budget bottles.

Businesses focusing on the lowest price points will feel the most pressure. Their already narrow profit margins leave little room to manage rising costs, explained Rabobank beverage strategist Stephen Rannekleiv. The supply shortfall may also affect quality. Some lower-grade wines could be mixed into higher-value offerings, effectively causing an overall step down in quality tiers, he added.

Europe, which produces 65% of the world's wine and consumes 57%, suffered the most severe impacts. Vineyards there were damaged by spring frosts and hailstorms, followed by summer drought. Output across the continent declined 15%, with Italy down 21%, France 18%, and Spain 15%.

Other regions faced challenges as well. California wildfires ruined portions of the crop, while drought stressed vineyards in South Africa. Unseasonably warm conditions can lead to earlier, smaller grapes. Rannekleiv noted the global harvest ultimately proved more disappointing than anticipated.

The effects may ripple into adjacent sectors. With less wine available, there will be reduced supply for conversion into products like brandy or vinegar, potentially straining those industries.

Man sentenced to 38 years in prison for Fort Collins killing
FORT COLLINS, Colo. (AP) — A 19-year-old man was sentenced to 38 years in prison for stabbing to death a Fort Collins man last year.
The Fort Collins Coloradoan reports Dylan Thompson was sentenced Monday after pleading guilty in April to second-degree murder in the death of 65-year-old William Grabusky.
Fort Collins police found Grabusky dead inside his apartment in August 2017 after his out-of-state wife requested a welfare check.
Thompson told the court Monday that he killed Grabusky in self-defense after the man had tried to sexually assault him at knifepoint. Thompson said he took control of the knife and stabbed Grabusky in the chest.
Attorneys say Grabusky and Thompson had connected weeks before the killing after Thompson posted an ad on Craigslist seeking a "sugar daddy-type situation."

According to legal representatives, the two had initially made contact through a Craigslist advertisement in which Thompson was seeking a financial arrangement akin to a "sugar daddy" relationship.

DES MOINES, Iowa (AP) - A lawsuit claims Iowa's new voter identification law violates the state constitution.
Priorities USA Foundation says the lawsuit was filed Wednesday in Polk County District Court in Des Moines. The national group, which is covering legal costs, provided a copy of the lawsuit.
It's the first legal challenge against the new ID requirement and its provisions. Parts of the law will be in effect for Iowa's upcoming June 5 primary, though a requirement to show ID to cast a regular ballot won't be in place until 2019.

Iowa Secretary of State Paul Pate is named as a defendant in the suit. His office did not respond to a request for comment.

Sooty the possum was lucky to escape from a combustion stove at a Pimlico house.
Sooty the possum was lucky to escape from a combustion stove at a Pimlico house. Jeanette Dundas
WHEN Pimlico man Brian lit the fire in his slow combustion stove, smoke poured out into the room.
The flue was obviously blocked.
But, almost immediately after, a possum dropped into the fire.
Brian acted quickly and got the possum out, but was unsure if it had sustained burns, so he called WIRES for help.
Sooty, as the young possum was named, was extremely lucky.
After rescue and examination it turned out that she had sustained minimal damage as she had avoided the hot part of the fire box. Her main concern was smoke inhalation.
Possums, gliders and many bird species use hollows as homes. Sadly, as human habitat expands, these are no longer as easy to find. A chimney or flue looks very much like a hollow log and clearly this possum had been seeking shelter in this man-made home.
Sooty is fairly young and should most certainly have still been with her mum, but she was not in good body condition, indicating she may have lost her mum some time prior to sheltering in Brian's flue.
She has now been in care with WIRES for a week and is doing well.
Shortly she will be transferred to a large aviary till she is ready to be released back to the wild.
If you have a fireplace it is a good idea to ensure you have an adjustable stainless steel chimney cap.
It is the only way to prevent animals from entering your chimney or flue.
Please call WIRES on 66281898 should you find a native animal in trouble.
rewrite:
A fortunate possum, later named Sooty, managed to survive an incident involving a wood-burning heater at a residence in Pimlico. After the homeowner, Brian, started a fire, smoke unexpectedly filled the room because the chimney passage was obstructed. Shortly thereafter, a possum fell into the flames. Brian promptly rescued the animal but, concerned about potential injuries, contacted the wildlife rescue organization WIRES for assistance.

The juvenile possum proved to be remarkably lucky. Upon assessment, rescuers found she had suffered only minor harm, having largely missed the hottest areas within the stove. Her primary injury was from breathing in smoke. Tree hollows, which serve as natural shelters for possums, gliders, and various birds, are becoming scarce due to urban development. To a wild animal, a chimney or flue can resemble a hollow log, which likely explains why this possum sought refuge there.

Sooty is relatively young and would typically still be dependent on her mother. Her poor physical condition suggests she may have been orphaned before entering Brian’s chimney. After a week in WIRES care, she is recovering well. Her next step will be a stay in a spacious outdoor enclosure until she is fully prepared to return to her natural habitat.

Homeowners with fireplaces are advised to install an adjustable stainless steel chimney cover. This is the most effective method for keeping wildlife out of chimneys and flues. If you encounter a native animal in distress, please reach out to WIRES at 66281898.

Nigerian Lady narrates her hilarious experience living in Canada and how she was arrested crossing a rail track
A Nigerian lady identified as “Blackmigrantgirl” on twitter took to the microblogging platform to share how she got a ticket for crossing “ordinary railtrack”
Read her hilarious ordeal below;
The logical side of me understands why I got the ticket but I am still unhappy about it. Let me explain what happened.
I had to travel by bus and by train from the venue of a job interview I attended today, back to the home of my hosts on the other side of town- in Stouffville. My bus arrived the train station with very little time to spare for the departure time of the train to Stouffville. Unfortunately for me, the closest route from the bus terminal to the train platform is now blocked off due to ongoing construction. I then had to make a dash for it across from the bus to the train station, following the longer route, down the stairs and then up another flight of stairs to the departure platform.
Only for me to get to the departure platform to discover that I was on the wrong platform and the train was on the far side of the station.
Adrenalin had already kicked in from all the running and I gave it free rein to cross the train track to get on my train. I didn’t even have enough time to think about the consequences of what I was doing.
Of course I got caught ????
Next thing I know, a security guard is walking up to me and asking me to step out of the train. Everyone was looking at me like I stole. Chai! My father in heaven oh.
Long story short, to my utter disbelief, th4e security guard wrote me a ticket for 180 Canadian dollars. All my explanation of being late, being new to Canada, not knowing I was violating a bye-law fell on deaf ears.
Now I have to call the courthouse tomorrow, to beg for a lesser fine.
Honestly, I’m just tired???????. I just hope I am hired for the job that brought me downtown today”
Do you have similar experience? Share with us in the comment section below
rewrite:
A Nigerian woman using the social media handle "Blackmigrantgirl" recently recounted an amusing yet frustrating incident from her life in Canada, where she received a citation for walking across railway tracks. She shared the full story online.

While part of her recognizes the rationale behind the penalty, she remains displeased with the situation. Here is how the events unfolded: After attending a job interview, she needed to return by bus and train to her hosts' residence in Stouffville, which is across the city. Her bus reached the train station with barely any time left before her train's scheduled departure. To make matters worse, the most direct path from the bus stop to the correct platform was closed because of construction work. This forced her to sprint along a more roundabout path, which involved going down one set of stairs and up another to reach the boarding area.

Upon arriving at the platform, she realized she was on the wrong side of the station—her train was waiting on the opposite platform. Fueled by the adrenaline from rushing, she impulsively decided to cross the tracks directly to reach her train, without pausing to consider the potential repercussions.

Unsurprisingly, she was immediately apprehended. A security officer approached and instructed her to exit the train. She felt intensely scrutinized by the other passengers, as if she had committed a theft. To her complete shock, the officer issued her a fine of 180 Canadian dollars. All her appeals—citing her lateness, her recent arrival in Canada, and her ignorance of the local ordinance—were completely ignored.

Now she must contact the courthouse the following day to plead for a reduction in the penalty. She expressed sheer exhaustion from the ordeal and shared her hope that she ultimately gets the job that prompted her downtown trip. She concluded by inviting others to share if they have had comparable experiences.

Four men are facing charges in connection with a Halifax home invasion that left a man injured, though police say he was not the intended target.
Halifax Regional Police responded to a home on Acadia Street shortly before 2 a.m. Tuesday after receiving a report that two men had forced their way inside.
Police say the men had their faces covered, were dressed in black, and one was armed with a knife. The suspects fled the scene in a vehicle, which was spotted by a responding officer not far from the home.
The vehicle was stopped and four suspects were arrested. They were held in police custody overnight.
A resident of the home was sent to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries and has since been treated and released.
Police say the investigation has revealed that the victim and suspects are not known to each other, and the victim was not the intended target.
Shaquean James Bowden, 21, and Anthony Alfrado Corradini, 19, both of Halifax, and Darcy Raymond Delbert Caldwell, 28, and Kerry Lee Sampson, 31, both of Windsor, have all been charged with one count each of break and enter, assault with a weapon, assault causing bodily harm, and possession of a weapon for a dangerous purpose.
Corradini has also been charged with one count of disguise with intent and three counts of breach of probation.
All four men are due to appear Wednesday in Halifax provincial court.

Antivirus Giant McAfee Acquires VPN Provider TunnelBear
Internet security company McAfee has bought VPN provider TunnelBear. McAfee hasn't announced how much the deal is worth, but in a statement the company said it plans to integrate TunnelBear's services into its own VPN service, Safe Connect.
"We're confident this acquisition will serve both our end users and partners by embedding its best-in-class, hardened network into our Safe Connect product," said McAfee CEO Christopher Young.
The End of Free VPN?
There's a chance this acquisition could spell the end of TunnelBear's free service. It's currently first in our roundup of the best free VPNs , but that could all change when it's integrated into McAfee Safe Connect, which has a different pricing model.
McAfee Safe Connect offers a free seven-day trial, but after that there's a subscription fee of $7.99 per month, or $47.88 per year.
There could also be a change in TunnelBear's terms. The Canadian company is known for its clear privacy policy, which explains every piece of data it collects from its users and why, but once the McAfee purchase is complete, it'll need to abide by US laws. If you currently use TunnelBear, it's well worth keeping an eye out for anything new.
What's Next for McAfee
The start of 2018 has been a busy time for McAfee. At last month's Mobile World Congress, it demonstrated a new feature for Amazon Alexa that lets you check the security of your home network and change its settings with just your voice. For example, you can see how many devices are connected, set a time limit for your child's iPad, and disconnect any devices you don't recognize.
Last month, the company also announced a deal with European internet provider Telefonica, providing security software for home and mobile networks. McAfee Secure Home Platform will be integrated with Telefonica's broadband routers, with extra protection for users' phones when they're out and about.
Could we soon see a voice-activated VPN from McAfee, or routers with TunnelBear tech built in? We'll be keeping an eye out.

rewrite:
McAfee, a major player in cybersecurity, has purchased the virtual private network company TunnelBear. The financial terms were not disclosed, but McAfee indicated it intends to merge TunnelBear's offerings with its existing Safe Connect VPN platform.

Christopher Young, McAfee's Chief Executive, stated the move aims to benefit customers and partners by incorporating TunnelBear's robust network infrastructure into the Safe Connect service.

This development may lead to the discontinuation of TunnelBear's complimentary VPN tier, which currently tops many lists of free services. Integration into McAfee's system, which operates on a distinct subscription basis, could alter its availability. Safe Connect provides a one-week free trial, followed by monthly charges of $7.99 or an annual rate of $47.88.

Additionally, TunnelBear's operational policies may shift. Recognized for its transparent privacy guidelines that detail all user data collection, the Canada-based firm will now be subject to United States regulations post-acquisition. Existing users are advised to monitor for updates to its terms.

McAfee has been active in early 2018. Recently, it showcased an Amazon Alexa skill enabling voice-controlled security checks and management for home networks. This allows users to review connected devices, impose time restrictions on specific gadgets like a child's tablet, and remove unfamiliar hardware from the network.

The company also entered a partnership with European telecom operator Telefonica to supply security solutions for residential and mobile internet services. Its Secure Home Platform will be embedded in Telefonica's routers, offering enhanced protection for mobile devices outside the home.

Future possibilities include a voice-command VPN from McAfee or networking hardware incorporating TunnelBear's technology, developments that will be watched closely.

Boeung Kak community members protest outside of the Council of Ministers office in Phnom Penh yesterday. Heng Chivoan
Authorities thwart Boeung Kak event
Some 30 Boeung Kak land activists yesterday were blocked by 50 Daun Penh district security guards from delivering a petition to the Council of Ministers seeking Prime Minister Hun Sen’s intervention in helping release fellow activist Tep Vanny.
The group of women claimed they were travelling by tuk-tuk to deliver the petition when they were stopped by security forces from leaving their neighbourhood.
The petition asks the premier to help free Vanny, who was arrested in August for taking part in a cursing ceremony. Since then, the court decided to revive two long-dormant cases against her, convicting her in one of them for allegedly using violence during a protest near Hun Sen’s house in 2013.
The petition also asks Hun Sen to stop arresting Boeung Kak women, and to help resolve the community’s land disputes.
“We are disappointed. This is the first time that authorities came and picked up the petition at the community,” said community representative Bov Sophea. “I think they tried to negotiate to avoid any problems.”
Kong Chamroeun, a representative of Hun Sen’s cabinet, picked up the petition and said it would be forwarded to the premier.
rewrite:
Residents of the Boeung Kak neighborhood gathered in protest yesterday in front of the Council of Ministers building in Phnom Penh. Heng Chivoan
Security personnel prevent Boeung Kak gathering

They sought Prime Minister Hun Sen's assistance in securing the release of fellow campaigner Tep Vanny.
The women stated they were en route by tuk-tuk to present the appeal when security personnel intercepted them, barring their exit from the community.
Their plea calls on the Prime Minister to aid Vanny, detained in August for involvement in a ritual involving curses. Subsequently, the court reactivated two inactive legal proceedings against her, finding her guilty in one related to accusations of aggressive conduct during a 2013 demonstration close to Hun Sen's residence.
The appeal further requests that Hun Sen cease the detention of Boeung Kak women and assist in settling the area's ongoing land conflicts.
"We are disheartened. Authorities have never before come to collect our petition directly from the community," remarked community spokesperson Bov Sophea. "I believe they aimed to engage in discussions to prevent potential issues."
Kong Chamroeun, an official from the Prime Minister's office, accepted the document and assured it would be delivered to Hun Sen.

A man dressed only in his pyjamas when seen by police outside his car failed to provide a breath test.
Kenneth Roberts, 53, explained how he had earlier gone in the Landrover to take his dog for a walk.
When they returned to the vehicle it would not start, so he walked home, a court in Mold was told.
Later in the pub he was warned of the danger of leaving his vehicle and walked back to ensure it was locked.
But he got soaked from the rain and was in the process of changing his overalls, with his pyjamas underneath, when the police arrived.
Roberts told Flintshire Magistrates Court that he did not provide a breath specimen at St Asaph police station on October 28 because he did not think he had done anything wrong.
He admitted failing to provide a breath specimen when suspected of being ‘in charge’ of the Landrover.
Roberts escaped a driving ban following a plea by barrister Owen Edwards, defending, that it would cause him exceptional hardship.
Roberts, of Main Road in Ffynnongroyw, was fined £650 with £85 costs and a £65 surcharge.
Magistrates said they believed it was a deliberate refusal, but they accepted that to ban him would mean the loss of his job.
That would mean the loss of his home and the effect that would have on his wife and his daughter.
His father-in-law and his sister also relied upon him being able to drive.
Magistrates said they accepted there was no suggestion that he intended to drive and the fact that the Landrover would not start at the time had influenced their decision.

Later, while at a pub, he was cautioned about the risks of abandoning his vehicle and returned to secure it. During this errand, he became drenched by rain and was in the midst of changing his outer clothing—with pajamas worn beneath—when police approached.

At Flintshire Magistrates Court, Roberts stated he refused the breath test at St Asaph police station on October 28, believing he had committed no offense. He pleaded guilty to failing to provide a specimen while suspected of being in charge of the vehicle. They concluded his refusal was intentional but acknowledged that disqualification would cost him his employment.

This job loss, in turn, would jeopardize his home and adversely impact his wife and daughter. Additionally, his father-in-law and sister depend on his ability to drive. The bench noted there was no indication he planned to drive and considered the fact that the Land Rover was inoperable at the time, which influenced their ruling. Roberts, residing on Main Road in Ffynnongroyw, received a £650 fine plus £85 in costs and a £65 surcharge.

MOGADISHU, Somalia (AP) — A Somali police officer says a suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at a security checkpoint near Mogadishu's international airport, killing at least three people.
Capt. Mohamed Hussein says the bomb detonated Monday as security forces were searching cars at the checkpoint, a few hundred meters (yards) from the main base of the African Union peacekeeping mission.
The checkpoint is close to United Nations offices and the Peace Hotel, which is often frequented by foreigners and officials. The powerful blast blew roofs off nearby buildings.
A second blast and heavy gunfire could be heard at the checkpoint after the attack, but there were no immediate details.
The al-Qaida-linked Islamic extremist group al-Shabab, which often carries out such attacks, quickly claimed responsibility for Monday's attack through its radio arm, Andalus.
Despite being ousted from most of its key strongholds across large parts of south and central Somalia, the homegrown group continues to wage deadly attacks across the country.
Somalia's capital has seen frequent bomb attacks at hotels and military checkpoints. In July, two al-Shabab suicide bombers detonated explosives-laden cars outside the office of the U.N.'s mine-clearing agency and an army checkpoint near the African Union's main base, killing 13.
The assaults have threatened this Horn of Africa nation's attempts to rebuild from decades of chaos. The country's presidential election, a key step toward recovery, already has been delayed multiple times because of security and other concerns.

The bombing occurred while officers were inspecting vehicles at the site, which lies only a short distance from the primary headquarters of the African Union's peacekeeping forces. This area is also near U.N. facilities and the Peace Hotel, a common gathering place for international visitors and officials. The force of the explosion was severe enough to tear the roofs from adjacent structures.

Following the initial blast, sounds of a second explosion and sustained gunfire emanated from the checkpoint, though specific information was not immediately available. The militant organization al-Shabab, affiliated with al-Qaida, promptly asserted responsibility for the assault via its radio broadcast, Andalus. Although pushed out from many major territories in southern and central Somalia, this domestic insurgent group persists in launching lethal attacks nationwide.

Mogadishu regularly experiences bombings targeting hotels and security posts. For instance, in July, two al-Shabab suicide attackers detonated car bombs near a United Nations de-mining office and a military checkpoint close to the AU base, killing thirteen people. These ongoing violent incidents jeopardize Somalia's efforts to recover after years of instability. The nation's repeatedly postponed presidential election, a crucial milestone in its rehabilitation, has been delayed further due to security threats and other issues.
