Standing seven feet tall and hailing from Nigeria, Azubuike was a regular starter last season, posting averages of 13 points and seven rebounds per game. His 77 percent field goal accuracy set a conference record and led the country.

His style is that of a classic interior center, which has led to questions about his fit in the modern NBA. The league's faster style and preference for centers who can score from distance do not align with his current game, making the development of a perimeter shot a probable focus during his upcoming season.

Azubuike noted he gathered valuable evaluations from NBA figures recently. By not retaining an agent, he maintained the option to withdraw by this week's cutoff date.

NEW YORK (AP) - The New York Jets signed former Lions linebacker Brandon Copeland and re-signed defensive lineman Xavier Cooper on Monday.
Copeland missed last season after tearing a pectoral muscle during the preseason. He had 30 tackles and one forced fumble in 32 games the previous two seasons with the Lions.
The 26-year-old Copeland is expected to serve as a backup on defense and be a key part of the Jets' special teams unit.
"Too many different levels of excitement to put into words," Copeland told the Jets' website. "Coming off of injured reserve, having to sit every Sunday, Monday and Thursday and watching other people play, I'm first and foremost excited to get back to the game that I love."
He signed with Baltimore as an undrafted free agent out of Penn in 2013 and spent time later that season on Tennessee's practice squad. After signing with Orlando of the Arena Football League in 2015, Copeland impressed Detroit after participating in the NFL Veterans Combine. His grandfather, Roy Hilton, played for the Baltimore Colts against the Jets in the Super Bowl in 1969.
"He played defensive end against Joe Namath and all those guys," Copeland said. "I know he's going to be very proud of his grandson and now my job is to continue to make him proud."
Cooper was not tendered as a restricted free agent, but was brought back to serve as a rotational defensive lineman. He had 16 tackles and one sack in eight games, and his play increased when Muhammad Wilkerson was benched at the end of last season.
Cooper was a third-round pick by Cleveland out of Washington State in 2015. He has also spent time with San Francisco, and has 56 career tackles and three sacks.

Expressing his enthusiasm on the team's official site, Copeland stated that after a year on injured reserve, watching games from the sidelines has made him incredibly eager to return to the sport he is passionate about.

His professional journey began in 2013 when he joined the Baltimore Ravens as an undrafted free agent from the University of Pennsylvania. He later spent time on the Tennessee Titans' practice squad that same year. Cooper, meanwhile, was re-signed after not receiving a restricted free agent tender. He is expected to resume his role in the defensive line rotation. Originally a third-round draft choice by the Cleveland Browns in 2015 out of Washington State, Cooper has also been with the San Francisco 49ers, accumulating 56 tackles and three sacks over his career.

Constable charged after overturning new police pickup at De Hoop
A policeman who was reportedly driving a police pickup when it crashed last week was yesterday placed on $40,000 bail.
The incident occurred on May 22, 2018 on the De Hoop Public Road, Mahaica, East Coast Demerara, resulting in extensive damage to the vehicle, PWW 5411.
According to the police, Constable Wellon Carr, 26, of Bee Hive, East Coast Demerara, was slapped with a dangerous driving charge.
The constable, who is stationed at Mahaica Police Station, appeared before Magistrate Wanda Fortune at the nearby Mahaica Magistrate’s Court and pleaded not guilty.
The case has been postponed to June 22 for trial.
Following the accident last week, Police Commissioner (ag), David Ramnarine, ordered a “thorough investigation” which involved one of the new Chinese pickups that was donated late last year.
According to a police statement, the crash occurred about 08:15hrs, on the De Hoop Public Road.
The statement confirmed that the Foton Tunland Pickup, was part of the Chinese grant last year, that also included ATVs, motorcycles and buses.
The police force said that the vehicle was driven by a constable under the command of a Corporal. They were proceeding west along the southern side of the road when the driver reportedly swerved further south from a cow.
In the process, he allegedly lost control and the vehicle careened off the road and came to a halt after it collided with a house and turned turtle.
“The two ranks along with another who was in the back seat, received minor injuries. They were taken to the Mahaicony Cottage Hospital where they were treated and sent away.
No one was in the house at the time of the incident,” the police said.
rewrite:
A police officer has been granted bail after being accused of reckless operation of a service vehicle that overturned recently at De Hoop. The constable, released on a $40,000 bond, faced the charge in connection with a collision that took place on May 22, 2018, along the De Hoop Public Road in Mahaica, East Coast Demerara. The crash caused significant harm to the pickup truck, identified as PWW 5411.

The accused, 26-year-old Constable Wellon Carr from Bee Hive, East Coast Demerara, is assigned to the Mahaica Police Station. He entered a plea of not guilty when he appeared before Magistrate Wanda Fortune at the Mahaica Magistrate’s Court. Proceedings have been adjourned until June 22, when the trial will commence.

Acting Police Commissioner David Ramnarine mandated a comprehensive inquiry into the event, which involved one of the recently acquired pickup trucks provided through Chinese assistance. Official reports note the time of the accident as approximately 8:15 a.m. on the same roadway. The damaged Foton Tunland pickup was among the items supplied by China the previous year, a donation that also featured all-terrain vehicles, motorcycles, and buses.

Authorities stated the constable was driving under the supervision of a corporal. While traveling westward on the road’s southern edge, the driver reportedly steered sharply to avoid a cow, leading to a loss of control. The vehicle then left the roadway, struck a house, and overturned. Two officers in the vehicle and a third in the rear sustained minor wounds and received treatment at Mahaicony Cottage Hospital before being released. The house was unoccupied at the time of the crash.

Harvard University Professor Jonathan L. Walton called the NRA a “domestic terrorist organization” during a speech at the campus’s Memorial Church.
advertisement
“We have to have the courage to call the NRA exactly what it has become — a domestic terrorist organization that places profit above the lives of the American people,” Dr. Jonathan Walton said at the Memorial Church of Harvard University.
Walton’s remarks were made available as a blog post on Harvard’s website. Walton, a Professor of Christian Morals and a minister at the Memorial Church at Harvard University, argued that America is “sick.”
“This nation is sick. Our cultural anxiety, toxic masculinity, and racial, religious, and ethnic bigotries are eating away at the soul of this nation,” he said. “It even caused us to elect a madman to the presidency that embodies the worst aspects of our country’s cultural disease. We have much to work through as a nation. But until we do, we cannot allow men like Dylan Roof, Omar Mateen, and Stephen Paddock such easy access to handheld weapons of mass destruction. ”
Walton cited work from the T.H. Chan School of Public Health at Harvard University. Research from the school argues that gun violence is a public health crisis in the United States. “U.S. children are fourteen times more likely to die by gun violence than any other developed nation. People die by gun at thirty times the rate of the United Kingdom. This is not normal,” Walton added.
Walton finished by condemning those who express concern about the gun violence in Chicago. “And please stop with the racialized red herring about Chicago, as if those who love to cite violence on that city’s Southside give a damn about the hell these people are catching each day,” he said. “It is time to stop the madness and excuses. We have to have the courage to call the NRA exactly what it has become — a domestic terrorist organization that places profit above the lives of the American people.”
rewrite:
In a recent address delivered at Harvard University's Memorial Church, Professor Jonathan L. Walton characterized the National Rifle Association as a group akin to domestic terrorists. He asserted that the organization prioritizes financial gain over the safety and lives of citizens in the United States.

His prepared comments were later published as an online article by the university. Walton, who serves as both a professor of Christian ethics and a minister at the church, contended that America is afflicted by a profound sickness. He described a national malaise fueled by widespread cultural unease, harmful expressions of masculinity, and deep-seated prejudices rooted in race, religion, and ethnicity, all of which are corroding the country's core. He further connected this climate to the election of a president who, in his view, personifies the most damaging elements of this societal illness. Walton emphasized that the nation has significant issues to resolve, and until that work progresses, individuals such as Dylan Roof, Omar Mateen, and Stephen Paddock must not be granted such straightforward access to firearms, which he termed portable weapons of mass destruction.

To support his argument, he referenced studies conducted by Harvard's T.H. Chan School of Public Health, which frame gun violence as a severe public health emergency. He highlighted statistics showing that children in the U.S. face a risk of firearm death fourteen times greater than their peers in other developed nations, and that the overall rate of gun fatalities is thirtyfold that of the United Kingdom, stating these figures are aberrant.

In conclusion, Walton criticized the frequent and, in his view, racially charged references to gun violence in Chicago, suggesting that those who cite it often lack genuine concern for the daily suffering in affected communities. He called for an end to irrationality and justifications, reiterating that courage is required to identify the NRA truthfully—as a domestic terrorist entity that values profit above human life.

VALENCIA, Spain — The Egyptian Football Federation says Mohamed Salah's shoulder injury will not keep him out for longer than three weeks, meaning he should be fit to play at least some part in the country's World Cup campaign.
The Liverpool forward was injured in the first half of Saturday's Champions League final against Real Madrid and left the field in tears. Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp said after the game that Salah's World Cup campaign was in jeopardy but the EFA gave an optimistic update on Wednesday after its president Hani Abu Reda, national team coach Hector Cuper and doctor Mohamed Abou El-Ela met with the forward in Valencia, where the 25-year-old is undergoing treatment and rehabilitation.
A post on the federation's Facebook page said that "the period of absence of Salah due to injury will not exceed three weeks."
That could still rule him out of Egypt's opening World Cup match on June 15 against Uruguay, with their second against hosts Russia coming four days later.

The Liverpool attacker sustained the injury during the initial half of the Champions League final last Saturday against Real Madrid and was visibly emotional as he exited the pitch. While Liverpool's Jurgen Klopp initially expressed concern that Salah might miss the tournament, the EFA provided a more hopeful outlook following a meeting in Valencia between Salah, federation president Hani Abu Reda, coach Hector Cuper, and team doctor Mohamed Abou El-Ela. Salah is currently receiving care and therapy there. An official update on the federation's social media stated his recovery timeline should not surpass three weeks. This may still prevent him from playing in Egypt's first World Cup game versus Uruguay on June 15, and potentially their subsequent match against Russia four days later.

FILE PHOTO: Dominique de Villepin makes a statement as part of his New Year's wishes to the media January 16, 2012 in Paris. REUTERS/Charles Platiau
PARIS Former Prime Minister Dominique de Villepin, a conservative Gaullist who won global celebrity by opposing U.S. plans for war in Iraq, said on Thursday he would back centrist candidate Emmanuel Macron in Sunday's presidential election.
"There is a new path, which Emmanuel Macron wants to open, and that is to unite," Villepin told Le Parisien newspaper.
He said in the face of the traditional left-right party system that was imprisoned by its own divisions and extremes that were determined to flip the table over the choice of Macron was obvious.
Villepin, prime minister between 2005-2007 under then president Jacques Chirac, is best known internationally for announcing Chirac's refusal to join a war against Saddam Hussein's Iraq in an impassioned speech at the United Nations in 2003 when he was foreign minister.
(Reporting by John Irish; editing by Michel Rose)
rewrite: In a 2012 file photograph, former French Prime Minister Dominique de Villepin is shown delivering New Year's remarks to the press in Paris. The conservative Gaullist, who gained international recognition for his stance against the U.S.-led invasion of Iraq, declared on Thursday his support for centrist Emmanuel Macron in the upcoming presidential vote. Villepin stated to Le Parisien that Macron represents a novel and unifying direction for the country. He explained that, confronted with a rigid left-right political structure paralyzed by internal conflict and radical factions, endorsing Macron was a clear decision. Serving as prime minister from 2005 to 2007 under President Jacques Chirac, Villepin is most famous globally for a 2003 address to the U.N. as foreign minister, where he forcefully declared France's opposition to the war in Iraq.

News of CBA CEO’s departure comes as bank faces court action launched by AUSTRAC
Commonwealth Bank of Australia CEO Ian Narev will leave CBA by the end of FY18.
The chair of the bank’s board, Catherine Livingstone, this morning announced details of the CEO’s departure. The exact timing will depend on the “outcome of an ongoing comprehensive internal and external search process,” Livingstone said in a statement.
“Succession planning is an ongoing process at all levels of the Bank. In discussions with Ian we have also agreed it is important for the business that we deal with the speculation and questions about his tenure. Today’s statement provides that clarity and will ensure he can continue to focus, as CEO, on successfully managing the business.”
Narev’s impending departure comes as the bank faces accusations of failing to meet its obligations under Australia’s anti-money-laundering rules.
AUSTRAC, which enforces the anti-money-laundering regime, has launched Federal Court action against the bank.
The bank has blamed a “coding error” for a failure to generate mandatory reports relating to large cash deposits made using its Intelligent Deposit Machines (IDMs).
AUSTRAC has said that CBA failed to report 53,506 “threshold transactions” — transactions involving $10,000 or more — between 5 November 2012 and 1 September 2015.
“Suspected money laundering was conducted through CommBank accounts, by way of cash deposits, many through IDMs, followed immediately by international and domestic transfers,” an AUSTRAC court filing states.
CBA has been accused of failing to report suspicious matters either on time or at all involving transactions totalling over $77 million.
The bank has said that when the IDMs were first rolled out, the correct threshold transaction reports (TTRs) were generated. However after a software update “a coding error occurred which meant the IDMs did not create the TTRs needed.”
Earlier this month CBA reported statutory net profit after tax of $9.93 billion for the full year, up 7.6 per cent, and cash net NPAT of $9.88 billion, up 4.6 per cent. The Commonwealth Bank of Australia’s IT services expenses hit $1.94 billion in the 12 months ending 30 June, the bank reported.
rewrite:

This announcement was made by the board's chair, Catherine Livingstone, who stated that the precise date of departure is contingent upon finding a suitable successor through a thorough search process currently underway.

Livingstone emphasized that planning for leadership transitions is a continuous activity within the institution. She noted that the decision to clarify Narev's tenure was mutual, aimed at ending speculation and allowing him to concentrate fully on his duties as CEO in steering the bank.

This news emerges while the financial institution is confronting legal proceedings initiated by AUSTRAC, the national agency responsible for enforcing anti-money laundering laws. The regulator alleges that CBA did not comply with its legal requirements to report certain financial activities.

According to the court action, the bank neglected to submit 53,506 mandatory reports for cash transactions exceeding $10,000, which occurred over a nearly three-year period. AUSTRAC's filings further claim that accounts at the bank were used for suspected money laundering, where cash was deposited—often via automated deposit machines—and then rapidly transferred elsewhere.

The bank attributes this widespread reporting failure to a software flaw, stating that while its Intelligent Deposit Machines initially generated the required alerts, a subsequent update introduced a coding error that halted these reports. CBA is also accused of not reporting, or delaying reports on, suspicious activities worth more than $77 million.

Despite these legal challenges, CBA recently disclosed strong annual financial results, including a statutory net profit approaching $10 billion, which reflects a significant increase. The bank also reported substantial expenditures on information technology services, which totaled nearly $2 billion for the past financial year.

While she did not identify the journalist, she did later specify that they are male.

On Tuesday afternoon, New York Times features writer and documentary filmmaker Jacob Bernstein confessed that he had been the one gossiping about the First Lady.

“My mistake, referring to unfounded rumors, shouldn’t reflect on anyone else and I apologize profusely,” he continued.
Ratajkowski is known perhaps as much for her political stances, particularly concerning feminism, as she is for her modeling. The outspoken Bernie Sanders supporter has long maintained that women can be both intelligent and sexual — if and when they choose.

One day after news broke that Selena Gomez recently sought treatment in New York City for depression and anxiety, the star stepped out Friday in Los Angeles looking happy and healthy.
Wearing vintage overalls, the singer, 25, met up with friends at Mexican restaurant Casa Vega in Los Angeles for lunch.
On Thursday, a source close to Gomez confirmed she completed a two-week treatment program after feeling “like she needed to get away and focus on herself with no distractions.”
The entertainer reportedly stayed on-site at the center and underwent therapy, ate healthy meals and took Pilates and meditation sessions.
“She came back feeling very empowered,” said the source. “She feels and looks great. She’s still working on new music and is excited about it.”
Gomez is still going strong with on-again beau Justin Bieber, 23, who the source says has been supportive of her decision to focus on her emotional health.
RELATED VIDEO: Selena Gomez Visits Childhood Home and Wonders If It ‘Could Have Been Better Than My Life Today’
In 2016, she also stepped away from the spotlight and sought professional treatment after suffering from “anxiety, panic attacks and depression” as side effects of her lupus.
Gomez — who underwent a kidney transplant with an organ donated by her longtime friend Francia Raisa last summer — has gotten increasingly candid about her struggles with mental health and the challenges she’s faced growing up in the spotlight.
In her first public appearance after her career break, Gomez got emotional onstage at the American Music Awards when thanking her fans for their unwavering support.
“I think it’s safe to say that all of you know my life whether I like it or not. I had to stop because I had everything and I was absolutely broken inside,” she told the audience. “I kept it all together enough to where I would never let you down but I kept it too much together to where I let myself down. If you are broken, you do not have to stay broken.”
rewrite:
Following reports that Selena Gomez had received care in New York for anxiety and depression, the celebrity was seen in Los Angeles the next day appearing cheerful and well. The 25-year-old artist, dressed in a pair of classic overalls, joined some companions for a midday meal at Casa Vega, a Mexican eatery in LA.

A confidant verified on Thursday that Gomez had just finished a fortnight of dedicated treatment, explaining she had felt the necessity to retreat and concentrate on herself without interruptions. During her time at the facility, she participated in therapeutic sessions, maintained a nutritious diet, and engaged in Pilates and meditation practices. The insider noted that she returned from the experience with a strong sense of personal strength, adding that she appears and feels wonderful and remains actively and enthusiastically involved in creating new music.

Gomez continues to maintain her rekindled relationship with Justin Bieber, 23, who, according to the source, has been understanding and supportive of her choice to prioritize her emotional well-being. This is not the first time Gomez has taken a break for her health; in 2016, she also retreated from public life to receive professional help for anxiety, panic attacks, and depression, which were complications related to her lupus diagnosis.

Having undergone a kidney transplant last summer, with her friend Francia Raisa as the donor, Gomez has become more open in discussing her mental health challenges and the difficulties of maturing under constant public scrutiny. At the American Music Awards, marking her return to public events, she became tearful while addressing the audience. She expressed gratitude for her fans' steadfast support, acknowledging that while the public is deeply familiar with her life, she felt compelled to pause her career. Despite having outward success, she felt internally shattered. Gomez shared that she had worked hard to avoid disappointing others but, in doing so, had neglected her own needs. She concluded with a message of hope, affirming that those who feel broken are not obligated to remain in that state.

President Donald Trump on Monday dismissed questions about his two-day delay before condemning hate groups by name after a white supremacist rally turned deadly over the weekend.
“Mr. President, can you explain why you did not condemn those hate groups by name over the weekend?” CNN’s Jim Acosta asked Trump after a bill signing ceremony at the White House.
“They’ve been condemned,” Trump replied. “They have been condemned.”
Trump did in fact condemn “criminals and thugs, including the KKK, neo-Nazis, white supremacists, and other hate groups” on Monday from the White House, but only after intense criticism after he blamed “many sides” for the carnage in Charlottesville on Saturday.
The white supremacist rally in the city was held in response to the planned removal of a statue of Confederate Gen. Robert E. Lee. One man who had earlier been photographed with a white supremacist group allegedly drove his car into a crowd of counter-protesters, killing one and injuring more than a dozen.
Acosta followed up, referencing a planned press conference that Trump on Friday had promised would occur Monday: “And why are we not having a press conference today? You said on Friday we’d have a press conference?”
“We had a press conference,” Trump said. “We just had a press conference.”
Trump had not just held a press conference. That would involve answering journalist’s questions at more length than responding to shouted requests after a bill signing.
“Can we ask you more questions, then, sir?” Acosta asked.
“It doesn’t bother me at all, but I like real news, not fake news,” Trump responded. “You’re fake news. Thank you everybody.”
Acosta shouted as Trump left: “Haven’t you spread a lot of fake news yourself, sir?”
Watch below via ABC News:
rewrite:
On Monday, President Donald Trump deflected inquiries regarding his two-day hesitation to specifically denounce extremist factions following a lethal white nationalist gathering. During a White House event for signing a bill, CNN correspondent Jim Acosta questioned Trump, asking why he had not named these groups over the weekend. Trump asserted that they had already been denounced.

Earlier that day, facing significant backlash for initially attributing the violence in Charlottesville to "many sides," Trump did issue a statement from the White House condemning "criminals and thugs," explicitly listing the KKK, neo-Nazis, white supremacists, and similar organizations. The deadly incident occurred when a man, previously seen with white supremacists, rammed his vehicle into opposing demonstrators, resulting in one death and multiple injuries. The original rally had been organized to protest the removal of a statue of Confederate General Robert E. Lee.

Acosta then referenced a promised Monday press conference that Trump had announced the previous Friday, questioning its absence. Trump claimed a press conference had just occurred, although the brief exchange with reporters after a bill signing did not constitute a formal question-and-answer session. When Acosta requested to pose further questions, Trump retorted by criticizing what he called "fake news," directly labeling Acosta as such, before concluding the interaction. As the president departed, Acosta called after him, asking if Trump himself had not disseminated false information.

Pret A Manger’s soon-to-open Penn Station eatery will have a full-service 12-seat U-shaped beer and wine bar, The Post has learned.
The bar concept, tested for years in London, is the first of its kind for Pret in the US.
It will feature beer in bottles and on tap and wine from California, Italy and New Zealand, the company said.
The Penn Station location — at 5,968 square feet, twice as big at its standard location — will also feature communal tables as well as high-top cocktail seating.
“Our baristas make thousands of coffees every day for our customers, so we thought, why not offer beer and wine too,” said Joanne Brett, president of the company’s operations in the US, where it has 76 eateries in New York, Boston, Washington, DC, and Chicago.
By adding alcohol to its menu, Pret joins a handful of other quick-service eateries — Shake Shack and Chipotle, for example, plus fast-food spin-off BK Whopper Bar in Miami.
If the Penn Station bar concept is a hit, Pret may expand it to other US locations, Brett told The Post.
Earlier this year, Starbucks ended its year-old beer and wine program in more than 400 stores — but may add alcohol to the menu at its upscale Roastery stores, according to several reports.
At the Penn Station Pret, customers will have to purchase their food separately and bring it to the bar, a Pret spokeswoman said.
With 450 eateries worldwide, privately owned Pret is opening another 12 stores in the US this year, compared with nine new stores last year, the spokeswoman said.
rewrite:
According to a report, Pret A Manger is preparing to launch a novel bar at its upcoming Penn Station location. This U-shaped, twelve-seat counter will provide full beverage service, marking the brand's initial American foray into a concept long trialed in its British outlets. The selection will include draft and bottled beers alongside wines sourced from regions like California, Italy, and New Zealand.

Spanning nearly 6,000 square feet, this site is double the company's typical footprint and will incorporate shared tables and elevated seating for drinks. Joanne Brett, the U.S. operations head, explained the logic behind serving alcohol, noting that since baristas already prepare countless coffees daily, adding beer and wine was a natural progression. This move aligns Pret with other limited-service chains such as Shake Shack and Chipotle, which have also incorporated alcoholic options.

The success of this Penn Station experiment could lead to its introduction at other U.S. shops. This development follows Starbucks' recent decision to discontinue its evening alcohol program in hundreds of cafes, though it might retain such offerings in its premium Roastery locations. At Pret's new venue, patrons must buy their meals separately from the bar service. The privately held global chain, which operates 450 shops, is accelerating its U.S. growth, with twelve new stores planned for this year compared to nine in the previous year.

Nine year NFL veteran Jarvis Green went from winning two championships with the New England Patriots and Tom Brady to becoming the CEO of Oceans 97, a National Minority Supply Diversity Chain Company that began in 2015.
This new, gourmet line features easy-to-cook meals of shrimp packaged in bags, with four flavors of sauce to choose from; New Orleans Style BBQ, Cajun Curry, Chimichurri, and Garlic Butter. The shrimp is domestic, wild caught, Gulf of Mexico shrimp, caught by US Gulf Coast fisherman and processed in Louisiana. The product ships in dry ice directly to the customer and arrives ready for cooking a delicious and satisfying family meal or when entertaining.
Green owed a friend a favor. That particular friend already had a shrimping business with 90 employees and access to 800 shrimping boats in Vietnam and so he jumped on the idea to get into the shrimping business.
“I had opportunities to go do coaching,” Jarvis Green told Brandon ‘Scoop B’ Robinson on the Scoop B Radio Podcast.
“I had opportunities to go do broadcasting, being an analyst, boot camps, clinics all that stuff, you know, with ESPN.”
Green took an unpaid internship and learned everything about shrimp and by the end of his internship. he even made purchasing orders to distributors. “Worked from the ground up,” he said. “From the first person in the shrimp plant, sweeping, mopping, cleaning bathrooms, cleaning the kitchen area.”
From there, he created Oceans 97, a nod to his uniform number. Through the relationship with Dole & Bailey, Oceans 97 shrimp is distributed to major financial institutions throughout New England and other products remain available in multiple grocery retail locations around the country. “When you taste it, it’s just on your pallet,” he said.
“It’s savoriness and it just sticks with you man, you want to go grab a glass of wine and just wash it down. It’s elegant, fine dining at its best for under $10.99.”
rewrite:

Its flagship offering is a premium collection of convenient shrimp meals, featuring domestic, wild-caught shrimp from the Gulf of Mexico. Sourced by fishermen along the U.S. Gulf Coast and processed in Louisiana, the shrimp is delivered directly to consumers in packaging cooled by dry ice. Each order includes a selection of four gourmet sauces: New Orleans Style BBQ, Cajun Curry, Chimichurri, and Garlic Butter, providing a simple solution for preparing a quality dinner at home, whether for family or guests.

Green’s entry into this industry originated from a favor owed to a friend who operated an established shrimp enterprise with a substantial workforce and connections to hundreds of fishing vessels in Vietnam. Intrigued by the opportunity, Green decided to pursue the venture. He had other prospects, including roles in coaching, sports broadcasting, analysis, and running training clinics, some with networks like ESPN. Instead, he committed to an unpaid internship to thoroughly understand the shrimp business. Starting with the most basic tasks—sweeping floors, mopping, cleaning restrooms and kitchen spaces—he worked his way up, eventually gaining the expertise to place purchase orders with distributors.

He later launched Oceans 97, a name that honors his former jersey number. A partnership with Dole & Bailey enables the distribution of Oceans 97 shrimp to prominent financial institutions across New England, while other products are stocked in various grocery retailers nationwide. Green describes the flavor as memorable and rich, leaving a lasting impression that pairs well with a glass of wine. He emphasizes that the product delivers an upscale dining experience, elegance and all, for a price point below $10.99.

At the age of 16 Herman's activities had already been picked up by the judicial authorities. He was locked up in a closed youth detention centre outside Brussels. In 2005 he is sentenced to 30 months in jail following a conviction for GBH and burglary. Two years later he gets 12 months for drugs related offences plus an extra four months on account of his recalcitrant behaviour. Three years is his sentence in 2008 for violent theft and resisting arrest. In 2009 he enjoys penitential leave for 16 hours for a first time. He will enjoy penitential leave on 14 occasions during his jail career. A further 16 months in jail is his lot in 2010 for GBH and resisting arrest.
At the end of 2015 Herman switches to a limited detention regime: he's allowed out during the day but must return to prison at night. This is ended in 2016 after he fails to return to jail in the evenings. In 2016 Herman is given a further 12 months for theft, but is again awarded penitential leave in 2016.
On Monday of this week Herman leaves prison thanks to his penitential leave permit. He's enjoyed this on 13 occasions in the past without any problems. This time it goes wrong and the spate of killings begins.
rewrite:
By sixteen, Herman had already drawn the attention of the courts, resulting in his placement within a secure juvenile facility near Brussels. A 2005 conviction for serious assault and break-ins led to a thirty-month prison term. Subsequent sentences followed: a year in 2007 for drug crimes, extended by four months due to non-compliance, and a three-year term in 2008 for a violent robbery and evading police. His first brief release of sixteen hours occurred in 2009, a privilege he would later receive fourteen times throughout his incarceration. Another sixteen months were added in 2010 for grievous bodily harm and resisting arrest.

Late in 2015, he transitioned to a partial confinement system, permitting daytime freedom with nightly returns to prison, which was revoked in 2016 after he violated the curfew. That same year, a further twelve-month sentence for theft was imposed, yet he was again granted temporary release.

This Monday, Herman departed prison under such a release permit, a measure he had utilized thirteen times previously without incident. On this occasion, however, the outcome was tragically different, marking the start of a deadly series of events.

BRUSSELS A country's spending on development aid and on defence are separate items, NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg said on Friday, responding to German comments about NATO's target for increasing military budgets.
German Foreign Minister Sigmar Gabriel had said on Thursday that it was not realistic for Germany to spend 2 percent of its economic output on defence and that other spending, such as development aid, should be taken into consideration.
"Diplomacy, development aid, economic cooperation can be important to help stabilise a region," Stoltenberg told a news conference in Brussels.
"We have international targets, guidelines, for development aid, 0.7 percent of GDP and then we have a NATO agreement on moving towards 2 percent. But those are two different things, even though both are important," he added.
"It is not either development or security, it is development and security and the foundation of development is to have peace and security."
(Reporting by Robert-Jan Bartunek; editing by Philip Blenkinsop)
rewrite:
NATO's chief Jens Stoltenberg stated on Friday that a nation's expenditures for development assistance and for military needs are distinct, addressing recent remarks from Germany. This came after German Foreign Minister Sigmar Gabriel expressed that expecting Germany to allocate two percent of its economic output to defense was unrealistic, suggesting that other outlays like development aid be factored in.

Speaking in Brussels, Stoltenberg acknowledged that diplomacy, development aid, and economic collaboration can significantly contribute to regional stability. He clarified that while international benchmarks exist for development aid, such as the 0.7 percent of GDP target, and a separate NATO pact aims for members to approach spending 2 percent on defense, these are separate commitments. Both are crucial, he emphasized, explaining that security and development are not a choice between one or the other. Instead, development relies on a foundation of peace and security, making the two complementary objectives.

Vigil for Man Who Died After Crashing Into El Cajon Building
The family of a man who died after crashing into an El Cajon building has planned a vigil to celebrate his spirit.
Police believe Dreivon Young, 46, lost consciousness behind the wheel of his truck before he drove through a parking lot and crashed into a structure on the 1400 block of Cuyamaca Street on Monday.
Young was transported to the hospital where he later died.
Lisa Dennison, the mother of Young's three sons, said she drove to the scene immediately after being notified by a neighbor who recognized Young's truck in pictures from the scene.
Man Slams Truck into El Cajon Building in Fatal Crash
NBC 7's Ashley Matthews is at the scene of the crash where a man died after losing consciousness behind the wheel and driving into a building. (Published Monday, Jan. 29, 2018)
“He used to come over, you know, and see my sons a lot. So where I live, everyone knows his truck” Dennison explained.
Dennison and Young were together for 6 years and in that time had three sons. They’ve remained friends for over 20 years.
She told NBC 7 that she is trying her hardest to stay strong for their children.
“I try to hold my feelings back where they don’t see me cry or whatever," she said. “So every night I come up and light his candles."
A memorial near the boarded up windows where the truck crashed has been growing throughout the week. Dennison said she feels like she is still in shock.
“His truck really went through this building?” Dennison said, looking at the crash site.
Dennison and her sons are waiting for the autopsy to understand how this horrible accident happened.
Until then, the family is looking forward to a vigil planned Saturday at 6:00 p.m. at 1417 Cuyamaca Street.
“I just want everyone to smile and look up and know they all came -- Dreivon, we all came here to see, to feel your spirit and just be happy you know."

Chinese politics in the main is carried out in the shadows, shielded from public scrutiny and producing pre-determined outcomes through a process termed democracy according to socialism with Chinese characteristics.
China's rubber-stamp legislature, the National People's Congress, is no different, with the nearly 3,000 delegates unfailingly voting according to the program handed down to them by the Communist Party leadership.
This year's session saw the approval of constitutional amendments allowing President Xi Jinping to continue in office for an unlimited number of terms and reappointing him as head of state by a margin of 2,970 to none.
More than ever, the rank and file of the one-party authoritarian state appear as faceless cogs and silhouettes in the wheel of governance, devoid of personal views that might clash with the leadership's and content to serve a regime that has delivered relative prosperity and political stability to China for four decades.

The National People's Congress, a legislative body that routinely endorses pre-established agendas, follows this pattern. Its approximately 3,000 delegates consistently align their votes with the directives of the ruling Communist Party. During the most recent assembly, constitutional changes were passed unanimously—2,970 votes in favor, zero against—to remove term limits for the presidency, thereby reinstating Xi Jinping. Within this centralized system, individual members increasingly function as anonymous components of the state machinery, setting aside personal opinions that could diverge from the official line. They generally support a governance model that has maintained economic growth and social order in the country for over forty years.

BATON ROUGE, La. — A senior federal judge in Louisiana died Saturday, days before he was to preside over the trial of a private investigator accused of trying to get Donald Trump’s tax returns illegally during the 2016 presidential campaign, court officials said.
Chief Judge Brian A. Jackson of Louisiana’s Middle District said Saturday in a statement that Judge James J. Brady had died. Michael McConnell, clerk of court for the district, confirmed that Brady died Saturday at a Baton Rouge hospital after a brief illness.
Brady was to preside as jury selection began Monday in the trial of Jordan Hamlett. It was not immediately clear what would happen with the trial following Brady’s death.
The 32-year-old Lafayette resident is charged with misusing a Social Security number in his attempts to access Trump’s tax information through a government website. Authorities say Hamlett failed in his attempts to get Trump’s tax returns several weeks before last year’s presidential election.
Hamlett’s attorney says he didn’t have “intent to deceive” — a key element of the charge he faces.
Every president since Jimmy Carter has released tax returns, in what has become an American tradition during presidential elections. Trump has refused to release his.
A biography on the court’s website says Brady was nominated to the bench in 1999 by then-President Bill Clinton and assumed senior status in December 2013. Senior status is a form of semi-retirement for federal judges, who get lifetime appointments. It enables them to take reduced caseloads while continuing to draw a salary.
The district’s chief judge said in his statement that Brady’s fellow judges “mourn the loss of our esteemed colleague and friend.” He continued, “Judge Brady’s remarkable career as a federal judge was exemplary and his commitment to providing equal justice under the law resonated throughout his career as a lawyer and a judge. He will forever be remembered for his extraordinary integrity, compassion and devotion to the rule of law.”
Louisiana Gov. John Bel Edwards said in a statement that Brady “represented honesty, fairness and integrity on the federal bench in Louisiana, and his wisdom in the courtroom will be sorely missed.”
Acting U.S. Attorney Corey R. Amundson called him “a great man, and a dedicated jurist with tremendous compassion, integrity and ability.”

Hamlett, a 32-year-old from Lafayette, faces accusations of improperly using a Social Security number in an effort to acquire Trump's tax information via a government website. Prosecutors state that these unsuccessful attempts were made in the weeks preceding the presidential election last year.

According to Hamlett's lawyer, his client lacked "intent to deceive," which is a fundamental component of the accusation against him.

The release of tax returns has been a customary practice for presidential candidates since the administration of Jimmy Carter. Trump has notably broken with this tradition by declining to make his returns public.

Acting U.S. Attorney Corey R. Amundson described him as "an exceptional individual and a committed judge, possessing profound empathy, integrity, and skill."

Is there a chance that power suit you put on daily is the reason behind your drive and success? Is there also a chance those jeans and polo shirts that make up your work wardrobe are dragging you down? Finally, could the clothing choices have nothing to do with one’s productivity at work?
Vishal Agarwal, who used to be the managing director at GE, just wrote a new book suggesting that the productivity of workers who tend to go more casual may be “taking a vacation.” In the book titled “Give to Get: A Senior Leaders Guide to Navigating Corporate Life,” he argues that even “techies” need to start dressing for success.
In an interview Mike Doria did with Agarwal, he does clarify saying that if you are in a job that requires a suit, like a lawyer or CEO, then suits and standards need to be in place daily to “be on their best foot, to be commercially intensive, to get going. And I feel that in those environments like investment banking, corporate, consulting, legal -- that (dressing casually) does impede productivity.
Agarwal said workers need to fit the brand so if the brand does allow for a more casual dress code, that is fine as long as it fits the company’s casual standard. But he added that sloppy clothes and not being clean-shaven is not “business casual.” The four dress categories for work do have some crossover but Agarwal said your company’s handbook should clear up any confusion. In all his leadership roles, Agarwal said he’s never seen any data, other than anecdotal, suggesting incremental output from employees who are dressed casually.

rewrite:
Could the professional attire you select each morning actually fuel your ambition and achievements? Conversely, might a habitual wardrobe of denim and relaxed shirts subtly hinder your performance? Or is it possible that what we wear holds no real sway over our workplace efficiency?

Former GE managing director Vishal Agarwal explores these questions in his recent book, "Give to Get: A Senior Leaders Guide to Navigating Corporate Life." He proposes that employees who consistently opt for very informal clothing might see their effectiveness decline, implying their productivity is "on a break." Agarwal contends that even professionals in technical fields should consider dressing more formally to enhance their prospects.

In a discussion with interviewer Mike Doria, Agarwal elaborated. For roles where formal suits are the norm—such as in law, executive leadership, or investment banking—maintaining that standard daily is crucial. He believes it helps individuals present their best selves, stay commercially focused, and maintain momentum. In these high-stakes sectors like consulting, corporate finance, and legal services, a casual approach to attire can, in his view, actually obstruct productivity.

Agarwal emphasizes aligning with a company's image. If an organization permits a relaxed dress code, that is acceptable provided employees adhere to its specific definition of casual wear. He cautions, however, that wrinkled clothing or poor grooming does not qualify as "business casual." While the four general categories of work attire can overlap, Agarwal points to a company's official guidelines as the ultimate clarifier. Throughout his career in leadership, he notes never encountering concrete evidence—only personal stories—that dressing casually boosts an employee's work output.

Fighters and team members prepare backstage before matches of a Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) competition in Kabul, Afghanistan March 30, 2017. REUTERS/Omar Sobhani
An Afghan athlete is checked before a mixed martial arts (MMA) match in Kabul, Afghanistan March 30, 2017. REUTERS/Omar Sobhani

An Afghan fighter in knockout in the ring during a mixed martial arts (MMA) match in Kabul, Afghanistan March 30, 2017. REUTERS/Omar Sobhani
KABUL In a custom-built arena in Kabul, crowds cheered as young Afghan men punched, kicked, and wrestled in the country's first professional mixed martial arts league, a welcome distraction to the violence besetting the country.
While cricket and football more commonly grab public attention in Afghanistan, fighters and fans see martial arts not just as entertainment but as a constructive pastime for youths in a country torn by war and economic malaise.
Against a soundtrack of booming music and shouts of encouragement, sweat and blood mixed inside the cage. Each match, however, ended in a hug.
"I think it provides a very good platform for the social frustrations that we have here in Afghanistan," said Kakal Noristani, who a year and a half ago helped found the Snow Leopard Fighting Championship.
To date, only men have competed in the handful of competitions, but organizers say they are training women fighters. The walls of the club feature posters of American martial arts competitor Ronda Rousey.
Noristani and his partners want to develop mixed martial arts as a professional sport in Afghanistan, hoping to host foreign fighters and send Afghan competitors abroad.
"We’ve just begun here in Afghanistan," Noristani said. "The professional structure was non-existent before this."
That's helped some fighters dream of national and international glory.
"This is the wish of every fighter: To reach the highest level and be able to fight abroad," said Mir Baba Nadery, who won his match that night.
Outside the cage, spectators expressed gratitude for a diversion from the country's woes.
"Coming to these kind of events takes your mind off of our problems," said Nadia Sina. "We are happy to see such an organization encouraging sportsmen and improving the sport in the country."
(Writing by Josh Smith; editing by Richard Lough)

In Kabul, Afghanistan, on March 30, 2017, competitors and their teams made final preparations behind the scenes for an upcoming Mixed Martial Arts event. At the same competition, a combatant undergoes a pre-fight inspection. Following a successful bout, another athlete revels in his win, while a different fighter is shown having been knocked out in the ring. All these scenes were captured by photographer Omar Sobhani.

Within a specially constructed venue in the Afghan capital, spectators roared their approval as local youths engaged in striking and grappling contests. This inaugural professional MMA promotion offered a temporary respite from the persistent conflict plaguing the nation. Although sports like cricket and soccer typically dominate the public consciousness, participants and supporters view martial arts as more than mere spectacle. They consider it a positive outlet for young people in a nation struggling with the effects of prolonged war and financial hardship.

Inside the fighting enclosure, the din of loud music and supportive yells accompanied the intense physical exchanges. Despite the visible exertion and occasional bloodshed, every contest concluded with an embrace between the adversaries. Kakal Noristani, a co-founder of the Snow Leopard Fighting Championship established roughly eighteen months prior, remarked, “I believe it offers a very positive channel for the societal tensions we experience in Afghanistan.”

Thus far, a limited number of events have featured exclusively male athletes, but officials note they are instructing women as well. The gym’s decor includes images of international star Ronda Rousey. Noristani and his colleagues aim to cultivate MMA as a professional pursuit locally, with aspirations to eventually stage events with international fighters and send Afghan athletes to compete overseas. “We are only at the start in Afghanistan,” Noristani explained. “A professional framework was completely absent before this initiative.”

This new structure has allowed fighters to envision achieving recognition both at home and internationally. Mir Baba Nadery, victorious that evening, stated, “Every combatant shares this goal: to attain the top tier and compete in other countries.” Among the audience, there was appreciation for this brief escape from daily hardships. Attendee Nadia Sina expressed, “Being at events like this helps you forget our troubles. We are pleased to see an organization fostering athletes and advancing sports here.” This report was written by Josh Smith and edited by Richard Lough.

After thrilling more than 8 million people worldwide, CORTEO will visit Chattanooga at the McKenzie Arena for a limited run of six performances, from May 10 to 13, 2018.
This unique production directed by Daniele Finzi Pasca premiered in Montreal in April 2005 and has visited 64 cities in 19 countries.
CORTEO, which means cortege in Italian, is a joyous procession, a festive parade imagined by a clown. The show brings together the passion of the actor with the grace and power of the acrobat to plunge the audience into a theatrical world of fun, comedy and spontaneity situated in a mysterious space between heaven and earth.
The clown pictures his own funeral taking place in a carnival atmosphere, watched over by quietly caring angels. Juxtaposing the large with the small, the ridiculous with the tragic and the magic of perfection with the charm of imperfection, the show highlights the strength and fragility of the clown, as well as his wisdom and kindness, to illustrate the portion of humanity that is within each of us. The music turns lyrical and playful carrying CORTEO through a timeless celebration in which illusion teases reality.
The cast of CORTEO includes 51 acrobats, musicians, singers and actors from all around the world.

BLOEMFONTEIN, South Africa — South Africa openers Aiden Markram and Dean Elgar both made centuries to punish Bangladesh's decision to bowl first in the second test on Friday.
Markram was 135 not out and Elgar fell for 113 to break their 243-run stand for the opening wicket. South Africa moved to 256-1 at tea on the opening day at Mangaung Oval in what was shaping up to be a repeat of the first test.
Then, Bangladesh misread the pitch, put South Africa in to bat, and the South Africans made 496-3 declared in their first innings on the way to a comfortable victory.
Elgar made a second century in two tests after his 199 in that big first-innings score in the first game. Markram, out for 97 on his debut in the first test, did complete a maiden test hundred this time in Bloemfontein.
He had hit 21 fours and was with Hashim Amla (1 not out) at the tea break. South Africa was moving along swiftly at over 4 1/2 runs an over.
Elgar now has five centuries in 2017 and is the leading scorer in test cricket this year. He and Markram have put on two big opening partnerships in their first two tests playing together, 196 in the opening game and the double-century stand on Friday.
Elgar fell to a short-ball tactic that Bangladesh persevered with through most of the day, and ultimately had success with. Subashis Roy banged in a short one, Elgar went for a hook, and was caught at backward square leg by Mustafizur Rahman.
The touring bowlers reverted to the short stuff after getting little out of the pitch early on. They were also wayward, conceding 38 boundaries in the first two sessions.
Bangladesh made four changes to its lineup for the second and final match, dropping three bowlers and bringing in Subashis, Rubel Hossain and Taijul Islam. South Africa was without injured strike bowler Morne Morkel. Wayne Parnell replaced him.
By The Associated Press

By the tea interval, the host nation had reached 256-1 at Mangaung Oval, suggesting a pattern similar to the previous test might emerge. In that earlier contest, Bangladesh also erred in assessing the conditions, invited South Africa to bat, and watched them declare at 496-3 before securing a straightforward win.

Elgar recorded his second hundred in consecutive matches, following his 199 in the first test. Markram, who was out for 97 in his debut test, now achieved his first test century here. He had struck 21 fours and was joined at the break by Hashim Amla, who was on 1. The scoring rate exceeded 4.5 runs per over, maintaining a brisk pace.

With five test hundreds this year, Elgar is currently the top run-scorer in the format for 2017. Together, he and Markram have now shared two substantial opening stands in their first two tests as a pair: 196 in the initial match and their 200-plus partnership this Friday.

Elgar’s dismissal came from a persistent short-pitched bowling strategy employed by Bangladesh throughout much of the day. Subashis Roy delivered a bouncer that Elgar attempted to hook, resulting in a catch by Mustafizur Rahman at backward square leg. The visiting bowlers turned to short deliveries after finding little assistance from the pitch early on and struggled with their line, allowing 38 boundaries in the first two sessions.

For this final match of the series, Bangladesh altered their side with four changes, including three bowling swaps that introduced Subashis, Rubel Hossain, and Taijul Islam. South Africa missed injured fast bowler Morne Morkel, with Wayne Parnell taking his place.

HEMPSTEAD, N.Y. — Grant Riller scored 24 points, Jarrell Brantley poured in 23 more, including the winning layup, and Charleston edged Hofstra 86-85 on Saturday night to take sole possession of first place in the Colonial Athletic Association.
Trailing by a point after Hofstra’s Justin Wright-Foreman sank a 3-pointer with 18 seconds left, Charleston (18-6, 9-3) took the ball down the right side of the court and got it inside to Brantley, who dribbled twice to his right before breaking left to drop in the winning bucket with three seconds remaining.
Joe Chealey added 19 points and Nick Harris had 10 for Charleston, which shot 57 per cent and got 18 assists on its 30 baskets to pick up its sixth straight win.
Wright-Foreman finished with 24 points to lead Hofstra (14-10, 7-5), Eli Pemberton added 20, Jalen Ray got 11 and Kenny Wormley 10.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has again upped its forecast for global growth this year due to buoyant financial markets and a cyclical recovery in manufacturing and trade.
The Washington-based organisation’s forecast rose from 3.1 per cent last year to 3.4 per cent in January. In its latest World Economic Outlook, published on Tuesday, it said it nows sees global growth rising 3.5 per cent in 2017.
The body kept it projection for 2018 unchanged at 3.6 per cent.
However, while highlighting a number of positive developments the body warned that binding structural impediments continue to hold back a stronger recovery with “a balance of risks that remains tilted to the downside, especially over the medium term.”
“Structural problems- such as low productivity growth and high income inequality - are likely to persist. Inward-looking policies threaten global economic integration and the cooperative global economic order, which have served the world economy, especially emerging market and developing economies, well,” the IMF said in its latest World Economic Outlook.
The IMF revised Britain’s growth forecast to 2 per cent for 2017, up a half percentage point from January. It said negative effects from the UK’s vote to leave the European Union are taking longer to materialise.
The organisation held its 2017 US growth forecast steady at 2.3 per cent, which still represents a substantial jump from 1.6 per cent growth in 2016, partly due to expectations that president Donald Trump will cut taxes and increase government spending.
The IMF lifted Japan’s 2017 growth projection by 0.4 percentage point from January, to 1.2 per cent, while the euro zone and China both saw a 0.1 percentage point growth forecast increase to 1.7 per cent and 6.6 per cent, respectively.
Additional reporting: Reuters

Its forecast for 2018 remains steady at 3.6 percent.

Despite noting several favorable trends, the IMF cautioned that deep-seated structural obstacles are still preventing a more robust rebound. It stated that the overall risks remain skewed negatively, particularly over the next several years.

Persistent issues like sluggish gains in productivity and significant disparity in earnings are expected to continue. Policies that turn inward endanger worldwide economic unity and the collaborative international framework, which have greatly benefited the global economy, particularly emerging and developing nations.

For the United Kingdom, the IMF raised its 2017 growth outlook to 2 percent, a half-point rise from its January figure. It noted that adverse consequences from the Brexit referendum have been slower to appear than initially anticipated.

The fund maintained its projection for United States growth this year at 2.3 percent, a notable acceleration from the 1.6 percent recorded in 2016. This revision partly reflects anticipated fiscal stimulus under the Trump administration.

Japan’s growth forecast for 2017 was raised by 0.4 percentage point to 1.2 percent. Meanwhile, projections for both the euro area and China were edged up by 0.1 percentage point, to 1.7 percent and 6.6 percent, respectively.

DETROIT (AP) - Detroit Tigers pitching prospect Franklin Perez is expected to miss at least three months with a right lat strain.
The Tigers say Perez was injured in a minor league game Sunday. There is no surgery recommended at this point, but the recovery is expected to take a minimum of 12 weeks.
Perez, a 20-year-old right-hander, was acquired by Detroit in the trade that sent Justin Verlander to Houston last season. Perez went 6-3 with a 3.02 ERA across two levels of the minors last year. He made 10 starts at Class A and six at Double-A. Baseball America tabbed Perez as Detroit's top prospect this offseason.
The rebuilding Tigers aren't expected to contend this year, but Perez figured to be a prospect to watch, no matter where in Detroit's system he ended up pitching.

The 20-year-old right-handed player joined the Tigers in the deal that moved Justin Verlander to the Houston Astros prior to this season. Last year, Perez compiled a 6-3 record and a 3.02 earned run average, pitching at both Class A and Double-A levels. He was recently named the team's premier minor league talent by Baseball America.

Although the Tigers are in a rebuilding phase and not anticipated to be competitive this season, Perez was considered a significant player to monitor within their farm system.

Sending children off to college or into the real world is usually a proud time for parents. But there also can be sadness, especially when it's the last child to leave home. Empty nest syndrome isn't a clinical diagnosis. Instead, it's a phenomenon in which parents experience feelings of sadness and loss when the last child leaves home.
"It's common for parents to find letting go to be a painful experience — even though they actively encourage their children to be independent," says Dr. Jessica Sosso, Family Medicine, Mayo Clinic Health System. "Parents might find it difficult to suddenly have no children at home who need their care. They might miss being a part of their children's daily lives and their constant companionship. Parents with only one child or those who strongly identify with their role as a parent might have a particularly difficult time adjusting."
Sosso explains that as hard as the change may be, having an empty nest can bring benefits to parents. Recent studies suggest that an empty nest might reduce work and family conflicts. Having an empty nest also gives parents a new opportunity to reconnect with each other, improve the quality of their marriage and rekindle interests for which they previously might not have had time.

Known as empty nest syndrome, this is not a formal medical condition but a situation where caregivers encounter grief and a sense of void after their last child moves out.

Dr. Jessica Sosso of the Mayo Clinic Health System’s Family Medicine department notes that while parents support their children’s independence, the separation can still be distressing. She points out that adjusting to a home without children needing daily care is challenging. Parents may long for the regular involvement in their children’s activities and the closeness they shared. Those with a single child or who deeply value their parenting role might struggle even more with this adjustment.

Dr. Sosso adds that despite the difficulty, an empty nest can offer advantages. Research indicates it may lessen tensions between job and family responsibilities. It also provides a chance for partners to strengthen their relationship, enhance their marital bond, and pursue personal interests that were previously set aside.

Keith Chegwin had a varied career, from presenting Swap Shop to appearing on Celebrity Big Brother.
The star, also known for hosting children’s game show Cheggers Play Pop, died aged 60 after battling a progressive lung condition.
Here are some of his key moments.
1. On a TV show Chegwin looked on in horror as comedian Bobby Davro faceplanted the floor.
I have known Keith Chegwin for many years He was one of the nicest guys I've ever met in this biz I had been told he was very poorly but unable to contact him for a while What a dreadful shame to lose such a lovely friend Love to his family RIP Cheggers! I'll miss that smile 💔 — Bobby Davro (@BobbyDavro1) December 11, 2017
Screams erupted from the audience as Davro, who could not break the fall as a result of being in the stocks, fell face first.
Davro ended up pulling all the ligaments in his back and needing stitches in his chin.
2. In 1992 Chegwin revealed his fight with alcoholism on This Morning.
He openly told presenters Richard Madeley and Judy Finnigan: “I am an alcoholic. It’s a disease.”
3. Chegwin said in 2011 that film director Roman Polanski once told him to take his underwear off.
Chegwin accused Roman Polanski of asking him to remove his underwear (Joel Ryan/PA)
The teenager was working on the 1971 film Macbeth when the incident happened. Chegwin told the Telegraph: “With Polanski, you just did what he told you to do.
“There was one scene where we all run into a banqueting hall and go to sleep for the night, and he just looked at Martin Shaw and me and said: ‘Take your underpants off.’
“And he was the boss so you go: ‘Fine, OK.’ We just did it. Couldn’t work out why; still don’t know why.”
4. The morning after a BAFTA ceremony, Chegwin doorstepped Steve Coogan in a hotel for Channel 4’s The Big Breakfast.
A friendly Coogan invited Chegwin into his hotel room, where a camera crew followed, catching sight of his girlfriend in bed.

Police investigate armed robbery on Lionel Street
By News-Argus Staff
Published in News on October 6, 2017 10:19 AM
Goldsboro police are investigating after a man was robbed at gunpoint on Lionel Street Thursday afternoon, according to a police incident report.
According to the report, a man was walking on the 100 block of Lionel Street just after noon Thursday, when he heard a vehicle approach him from behind. When the vehicle drove up next to him, the driver rolled the window down, pointed a handgun at him and yelled "Give it up, man."
The victim responded "I don't have anything to give you," prompting the suspect to exit the vehicle and walk toward the victim. The suspect then took the victim's smartphone, valued at $100, and left moving north on Lionel Street, according to the report.
Police Major Anthony Carmon said that the police department has a suspect in the case, but that suspect has not been charged with anything yet.

As stated in the incident documentation, a man was walking along the 100 block just after midday when a car pulled up beside him. The driver lowered the window, brandished a firearm, and demanded that the man hand over his possessions.

The individual told the assailant he had nothing to surrender. In response, the armed person got out of the car, approached the pedestrian, and seized his mobile phone, which is worth approximately one hundred dollars. The perpetrator then fled, heading north on the same street.

Police Major Anthony Carmon confirmed that investigators have identified a person of interest in the robbery. However, no formal charges have been filed against this individual at this time. This account was published in the News-Argus on October 6, 2017.

England may have qualified for the World Cup following Thursday's scruffy 1-0 win over Slovenia but manager Gareth Southgate admits they have a "hell of a lot of work to do" if they are to be contenders in Russia next year.
Captain Harry Kane grabbed an injury-time winner at Wembley to secure top spot in Group F but it was another unconvincing display from Southgate's players and the former Middlesbrough boss knows they must improve over the next eight months.
"I think this team has potential, but we've got a hell of a lot of work to do," he told ITV Sport.
"They've come here on the back of what happened in the last European Championships, they've had the change of coach, they've had a lot of difficulties to deal with through the campaign.
"But we're there [at the World Cup] and now we build and we look to where we can improve all the time.
"Joe Hart [made] big saves at important times and that's where his experience has come through.
"We know where we have to do better but that's for tomorrow. Tonight, we go to the World Cup and that's fantastic."
Late goals have underpinned England's successful qualifying campaign - Kane scored a late equaliser away to Scotland in June, while Adam Lallana struck deep in stoppage-time to earn a 1-0 win in Slovakia in September 2016, which turned out to be Sam Allardyce's sole game in charge.
And Southgate believes it is no coincidence it happened again on Thursday.
Job done! Qualified for the World Cup! A really great feeling. 👌 #ThreeLions 🦁🦁🦁 pic.twitter.com/ELzNGYoq5B — Harry Kane (@HKane) October 5, 2017
"We played a team who have only conceded four goals in the competition - and you saw why," Southgate added.
"They defended resolutely, they broke the game up when they had to, they took yellow cards when they had to.
"We weren't quite as sharp as we hoped to be with the ball. But we stuck at it and it's not a coincidence if you keep scoring late goals.
"Late goals have been key and we knew they had to win. We changed formation to go two up front at the end."
rewrite:
England secured their place in the World Cup with a narrow, untidy 1-0 victory against Slovenia on Thursday. However, manager Gareth Southgate conceded that the squad faces a tremendous amount of progress to become genuine challengers for the tournament in Russia next summer. A stoppage-time goal from skipper Harry Kane at Wembley ensured first place in Group F, yet the overall performance lacked conviction, leaving Southgate aware that significant enhancements are required in the coming months.

Southgate stated to ITV Sport that while the side possesses promise, considerable effort lies ahead. He noted the team has been operating under the shadow of their previous European Championship exit, alongside a shift in coaching leadership and various challenges encountered throughout the qualifying stages. Nevertheless, with qualification achieved, the focus now turns to continuous development and identifying areas for growth. He highlighted goalkeeper Joe Hart’s crucial interventions during the match as demonstrations of his valuable know-how. Southgate acknowledged that while improvements are necessary, those concerns can be addressed later; for the moment, celebrating World Cup qualification is the priority.

This qualifying cycle has repeatedly seen England find decisive goals in the closing moments. Beyond Kane’s late effort against Slovenia, he also netted a last-gasp equalizer versus Scotland in June, and Adam Lallana scored deep into added time to secure a 1-0 win in Slovakia in September 2016—a match that proved to be Sam Allardyce’s only game as manager. Southgate feels it is not mere chance that this pattern reoccurred in the latest fixture.

Reflecting on the match, Southgate pointed out that Slovenia had allowed only four goals throughout the entire qualifying competition, and their disciplined defensive approach was evident. He described how they defended stubbornly, disrupted play effectively, and accepted tactical yellow cards when needed. England, he admitted, lacked the desired sharpness in possession but persisted until the end. He emphasized that consistently scoring late goals is not accidental; such decisive moments have been fundamental to their campaign. Aware that Slovenia needed a win, England adapted their strategy late in the game, switching to a formation with two forwards to secure the vital result.

How long does it take to make a life-altering decision? Netflix’s new series Seven Seconds asks viewers just that as it takes the audience down a dark and all-too-real rabbit hole.
Seven Seconds, created by Veena Sud, follows the aftermath and investigation into a hit-and-run that killed Brenton Butler, a black teenager in Jersey City. Viewers watch as the cops who were involved in the accident try to cover their tracks and the Butler family reels from the crime. The show also allows the audience to look into the lives of the lawyer, KJ Harper, prosecuting the case and Fish, the detective who pushes Harper to look deeper into the case.
This drama is a must-see series, even though it can be hard to watch as the unfolding events feel as though they have been ripped directly from the headlines. What makes this story so compelling is how it portrays the aftermath of the accident.
The acting in this series is phenomenal. Regina King and Russell Hornsby’s heartwrenching performances as Brenton Butler’s parents make the drama all the more tragic. Yes, the couple loses their son, but as the investigation drags on and the hope of getting justice for their son drifts farther away, they find themselves pushing the other away in their grief. It is through their love of their son that the audience learns who Brenton Butler was.
Beau Knapp, as Peter Jablonski, the driver of this tragedy, portrays a man racked with guilt over his actions and fear of what will happen to him if he comes forward. Clare-Hope Ashitey performs beautifully as the self-pitying and disillusioned and often intoxicated KJ Harper.
Seven Seconds is available on Netflix and has 10 hour-long episodes. The series is rated TV-MA. Fans of Seven Seconds may also enjoy The Killing, another series by Veena Sud, which follows the lives of two detectives as they investigate murders. Those looking for lighter fare should give Netflix’s Nailed It a try. It’s an amusing baking competition where amatuer bakers try to recreate fancy cakes to win the prize.

What duration is needed to arrive at a choice that forever changes a life? This is the central question posed to its audience by the new Netflix program *Seven Seconds*, which guides viewers into a bleak and unsettlingly plausible descent.

Developed by Veena Sud, the series chronicles the consequences and inquiry surrounding a fatal hit-and-run involving Brenton Butler, an African American adolescent from Jersey City. The narrative unfolds as the officers connected to the incident attempt to conceal their involvement, while the Butler family struggles with profound shock and loss. Simultaneously, the show provides insight into prosecutor KJ Harper, who handles the case, and Detective Fish, who urges Harper to pursue the investigation more thoroughly.

Despite being challenging to view due to its stark realism—often feeling as if taken straight from current news—this drama is essential viewing. Its power lies in the detailed exploration of the accident's ripple effects.

The performances throughout are exceptional. Regina King and Russell Hornsby deliver deeply moving portrayals as the grieving parents, amplifying the story's tragedy. Their loss is compounded as the prolonged investigation diminishes hopes for justice, causing their shared sorrow to drive a wedge between them. Through their enduring love for their son, the audience gains a sense of who Brenton Butler was.

Beau Knapp, playing Peter Jablonski—the driver responsible—effectively captures a character consumed by remorse and terror over the potential consequences of confession. Clare-Hope Ashitey excels as the frequently inebriated and cynical KJ Harper, a figure mired in self-doubt and disillusionment.

*Seven Seconds* streams on Netflix, comprising ten episodes each roughly an hour long, and carries a TV-MA rating. Viewers who appreciate this series might also like *The Killing*, another of Veena Sud's projects, which shadows two homicide detectives. For those seeking less intense entertainment, *Nailed It* on Netflix offers a humorous alternative; it features novice bakers attempting to replicate elaborate confections in a comedic contest for a reward.

Batting first, India's innings faltered early and often, ultimately being dismissed for a total of 112 runs within 38.2 overs. The top scorer for the side was M.S. Dhoni, who managed 65 runs before being caught. Other notable contributions were minimal, with only S. Iyer (9), H. Pandya (10), and K. Yadav (19) reaching double figures. The Sri Lankan bowling attack was dominant, led by Suranga Lakmal who took four wickets for only 13 runs in his ten overs. Nuwan Pradeep and Angelo Mathews provided strong support, claiming two and one wicket respectively.

In response, Sri Lanka comfortably chased down the target, finishing at 114 for the loss of three wickets in just 20.4 overs. Their innings was anchored by Upul Tharanga, who scored 49 runs, and supported by Angelo Mathews (25 not out) and Niroshan Dickwella (26 not out). The Indian bowlers, including B. Kumar, J. Bumrah, and H. Pandya, each took a single wicket but were unable to contain the scoring rate or build sufficient pressure to defend the low total.

The match officials were umpires Anil Chaudhary and Simon Fry, with Paul Reiffel serving as the television umpire and Jeff Crowe as the match referee. The final result was a convincing seven-wicket win for Sri Lanka.
