Negão the dog was abandoned at a gas station in Mogi das Cruzes, Brazil. He was left with nothing. But thanks to the kindness of the station’s owners, he would soon have a new family and a job to boot.
It was two years ago when Negão was left at the Shell gas station. Luckily, co-owner Sabrina Plannerer and her partner wasted no time taking in the abandoned dog and giving him a loving home.
“We adopted him immediately and got him all the care animals need,” Plannerer told The Dodo. “We took him to the vet to get vaccinated and de-wormed. We bought him food, a dog house and a leash to take him on walks.”
They also gave him a job as a greeter at the gas station. He even has his own employee ID badge.
“Negão waits for people to arrive, and then goes up to say hello, winning them over with his charms,” Plannerer told The Dodo. “Customers love him. Some people even bring him toys.”
He’s definitely the cutest gas station employee we’ve ever seen!
rewrite:
In Mogi das Cruzes, Brazil, a dog named Negão was deserted at a fuel station with no belongings. However, the compassion of the station’s proprietors quickly turned his fate around, providing him with both a home and a purpose.

Two years prior, Negão had been left behind at a Shell station. Fortunately, co-owner Sabrina Plannerer and her companion promptly welcomed the stray into their lives, ensuring he received a secure and affectionate environment. Plannerer explained to The Dodo that they took swift action to adopt him, arranging essential veterinary treatments like vaccinations and parasite control, along with supplying food, shelter, and walking gear.

Beyond a home, they offered him a role as the station’s official welcome host, complete with a personalized identification badge. Negão now eagerly greets arriving customers, endearing himself with his friendly nature. According to Plannerer, patrons are delighted by him, with some even bringing gifts like toys. Undoubtedly, he stands out as the most adorable employee ever seen at a gas station.

LAS VEGAS (AP) — The Latest on civil trial involving Las Vegas Strip headliner David Copperfield and a British tourist who claims he was seriously hurt in a fall while taking part in a signature Copperfield illusion in 2013 (all times local):
12:30 p.m.
A judge in Las Vegas has rejected a call by David Copperfield's attorney for a mistrial based on the amount of media coverage that a civil negligence lawsuit involving the world-famous illusionist is getting.
Attorney Elaine Fresch complained Tuesday about interviews involving plaintiff Gavin Cox's attorney, Benedict Morelli.
Fresch noted that one interview aired on CBS-TV just hours before proceedings resumed.
Under questioning by Nevada state court Judge Mark Denton, three jurors said they turned off broadcasts when they saw references to the case on the news during a five-day break in the civil trial.
The judge allowed the trial to resume.
Copperfield is on the stand answering questions from Morelli about whether Copperfield knew of anyone besides Cox who was injured taking part in the magician's audience-volunteer illusion over nearly 20 years he has performed it.
____
9 a.m.
Las Vegas Strip headliner David Copperfield is due to return to the witness stand in a lawsuit by a British tourist who claims he was seriously hurt in a fall while taking part in one of Copperfield's signature illusions in 2013.
The magician resumes testimony Tuesday after last week revealing secrets behind a trick that appears to make volunteer audience members vanish onstage and appear a few moments later in the back of the theater.
Plaintiff Gavin Cox of Kent, England, alleges he fell after being hurried by stagehands through an MGM Grand hotel alleyway coated with a powdery residue near a trailer-sized trash bin.
Copperfield's lawyers lost pretrial bids to close proceedings to the public to avoid revealing performance secrets

rewrite:
In Las Vegas, a civil trial continues involving magician David Copperfield and a British man, Gavin Cox, who alleges he sustained major injuries from a fall during a 2013 performance. The plaintiff claims the accident occurred while he was participating in a classic Copperfield illusion.

Earlier today, the judge overseeing the case denied a motion from Copperfield’s legal team to declare a mistrial. The defense attorney, Elaine Fresch, argued that extensive media attention, including a recent television interview with the plaintiff’s lawyer, Benedict Morelli, could prejudice the jury. Judge Mark Denton questioned jurors about their exposure to this coverage during a break in proceedings; three indicated they had switched off news reports upon recognizing the case. The judge permitted the trial to move forward.

Copperfield returned to the witness stand for further questioning by Morelli. The line of inquiry focuses on whether the magician was aware of any other participants being injured over the two decades he has performed the audience-involvement illusion in question.

In prior testimony, Copperfield disclosed details of the trick, which seemingly makes volunteers disappear from the stage and reappear elsewhere in the venue. Cox’s lawsuit states that after the illusion, stagehands rushed him through a service corridor at the MGM Grand hotel, where he slipped on a dusty substance near a large dumpster.

Before the trial, Copperfield’s attorneys unsuccessfully sought to close the courtroom to the public, aiming to protect proprietary secrets of his act. Cox and his spouse are requesting monetary compensation, though the exact amount has not been specified.

MILAN, April 28 Saipem has teamed up with Italy's state railways to bid for work on a Russian high-speed train project as the Italian oil engineering and contracting firm seeks new business to offset an ongoing slump in the energy industry.
Oil service groups like Saipem have been hit by a sharp fall in oil prices since mid-2014 that has led energy majors to cut billions of dollars in costs and delay investments.
Oil and gas exploration and development firms spent just 400 billion euros ($436 billion) on projects last year compared to 700 billion euros in 2014, according to Saipem CEO Stefano Cao.
"We've signed a memo of understanding with Ferrovie dello Stato (Italy railways) to make a joint bid for a part of the Moscow-Kazan project," Cao told shareholders at a meeting on Friday.
The Moscow–Kazan project, first proposed in 2009, is a 770-km (480-mile) high-speed rail link between the two Russian cities.
If the bid with Ferrovie was successful, the work could be worth a total of about $3 billion, Cao said.
To offset the slump in the oil and gas sector, Saipem has said it plans to grow business lines in areas like engineering, renewable energy and energy platform dismantling.
But Cao said no talks with the Russians were underway yet about the rail project and he did not expect the work to be booked in the company's backlog in the short term.
Italy's state railways, which has plans to list on the Milan market, is looking to expand its business abroad.
It has operations in Germany and Greece and is looking to bid in tenders in the Britain.
($1 = 0.9177 euros) (Reporting by Stephen Jewkes; Editing by Edmund Blair)
rewrite:
In a strategic move to counterbalance the downturn affecting the energy sector, the Italian engineering firm Saipem has formed a partnership with the national railway operator, Ferrovie dello Stato. Together, they intend to submit a proposal for a segment of a high-speed rail initiative in Russia. This collaboration emerges as companies such as Saipem face significant challenges due to the prolonged decline in oil prices, which began in 2014. This downturn has compelled major energy players to substantially reduce expenditures and postpone new ventures.

Stefano Cao, Saipem's Chief Executive, provided context by noting a dramatic decrease in global spending. Investment in oil and gas exploration and development plummeted to approximately 400 billion euros last year, a sharp drop from the 700 billion euros allocated in 2014. During a recent shareholder assembly, Cao confirmed the memorandum of understanding with the state railways for a joint bid on the Moscow-Kazan high-speed rail line. This long-planned project, covering 770 kilometers between the two Russian cities, represents a major infrastructure endeavor.

Cao indicated the potential value of the contract could reach around three billion dollars should their bid prove successful. However, he clarified that discussions with Russian authorities have not yet commenced, and the project is unlikely to be added to the company's order portfolio in the immediate future. In pursuit of growth beyond its traditional oil and gas services, Saipem aims to develop its operations in engineering, renewable energy, and decommissioning. Concurrently, Ferrovie dello Stato is seeking international expansion opportunities, with existing activities in Germany and Greece, and plans to participate in upcoming tenders in the United Kingdom, as it prepares for a potential listing on the Milan stock exchange.

Lawyer Lorenzo Gadon on Tuesday claimed that Chief Justice Maria Lourdes Sereno gave cash to officials of the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP), sourcing the money from the judiciary’s funds.
Gadon, who filed the impeachment complaint against Sereno who is on leave, said the chief justice gave allowances to the IBP officers, which is why they supported her in connection with the impeachment complaint and the quo warranto petition filed against her by Solicitor General Jose Calida.
“The reason why I filed an impeachment case against Chief Justice Sereno was because of her own fault and it is obvious from the results of the House committee on justice that she had committed so many corrupt acts,” Gadon said in a speech during the conference on empowering women law enforcers held in Camp Aguinaldo, the headquarters of the Philippine military.
Gadon has accused Sereno of not acting on petitions to provide survivors’ benefits to the families of judges who died.
“Majority of those judges are female, 95 percent are female, and their age was at about 80 years old. They failed to receive benefits even if it was under the law,” he said.
Gadon claimed that the “Sereno Supreme Court” provided allowance to IBP officials. “You can see that the IBP officials have been siding with her,” he added.
Jojo Lacanilao, one of the lawyers of Sereno, disputed Gadon’s claims.
“He is again lying and perjuring himself,” Lacanilao told reporters in a text message.
“Attorney Gadon is full of lies just like the impeachment complaint he filed. He also has no evidence on the accusations he was hurling against CJ Sereno,” he added.
On Monday, Jover Laurio of Pinoy Ako Blog filed a disbarment case against Gadon for allegedly violating his oath as a lawyer and the Code of Professional Responsibility when he filed the “baseless unactionable criminal complaint” against Sereno.
rewrite:
During a Tuesday address, attorney Lorenzo Gadon alleged that Chief Justice Maria Lourdes Sereno utilized the judiciary's financial resources to provide monetary gifts to leaders of the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP). Gadon, the individual who initiated the impeachment proceedings against the currently on-leave chief justice, asserted that these payments explain the IBP leadership's backing of Sereno regarding both the impeachment case and the separate quo warranto challenge brought by Solicitor General Jose Calida.

Speaking at a women law enforcers' conference at Camp Aguinaldo, the Philippine military's main headquarters, Gadon stated his impeachment action was a direct consequence of Sereno's personal misconduct. He pointed to findings from the House justice committee as clear evidence of her numerous alleged corrupt activities.

Among his further accusations was that Sereno neglected legal petitions seeking death benefits for the families of deceased judges. Gadon emphasized that most of these judges were women, approximately 95 percent, often around 80 years old, who were unlawfully denied these entitlements. He connected this to his central allegation, contending that what he termed the "Sereno Supreme Court" funneled allowances to IBP officials, thereby securing their support. "You can observe the IBP officials consistently aligning with her," he remarked.

These claims were firmly rejected by Jojo Lacanilao, a member of Sereno's legal team. In a statement to the press, Lacanilao accused Gadon of repeated falsehoods and perjury. He characterized Gadon as fundamentally dishonest, drawing a parallel to the impeachment complaint itself, and stated that Gadon possesses no proof for his allegations against the Chief Justice.

This development follows a recent disbarment case lodged against Gadon by blogger Jover Laurio of Pinoy Ako Blog. Filed on Monday, the case charges Gadon with breaching his professional oath and ethical codes by submitting a criminal complaint against Sereno that is described as groundless and without legal merit.

Schaeffler is the main sponsor of the Audi Sport ABT Formula E team, so the company has access to the appropriate hardware. It took four electric motors from the FE01 race car and stuffed them into the RS3. The motors produce a combined 1,180 horsepower. That makes the 400 hp produced by the RS3’s stock 2.5-liter turbocharged inline-five seem positively timid.
Dubbed 4ePerformance, the electric RS3 can reach 124 mph from a standstill in 7 seconds, according to Schaeffler. The company didn’t mention a 0 to 60 mph time, but we reckon the 4ePerformance can do the job a bit quicker than Audi’s claim of 3.9 seconds for the stock RS3.
Besides the raw power, the electric RS3 should possess decent agility. Two motors power each axle, giving the car all-wheel drive (this is an Audi, after all) and gearboxes at both axles enable torque vectoring. This means power can be shifted side to side to help nudge the car around corners. Two battery packs with a total capacity of 64 kilowatt hours power the car, and Schaeffler appears to have used the bodywork from the Audi RS3 LMS race car as well.
Audi previously tried to build and market its own all-electric performance car, the R8 e-tron, but production ended after just a few examples were built. The German automaker is now focusing its attention on the more practical e-tron SUV, which is expected to launch later this year. Audi will likely introduce additional all-electric models after that as part of parent Volkswagen Group’s electrification push.
Formula E is attracting more manufacturers. The field already includes the likes of Audi, BMW, and Jaguar, with Mercedes-Benz and Porsche set to join the series as well. Nissan will also replace its alliance partner Renault in Formula E. As automakers also launch more electric road cars, Formula E will likely grow in importance as a marketing tool.
rewrite:
As the primary sponsor for the Audi Sport ABT Formula E racing team, Schaeffler was able to source key components directly from the race circuit. The engineering team installed four electric motors, taken directly from the FE01 Formula E vehicle, into an Audi RS3. Together, these motors generate a staggering 1,180 horsepower. This immense output renders the standard RS3's 400-horsepower, 2.5-liter turbocharged five-cylinder engine quite modest by comparison.

Named the 4ePerformance, this all-electric demonstrator can accelerate from a complete stop to 124 miles per hour in just seven seconds, as reported by Schaeffler. While the firm did not provide a zero-to-sixty mile per hour estimate, it is reasonable to assume this electric model would surpass the factory RS3's claimed 3.9-second time for that sprint.

Beyond sheer power, the vehicle is engineered for enhanced handling. With two motors driving each axle, it features all-wheel drive—a hallmark of Audi. Dedicated gearboxes on both axles also allow for torque vectoring, enabling precise distribution of power between the wheels to improve cornering agility. The system is energized by two battery packs combining for 64 kilowatt-hours of capacity. Schaeffler also seems to have incorporated body components from the track-focused Audi RS3 LMS.

Audi's prior venture into a dedicated electric performance model, the R8 e-tron, saw very limited production before being discontinued. The manufacturer is currently concentrating on more mainstream electric vehicles, such as the upcoming e-tron SUV. Following this launch, Audi is anticipated to expand its all-electric offerings, aligning with the broader electrification strategy of its parent company, the Volkswagen Group.

The Formula E championship continues to gain momentum among major carmakers. Current participants include Audi, BMW, and Jaguar, with Mercedes-Benz and Porsche poised to enter the competition. Nissan will also take over the entry from its alliance partner Renault. As the automotive industry shifts toward electric road cars, Formula E is increasingly viewed as a vital platform for showcasing technology and marketing these new vehicles.

Investigators determine the blaze to be accidental and related to a passing train
Firefighters responded Monday afternoon to a small vegetation fire near Gaviota, according to the Santa Barbara County Fire Department.
The blaze burned along the railroad tracks south of Highway 101, near Mariposa Reina, according to Fire Department spokesman Mike Eliason.
Capt. David Sadecki said Tuesday that the cause of the fire was most likely related to a passing train and was considered accidental.
Several engine crews and at least one water-dropping helicopter were dispatched to the fire, which broke out at about 3:45 p.m.
The fire, which charred about an acre, was burning in grass and light chaparral, Eliason said.
At the time of the blaze, there were sustained winds of 15 to 20 mph, with gusts to 25 mph, Eliason said.
“It was putting up some pretty good flames, but it just ran out of real estate,” Eliason said.

The incident occurred along the railway lines close to Mariposa Reina, just south of Highway 101, as detailed by spokesperson Mike Eliason.

Captain David Sadecki stated on Tuesday that the investigation points to the train as the probable cause, deeming the incident accidental. The fire ignited around 3:45 p.m., prompting the deployment of multiple engine companies and a helicopter equipped to drop water. It consumed approximately one acre of grassland and light brush.

Eliason noted that conditions at the time included steady winds of 15 to 20 miles per hour, with occasional gusts reaching 25 mph. He described visible flames but added that the fire's spread was limited by the available terrain.

A Church Warsop man who was stranded in Mansfield after losing his wallet on a drunken night out, borrowed a car to get home and argued with police when he was stopped, a court heard.
Samuel Billyeald was stopped in his pal’s BMW, on Albert Street, at 1.15am, on November 25, because he was driving without any lights.
“He was arrested because there was no attempt to provide a specimen,” said prosecutor Daniel Pietryka.
“One minute he was compliant and the next he refused to cooperate. He was being difficult and had to be restrained.”
Billyeald, 22, of Laurel Avenue, admitted driving without insurance, or a licence, and failing to cooperate with a preliminary test or to provide a specimen for analysis, when he appeared at Mansfield Magistrates Court, on Monday.
Abbie Edwards, mitigating, said: “This is totally out of character. He went out socialising in Mansfield town centre. He had consumed too much alcohol to drive.
“He lost his wallet and house keys and had no way to find his way home. Regretably, he decided to borrow a friend’s car. He did think about walking but it was very cold.
“He panicked when the police pulled him over and that’s why he refused to give a breath sample. He was clearly affected by the alcohol. He is very remorseful and ashamed.”
Ms Edwards said Billyeald has “quite severe mental health issues.”
He has one previous conviction for threatening behaviour, from April this year, which puts him in breach of a suspended sentence, the court heard.
Probation officer Sarah Alderton said: “He knew that the offence would put him in breach of a suspended sentence order. He chose to make a foolish mistake.”
She said he claimed to be a social drinker, but acknowledged that both offences were committed when he was drunk.
Billyeald was given a 12 month community order, with a two month curfew, from 7pm to 7am, and the operational period of his suspended sentence was extended by two months.
He was banned from driving for 12 months. He must pay £85 court costs and an £85 victim surcharge.
rewrite:
A Mansfield court was told that Samuel Billyeald, a resident of Church Warsop, found himself stuck in Mansfield following a night of heavy drinking during which he misplaced his wallet. In an attempt to return home, he took a friend's BMW without securing proper authorization. Police intercepted the vehicle on Albert Street in the early hours of November 25 after noticing its headlights were off.

According to prosecutor Daniel Pietryka, Billyeald was taken into custody for not agreeing to a breathalyzer test. His behavior during the stop was inconsistent, alternating between cooperation and refusal, ultimately requiring officers to physically subdue him.

The 22-year-old defendant, who lives on Laurel Avenue, pleaded guilty to multiple charges at Mansfield Magistrates' Court. These included operating a vehicle without insurance or a valid license, as well as declining both a roadside screening and a subsequent evidential test.

In his defense, Abbie Edwards explained that the incident was unusual for Billyeald. After an evening in Mansfield where he drank excessively, he realized he had lost his wallet and keys, leaving him stranded. Although he considered walking, the low temperatures led him to the unwise decision of borrowing a car. Edwards stated that her client reacted with panic when stopped by police, resulting in his refusal to provide a sample, and that he now feels profound regret and embarrassment. She also noted he struggles with significant mental health difficulties.

The court learned Billyeald had a prior conviction for threatening behavior from April, which violated the terms of a suspended sentence. Probation officer Sarah Alderton reported that he was aware his actions would breach that order, yet he proceeded with what she termed a "foolish mistake." While Billyeald describes himself as a casual drinker, Alderton observed that both offenses occurred while he was intoxicated.

Magistrates imposed a 12-month community order with a two-month nightly curfew from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m., and extended the probationary window of his suspended sentence by two months. He also received a 12-month driving prohibition and must cover £85 in court costs plus an £85 victim surcharge.

Property developer China Evergrande's 2018s were bid at a cash price of around 104, according to Tradeweb. The developer reported that its 2016 core profit jumped 89% year on year to Rmb20.81bn, thanks to strong increases in property prices and volumes.

BUSINESS NEWS
St. Rose Health Center provides cardiac rehabilitation for patients after a heart-related event but they also realize the importance of preventing problems from occurring in the first place.
Since February is American Heart Month, Shannon Deines, imaging supervisor, shared information on the three cardiovascular screenings available at St. Rose. She encourages the community to take advantage of these screenings to help prevent a variety of concerns.
“Each non-invasive test takes less than 30 minutes and the cost is very affordable,” Deines said. “Anyone concerned about cardiovascular disease is encouraged to call for an appointment.
“When screens detect a problem, we refer patients to their primary-care physicians,” she added. “When a problem is not detected, the patient can enjoy peace of mind.”
One screen checks for peripheral arterial disease (PAD) to help determine the risk of blockages in leg arteries.
“Those who are wondering about PAD might consider a few questions,” Deines suggested. “For example, do you have leg cramping, aching or fatigue when you walk? Do you have poorly healing ulcers on your feet or toes? Do you smoke, or have hypertension, diabetes or high cholesterol?”
A stroke scan also is available at St. Rose. This is an ultrasound test to see inside the carotid arteries in the neck. It can detect early signs of plaque build-up.
And the third screening involves a scan for an abdominal aortic aneurysm, which is a ballooning of the arterial wall that may cause the artery to burst.
A doctor’s referral is not necessary for any of these screenings, and the fee for each is $30. However, if someone chooses to have all three at the same time, the total cost is $75. Cash and checks are accepted.
“When screening results are available, we mail them to the patients,” Deines noted. “They can share results with their doctors.
“If any concerns are detected,” she elaborated, “we will recommend they follow up with their doctor for further testing. This type of preventive health care can go a long way to preventing or alleviating more serious conditions in the future.”
rewrite:
In recognition of American Heart Month, St. Rose Health Center is highlighting its commitment to heart health, extending beyond cardiac recovery to emphasize crucial preventive measures. Shannon Deines, the imaging supervisor, detailed three affordable cardiovascular assessments offered by the facility, urging community members to utilize these services for early detection.

Each screening is a non-invasive procedure requiring under half an hour. Deines stresses that individuals with any worries about heart disease should schedule an appointment. The process provides clarity: if results indicate an issue, patients are directed to their primary doctor, while normal findings offer significant reassurance.

The first assessment evaluates peripheral arterial disease (PAD), identifying risks for blockages in leg arteries. Deines recommends it for people experiencing symptoms like leg cramps, pain, or tiredness while walking, those with slow-healing foot sores, or individuals with risk factors including smoking, high blood pressure, diabetes, or elevated cholesterol.

A second option is a stroke scan, utilizing ultrasound to examine the carotid arteries in the neck for early plaque accumulation. The third screening checks for an abdominal aortic aneurysm, a dangerous swelling in a major artery that could rupture.

No physician referral is needed for these tests. Each scan costs $30, or all three can be completed together for a reduced total of $75, with payment accepted via cash or check. Once ready, results are mailed directly to patients for them to discuss with their physicians. Deines explains that if a screening reveals potential problems, they advise consulting a doctor for more comprehensive evaluation. Such proactive steps, she concludes, are vital for preventing or mitigating severe health complications later on.

GLENDALE, AZ - Arizona twins are going to have a unique story to tell for the rest of their lives after they were born in different years.
Holly and Brandon Shay weren’t expecting their boys to arrive for another few weeks, however, they were shocked when Banner Hospital in Glendale admitted them on New Year’s Eve.
After six exhausting hours of labor, their first son, Sawyer, was born at 11:51 p.m.
“I wanted to make sure he was OK, and they had to keep reminding me that I had to push," Holly said.
Just one minute after midnight on January 1, 2017, their second baby, Everett, was born.
The boys who previously shared nine months in the same space won’t be sharing a birthday -- or even their birth year.
“I think Sawyer might give his brother a hard time,” Brandon said. “I think it’s mostly going to be Sawyer teasing Everett over him being the eldest.”
rewrite: A set of twins in Arizona will have an extraordinary tale to recount, as they were born in separate calendar years. Holly and Brandon Shay anticipated the arrival of their sons several weeks later, but were surprised when admitted to Banner Hospital in Glendale on December 31st. Following six hours of strenuous labor, their first child, Sawyer, arrived at 11:51 p.m. Holly noted her concern for the baby required staff to remind her to continue pushing. Merely one minute into the new day of January 1, 2017, their second son, Everett, was delivered. The twins, who spent nine months together in the womb, will not share a common birthday or even the same year of birth. Brandon humorously speculated that Sawyer may later jest about being the older sibling.

DALLAS (AP) - Two Dallas police officers were critically wounded in a shooting Tuesday outside a home improvement store, authorities said.
Police Chief U. Renee Hall said a store loss-prevention officer also was shot in the incident about 4:15 p.m. outside a Home Depot in northern Dallas.
In a tweet about the shooting Tuesday evening, the Dallas Police Department said the officers were critically wounded. During a news conference Tuesday night at Texas Health Presbyterian Hospital Dallas, Hall declined to give an update on their conditions, citing consideration for the privacy of the officers' families.
"We're asking you to continue praying for our officers," Hall said.
The two police officers went to the store to assist an off-duty police officer with taking a man into custody and then the shooting happened.
A 29-year-old man is being sought as a person of interest. Hall said the man left the scene in a white pickup truck.
"I continue to be upset at the lack of respect of our police in this city and in our country," said Mayor Mike Rawlings, who also attended the hospital news conference.
In 2016, four Dallas police officers and a transit officer were shot dead by a sniper in an ambush that came toward the end of a peaceful protest over the police killings of black men that had occurred in other cities.

rewrite:
On April 24, 2018, a shooting occurred outside a Home Depot store in northern Dallas, leaving two police officers and a store security agent with critical injuries. The incident took place around 4:15 p.m. Authorities reported that the officers had arrived at the location to provide support to an off-duty colleague who was attempting to detain an individual. The situation escalated, resulting in gunfire.

Dallas Police Chief U. Renee Hall addressed the media during a press briefing held at Texas Health Presbyterian Hospital later that evening. She chose not to disclose specific details regarding the wounded officers' medical status, emphasizing the need to respect the privacy of their families. Instead, she requested the public to keep the officers in their thoughts and prayers. Mayor Mike Rawlings, who was also present, expressed his frustration over what he described as a widespread disrespect toward law enforcement personnel in Dallas and across the nation.

Law enforcement personnel initiated a search for a 29-year-old male considered a person of interest in the case. According to Chief Hall, the individual fled the scene in a white pickup truck. Police concentrated their efforts near an ExtraSpace Storage facility located just south of the Home Depot. Meanwhile, additional officers were stationed at the hospital's emergency entrance to provide security.

This violent event evoked memories of a prior tragedy in Dallas. In 2016, during a demonstration concerning police-related fatalities of black men in other parts of the country, a sniper ambush claimed the lives of five officers. The Associated Press issued a correction to an earlier version of this report, confirming the year of that earlier attack as 2016.

Photographs from the scene depicted police actively searching the area and maintaining a presence at the hospital. All rights to this reporting are reserved by The Associated Press.

RUSSIAN TIME heads into the 13th GP2 season with a new line-up comprising 22-year-old Russian Artem Markelov and Italian 21-year-old Luca Ghiotto.
Markelov and Ghiotto were both top 10 championship finishers in the 2016 series, with Artem winning the Monaco feature race and finishing on the podium in the season finale at Yas Marina. Luca, meanwhile, finished runner-up in the Hockenheim feature event and claimed four podiums in all, including a win at Sepang en route to his 111 points.
Both men have impressive records in the junior racing categories, with Markelov a former runner-up in the German F3 championship and Ghiotto vice-champion in both Formula Abarth and Formula Renault 2.0 before taking pole position at Spa on his GP3 debut. His 2015 GP3 campaign saw him finish runner-up to current Force India F1 driver Esteban Ocon, beaten by eight points despite five victories and eight podiums.
"We made an important step last year," Markelov said, "with a win and a top 10 finish in the championship. The GP2 series is highly competitive and I’m looking forward to doing even better in 2017 and challenging for more wins and hopefully becoming a consistent front-runner."
Speaking about the season ahead, Ghiotto said: "Let me firstly thank all at RUSSIAN TIME for the great opportunity they have offered me. Having crossed their cars a few times in 2016, I know how good they are! I think we have great potential to develop together. I’m looking forward to working with my new team mate Artem, and can’t wait to hit the track in March to start work."
Team principal Svetlana Strelnikova added: "I’m delighted to be able to announce such a promising line-up that will hopefully allow us to challenge for the teams’ championship that we won in 2013. The fact that four different teams have claimed the title in the past four seasons is a good illustration of just how competitive the series is. We are all hugely looking forward to it."

Ghiotto achieved second place in the Hockenheim feature race and collected a total of four podium finishes. This included a win in Sepang, contributing to his season tally of 111 points.

Their prior careers in junior formulae are equally notable. Markelov previously placed second in the German F3 championship. Before his GP3 debut, where he took pole at Spa, Ghiotto was the vice-champion in both Formula Abarth and Formula Renault 2.0. He then finished as runner-up in the 2015 GP3 championship, narrowly losing to Esteban Ocon—now a Force India F1 driver—by just eight points, despite securing five wins and eight podiums.

Reflecting on progress, Markelov stated the previous year represented significant advancement, highlighted by a race win and a championship top-ten result. He emphasized the intense competition within GP2 and expressed his eagerness to improve further in 2017, aiming for more victories and consistent performance at the front.

Ghiotto conveyed his gratitude to RUSSIAN TIME for the opportunity, noting his encounters with their cars in 2016 had shown him their capability. He believes the partnership holds substantial potential and is excited to collaborate with his new teammate, Markelov, anticipating the start of track action in March.

Team Principal Svetlana Strelnikova shared her enthusiasm for announcing a lineup with such strong prospects. Senator Cynthia Villar quashed fears on Thursday that she would be proposing a ban on the serving of unlimited rice or unli-rice in restaurants and food outlets.
“I am not planning to make a law banning ‘unli-rice.’ Not at all,” Senator Cynthia Villar said in a statement.
Villar issued the statement amid reports that she wanted to ban unli rice.
ADVERTISEMENT
“I just voiced out my concern that eating too much rice is one of the main causes of high blood sugar that leads to diabetes,” the senator said.
“I cannot prevent people from eating unlimited amount of rice. It is their choice. It was just a genuine expression of concern on my part,” she added.
The unli-rice issue came up during Wednesday’s hearing of the Senate committee on agriculture and food, which Villar chairs.
“Unlimited rice is bad for the health. We should learn how to eat more vegetables,” the senator said during the hearing.
READ: Unli-rice is unhealthy, says Villar
In Thursday’s statement, Villar recognized that it would be difficult to stop Filipinos from eating rice “as the Philippines is a nation or rice eaters.”
“But to decrease health risks, cutting down on rice is still a good idea,” she said.
The senator cited a study, which showed that eating one plate of white rice everyday increases the risk of developing diabetes by 11 percent. Health experts, she said, also recommend adding 20% of brown rice to the daily white rice consumption as it can reduce the risk of diabetes by around 16%.
ADVERTISEMENT
“Rice causes an increase in the level of sugar in the blood, which makes pancreas produce more insulin and cause frequent spikes in blood sugar level leading to diabetes. When not managed, diabetes may cause organ malfunction leading to death,” Villar said.
The senator earlier urged concerned government agencies such as the Department of Agriculture, Department of Social Welfare and Development, and the Department of Health (DoH) to align their programs in order to promote better nutrition and health among the young Filipinos.
“I have recommended to the government departments and they are doing it in some areas already to incorporate vegetable gardening in schools in the feeding program, for instance. They can also source the ingredients locally, particularly the perishable produce, to help the small farmers and cooperatives,” she said. CBB/rga

Senator Cynthia Villar moved to dispel concerns on Thursday, clarifying that she has no intention of seeking legislation to prohibit restaurants from offering unlimited rice, often termed "unli-rice." She explicitly stated that a ban is not under consideration. Her remarks came in response to circulating reports suggesting she supported such a restriction.

Villar explained that her earlier comments were rooted in health considerations. She expressed worry that excessive rice consumption is a significant factor in elevating blood sugar, which can lead to diabetes. The senator emphasized that she cannot and does not wish to control individual dietary choices, framing her input as a sincere expression of concern for public well-being.

This topic emerged during a Wednesday session of the Senate committee on agriculture and food, which Villar leads. In that forum, she noted the health drawbacks of unlimited rice and advocated for a greater emphasis on vegetable consumption.

In her subsequent statement, Villar acknowledged the cultural importance of rice in the Philippines, describing it as a nation of rice consumers. She conceded that completely discouraging its intake would be challenging. However, she maintained that reducing rice portions is a beneficial practice for mitigating health risks.

Citing research, Villar indicated that daily consumption of a plate of white rice may raise diabetes risk by approximately 11 percent. She also referenced health advice suggesting that substituting 20 percent of white rice with brown rice could lower diabetes risk by about 16 percent. She elaborated on the physiological impact, explaining that rice elevates blood sugar, prompting increased insulin production from the pancreas. Frequent spikes in blood sugar can lead to diabetes, which, if unmanaged, may result in organ failure and mortality.

Previously, Villar has encouraged relevant government bodies—including the Departments of Agriculture, Social Welfare and Development, and Health—to synchronize their initiatives to improve nutrition and health outcomes for Filipino youth. She has proposed integrating vegetable gardening into school feeding programs, noting that some areas have already begun this practice. Additionally, she advocates for locally sourcing perishable ingredients in these programs, which would simultaneously support small-scale farmers and cooperatives.

YOUNGSTOWN, Ohio (AP) -- Cole Gentry scored 21 points and Mark Hughes added 15 points on 5-of-10 shooting from 3-point range to power Wright State to an 83-57 romp over Youngstown State on Saturday.
Gentry connected on 8 of 13 shots from the floor to help the Raiders (18-7, 10-2 Horizon League) finish 29 of 51 (57 percent). Gentry hit 3 of 6 shots from distance as Wright State shot 41 percent (9 of 22) from beyond the arc. The Raiders held the Penguins (6-19, 4-8) to 31-percent shooting from the floor (20 of 65) and 18 percent (3 of 17) from long range.
Braun Hartfield was the lone Penguin in double figures with 20 points. He added six rebounds and three steals. Naz Bohannon had 13 rebounds to go along with nine points.
Hartfield scored seven as the Penguins jumped out to a 9-2 lead, but Hughes hit two 3s in a 14-0 run and Wright State, which led 40-25 by halftime, never trailed again.

As a team, Wright State shot 57 percent from the field and 41 percent from three-point territory. Defensively, they limited Youngstown State to just 31 percent shooting overall and 18 percent on three-point attempts. For the Penguins, Braun Hartfield scored 20 points and collected six rebounds, while Naz Bohannon grabbed 13 rebounds. Although Youngstown State began the game with a 9-2 advantage, Wright State responded with a 14-0 surge, took a 40-25 halftime lead, and maintained control for the remainder of the contest.

BANGKOK, March 30 Mudman Pcl, which runs cafes and restaurants such as Au Bon Pain and Dunkin' Donuts in Thailand, plans to raise 1.1 billion baht ($32 million) in an initial public offering (IPO) to help repay debt and fund expansion.
The company plans to sell about 211 million new shares at 5.25 baht each, parent firm Sub Sri Thai (SST) said in a statement to the stock exchange on Thursday.
Of the total, up to 41.44 million shares will be offered to SST's existing shareholders on March 29-31 and the rest will be sold to the public on April 3-5, it said.
Maybank Kim Eng Securities (Thailand) is the IPO lead underwriter and Siam Commercial Bank is the financial adviser.
Mudman also runs the Baskin Robbins franchise in Thailand as well as its own brand Greyhound Cafe.
Overall, it has 439 branches of Au Bon Pain, Dunkin Donuts, Baskin Robbins and Greyhound restaurants and cafes in Thailand and is planning to open its first Greyhound Cafe in London this year. ($1 = 34.4 baht) (Reporting by Wirat Buranakanokthanasan; writing by Orathai Sriring; editing by David Clarke)

WorkSafeBC wants you to keep safe while hanging those Christmas lights this year
On average more than 930 workers in British Columbia are seriously injured each year due to falls from ladders and many of those incidents were preventable.
With the holiday season in full swing, WorkSafe BC wants you to know that using a ladder around the house has risks too.
WorkSafeBC has released six new ladder-safety videos to remind workers, employers and homeowners to use ladders safely, both on the job and while decorating at home for the holidays.
“Last year, more than 1,000 workers were seriously injured in falls from height, including while using step ladders, extension ladders and scaffolding,” says Dan Strand, Director of Prevention Field Services for WorkSafeBC.
“The new videos and our ladder safety resources illustrate how the right ladder, the correct positioning and hazard assessments could prevent a life-changing serious injury or death.”
From 2012 to 2016, six workers died and there were 4,920 accepted time-loss claims — including 1,634 serious injuries — as a result of falls from ladders across all industries in B.C.
It’s time to use ladders safely:
Select the right ladder for the job and ensure the ladder is long enough to extend one metre above the upper landing
Place the ladder on a firm, level surface and inspect it before each use to ensure it’s in good working condition, looking for issues such as cracks or loose rungs
Always maintain three points of contact while climbing a ladder: two feet and one hand or two hands and one foot
Don’t carry heavy or bulky objects while climbing up or down a ladder
Don’t work from the top two rungs of the ladder or have more than one worker on a ladder at once
Wind, rain, and snow may pose additional hazards that need to be mitigated
Check for power lines and ensure a minimum distance of three metres can be maintained at all times before starting work

WorkSafeBC encourages everyone to prioritize safety when installing holiday lights this season. Each year in British Columbia, falls from ladders result in serious injuries for over 930 workers on average, with most of these accidents being avoidable. As festive activities increase, WorkSafeBC highlights that domestic ladder use also carries significant risks.

To promote safe practices, WorkSafeBC has introduced six instructional videos aimed at employees, businesses, and residents. These resources stress the importance of ladder safety in both workplace and home settings, especially during holiday decorating. Dan Strand, Director of Prevention Field Services at WorkSafeBC, notes that in the past year, more than 1,000 workers suffered severe injuries from falls involving various types of ladders and scaffolding. He emphasizes that these new materials demonstrate how proper equipment selection, correct setup, and risk evaluation can avert catastrophic injuries or fatalities.

Between 2012 and 2016, ladder-related falls in B.C. led to six fatalities and 4,920 time-loss claims, which included 1,634 major injuries across all sectors. To prevent such incidents, follow these guidelines: Choose an appropriate ladder that reaches at least one metre above the landing point. Position it on stable, even ground and examine it for defects like cracks or unstable steps before every use. When ascending or descending, keep three limbs in contact with the ladder—either both hands and one foot or both feet and one hand. Avoid lifting large or heavy items while on the ladder. Never stand on the top two steps or allow more than one person on a ladder simultaneously. Account for weather conditions such as wind, precipitation, or snow, which can increase danger. Also, survey the area for overhead power lines and maintain a clearance of at least three metres at all times during the task.

For further reference, a ladder safety document is available online. To notify us of any errors, please contact newstips@kelownacapnews.com. You can also reach Carmen Weld at carmen.weld@bpdigital.ca. Stay connected by liking our Facebook page and following us on Twitter.

Gunning for a return ticket to the zonal playoffs, Ceres Negros FC takes on Home United FC in the final match day of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Cup 2018 Asean zone group stage today at the Panaad Park and Stadium in Bacolod City.
The defending champion Yellow Busmen square off with the Protectors at 6 p.m.
Ceres Negros leads Group F with 13 points on an unbeaten record of four wins and a draw.
The Philippine titlist only needs a stalemate to enter the knockout phase for the second consecutive year.
Last season, Ceres beat Home United to emerge as the first Filipino club to rule the Asean zone. Head coach Risto Vidakovic wants to make history anew.
“We are not playing against Home United. We’re playing because we want to make history. We have the opportunity to make an excellent finish on the group stage and be on top of the group,” said Vidakovic.
Home, on the other hand, stands at No. 2 with 10 points on a 3-3-1 win-draw-loss record.
The Singaporean booters need to win by five goals or more to edge out the Filipino squad in the race to the playoffs.
Mentor Aidil Sharin, who is eager to steer his Protectors to an upset victory, reminds his wards to keep their transition defense sturdy.
“Our mind is to win and get three points. That’s the main objective to come here. But we have to be smart in how we’re going play and of course be very tight during the counter-attack,” said Sharin.
The first meeting between the two regional powerhouse teams ended in a 1-1 draw at the Jala Besar Stadium last February 27.
Shahril Ishak scored the opening goal via a penalty kick for Home but Super Herrera hit an equalizer for Ceres late in the game.
Meanwhile, Global Cebu FC looks to close its campaign on a bright note against Bali United FC in a non-bearing match at the Kapten I Wayan Dipta Stadium in Indonesia.
The People’s Club and the Tridatu Warriors battle for pride at 7 p.m.
rewrite:

The defending Asean champions, Ceres Negros, currently top Group F undefeated, having earned thirteen points. A single point from this match would guarantee their progression to the knockout stage for another year. Last season, the team made history as the first from the Philippines to win the zone, a feat coach Risto Vidakovic is determined to repeat. He emphasized that the focus is on creating another historic achievement by finishing the group stage strongly and maintaining their leading position.

Home United, in second place with ten points, faces a steeper challenge. To overtake Ceres and claim the group’s top spot, the Singaporean side must win by a margin of at least five goals. Their coach, Aidil Sharin, has stressed the importance of a victory while cautioning his team to remain disciplined, particularly in defensive transitions, to handle counter-attacks effectively.

The previous clash between these sides ended in a 1-1 draw. Home United took an early lead from a penalty by Shahril Ishak, but Ceres equalized later through Super Herrera.

In a simultaneous but inconsequential match in Indonesia, Global Cebu FC will play Bali United FC. Both teams, out of contention, will compete for pride as they conclude their tournament participation.

The PFL finalizes the venue of the Global Cebu vs Ceres-Negros finals match
Published 8:28 PM, December 11, 2017
MANILA, Philippines – The Philippines Football League (PFL) announced on Monday, December 11, that the finals knockout match between Global Cebu FC and Ceres-Negros FC will be held at the Pana-ad Stadium in Bacolod on Saturday, December 16.
Prior to the announcement, Global Cebu FC sent an appeal to the PFL that stated they were "exercising their right to host the PFL final" based on the argument that they were included in the fixture whose winner had the right to host the final.
(READ: Global Cebu FC wants to host PFL finals in Cebu City Sports Complex)
According to the statement released by the PFL, the league arrived at a decision after the second finals series meeting with the clubs. In their first meeting held on Wednesday, November 29, 2017, the top 4 clubs were "invited to signify their intention to host the Finals," but are still subjected to the PFL "making the final decision in accordance with Article 2.11 of the PFL Tournament Regulations."
Only FC Meralco Manila and Ceres signified their intent to host the final match, where the Manila team would have hosted it in Rizal Memorial Stadium. Cebu City Sports Complex was not available due to the "pitch and lighting" conditions, while University of the Makati "would not be able to host back-to-back matches."
The PFL also cited that they arrived at the decision to host it at Pana-ad due to "a variety of factors including, but not limited to, venue availability, commercial, marketing, and financial considerations."
The finals match will kick off at 6 pm on Saturday, while the 3rd and 4th place match between Meralco and Kaya FC will take place on Friday, December 15 at the Rizal Memorial Stadium but the time is yet to be finalized. – Rappler.com
rewrite:
The Philippines Football League has confirmed the location for its championship game between Global Cebu and Ceres-Negros. The announcement was made on Monday, December 11, 2017, specifying that the decisive match will be played at Pana-ad Stadium in Bacolod on Saturday, December 16.

This decision followed a formal request from Global Cebu, which asserted its entitlement to stage the final. The club based its claim on its participation in a prior fixture where the victorious team earned hosting rights. The league's statement explained that the verdict was reached during a second meeting with the involved clubs concerning the finals series. In an initial gathering on November 29, the top four teams were asked to indicate their interest in hosting the event, though the PFL retained the ultimate authority to choose the venue under its official regulations.

Only two clubs, FC Meralco Manila and Ceres-Negros, expressed a desire to host. Meralco proposed using Rizal Memorial Stadium in Manila. The preferred stadium in Cebu City was ruled out because of inadequate field and lighting conditions, and another potential venue in Makati could not accommodate consecutive games.

The league selected Pana-ad after evaluating several criteria, such as stadium access and various commercial and financial aspects. The championship is scheduled for a 6 p.m. start. Meanwhile, the match for third place between Meralco and Kaya FC is set for Friday, December 15, at Rizal Memorial Stadium, with the exact time still to be determined.

With the Dunlop MSA British Touring Car Championship returning for rounds four, five and six this weekend at Donington Park. Team Shredded Wheat Racing with Gallagher hope that this is the circuit to kick off their 2018 silverware collection following a topsy-turvy meeting at Brands Hatch earlier this month.
The damp conditions played havoc with the assured competitive nature of the Motorbase prepared Ford Focus RS, therefore Brands Hatch was seen as a bit of a disappointment for the team during both qualifying and the races. The highest placed finish over the weekend went the way of Tom Chilton who finished fifth at the first race of the day.
Considering the success that Motorbase have had previously at Donington where they have scored victories in 2011, 2012 and 2016, the team is confident that the trend for good results at the circuit will continue.
Oly Collins Team Manager commented on why he believed the team should have a better weekend than they did at Brands, “On paper, Donington should suit the RS better than the Brands Indy circuit.
“It’s a little faster and the aero and chassis improvements that we’ve made to the Focus should make a big difference there.
“We went well at the media day test last month and it’s been a happy hunting ground for us in the past, so we’re aiming to continue that trend this weekend and hopefully bag ourselves some new silverware to take home on Sunday night!”
Chilton also echoed these sentiments, “I was second fastest there on media day and we showed at Brands Hatch that we have the pace to be challenging for wins.
“I can’t wait to shake off the run of bad luck we had at Brands Hatch and get our championship challenge off the ground this weekend.”
Whilst James Cole, driver of the #20 Focus RS is assured by the speed shown by the car during the early stages of this year, “I think the pace we’ve shown so far during pre-season and also at Brands demonstrates the potential of where we should be.
“We’ve reset after the bad luck we had during the opening rounds and it’s time to show what were capable of this weekend.”
rewrite:
The Dunlop MSA British Touring Car Championship resumes this weekend at Donington Park for its fourth, fifth, and sixth rounds. Team Shredded Wheat Racing with Gallagher is optimistic that this venue will mark the beginning of their 2018 podium successes, after an inconsistent and challenging event at Brands Hatch earlier this month.

At Brands Hatch, wet weather disrupted the normally reliable performance of the Motorbase-prepared Ford Focus RS, making the entire weekend somewhat unsatisfactory for the squad in both qualifying and the races. Tom Chilton secured the team's best result by taking fifth place in the weekend's opening contest.

Given Motorbase Performance's prior achievements at Donington Park, which include race wins in 2011, 2012, and 2016, the team is positive that its history of strong showings at this track will persist.

Team Manager Oly Collins explained his reasons for expecting a more successful weekend than the last. "Theoretically, Donington is a better match for the RS than the Brands Hatch Indy circuit," he said. "It's a somewhat quicker track, and the aerodynamic and chassis upgrades we've implemented on the Focus ought to be particularly beneficial there. Our performance was solid during the media day test last month, and this has traditionally been a successful venue for us. Our goal is to maintain that pattern this weekend and, with any luck, secure some fresh trophies by Sunday evening."

Chilton shared this outlook, stating, "I set the second-fastest time there on media day, and our pace at Brands Hatch proved we can fight for victories. I'm eager to move past the misfortune we encountered at Brands and properly launch our championship campaign this weekend."

James Cole, pilot of the #20 Focus RS, draws confidence from the car's demonstrated speed in the early part of the season. "The performance we've revealed in pre-season testing and even at Brands indicates our true potential," Cole remarked. "We've put the setbacks from the initial rounds behind us, and now it's time to demonstrate what we can achieve this weekend."

An award-winning board game café in Sharnbrook is inviting families to enjoy some quality time together next weekend (Saturday and Sunday, July 14/15) at a Teenage Appreciation event.
Ready Steady Roll, at Ivy Lodge Farm off the A6, says teenagers who visit with their parents will get a free slice of cake while they play any board games from their more than 300 game collection.
Ready Steady Roll
Darrell Cannon, owner of Ready Steady Roll, said: “It may be a hard sell to get a teenager to play board games if their memories of board games are marathon sessions of Monopoly ending with arguments
“But there is a whole world of games that are fun, interesting and much less rage inducing!
“We pride ourselves on finding a game for everyone, even people who think they don’t like board games - plus we have delicious homemade cake made by my wife Charlotte!
“Parents are always looking for ways to get their teenagers off the latest technological fad, from Snapchat to Fortnite, and board games are the perfect remedy.
“I love it when a family come in with a sceptical teenager and within minutes they are sat around a table, laughing and having a great time together.
“Teenagers have a lot of stress in their lives, from exams to social media pressures, so spending quality time together as a family, whether that’s by playing a board game or going on a walk in so important everyone’s wellbeing.”
Ready Steady Roll started life as a monthly Pop Up event in Sharnbrook Village Hall. It is based at Ivy Lodge, in Sharnbrook, 10 minutes down the A6 from Rushden.
Anyone can visit from Wednesday to Sunday during the day with booking recommended either on 07584 484101 or info@readysteadyroll.co.uk
Visit www.readysteadyroll.co.uk for more.
rewrite:

Ready Steady Roll, situated at Ivy Lodge Farm just off the A6, will offer a complimentary piece of cake to any teenager accompanied by a parent, all while they explore the café's vast library of over 300 games.

Darrell Cannon, the café's proprietor, remarked that convincing adolescents to play board games can be challenging if they recall only tedious, quarrelsome matches like Monopoly. He emphasized that a broad spectrum of entertaining and engaging games exists which are far less likely to cause frustration.

The café takes pride in matching every visitor with a suitable game, even those convinced they dislike the pastime. Cannon also highlighted the appeal of freshly baked cakes made by his wife, Charlotte.

He noted that parents often seek activities to divert their teens from current digital trends, such as social media apps or popular video games, and suggested board games serve as an ideal alternative. Cannon described the rewarding sight of a initially reluctant teenager quickly becoming absorbed in laughter and fun around a table with their family.

Recognizing the stresses teenagers face, from academic pressures to the demands of social media, Cannon stressed the value of dedicated family time for collective well-being, whether through gameplay or other shared activities.

Originally beginning as a monthly pop-up in Sharnbrook Village Hall, Ready Steady Roll is now permanently housed at Ivy Lodge, a short ten-minute drive from Rushden along the A6.

WELLS, ME (CBS Local) – A friendly dog’s “thank you” to the firefighter who rescued him from a roof has gone viral.
The pup in Wells, Maine got himself into a rough situation over the Memorial Day weekend when he escaped out the second floor window of his owner’s home and was trapped on a small porch roof.
“We received numerous calls but one concerned citizen, Phil Burke, discovered him early on and notified us. Another awesome citizen stood by with the dog until we could arrive on scene!” Wells Police wrote on Facebook.
When a firefighter climbed up to help the dog get back inside, the grateful pup became more interested in showing his appreciation than getting off the roof. Police on the ground recorded the friendly dog circling Fire Department Captain Jeff Nawfel and giving him a bunch of kisses on the face before getting a final nudge back into his home.
The dog’s “thank you” was posted on May 27 and has already been viewed over 16,000 times. “Thank you to all that called and helped save him,” officers wrote on Facebook.
rewrite:
WELLS, ME (CBS Local) – A firefighter's rescue of a dog from a rooftop in Maine has captured widespread attention online due to the animal's affectionate response. Over the Memorial Day holiday, the pet managed to get out through an upstairs window in its owner's house, becoming stranded on a narrow section of roof below.

Local authorities reported receiving multiple alerts. A resident named Phil Burke first noticed the stranded animal and contacted emergency services, while another helpful individual stayed with the dog until help came. Upon arrival, a firefighter ascended to the roof to guide the pet to safety.

Rather than immediately heading inside, the appreciative dog focused on expressing its gratitude. It circled around Fire Captain Jeff Nawfel, covering his face in licks before finally being gently guided back through the window. The Wells Police shared the video of this thankful reunion on Facebook on May 27, where it quickly amassed over 16,000 views. The department extended thanks to everyone who reported the incident and assisted in the successful rescue.

Police are warning people intending to tramp the Tongariro Alpine Crossing to be fully prepared after an English tourist plunged 100m down rocks and ice this morning.
Senior Constable Barry Shepherd of Taupō Police said trampers should carry an ice axe and crampons - and know how to use them.
Taupō's Greenlea helicopter this morning flew a paramedic and Land Search and Rescue volunteer to Mt Tongariro to rescue an English woman who had slipped on ice at Red Crater and fallen 100m down the mountain into a ravine.
She was "pretty beaten up" by the fall down through rocks and ice, including a knocking her head and suffering bruises and cuts, Mr Shepherd said.
Advertisement
The woman, 30, who has been living and working in New Zealand, set out from the Mangatepopo carpark this morning at 4am with a young Austrian woman as a companion.
The fall occurred at about 7.30am and the alarm was raised 10 minutes later.
The helicopter flew from Taupō Airport to Mt Tongariro and dropped off a paramedic near Emerald Lakes, who made his way to the woman.
It then unloaded the SAR volunteer who used an ice axe and crampons to reach the Austrian woman perched on the icy slope below the summit of Red Crater, where she had remained.
She had been in voice contact with her friend, although she could not see her, and initially feared she had been killed in the fall.
Shepherd said both women did the right thing in staying put and calling for help but there was always ice on the Tongariro Alpine Crossing at this time of year and people needed to be properly prepared.
"It's icy up there, that whole Red Crater summit was icy.
"It'll thaw and soften around late morning but freezes overnight and will be frozen in the mornings, and if you get a bit of cloud and it stays under cloud, it won't thaw out at all."
If people did not know how to use an ice axe and crampons, they should use a guiding service across the crossing, he added.
The injured woman was flown to Rotorua Hospital.
rewrite:
Authorities are cautioning hikers planning to traverse the Tongariro Alpine Crossing to ensure they are adequately equipped, following a serious incident this morning involving a British visitor who fell approximately 100 meters over rocky and icy terrain.

Barry Shepherd, a Senior Constable with the Taupō Police, emphasized that those undertaking the trek should have an ice axe and crampons in their gear, and must be proficient in their use. This advice comes after a rescue operation was launched earlier today. A helicopter from Greenlea in Taupō transported a paramedic and a volunteer from Land Search and Rescue to Mount Tongariro. Their mission was to assist a woman from England who had lost her footing on ice near Red Crater, tumbling down a steep gully.

According to Shepherd, the 30-year-old woman, who resides and works in New Zealand, sustained significant injuries from the descent over rocks and ice, including head trauma, lacerations, and bruising. She had begun her hike from the Mangatepopo car park at 4 a.m., accompanied by a younger woman from Austria. The accident happened around 7:30 a.m., and emergency services were alerted shortly after.

The rescue helicopter landed near Emerald Lakes to deploy the paramedic, who then proceeded to the injured hiker. Subsequently, the search and rescue volunteer was dropped off. Using specialized mountaineering equipment, this volunteer reached the Austrian companion, who had stayed in place on a frozen slope below Red Crater's peak. The companion had maintained auditory contact with her friend after the fall but, unable to see her, initially feared the worst.

Shepherd commended both individuals for remaining stationary and summoning help promptly. He reiterated that icy conditions are consistently present on the crossing during this season, necessitating proper preparation. "The area is icy, particularly the entire Red Crater summit," he stated. "While it may melt and soften later in the day, it refreezes overnight and remains frozen in the early hours. If cloud cover persists, the ice might not thaw at all."

He further advised that anyone not confident in using ice axes and crampons should consider hiring a professional guide for the journey. Following the rescue, the injured woman was airlifted to Rotorua Hospital for medical treatment.

Severe thunderstorm watch canceled for this evening
hello
The severe thunderstorm watch originally scheduled to last until 8 p.m. was canceled early as the storms moved out of the area.
Cook, DuPage, Kane, McHenry, Lake, Will and many other northern Illinois counties were part of the watch from the National Weather Service in Chicago. There also was a warning for DuPage, Will and parts of Kane and Cook counties that lasted until 5:45 p.m.

Crystal Palace have gone down in Brondby manager Alexander Zorniger's estimations, following a second collapsed move for goalkeeper Frederik Ronnow.
The goalkeeper was the subject of a deadline day bid on Wednesday for the Eagles and was believed to be all set for the move to London, having seen a deal to Palace fall through last summer, too.
It was initially understood Brondby pulled out of the deal late on, but the Danish club seem to have their side of the story, too.
Boss Zorniger has been quoted by Danish newspaper, BT, and is happy to have kept Ronnow - for now - but is isn't happy with the treatment received by Palace.
"Frederik was in the same situation last summer. The same club would have the same player on the last day of the transfer window," he said, as quoted by BT.
"I don’t know if anyone can understand what they do, I’m not able to do. But he is still here and we’re very happy.
"Maybe they think it’s professional, but from my point of view it’s unprofessional. It’s disrespectful to another club."
Ronnow, himself, is gutted his Premier League dream has been crushed twice in the space of five months.
He was quoted: "I’m obviously annoyed, but also clear and motivated.
"I could choose to go and cry in the corner, but I wouldn’t get anything out of it."

Brondby's head coach, Alexander Zorniger, now holds a lower opinion of Crystal Palace after their second unsuccessful attempt to secure goalkeeper Frederik Ronnow. On the final day of the transfer window, Palace made an offer for Ronnow, and it appeared the keeper was poised to join the London club, repeating a scenario from the previous summer when an earlier agreement also disintegrated.

While initial reports suggested Brondby withdrew from negotiations at the last moment, the Danish side has presented its own perspective. Speaking to the Danish publication BT, Zorniger expressed contentment at retaining Ronnow for the time being, but conveyed clear dissatisfaction with Palace's conduct throughout the process.

Zorniger remarked, "Frederik experienced this identical scenario with the same club at the end of the previous transfer window. I cannot comprehend their actions, and I do not believe many others can either. However, we are pleased he remains with us. They may consider their approach professional, but I view it as quite the opposite—it shows a lack of respect toward another organization."

For his part, Ronnow is deeply disappointed that his opportunity to play in the Premier League has been thwarted twice within half a year. He stated, "Naturally, I am frustrated, but I remain focused and driven. I could simply give up and feel sorry for myself, but that would achieve nothing."

Last week, footage was released of a schizophrenic man writhing on the floor of his cell until he dies as California sheriff’s deputies laugh and smirk.
The Tribune of San Luis Obispo posted the approximately eight-minute-long video of Andrew Holland's death on January 22, 2017, last week. Holland, who was in jail for minor offenses, died after an embolism traveled to his brain. Blood clots, which typically cause embolisms, often occur after an extended period of sitting or lying down.
The footage contradicts the county officials' version of how Holland died. Contrary to what police stated, Holland was not "found unconscious and unresponsive" and was not "under the continual care of a physician" at the time of his death.
Holland was pronounced dead in his cell at 5:36 p.m. on January 22, 2017, only about an hour after he was released from being strapped to a plastic restraint chair for two days for hitting himself.
In an email Thursday, County Administrative Officer Wade Horton said the video was "extremely painful to watch."
​"What happened to Andrew Holland was a tragedy that impacts our entire community," Horton wrote.
"Although we can't bring Andrew back, our county has made, and continues to make, changes in response to this terrible event."
Some of the reforms implemented including banning the use of restraint chairs, hiring an independent contractor to audit county procedures and establishing the Stepping Up initiative to reduce the number of mentally ill patients in prisons.
In July 2017, Holland's family was awarded a $5 million settlement from the county. They plan to use the settlement money to establish a nonprofit organization to advocate for civil rights of mentally ill people in jail.
"We had hope that his life would improve, but on January 22nd of this year, our son Andrew died a brutal and tortured death at the hands of the custodial staff at San Luis Obispo County jail," Holland's mother, Sharon, told reporters last July.
Although Horton did admit that the county is partly responsible for Holland's death, he did not specify whether any officials would face consequences over Holland's death.
rewrite:
Recently, a video became public showing a man with schizophrenia convulsing on the floor of a jail cell until he perished, while deputies from a California sheriff's department watched with amusement and derisive smiles. The San Luis Obispo Tribune published this roughly eight-minute recording last week, depicting the final moments of Andrew Holland on January 22, 2017. Holland, who was incarcerated for minor infractions, ultimately succumbed when a clot traveled to his brain. Such blockages, frequently stemming from prolonged inactivity, are a common cause of embolisms.

This evidence directly conflicts with the account provided by county authorities. Officials had claimed Holland was discovered already unconscious and without vital signs, and that he was receiving ongoing medical supervision. The video tells a different story. Holland was declared dead in his cell at 5:36 p.m. on that date, merely an hour after being freed from a restraint chair. He had been confined to that chair for 46 hours as a response to self-harming behavior.

Wade Horton, the County Administrative Officer, described the footage in a Thursday email as deeply distressing to view. He acknowledged the event as a community-wide tragedy and stated that while Holland cannot be restored to life, the county has enacted and is still pursuing reforms prompted by this incident. These changes include prohibiting restraint chairs, bringing in an external auditor to review county protocols, and launching the Stepping Up program to decrease the incarceration of individuals with mental health conditions.

Holland's family received a $5 million settlement from the county in July 2017. They intend to dedicate these funds to creating a nonprofit aimed at protecting the rights of mentally ill detainees. His mother, Sharon, expressed to reporters last July that their hopes for his improvement were shattered by what she called a brutal and agonizing death inflicted by jail personnel.

While Horton conceded some county responsibility in the matter, he did not clarify if any individuals would be held accountable for their roles in Holland's demise.

Kano State government has approved N4 billion for the construction of underpass and flyover that will connect Zaria Road/Silver Jubilee and Zoo Road in the metropolis.
In a statement in Abuja on the outcome of the 11th State Executive Council, SEC, meeting presided over by Governor Abdullahi Ganduje, the Commissioner for Information, Youth and Culture, Malam Muhammad Garba, said the project was aimed at reducing carbon emission and road accidents and to beautify the state capital.
Mohammed said: “Already, the government has begun the reconstruction, expansion, rehabilitation and upgrading of existing roads in the state in addition to the completion of the underpass at Sharada/Panshekara Road Junction, which has been completed and commissio-ned by President Muhammadu Buhari.”
Malam Garba said other council’s approval included $36,000 being payment of project fees to 18 admitted state-sponsored students in El-Razi University, Sudan; procurement of bed sheets for 31 secondary health facilities at N39 million; reconstruction work of Dawakin Kudu-Lahadin Makole Road in Dawakin Kudu Local Government at over N748 million.
Others, he said, included expansion/repairs of Giginyu-Kawo-Eastern Bypass Road in Nassarawa Local Government; rehabilitation works/upgrade of Fagwalawa Primary Healthcare Centre to Cottage Hospital at N588 million and 230 million, respectively.

MADISON — The bad news keeps coming for the Wisconsin basketball team.
On the same day guard D’Mitrik Trice was to undergo surgery on his foot that will keep him out indefinitely, Wisconsin announced Monday that freshman guard Kobe King will have season-ending knee surgery.
Advertisement
King injured his left knee during practice on Friday. After not being present during the first half of Saturday’s game against Marquette, the La Crosse native sat behind the bench during the second half of that loss.
“I’m disappointed that I’m not able to finish the season with my teammates,” King said in a tweet sent by UW. “But following my surgery, I plan to attack my rehab as aggressively as possible & come back stronger than ever. While I’m out, I look forward to watching our team continue to grow this season”
A prized recruit in the 2017 class, King was averaging 5.2 points and 1.4 rebounds for the Badgers over the first 10 games of the season. King is eligible to apply for a medical hardship waiver after the season. If granted, he would still have four years of eligibility remaining.
“I feel awful for D’Mitrik and Kobe,” coach Greg Gard said in a tweet sent by UW. “Fortunately, there is a silver lining that we were right under the minimum number of games to apply for a (medical hardship).”
The loss of King, combined with the uncertainty around Trice, is a significant hit for a team that was struggling to find its way even with that duo on the floor. As of now, the only true guards Wisconsin has coming off its bench are junior T.J. Sclundt, who played a career-high 13 minutes against Marquette, and true freshman walk-on Walt McGrory, who was expected to redshirt this season.
The Badgers are just 4-7 on the year, a mark that has them at three games under .500 for the first time since 2001. They’ll host Western Kentucky on Wednesday.

Portland
