CAMDEN, Ark. (KARK/NBC News) – A young Arkansas mother’s final moments were streamed on Facebook Live as friends watch helplessly from afar.
25-year-old Keiana Herndon went live Wednesday from a friend’s home, where she was staying with her young son.
The video starts out with Keiana singing. You see and hear her respond to viewers and even put the spotlight on her son.
A few minutes later, Keiana falls and the phone drops out of her hands.
Her uncle, Jeffrey Herndon, said he could hear his niece struggle to breath and her son scream in the background.
“It was real hard,” he said.
All the while, the number of eyes on her grew.
A friend showed up nearly 30 minutes after Keiana hit the floor.
Keiana’s father wishes someone watching would have acted sooner.
“It’s amazing for someone to sit there and see somebody or hear them take their last breath and nobody did anything,” said Richard. “So, I want to take my hat off to everybody that actual did something.”
rewrite:
In a tragic incident broadcast over social media, a 25-year-old Arkansas woman's last moments were witnessed by online viewers who were unable to intervene. Keiana Herndon was staying at a friend's residence with her small child when she began a live video stream. Initially seen singing and interacting with the audience, she even directed attention to her son. The situation changed abruptly when she collapsed, causing her phone to fall.

Her uncle, Jeffrey Herndon, recounted hearing his niece's labored breathing and the child's cries during the broadcast. He described the experience as profoundly difficult. As the live video continued, the viewership increased. Assistance arrived approximately half an hour after her fall.

Keiana's father, Richard, expressed dismay that no observers acted more quickly, stating it was shocking to know people watched or listened without intervening. He extended gratitude to those who ultimately responded to the situation.

input: Ten minutes, 74 hotdogs and an estimated 22,200 calories later, Joey "Jaws" Chestnut is once again the undisputed chow champion. Today marked Chestnut's 11th win at the annual Nathan's Famous Hot Dog Eating Contest in Coney Island."Seventy-four hot dogs -- I've earned it," he said after the event in an interview with ESPN. Chestnut marked a new world record set using his signature style of stuffing two frankfurters down his throat at a time. "This was a beautiful day. I love to eat and I tried to enjoy the food."For yet another year, the favorites in both the men's and women's categories -- Chestnut, 34, and Miki Sudo, 33, -- strutted off the stage after braving the broiling heat to brandish mustard title belts and oversized checks, proving they reign supreme when it comes to speed-eating encased meat.Chestnut, the current hotdog-eating world record holder from Vallejo, California , downed a whopping 74 weiners, dipping the buns in super-sized plastic cups of water during the 10-minute-long contest. Judges peered below and Nathan's helpers stood by with paper plates loaded with more hotdogs.Chestnut said he had "a vision" for this year's win, and seemed to be unfatigued after "10 minutes of work.""I'm going to keep riding the wave," he said of his carer on the competitive eating circuit.New Jersey native Carmen Cincotti finished second by eating 64 hot dogs. Third place finisher Darron Breedon got 43 frankfurters down.The Fourth of July event, considered by some to be the Super Bowl of competitive eating, also featured 74-year-old Rich "The Locust" LeFevre -- the oldest competitor in the contest's 101-year history.In the women's competition, Sudo, a native New Yorker by way of Japan and Hawaii, accomplished her goal to "5-pete" the competition by gobbling 37 hot dogs and water-dipped buns in 10 minutes."I had a comfortable lead, and I left room to eat more for next year," Sudo told ESPN while hoisting her pink title belt.Sudo's dad was in the crowd to watch her win. While her grand total was four fewer than her tally last year, it was nine more than the closest challenger, Michelle Lesco.Third place finisher Juliet Lee came in with just 25.
rewrite:
After consuming an estimated 22,200 calories in the form of 74 hot dogs over ten minutes, Joey “Jaws” Chestnut has reaffirmed his status as the premier competitive eater. He secured his eleventh victory at the iconic Nathan’s Famous Hot Dog Eating Contest on Coney Island this Fourth of July. In a post-event ESPN interview, Chestnut remarked, “Seventy-four hot dogs—I’ve earned it.” He established a new global benchmark by employing his trademark method of swallowing two frankfurters simultaneously. “It was a perfect day. I enjoy eating and I made sure to savor it,” he added.

Once again, the predicted winners in both the men’s and women’s divisions—Chestnut, 34, and Miki Sudo, 33—triumphed under the intense summer sun, each claiming mustard-colored championship belts and giant ceremonial checks. Their performances demonstrated continued dominance in the rapid consumption of sausages.

Chestnut, the reigning world record holder from Vallejo, California, consumed his 74 hot dogs by softening the buns in large cups of water throughout the ten-minute event. Officials observed closely while assistants stood ready with platters of additional food. Chestnut shared that he had envisioned this victory and felt surprisingly fresh after what he called “ten minutes of work.” Regarding his professional eating future, he stated, “I plan to keep this momentum going.”

Carmen Cincotti of New Jersey placed second by eating 64 hot dogs, and Darron Breedon finished third with 43. The historic contest, often called the Super Bowl of competitive eating, also included 74-year-old Rich “The Locust” LeFevre, the oldest participant in the event’s century-long history.

In the women’s competition, Sudo—a New Yorker with roots in Japan and Hawaii—achieved her aim of a fifth consecutive title by consuming 37 hot dogs with water-dipped buns in the allotted time. Holding her pink championship belt, she told ESPN, “I maintained a solid lead and kept something in reserve for next year.” Her father was present to witness the win. Although her total was four fewer than the previous year, it exceeded her nearest rival, Michelle Lesco, by nine. Juliet Lee finished in third place with 25 hot dogs.

Dubai: Initial data on Abu Dhabi hotels released by STR on Monday highlighted that increases in supply had outstripped demand by 1.5 per cent, whilst room occupancy was down -1.4 per cent to 74.2 per cent.
The findings from STR, a data analytics service headquartered in London, England, are based on daily data from January, presenting year over year comparisons on rates and occupancy.
The preliminary data indicates sharp rate declines, including a drop of -10 per cent in the city’s average daily rate (ADR) to Dh 465.80.
In addition to the fall in ADR, the revenue per available room (RevPAR) slipped by -11.2 per cent to Dh 345.68.
STR analysts note in the statement that Abu Dhabi’s ADR levels were once again pressured by supply growth in the market. However, the market’s hotels did record a significant uptick in RevPAR (+23.6%) on the last day of the month, mainly due to the Global Space Congress (January 31-February 1).
The situation is largely the same in Dubai, with a number of new hotels in 2016 coupled with slower demand pushing hotels’ profits down 6.8 per cent year-on-year.

As speculation mounts over the Prime Minister's future, here is a look at how Theresa May could be replaced.
According to Conservative Party rules, a leadership contest can be triggered in two ways, with the most obvious being if Mrs May resigns.
If the PM is determined to stay, a leadership election can be triggered if 15% of Tory MPs write to Graham Brady, the chairman of the 1922 Committee - made up of backbench Conservative MPs - saying they no longer have confidence in the leader.
Some 48 MPs would be needed to oust Mrs May with the party's current crop of 318 MPs, including the speaker and deputy speaker.
Once that threshold is crossed, Mr Brady would announce the start of the leadership contest and invite nominations, with candidates needing the support of at least two MPs to get on to the ballot paper.
If there is only one candidate, they will be automatically declared leader.
But if multiple MPs are successfully nominated, Tory MPs then vote, with the candidate achieving the lowest number of votes forced out of the race, until only two candidates remain.
Conservative Party members then vote for their preferred candidate on a "one member, one vote" basis, with the winner becoming the new leader.
When David Cameron resigned following the EU referendum, five Tory MPs stood for the leadership.
Mrs May and Andrea Leadsom were due to go to the ballot of the Conservative Party membership.
But Mrs May was formally confirmed as the new leader after Mrs Leadsom pulled out of the race.
In 2005, Conservative Party members chose Mr Cameron over David Davis, while in 2003 Iain Duncan Smith was ousted as leader after the chairman of the 1922 Committee received 25 letters from Tory MPs.
Michael Howard was then elected leader as the only nominated MP to replace him.
rewrite:
Amid growing conjecture regarding the Prime Minister's tenure, the mechanisms for a potential change in leadership are coming into focus. Under the regulations of the Conservative Party, a challenge for the top position can be initiated through two primary avenues. The most straightforward would be a voluntary resignation by the incumbent.

Should the Prime Minister choose not to step down, an internal election can be forced if 15 percent of sitting Conservative Members of Parliament submit letters expressing a loss of confidence to Graham Brady, who heads the 1922 Committee of backbench Tory MPs. Given the current parliamentary party count of 318, which includes the speaker and deputy speaker, this translates to a requirement of 48 letters.

Upon reaching this number, Mr. Brady would publicly declare the commencement of the contest and call for candidates. To enter the race, a contender must secure endorsements from a minimum of two fellow MPs. Should only one individual meet this condition, they would assume the leadership without further process.

If multiple candidates are validated, a series of elimination votes among Conservative MPs follows. In each round, the contender with the fewest votes is removed until just two finalists remain. The decision then passes to the broader Conservative Party membership, who select the victor through a direct, one-member-one-vote system.

Historical precedents illustrate this process. Following the Brexit vote, David Cameron's departure led to five MPs initially competing. Theresa May and Andrea Leadsom emerged as the final two, but May was confirmed as leader after Leadsom withdrew. In 2005, the membership selected David Cameron over David Davis. Earlier, in 2003, Iain Duncan Smith was removed after the 1922 Committee chairman received 25 letters from colleagues, leading to Michael Howard's uncontested election as the sole nominee.

ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. - Terry Kimball, an Uber passenger in St. Petersburg punched by his driver, has died as a result of his injuries, officials said Saturday, Aug. 12.
St. Petersburg police said no charges have been filed yet and the investigation continues.
Police said at 7:30 p.m. Thursday, Uber driver Kabir O' Farril Diaz, 38, picked up 56-year-old passenger Terry L. Kimball.
They had a dispute over the route the driver was taking. Diaz pulled over at a Quick Pick Foods store in St. Petersburg, where they had a physical altercation.
Authorities said the driver punched Kimball, and he did not regain consciousness.
"I saw this guy laying on the ground. This woman was pressing on his chest trying to bring him back," Carlton Reid said. "He wasn't responsive. It was pretty tough, really I was really scared, I didn't know what was going on with him and I was pretty worried."
Reid said he witnessed the aftermath of the fight.
Kimball went to the hospital with serious brain trauma and life-threatening injuries.
Police said a witness told them Kimball appeared to be the aggressor. A friend of Diaz told Tampa-based WFTS reporter Michael Paluska he has a baby on the way and is not a violent person.
According to Pinellas County court records Kimball's been arrested multiple times for crimes that include DUI, simple battery, resisting arrest, and disorderly intoxication.
"That's very sad," Reid said. "It really is I would like to know what happened now, truly."
Investigators are speaking with witnesses and they say Diaz, who has not been charged at this time, is cooperating.
rewrite:
Authorities in St. Petersburg, Florida, reported on Saturday, August 12, that a man who was assaulted by his Uber driver has succumbed to his wounds. The victim has been identified as Terry Kimball, a 56-year-old passenger.

According to police reports, the incident began on Thursday evening when driver Kabir O' Farril Diaz, 38, collected Kimball. A disagreement arose between the two regarding the chosen travel route. This led Diaz to stop the vehicle at a local convenience store, where a physical confrontation ensued. Officials state that Diaz struck Kimball, who subsequently lost consciousness.

Carlton Reid, who observed the scene afterward, described seeing a woman performing chest compressions on an unresponsive Kimball. Reid expressed his distress and concern over the situation.

Kimball was transported to a hospital with critical head injuries that ultimately proved fatal. While the inquiry is ongoing and no charges have been filed, police note that a witness described Kimball as the initial aggressor. A friend of Diaz, speaking to a local news reporter, characterized the driver as non-violent and mentioned he is expecting a child. Public records indicate Kimball had a history of prior arrests.

Investigators confirm they are interviewing witnesses and that Diaz is cooperating with the process.

Tina Turner's firstborn son, Craig Turner, died of apparent suicide Tuesday, the Los Angeles coroner's office confirms to USA TODAY. He was 59.
Police found him dead at 12:38 p.m. of an apparent gunshot wound inside his Studio City, Calif. home, according to Ed Winter, assistant chief of investigations for the Los Angeles.coroner's department.
An autopsy is pending.
Craig worked in real estate and was Tina Turner's firstborn son, whom she had at age 18 with saxophonist Raymond Hill. Craig was adopted by Ike Turner after they wed in 1962.
Turner told Oprah Winfrey in a 2005 interview that Craig was "a very emotional kid" who offered support when she was physically abused by Ike Turner.
Craig was in high school when Turner finally left the abusive relationship with Ike.
"Before you can really help them, you have to strengthen yourself," Turner said.
Tina Turner divorced Ike in 1978. She married German music producer Erwin Bach, her partner of nearly 30 years, in 2013.
Turner and Bach were in Paris Tuesday night attending a party for Giorgio Armani Prive Haute Couture.
USA TODAY has reached out to representatives for Turner.
© 2018 USATODAY.COM
rewrite:
The Los Angeles coroner's office has confirmed to USA TODAY that Craig Turner, the eldest son of Tina Turner, passed away on Tuesday in what appears to have been a suicide. He was 59 years old. Authorities discovered his body in his Studio City residence with a suspected gunshot wound, as reported by Ed Winter, an assistant chief investigator for the coroner's department. An examination to determine the exact cause of death is still underway.

Craig, who built a career in real estate, was born when Tina Turner was 18, and his biological father was saxophonist Raymond Hill. He was later adopted by Ike Turner following his marriage to Tina in 1962. In a 2005 conversation with Oprah Winfrey, Tina Turner described Craig as a deeply sensitive child who provided her comfort during the physical abuse she endured from Ike. She noted that he was a teenager when she ultimately escaped that violent marriage, reflecting that one must first find personal strength before being able to aid others.

Tina Turner and Ike divorced in 1978. She later wed Erwin Bach, a German music executive and her long-term partner of almost three decades, in 2013. On the evening of Craig's death, Turner and Bach were in Paris at a gala for Giorgio Armani Prive Haute Couture. USA TODAY has attempted to contact Turner's representatives for comment.

Johannesburg - Deputy President David Mabuza arrives in the Kenyan capital Nairobi on Thursday on a working visit and to attend the Madaraka Day (Freedom Day) celebrations, marking the day when Kenya gained independence from Britain in 1963.
South Africa and Kenya enjoy strong bilateral relations, with the two countries’ heads of state meeting on the margins of various international and multilateral engagements to discuss matters of mutual interest. South Africa also undertook a state visit to Kenya in 2016.
Following his re-election in November 2017, President Uhuru Kenyatta undertook a working visit to South Africa at the beginning of this year to attend the ruling African National Congress's annual anniversary celebrations in East London.
The latest engagement forms the basis for the invitation to the deputy president from Kenya's governing Jubilee Party to strengthen party-to-party relations as well as trade and economic relations on the occasion of the Madaraka Day celebrations.
During the working visit, it is envisaged that Kenyatta and Mabuza will discuss issues of mutual concern, including the proposed reform initiatives of the African Union, the ongoing security challenges in South Sudan and Somalia, as well as mutually beneficial economic opportunities between the two countries.
African News Agency/ANA
rewrite:
Deputy President David Mabuza of South Africa will travel to Nairobi, Kenya, this Thursday for official meetings and to participate in Madaraka Day festivities, which commemorate Kenya's attainment of independence from British rule in 1963. The two nations maintain a robust partnership, with their leaders frequently consulting during international forums on shared priorities. A state visit by South Africa to Kenya occurred in 2016.

After President Uhuru Kenyatta's re-election in late 2017, he traveled to South Africa earlier this year for a working visit, attending the African National Congress's yearly commemoration events in East London. This ongoing dialogue prompted Kenya's ruling Jubilee Party to invite the deputy president, aiming to bolster ties between their political parties and enhance commercial and economic cooperation during the independence celebrations.

The scheduled discussions between Kenyatta and Mabuza are expected to cover matters of common interest. These will likely include potential reforms within the African Union, current security issues in South Sudan and Somalia, and avenues for expanding economically beneficial partnerships between South Africa and Kenya.

Fabrizio Ravanelli Says He Is Interested In Dundee Managerial Job
Fabrizio Ravanelli says he is interested in taking over at Dundee after Paul Hartley’s sacking on Monday.
He told The Sun: “I believe I can keep Dundee in the Premiership and I am very interested in this job. I can save the club from relegation. I could definitely get results and get the best out of the Dundee players.
“I am ready to get a flight to Scotland very quickly. It is an exciting opportunity and I would love to go back. I am looking for a new project in management and this would be the perfect fresh start for me. I would bring energy, enthusiasm and motivation to the club.”
“Dundee are in danger but there are five games to play and I am 100 per cent confident that the team can survive.
“I was only at Dundee for a short period of time but it’s a special club and I love the passion of Scottish football. It is a fantastic country. I have played football in Britain and it would be an honour to manage there too.”
Paul Hartley was dismissed following Dundee’s 2-0 defeat to Hamilton on Saturday, their seventh successive loss, which leaves them 11th in the Scottish Premiership table

Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) is set to unveil a plan that would give American workers who want or need jobs guaranteed government jobs that pay at least $15 per hour and have health benefits.
The progressive Vermont senator’s guaranteed jobs plan would entitle any American a job or job training in U.S.-funded projects in infrastructure, the environment, caregiving, and education, but he did not provide a cost-estimate or plan to fund the proposal, the Washington Post reported.
A representative from Sanders’ office said no funding estimate was available for the project because staffers were still crafting the proposal.
Two other potential 2020 presidential candidates—Sen. Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Sen. Kristen Gillibrand (D-NY)—have expressed interest in crafting similar proposals.
“The goal is to eliminate working poverty and involuntary unemployment altogether,” said Darrick Hamilton, an economist at The New School who expressed support for a guaranteed jobs program. “This is an opportunity for something transformative, beyond the tinkering we’ve been doing for the last 40 years, where all the productivity gains have gone to the elite of society.”
Critics of the plan have said guaranteed jobs proposals would not be sustainable or affordable, and would cause massive job losses in the private sector.
Studies have shown that states and cities which choose to enact a $15 per hour minimum wage trigger job losses. A December 2017 study found that once California’s minimum wage hike takes effect in 2022, the state would lose 400,000 jobs.
“It completely undercuts a lot of industries and companies,” Brian Riedl, a senior fellow at the Manhattan Institute who opposes the program, told the Post. “There will be pressure to introduce a higher wage or certain benefits that the private sector doesn’t offer.”
The proposal is unlikely to gain favor with Republicans in control of Congress, and even most Democrats have slammed similar plans as unrealistic.
“It would be extremely expensive, and I wonder if this is the best, most targeted use of the amount of money it would cost,” said Ernie Tedeschi, an economist who worked for the Treasury during the Obama administration.
The Vermont senator’s proposal comes days after he declared President Trump’s agenda “dead” if the Democratic Party wins the majority in the House or Senate.
rewrite:
Senator Bernie Sanders, an independent from Vermont, is preparing to introduce an initiative aimed at ensuring employment for any American seeking work. Under this proposal, the federal government would provide jobs paying no less than fifteen dollars an hour, inclusive of healthcare coverage, to all willing and able adults. According to a report, the plan would offer positions or vocational training in publicly financed endeavors spanning sectors like infrastructure, environmental conservation, caregiving services, and education. However, specific financial details or a definitive funding strategy for the measure have not yet been disclosed by the senator.

An aide from Sanders' office indicated that a precise budgetary projection remains unavailable as the policy is still being developed. This concept has also attracted attention from other lawmakers considered potential presidential contenders, including Democratic Senators Cory Booker and Kirsten Gillibrand, who have shown openness to formulating comparable policies.

Proponents argue that such a program could eradicate working poverty and involuntary joblessness. One supportive economist described it as a transformative departure from decades of incremental policy, which have largely concentrated economic gains among the wealthiest tiers of society. They view it as a fundamental shift toward shared prosperity.

Opponents, however, contend that a federal job guarantee would be financially unsustainable and would destabilize the private labor market. Critics reference research indicating that substantial minimum wage increases, such as moving to a fifteen-dollar threshold, have historically resulted in significant employment reductions in certain regions. A conservative policy analyst warned that the plan would undermine many businesses by creating pressure to match public-sector wages and benefits, potentially leading to widespread private job losses.

The initiative faces steep political hurdles, particularly with a Republican majority in Congress, and even many Democrats have dismissed analogous ideas as impractical. A former economic advisor from the Obama administration questioned whether the enormous required expenditure represents the most effective use of public funds. Sanders' announcement follows his recent statement that President Trump's legislative goals would be thwarted should Democrats regain control of either congressional chamber in the upcoming elections.

PINK HILL, N.C. (WNCT) — A revival is underway in the small Lenoir County town of Pink Hill.
From home renovations to a complete overhaul of the internet system in town, the community is hard at work.
County leaders are hoping the changes in Pink Hill serve as an inspiration to other small towns in the region.
“Our town died,” said Susan Myers. “Everybody moved out, and I didn’t want that to happen here.”
Susan Myers moved to Pink Hill eight years ago, quickly becoming an active part of the small town. She says she knew something needed to be done to keep her new home from dying, too.
“We started buying up properties in downtown,” said Susan Myers.
Susan and her husband Al Myers now own 35 commercial or residential buildings, and whatever they could work to revive, they did.
“If you go around Pink Hill and see something that doesn’t look good, that’s because I haven’t been able to buy it,” Susan Myers said.
Community leaders like Lenoir County Commissioner J. Mac Daughety took notice of the changes in Pink Hill, and those leaders are using the revival in the town as a template for other small communities in eastern North Carolina.
“The things where citizens come together, groups come together, and they say, ‘Let’s make this a better community,’ that’s where you see a community like Pink Hill start to blossom,” Daughety said.
With the addition of nearly 2,400 pink roses around town, another initiative working to rejuvenate the spirit of the community, Commissioner Daughety hopes others are inspired to take action.
“I’m going to do what I can do,” Daughety said. “I’m going to try to motivate others to help do better things for our community. If I start the engine, then surely other people will get on board.”
Myers says no matter how you are able to get involved, you should do something.
“Some of us have money to invest, others have time to volunteer,” said Myers. “We can help in different ways, but we have to take the leadership, and we can’t depend on government to come help and save us.”
rewrite:
A transformation is taking place in the quiet community of Pink Hill, located in Lenoir County. Residents are actively engaged in a variety of improvement projects, ranging from updating houses to modernizing the entire local internet infrastructure. Officials from the county view this progress as a potential model for similar small towns throughout the area.

Susan Myers, a resident for the past eight years who immersed herself in town life, observed a troubling trend. “The community was fading,” she remarked. “People were leaving, and I was determined to prevent that here.” Motivated to protect her adopted home, she and her husband, Al, began acquiring real estate in the central business district. They now hold title to dozens of properties, both business and residential, and have focused their efforts on restoring each one. “Any building in Pink Hill that appears neglected is simply one I haven’t managed to purchase yet,” Susan Myers explained.

This noticeable revitalization has captured the attention of local figures such as Lenoir County Commissioner J. Mac Daughety. He sees Pink Hill’s experience as a blueprint for other small towns in eastern North Carolina. “When individuals and organizations unite with the shared goal of improving their surroundings, that’s how a place like Pink Hill begins to thrive,” Daughety stated. He highlighted the recent planting of almost 2,400 pink roses throughout the town as one example of a project designed to bolster community pride and hopes it encourages similar efforts elsewhere.

Daughety is committed to his role, saying, “I intend to contribute what I can and encourage others to also work toward enhancing our community. If I can help get things started, I believe more people will join in.” Myers echoes the call for broad participation, emphasizing that contribution comes in many forms. “While some have financial resources to contribute, others can offer their time and effort,” she noted. “There are numerous ways to assist, but it requires local initiative. We cannot simply wait for outside assistance to rescue us.”

DURHAM, N.C. — Raashean Davis matched his career-high with 23 points and grabbed 10 rebounds to lead North Carolina Central to a 72-61 Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference victory over Delaware State Saturday, keeping the Hornets winless in conference play.
Raekwon Harney scored at the basket in the final minute of the first half to give NC Central a 40-34 lead, but Artem Tavakalyan hit a 3 with :38 left to send Delaware State into intermission trailing by just three, 40-37.
Zacarry Douglas’ layup with 15:56 left in the game sparked an 8-0 run by the Eagles to go up by double digits, 54-44.
Reginald Gardner Jr. and Pablo Rivas scored 13 and 12 points, respectively, for NC Central (11-10, 5-2) and Jordan Perkins added 10 points, seven boards and six assists.
Jonathan Walker scored 19 points for Delaware State (2-21, 0-8). Tavakalyan added 17 points and Marquis Collins contributed 15.

There are three reasons to watch the Outback Bowl between the Florida Gators and Iowa Hawkeyes at 1 p.m. this afternoon:
You attended one of the schools and university pride is important to you
You hate yourself
You crave a free appetizer from Outback Steakhouse and you’re pulling for it to be coconut shrimp or a bloomin’ onion
In the interest of marketing, branding and bowl season, Outback is again giving away a bloomin’ onion if the SEC team (Florida) wins and an order of coconut shrimp if the B1G team (Iowa) wins. This practice has been in place since 2013 and the bloomin’ onion has won three of four games. It must be a real conflict if you’re an Iowa supporter but can’t get enough fried onions in your system.
There are some rules, though, which seems to go against Outback’s brand. You can only get one free item, you have to say “Outback Bowl” to your server, which seems demeaning, and the offer is only good the day after the game. This much like when Ross was offered a free crab cake appetizer when he was “stood up” on a blind date on an episode of Friends.

This scenario is reminiscent of an episode of *Friends* where Ross received a free crab cake after being abandoned on a blind date.

Hitting the heights: Bank stocks reached milestones Tuesday as their share prices continued to rise. Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase both hit all-time highs, with Goldman recouping all it had lost since the 2007 financial crisis. Bank of America traded in line with its book value for the first time since late 2008; it had traded as low as 15% of book value back in March 2009.
Ambitious move: Japan's SoftBank, which despite its name isn't a bank but a technology and communications conglomerate, made a big step into becoming a serious player in the financial services business Tuesday when it agreed to buy asset manager Fortress Investment Group for $3.3 billion. The acquisition of Fortress, which manages about $70 billion in assets in real estate, credit and private equity, fits Softbank chief Masayoshi Son's "ambitious long-term plans to become one of the world's biggest asset managers, focusing on technology but with a broader platform to raise money and shepherd companies across different sectors," the Wall Street Journal said.

The firm agreed to purchase asset manager Fortress Investment Group for $3.3 billion. According to the Wall Street Journal, this move aligns with CEO Masayoshi Son's vision to build a leading global asset management enterprise. The acquisition of Fortress, which oversees roughly $70 billion in real estate, credit, and private equity assets, is intended to create a broad platform for fundraising and guiding companies in various industries, with a core emphasis on technology.

SAN DIEGO (KUSI) — A man accused in the stabbing death of a plumber at a construction site in Oceanside pleaded not guilty Monday to a murder charge and was ordered held on $3 million bail.
Mikhail Schmidt, 30, of Oceanside, was arrested about 5 p.m. Thursday in the 900 block of The Strand, a few blocks from the under-construction home on Windward Way where the victim's body was found about 12 hours earlier, said Oceanside police Lt. Valencia Saadat.
Related Link: Arrest made in connection to death at Oceanside construction site
Jacob Laughlin Bravo, 37, was discovered in a trailer on the site in a pool of blood. Police said Bravo's body had "obvious signs of traumatic injury,'' but a motive for the slaying remains under investigation.
Schmidt faces 26 years to life in prison if convicted of murder with a knife-use allegation.
A readiness conference is scheduled for April 10 and a preliminary hearing for May 1.
rewrite:
In Oceanside, a man has entered a plea of not guilty to murder charges following the fatal stabbing of a plumber at a construction site. During a Monday court appearance, the judge set bail at $3 million. The suspect, identified as 30-year-old Mikhail Schmidt from Oceanside, was taken into custody last Thursday evening on The Strand, located just blocks from the Windward Way residence under construction where the victim was discovered earlier that day.

The victim, 37-year-old Jacob Laughlin Bravo, was found deceased inside a trailer at the location, having suffered severe traumatic wounds. Law enforcement reports the circumstances leading to the killing are still being examined. If found guilty of murder with the added allegation of using a knife, Schmidt could receive a prison sentence ranging from 26 years to life. Court proceedings are scheduled to continue with a readiness conference on April 10, followed by a preliminary hearing set for May 1.

March 19 (UPI) -- Actor Cynthia Nixon on Monday announced her bid to run for governor of New York, challenging incumbent Gov. Andrew M. Cuomo in the state's Democratic primary.
Nixon, known best for her role as Miranda Hobbes in HBO's Sex and the City, shared a video to Twitter declaring her candidacy and calling out leaders in government for "letting us down."
"Something has to change," she said. "We want our government to work again, on healthcare, ending mass incarceration, fixing our broken subway. We are sick of politicians who care more about headlines and power than they do about us. It can't just be business as usual anymore."
The 51-year-old Nixon is described as "a lifelong New Yorker and progressive activist" on her campaign donations page and if elected would be the first female and the first openly gay mayor of New York.
A Sienna College poll released Monday showed 66 percent of state Democrats prefer the incumbent Cuomo over 19 percent who prefer Nixon.
"With an overall 20-19 percent favorability rating -- 26-16 percent among Democrats -- Cynthia Nixon is far from a household name in New York," Siena College pollster Steven Greenberg said.
Cuomo, who has served two terms as governor, said last week he's "not nervous about whoever runs."
"There'll be people who run. That's called elections, and that's fine," he said.
Two former advisors for New York Mayor Bill de Blasio -- Bill Hyers and Rebecca Katz -- joined Nixon's campaign as advisors and her wife, Christine Marinoni, also recently stepped down from her role in his administration.
rewrite:
On Monday, March 19, Cynthia Nixon, the actress famous for portraying Miranda Hobbes on *Sex and the City*, declared her intention to enter the race for New York governor. She will compete against current Governor Andrew M. Cuomo in the Democratic primary. In a video announcement posted on Twitter, Nixon criticized state leadership for failing its citizens and emphasized the need for a shift in priorities.

She stated that residents are tired of officials who prioritize media attention and their own influence over addressing critical issues. Nixon highlighted urgent needs in healthcare, criminal justice reform, and repairing the city's subway system, arguing that the status quo is no longer acceptable. Her campaign website identifies her as a long-time resident of New York and a dedicated advocate for progressive causes. A victory would make her the state's first female and first openly gay governor.

Recent polling data from Siena College indicates Cuomo currently holds a strong lead among Democratic voters in the state. Pollster Steven Greenberg noted that Nixon remains relatively unknown to many New Yorkers, with a narrowly positive favorability rating. In response to her entry into the race, Governor Cuomo expressed a lack of concern, commenting that electoral challenges are a normal part of the political process.

Nixon's campaign team now includes Bill Hyers and Rebecca Katz, both former aides to New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio. Additionally, her spouse, Christine Marinoni, has recently resigned from a position within the mayor's administration.

Why it matters to you Fans of HBO's Insecure will get even more of the Issa Rae series in season 2, which will consist of 10 episodes instead of eight.
If you are still searching for closure after the ending of season 1 of the HBO series Insecure, you will not get it here. But you can get a glimpse into the new season. Insecure co-creator and lead actress Issa Rae released a teaser trailer for season 2 on Twitter on Wednesday.
The teaser trailer will surely agonize die-hard fans still reeling after season one’s emotional finale. At the end of last season, the relationship between Rae’s character, Issa, and her boyfriend, Lawrence, played by Jay Ellis, seemed to be over. In the teaser trailer, the two can be seen on a couch with a pillow in between them that reads “hella confused.”
Initially, season 2 was reported to consist of eight episodes, just like season one. But IMDB has listed acting credits for 10 episodes. Interestingly, Issa’s former love interest, Lawrence, is only credited with appearing in one episode in the new season — and not until episode 4. The first two episodes of the new season are entitled Hella Great and Hella Questions, respectively. With names like that, it may be safe to say we are in for an emotional roller coaster to start the new season.
When you watch the new season, it may not look the same as last season, thanks to all the new faces. Bosch‘s Spencer Garret appears as John Merril in six episodes this season, including the season premiere. Sarunas J. Jackson is another newcomer to the show. He’ll play the role of Alejandro ‘Dro’ Peña in six episodes. Jackson may be best known for his voice-over work on NBA 2K as Frequency Vibrations, the player character in NBA 2K16’s MyCAREER mode.
Insecure may have inspired a lot of relationship tweets last fall, but it was not a ratings hit. Season 1 averaged roughly 413,000 viewers per episode — and only one episode from its first season topped 500,000 viewers. Even without a Silicon Valley audience size, Rae still garnered a Golden Globe nomination for best actress in a comedy series.
Insecure returns to HBO at 10:30 p.m. ET on July 23.
rewrite:

Those hoping for definitive answers following the ambiguous conclusion of season one will need to wait, though a new preview provides some early clues. Series co-creator and star Issa Rae shared a brief teaser for the new season on Twitter, which will likely intensify the anticipation for fans still processing the prior season's finale.

The first season concluded with the apparent breakup between Rae's character, Issa, and her boyfriend Lawrence, portrayed by Jay Ellis. The new trailer hints at their ongoing complicated dynamic, showing them seated distantly on a couch with a pillow labeled "hella confused" separating them. While early reports suggested season two would mirror the first with eight installments, industry databases now indicate ten episodes. Notably, Lawrence is currently listed for only a single appearance late in the season, specifically in episode four. The titles of the opening episodes, "Hella Great" and "Hella Questions," suggest an emotionally turbulent start is in store.

The cast will see several additions, introducing new characters to the show's world. Spencer Garrett, known from *Bosch*, joins as John Merril for a six-episode arc beginning with the premiere. Another new face is Sarunas J. Jackson, set to play Alejandro 'Dro' Peña across six episodes. Jackson is perhaps recognized for his voice acting in the video game *NBA 2K16*, where he voiced the MyCAREER protagonist, Frequency Vibrations.

Despite not achieving blockbuster ratings—season one averaged about 413,000 viewers per episode, with only one surpassing half a million—the series sparked considerable online discussion about modern relationships. Its cultural impact was acknowledged when Issa Rae earned a Golden Globe nomination for Best Actress in a Comedy Series. *Insecure* makes its return to HBO on Sunday, July 23, at 10:30 p.m. Eastern Time.

SHANGHAI China's economic planner on Thursday approved China Eastern Airlines' (600115.SS)(0670.HK) 13.2-billion-yuan (1.54 billion pounds) plan for a base at an expansive new airport in Beijing that could eventually be the world's largest, when completed.
The National Development and Reform Commission said in a statement on its website that the base will cover 1.17 million square meters, and 30 percent of the investment, or 3.96 billion yuan, will be funded by China Eastern.
The remaining 92.4 billion yuan will be financed using domestic bank loans, the statement added.
China plans to complete the first phase by 2019, and will be able to serve 45 million passengers a year with four runways on the first opening. Two more phases would push the capacity to an annual count of 100 million passengers.
That would put the airport as the world's largest in surface area, roughly in line with Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, the world's busiest by number of annual passengers.
Upon completion, rival state carrier, China Southern Airlines Co Ltd (600029.SS), will also relocate to the new airport from the existing Beijing Capital International Airport, the airport project managers told reporters last year.
They said China Eastern and China Southern will handle 40 percent of the new airport's footfalls.
(Reporting by Brenda Goh; Editing by Sherry Jacob-Phillips)
rewrite:
China's National Development and Reform Commission gave its approval on Thursday for a major investment by China Eastern Airlines. The carrier will spend 13.2 billion yuan, equivalent to 1.54 billion British pounds, to establish a facility at Beijing's forthcoming aviation hub, which is designed to become one of the globe's biggest airports.

According to the commission's online announcement, the planned base will occupy 1.17 million square meters. China Eastern is providing 3.96 billion yuan, covering thirty percent of the total cost. The balance, amounting to 9.24 billion yuan, will be secured through loans from banks within the country.

The initial stage of the airport is scheduled for operation by 2019. It will feature four runways and is projected to accommodate 45 million travelers annually at the start. Following two subsequent expansion phases, passenger capacity is expected to rise to 100 million each year. This scale would make it the world's most extensive airport by physical size, comparable in passenger volume to the currently busiest global hub, Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport.

Airport officials stated last year that China Southern Airlines, another major state-owned carrier, will also move its operations from the current Beijing Capital International Airport to the new site. Together, China Eastern and China Southern are anticipated to manage forty percent of the new airport's passenger traffic.

rewrite:
On February 2nd, Reuters reported on Sprint Corp's financial results for the third quarter of its 2017 fiscal year. The telecommunications company announced its strongest retail customer growth in close to three years and revised its financial projections upward.

Sprint increased its full-year forecast for adjusted free cash flow, moving from an expectation of approximately breaking even to a new range of $500 million to $700 million. The company also raised its 2017 operating income outlook to between $2.5 billion and $2.7 billion. For adjusted EBITDA, Sprint anticipates a result near the middle of its previously stated range of $10.8 billion to $11.2 billion. Capital spending for the year, excluding devices leased indirectly, is now projected to be at the bottom of the $3.5 billion to $4 billion guidance.

For the quarter, basic earnings per share were $1.79, while diluted EPS stood at $1.76. Total operating revenue reached $8.239 billion, a decline from $8.549 billion in the prior-year period. Net income was significantly boosted by a roughly $7.1 billion benefit related to recent tax legislation. The company also noted approximately $100 million in non-recurring charges stemming from hurricane impacts and other items.

Key operational metrics showed mixed performance. The rate of postpaid customer attrition was 1.80%, compared to 1.67% previously. However, Sprint added 256,000 net new postpaid subscribers, though this was fewer than the 405,000 added a year ago. Prepaid customer turnover improved to 4.63% from 5.74%, resulting in 63,000 net additions versus a loss of 460,000 in the same quarter last year. The total number of wireless connections at the end of the quarter was 54.6 million.

Average revenue per user (ARPU) declined for postpaid services to $45.13 but increased for prepaid to $37.46. The company reported reducing its combined cost of services and sales, general, and administrative expenses by about $260 million year-over-year for the quarter, bringing the total reduction for the fiscal year to over $1 billion.

input: With having out a Core i7 "Broadwell" ThinkPad X1 Carbon laptop for the MoCA 2.0 network tests , I decided to run some end-of-year graphics tests on this Core i7 5600U system with OpenGL and Vulkan.The last time I had out this particular system with i7-5600 CPU sporting HD Graphics 5500, the Vulkan experience wasn't really working out at that time. But a half-year has passed and now it's in better shape for this low-power ultrabook.I ran tests with the Linux 4.10 and Mesa 13.1-devel Git stacks atop Ubuntu 16.10 x86_64.The HD Graphics 5500 on this i7-5600U ultrabook aren't the fastest, but at 800 x 600 for Dota 2 we see the performance is about the same between the Vulkan and OpenGL drivers.Still close at 1280 x 1024.The performance is rather low, but those are the numbers for those always craving fresh Intel graphics results.Unfortunately no Talos Principle results for Vulkan as the game was hanging in this configuration.Still working on some other fresh tests with Iris Pro Graphics as well as the Skylake HD Graphics that provide for more playable Linux OpenGL/Vulkan gaming experience. Great to see overall though how the Intel "ANV" Vulkan driver has matured this year and is quite a competent driver while the i965 Mesa driver has also advanced in 2016 to supporting OpenGL 4.5, performance optimizations, and other improved functionality.
rewrite:
While conducting MoCA 2.0 network evaluations with a Core i7 "Broadwell" ThinkPad X1 Carbon, I also performed some year-end graphics assessments on this same i7 5600U device using OpenGL and Vulkan. Previously, when testing this specific configuration with the i7-5600 processor and its HD Graphics 5500, Vulkan support was not fully functional. However, after six months, this energy-efficient ultrabook is now better equipped for such testing.

The benchmarks were executed on an Ubuntu 16.10 x86_64 system running Linux kernel 4.10 and the developmental Mesa 13.1 Git code. The integrated HD Graphics 5500 in this ultrabook is not high-performance hardware. At a resolution of 800 by 600 pixels in Dota 2, the Vulkan and OpenGL drivers delivered nearly identical frame rates, a trend that continued at 1280 by 1024. The achieved performance is modest, but these figures will interest those keen on the latest Intel graphics data.

Regrettably, Vulkan testing for The Talos Principle was not possible due to system freezes. Additional examinations are underway with Iris Pro and Skylake HD Graphics, which offer a more viable gaming experience on Linux with these APIs. It is encouraging to observe the significant progress of the Intel "ANV" Vulkan driver over the past year, which has become quite capable. Simultaneously, the i965 Mesa driver saw major advances in 2016, gaining OpenGL 4.5 compliance, performance enhancements, and expanded features.

Former New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg has vowed to write a $4.5 million check to the United Nations body that oversees climate change negotiations to make up the shortfall in the agency's budget caused by U.S. funding cuts.
President Donald Trump last year formally announced the U.S. would pull out of the Paris climate accord deal, stating that it was not fair. Congress also cut funding for the Bonn, Germany-based UNFCCC from $7.5 million in previous years to $3 million this year.
"America made a commitment and as an American if the government's not going to do it we all have responsibility. I'm able to do it,” Bloomberg told CBS News' "Face the Nation" on Sunday. “So, yes, I'm going to send them a check for the monies that America had promised to the organization as though they got it from the federal government."
Bloomberg has long championed the fight against global warming.
“America is part of the problem. America is a big part of the solution and we should go in and help the world stop a potential disaster," Bloomberg added.
Bloomberg's charitable foundation linked the donation to the billionaire philanthropist's effort, with California Gov. Jerry Brown, to show that the United States remains committed to the Paris climate accord despite Trump's plan to withdraw from the agreement.
In a statement late Sunday, Bloomberg Philanthropies said further donations would be made if the U.S. fails to pay its share of the budget in 2019.
rewrite:
Former New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg has committed to personally providing $4.5 million to cover a budgetary gap at the United Nations' climate change secretariat, resulting from a reduction in U.S. financial support. This follows the Trump administration's declared intention to exit the Paris climate agreement, citing unfair terms, and a congressional decision to lower funding for the UNFCCC from $7.5 million to $3 million for the current year.

In a television interview, Bloomberg stated that since the U.S. government is not fulfilling its pledge, he feels a personal duty to act. He plans to contribute the amount originally promised by the nation, effectively substituting for the missing federal funds. A long-time advocate for climate action, he emphasized that while the United States contributes significantly to the problem, it also holds a key role in finding solutions and preventing a global crisis.

His philanthropic organization connected this gift to a broader initiative, undertaken with California's governor, to demonstrate continued American dedication to the Paris accord's objectives. The foundation also indicated that additional private contributions may follow if the federal government does not restore its scheduled funding in the coming year.

NEW YORK — Fox News said Friday that the network’s legal counsel, who is named in lawsuits relating to the late former CEO Roger Ailes’ regime, is taking a “voluntary leave.”
Fox offered no additional details Friday on the departure of Dianne Brandi, including whether she is being paid or if she will return. She was a powerful leader at Fox under Ailes, who was forced out last year because of harassment charges.
Brandi has been named in pending lawsuits by former and current employees who alleged she did not act on complaints of harassment or discrimination against them by executives, and even retaliated against people who made charges. Brandi has denied the accusations.
She was named in cases filed by former on-air contributors Julie Roginsky and Andrea Tantaros, who both had complained about harassment by Ailes. She was also a part of a racial discrimination case involving several employees and a since-fired financial executive at Fox.
Douglas Wigdor, a lawyer for several of the people with cases against Fox, called the announcement of Brandi’s leave “long overdue.” He said the real question is whether Fox will apologize to the people he represents.
Former Fox co-president, Bill Shine, left the network in May after also being named in lawsuits for failing to correct behaviour at the network. Popular personality Bill O’Reilly was ousted this spring when it was revealed Fox had paid five women a total of $13 million to keep quiet about harassment allegations.

The network did not elaborate on the circumstances of Dianne Brandi’s exit, such as her compensation during this period or potential reinstatement. Brandi held significant influence during Ailes’ leadership, which ended last year following harassment claims.

Pending lawsuits from present and past staff members cite Brandi, accusing her of ignoring reports of harassment or bias by higher-ups and of taking punitive actions against those who voiced concerns. Brandi has refuted these allegations.

Earlier this year, prominent host Bill O’Reilly was removed after disclosures that the network paid five women a combined $13 million to settle harassment claims.

The UFC is in jeopardy of losing its UFC 222 main event, on March 3 in Las Vegas.
According to sources, featherweight champion Max Holloway has suffered an injury that will prevent him from defending his title against Frankie Edgar.
The UFC has not officially pulled Holloway from the event, but is expected to do so shortly. The promotion is already in the process of exploring other options for its main event.
This will mark the second time a title fight between Holloway and Edgar has fallen through. The two were supposed to meet at UFC 218 on Dec. 2 in Detroit, but Edgar was forced out with an injury.
Fighting out of Waianae, Hawaii, Holloway (19-3) is riding a 12-fight win streak. ESPN ranks Holloway the No. 5 pound-for-pound fighter in the world.
Edgar (22-5) has not fought since May 2017.
UFC 222 takes place at T-Mobile Arena.

resorted to attacking his 11-year-old son Barron.
Now, a petition has gone viral demanding that Barron and his mother Melania Trump move to the White House and leave New

wraps up his schooling.
“The U.S. taxpayer is paying an exorbitant amount of money to protect the First Lady in Trump Tower, located in New York City,”
the petition reads. “As to help relieve the national debt, this expense yields no positive results for the nation and should be cut
from being funded.”

“U.S. House of Representatives: Make Melania Trump stay in the White House or pay for expenses herself,” one petitioner signer

rewrite:
In recent months, critics of Donald Trump have reached new depths in their attempts to undermine him, extending their attacks to include his young son, Barron. A widely circulated petition is now calling for Barron and First Lady Melania Trump to relocate promptly from New York City to the White House. The Trump family has already stated they plan to move to Washington, D.C., this June, following the completion of Barron's school year.

The petition argues that protecting Melania Trump at Trump Tower in New York imposes a significant and unnecessary financial burden on taxpayers, diverting funds that could help reduce the national debt. It claims this security expenditure provides no tangible benefit to the country and should be eliminated.

So far, over 400,000 people have endorsed the appeal. One supporter urged the U.S. House of Representatives to require Melania Trump to either reside in the White House or cover her own security costs. Another commented that taxpayers should not be responsible for expenses if she opts to live separately from the president. This raises the question: is such a demand completely unreasonable?

Boston Tea Party is believed to be the first coffee chain in the UK to implement a complete ban on single-use plastic cups.
The independently-owned company, which has 21 branches across the Midlands and the South West, said the ban will come into effect on 1st June 2018.
Customers will be able to bring their own reusable cups, buy cups at the cafes at a subsidised rate or grab a loan cup, for which a deposit would have to be paid which would be refunded upon return to any of its outlets.
The coffee chain currently gives away around 340,000 takeaway hot drinks a year. Customers were previously offered a 25p discount on drinks if they used their own cup but only 2.8% of people took up the offer.
In the UK, only one in 400 of the estimated 2.5 billion plastic coated coffee cups are said to be recycled.
Sam Roberts, Owner and MD of Boston Tea Party said: “Lots of coffee chains are making pledges about how they plan to tackle cup waste in the future. But theirs is a future which is too far away. We need to stop right now.”
rewrite:
Boston Tea Party is considered the inaugural coffee shop chain in the United Kingdom to fully prohibit disposable plastic cups. This independent business, operating 21 locations throughout the Midlands and South West, announced the policy will start on June 1, 2018. Patrons have several options: they may bring their own reusable containers, purchase one at a reduced price in-store, or borrow a cup by paying a deposit that is fully refunded when the cup is brought back to any branch.

Annually, the chain serves approximately 340,000 hot beverages for takeaway. Previously, a 25-pence discount was provided to customers using personal cups, yet only 2.8% accepted this incentive. Across the UK, it is estimated that just one out of every 400 plastic-lined coffee cups—among roughly 2.5 billion used—actually gets recycled.

Sam Roberts, the Owner and Managing Director, stated: “Many coffee companies are announcing commitments to address cup waste at a later date. However, their timelines are distant. We must take action immediately.”

WASHINGTON, United States – The United States on Sunday sharply condemned a North Korean plan to test-fire an intercontinental ballistic missile and warned Pyongyang against “provocative actions.”
The toughly worded US statement called on “all states” to show the North that any unlawful actions would have “consequences.”
It was issued by the Pentagon at a sensitive time – just weeks before President Barack Obama is due to hand power over to his successor, Donald Trump.
ADVERTISEMENT
The statement came hours after Kim Jong-un, the North Korean leader, said his country was close to testing such a missile, which would be capable of reaching American shores.
“We are in the final stages of test-launching the intercontinental ballistic missile,” Kim said in a televised New Year’s speech, pointing to a string of nuclear and missile tests last year.
He said Pyongyang was now a “military power of the East that cannot be touched by even the strongest enemy.”
The Pentagon statement noted that “multiple UN Security Council resolutions explicitly prohibit North Korea’s launches using ballistic missile technology.”
It urged Pyongyang to “refrain from provocative actions and inflammatory rhetoric that threaten international peace and stability.”
The statement reaffirmed Washington’s “ironclad commitment” to defend its allies, using “the full spectrum of US extended deterrence capabilities.”
Pyongyang has never successfully test-fired an intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM), and analysts are divided over how close it is to doing so.
But all agree it has made enormous strides in that direction since Kim took over as leader from his father Kim Jong-Il, who died in December 2011.
rewrite:
On Sunday, the United States issued a firm condemnation of North Korea's announced intention to conduct an intercontinental ballistic missile test, cautioning the regime in Pyongyang to avoid any escalatory behavior. This strongly phrased warning from American officials urged the international community to demonstrate that such illegal endeavors would result in significant repercussions. The Pentagon released the declaration during a delicate political period, mere weeks before the scheduled transition from President Barack Obama to President-elect Donald Trump.

This response followed a New Year's address by North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, televised earlier that day, in which he declared his nation was nearing the final phase of preparations for an ICBM launch. Kim referenced a series of prior nuclear and missile tests, asserting that North Korea had become an invulnerable military force in the region. The U.S. Department of Defense emphasized that any launch employing ballistic missile technology directly violates several United Nations Security Council resolutions. It called upon North Korea to cease actions and statements that endanger global security and provoke instability.

The American statement further reinforced the unwavering pledge to protect its allies, promising to utilize the complete range of its defensive assets. While analysts hold differing opinions on how imminent a successful ICBM test might be, they concur that Pyongyang has never accomplished such a launch. Nevertheless, there is broad agreement that the country has made substantial advances in its missile program under Kim Jong-un's leadership since he assumed power following his father's death.

rewrite:
A prominent conservative cleric from Moscow, Archpriest Vsevolod Chaplin, has publicly advocated for Russia to restore its monarchical system, proposing that President Vladimir Putin be crowned as emperor. An alternative, he suggested, would be to return the Romanov dynasty to power, a century after its overthrow in 1917.

Speaking at an event for his latest publication, the archpriest expressed his view that Russia inherently possesses a monarchical spirit. He argued that the absence of a formal crown does not negate this, stating the institution could be revived with Putin at its helm. Other possibilities, according to him, include installing a Romanov descendant or an elected individual as sovereign.

He further elaborated that a deep-seated belief persists in Russia that the nation requires a tsar to lead it. However, this ruler, he clarified, must govern with counsel from the populace, emphasizing the critical role of the people. To facilitate this change, he called for constitutional revisions to permit a monarchy.

The 48-year-old priest, who is celibate, also holds controversial social views. He opposes including contraception in school curricula and previously advocated lowering the marriage age to 14 for girls and 16 for boys, without requiring parental consent. He believes women should ideally bear multiple children before age 20 and postpone professional ambitions until their forties, after raising a family.

Additionally, he asserts that individuals who have abortions, commit adultery, or are found guilty of corruption should face universal condemnation and, in certain instances, forfeit their property rights. He urges large, "virtuous" families to depart from major urban centers, which he deems morally corrupt, and resettle in government-provided rural communities. Among his more provocative remarks, he has stated that such families belong in these designated agricultural settlements.

DOHA, April 5 Qatar Petroleum (QP) and ExxonMobil will start drilling for oil and gas off the southern coast of Cyprus in 2018, the Qatari firm said after signing an exploration and production sharing contract with the Mediterranean island.
Exploring the Mediterranean's Levant Basin has become more attractive since Eni discovered Egypt's offshore Zohr field in 2015, the biggest gas field in the Mediterranean and estimated to contain 850 billion cubic metres of gas.
State-owned Qatar Petroleum and ExxonMobil were among bidders last year for a contract for Cyprus's offshore Block 10.
"A 3D seismic survey is already underway, as the consortium partners prepare to begin exploration drilling in 2018," QP said in a statement.
To maintain its dominance over competitors in the United States and Australia, QP is cutting costs at its domestic operations and seeking to expand overseas through joint ventures with international oil firms, QP said in February.
(Reporting by Tom Finn; Editing by Edmund Blair)
rewrite:
In early April, Qatar Petroleum announced that together with ExxonMobil, it will commence oil and gas exploration drilling in 2018 in waters south of Cyprus. This follows the signing of an exploration and production agreement with Cyprus for its offshore Block 10, for which both companies bid last year.

Interest in the Levant Basin region of the Mediterranean has grown significantly since Eni's 2015 discovery of the massive Zohr gas field off Egypt, which holds an estimated 850 billion cubic meters of natural gas.

According to a statement, a 3D seismic survey is currently in progress as the partnership prepares for the upcoming drilling campaign. Qatar Petroleum noted in February that it is pursuing cost reductions at home and international expansion through joint ventures to strengthen its competitive position against rivals in nations like the United States and Australia.

China will further tighten controls on individuals’ foreign currency purchases to try to curb massive capital flight from the country as the yuan falls sharply against the dollar.
Individuals wishing to convert yuan to foreign currencies will now have to provide more detailed information to their bank, including an explanation of the funds concerned in addition to their identity papers, said the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), according to AFP.
Each year individuals can convert up to the equivalent of $50,000, a maximum sum that will not change, it said on its website.
The tighter controls are aimed at preventing attempts to circumvent this quota.
The idea is to “combat illegal transactions, money-laundering and clandestine banks,” the agency said, vowing to multiply random checks and toughen its sanctions.
Banks must verify the authenticity of the information provided. In addition, from July, financial institutions will have to report to the central bank any international transfer exceeding 200,000 yuan ($28,800), in order to fight laundering, the central bank announced.
The tighter controls are part of an array of measures taken by the government to curb huge capital outflows.
The equivalent of about $1 trillion was transferred out of China in 2015 and another $690 billion in the first 10 months of 2016, according to Bloomberg Intelligence estimates.
Slower growth in China, the weakness of the yuan and the recent rise in US interest rates are encouraging savers to invest their money in other currencies.
The yuan is at its lowest in eight years against the dollar and the outflows are putting further pressure on the currency.
Authorities are trying to support it by buying yuan, drawing on China’s foreign exchange reserves, which fell by nearly $70 billion in November.
rewrite:
In an effort to stem significant capital outflows and stabilize the declining yuan, China is implementing stricter regulations on how citizens can obtain foreign currency. The State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) has announced that individuals seeking to exchange yuan must now submit more comprehensive documentation to their banks. This goes beyond standard identification to include a specific rationale for the requested conversion. The annual personal limit remains unchanged at a value of $50,000.

These enhanced measures are designed to close loopholes that might allow this quota to be bypassed. SAFE stated the goal is to counter unlawful activities such as money laundering and the operations of underground banking networks, pledging to increase spot inspections and impose harsher penalties. Banks are now responsible for confirming the accuracy of the information submitted by clients.

Separately, the central bank has declared that starting in July, any cross-border money transfer exceeding 200,000 yuan (approximately $28,800) must be reported by financial institutions. This is another step intended to prevent illicit financial flows.

These actions form part of a broader governmental strategy to address massive capital flight. Estimates indicate approximately one trillion dollars left China in 2015, followed by around $690 billion in the initial ten months of 2016. The exodus is driven by several factors, including China's economic deceleration, the yuan's depreciation, and comparatively higher U.S. interest rates, which incentivize moving savings abroad.

The currency recently hit an eight-year low against the dollar, and continued outflows exacerbate this downward pressure. To bolster the yuan, authorities are intervening in markets by purchasing it, utilizing the nation's foreign exchange reserves. These reserves saw a reduction of nearly $70 billion in November alone as a result of these support operations.

COLUMBUS, Ohio — The San Jose Sharks took advantage of its power plays and a Columbus scoring slump to get a needed win.
Kevin Labanc and Logan Couture each had a goal and an assist, and Martin Jones stopped 28 shots to lift the Sharks to a 3-1 win over the Blue Jackets on Friday night, snapping a four-game skid.
The Sharks' first two goals came on power plays, with Labanc getting a wide-open look at the net with a 5-on-3 advantage in the second period. Marc-Edouard Vlasic also scored for San Jose.
"The power play has been the key for us for the last 2 1/2 months," San Jose coach Peter DeBoer said. "The one thing we have is a lot of options there. We have a lot of guys who are comfortable on the power play, and they're playing with a lot of confidence right now."
Sergei Bobrovsky had 25 saves for the Blue Jackets, who have lost two in a row and five of their last seven. Boone Jenner had the lone goal as Columbus continues to have trouble finding the back of the net. The team has scored two or fewer goals in regulation in 11 of the last 12 games.
"We just have no rhythm offensively," Blue Jackets coach John Tortorella said.
Couture tallied 5:07 into the game with the Blue Jackets' Matt Calvert in the penalty box for tripping. Couture got his 22nd goal of the season when he snapped a shot from the high slot over the glove of Bobrovsky, who was shielded by 6-foot-5 defenceman Brent Burns.
Jenner tied the score 4:30 into the second period with his fifth goal of the season and first in 13 games when he rifled a shot off the bar from the top of the left circle.
Columbus was victimized on another power play at 10:20 in the second when Labanc scored from 15 feet out while Seth Jones and Nick Foligno served penalties. Tororella was so angry that he benched Foligno, the Blue Jackets' captain, for the rest of the period and much of the third.
Tortorella said the punishment didn't result from just the untimely penalty. "It was a few other things," he said, but declined to discuss it any further.
rewrite:
In Columbus, Ohio, the San Jose Sharks secured a crucial victory by capitalizing on their special teams opportunities and exploiting the Blue Jackets' ongoing offensive struggles. Kevin Labanc and Logan Couture both contributed a goal and an assist, while goaltender Martin Jones turned aside 28 shots, ending the Sharks' four-game losing streak with a 3-1 decision on Friday. Marc-Edouard Vlasic also found the net for San Jose.

The Sharks built their lead with two power-play goals. Labanc capitalized on a two-man advantage in the second period, firing into an undefended net. Head coach Peter DeBoer highlighted the team's consistent strength on the power play, noting, "It has been our driving force for much of the season. We're fortunate to have numerous skilled players who excel in those situations, and they are executing with great assurance."

For Columbus, Sergei Bobrovsky made 25 saves, but the team dropped its second consecutive game and fifth out of the last seven. Boone Jenner provided the sole offense, underscoring a persistent scoring drought; the Blue Jackets have managed two or fewer goals in eleven of their past twelve contests. "We have absolutely no flow or consistency in our attack," lamented coach John Tortorella.

Couture opened the scoring early in the first period during a Columbus penalty, beating Bobrovsky with a precise shot from the high slot for his 22nd goal of the year. Jenner equalized in the second frame, ending a personal 13-game goalless streak with a sharp shot from the left circle.

The Sharks reclaimed the lead on another power play later in the second period when Labanc scored from close range. Tortorella reacted strongly to the penalty that led to this goal, benching captain Nick Foligno for the remainder of the period and much of the third. The coach indicated the disciplinary action stemmed from multiple issues, not solely the ill-timed infraction, but chose not to elaborate further.

TRIPOLI May 3 Rival Libyan camps issued separate statements on Wednesday promising to calm tensions in southern Libya and fight terrorism, but offering no shared way forward for a political deal to unify the North African country.
The statements came a day after intense diplomatic pressure resulted in a meeting in Abu Dhabi between eastern-based commander Khalifa Haftar and the head of the U.N.-backed government in Tripoli, Fayez Seraj.
Haftar is the key figure for eastern factions that, frustrating international efforts to end Libya's conflict, spurned Seraj's Government of National Accord (GNA) after it was established in the capital last year.
There was no mention in the statement from Seraj of plans reported by pro-Haftar media on Tuesday to restructure the unity government's leadership and hold fresh elections next year.
A source close to the GNA leadership said the two sides had initially tried to agree on a joint statement before deciding to issue separate declarations.
Conflicting accounts of initial agreements and leaks of documents neither side signed have in the past confused international mediation and negotiations to end the conflict in Libya, which fell into factional fighting in the years after a 2011 civil war ousted Muammar Gaddafi. (Reporting by Aidan Lewis in Tunis, Ahmed Elumami in Tripoli and Ayman al-Warfalli in Benghazi; editing by Patrick Markey and John Stonestreet)
rewrite:
On Wednesday, opposing factions in Libya each released declarations pledging to reduce hostilities in the nation's southern region and to combat extremist groups. However, these separate pronouncements failed to outline any mutual strategy for a political settlement that would reunify the divided state.

This development followed a high-level meeting in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday between Khalifa Haftar, the military commander controlling eastern Libya, and Fayez Seraj, who leads the United Nations-supported administration in Tripoli. The talks occurred under significant international pressure. Haftar, whose eastern alliance has rejected the U.N.-backed Government of National Accord (GNA) since its formation in Tripoli last year, remains a central and disruptive figure in the prolonged conflict.

The statement from Seraj's side did not address reports from media supporting Haftar, which had cited plans to reorganize the unity government's leadership and conduct new elections in the coming year. An official close to the GNA indicated that efforts to produce a unified communiqué were abandoned in favor of individual releases.

Historically, such disjointed communications, along with disputed details of preliminary accords and the circulation of unsigned documents, have complicated international peace efforts. Libya has been mired in factional violence since the 2011 civil war that toppled Muammar Gaddafi, with numerous attempts at mediation struggling to gain traction.
