DAYTON, Ohio (WDTN) – Police in Dayton were called to the 2700 block of Wayne Avenue Sunday after a man said he was robbed.
The incident happened around 6:30 pm Sunday when a man was trying to sell a sweatshirt using a popular phone app.
When officers arrived they met with a man who said he was there to meet with a man to sell his “Peace Skateboard” sweatshirt using the app “Let Go”. The victim told police the person he was there to meet identified himself as Glen Smith, who claimed to be 15-years-old and could not drive.
According to a police report on the incident, when the victim arrived at the agreed meeting place, Smith was not there. Through several text messages, the victim agreed to meet Smith in another location.
When the victim arrived at the intersection of Maplewood Avenue and Kathleen Avenue, he met with Glen and a third person. The men talked for about an hour when Smith claimed he had lost his money. The victim then told Glen he had other things to do and had to leave.
According to the report, the man who identified himself as Glen Smith gave the sweatshirt to his masked friend who then ran off. When the victim confronted “Glen” about it Gen pulled a silver, semi-automatic handgun from his waistband and fired one shot into the air.
The victim then ran away and told police he heard a second shot fired.
No arrests have been made in this case.
rewrite:
In Dayton, Ohio, law enforcement responded to a call on Sunday evening in the 2700 block of Wayne Avenue regarding a reported theft. The event occurred at approximately 6:30 p.m. when an individual arranged to sell a hooded shirt through a widely-used mobile application.

Upon arrival, officers spoke with a man who explained he had planned to meet a buyer to sell a "Peace Skateboard" sweatshirt via the "Let Go" app. The seller informed police that the prospective buyer identified himself as Glen Smith, stating he was 15 years old and unable to drive. Official documents indicate the victim went to the initial meeting spot, but Smith was not present. After exchanging texts, they decided on a different location.

The meeting eventually took place at the corner of Maplewood and Kathleen Avenues, where the seller encountered Smith and another individual. After conversing for roughly an hour, Smith asserted he had misplaced his money. The seller then stated he needed to depart due to other obligations.

As detailed in the report, the person calling himself Glen Smith handed the sweatshirt to a companion whose face was covered, who then fled. When the victim questioned Smith, Smith drew a silver semi-automatic pistol from his waistband and discharged a round skyward. The victim escaped and reported hearing another gunshot as he left.

No suspects have been apprehended in connection with this incident.

Jenna Dewan Tatum is stepping up to the spotlight in Fox’s musical drama pilot Mixtape, our sister site Deadline reports.
From former Smash showrunner Josh Safran, Mixtape follows a diverse group of modern-day Angelenos, focusing on “the music that defines who they are.” Dewan Tatum will star as Joanna, described as a “young professional with everything always under control. She’s the most rational person she knows. And yet she’s a little guarded, as if always prepared for the worst.”
Currently playing host on NBC’s World of Dance, Dewan Tatum has previously held down roles on Lifetime’s Witches of East End and NBC’s The Playboy Club.
Megan Ferguson (Grace and Frankie) and Jahmil French (Degrassi: The Next Generation) have also been cast in the pilot. That trio joins previously announced cast members Callie Hernandez (La La Land) and Madeleine Stowe (Revenge).
Your thoughts on Mixtape’s latest additions? The pilot in general? Drop ’em in a comment below.

Dewan Tatum will portray Joanna, a character outlined as a composed and highly logical young career woman who nonetheless maintains a cautious demeanor, seemingly bracing for potential disappointment.

Dewan Tatum, currently the presenter for NBC's *World of Dance*, has prior acting credits including *Witches of East End* and *The Playboy Club*. She is joined in the pilot by Megan Ferguson of *Grace and Frankie* and Jahmil French from *Degrassi: The Next Generation*. A woman walks past a branch of The Co-operative Bank in London, Britain.
London: Britain’s Cooperative Bank, rescued from the brink of collapse by a group of hedge funds in 2013, has put itself up for sale as it seeks to build up its capital to meet regulatory requirements.
The bank said on Monday that it had made considerable progress implementing its turnaround plan, cutting its cost base by a fifth since 2014.
But it still expects to make a “significant loss” for last year and said that building up capital has proved difficult given low interest rates.
“As a result, and having concluded its annual planning review, the board is today commencing a sale process, inviting offers for all of the issued ordinary share capital in the bank,” the bank said.
The Bank of England’s Prudential Regulation Authority, which regulates Cooperative Bank, said it welcomed the measures announced on Monday.
“We will continue to assess the bank’s progress in building greater financial resilience over the coming months,” the PRA said in a statement.
The Cooperative Bank, which has four million customers, said it was also considering ways to raise equity capital from existing and new capital providers, and a potential “liability management exercise” of its outstanding public debt.
Last month, the bank said it expected its core capital ratio to fall below 10 per cent, falling short of regulatory requirements.
The bank’s immediate issue is the repayment of £400 million (Dh1.8 billion) worth of bonds that mature in September.
Co-op Bank nearly folded in 2013 with a £1.5 billion hole in its capital after losses from problem real estate loans.
The bank was rescued by bondholders, including hedge funds, mainly from the United States, who bet that rising interest rates and a cost-cutting turnaround plan would improve the bank’s fortunes and make them a return on their investment.

Despite this progress, it anticipates posting a considerable deficit for the previous year. It noted that accumulating the necessary capital has been challenging in a climate of persistently low interest rates. Consequently, following its yearly strategic assessment, the board has initiated a formal auction, soliciting bids for the entirety of its common shares.

The Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) of the Bank of England, the bank's supervisor, expressed support for the announced actions. In a released statement, the PRA indicated it would monitor the bank's efforts to enhance its financial stability in the months ahead.

Serving four million clients, The Cooperative Bank is also examining options to secure equity financing from current and prospective investors. Additionally, it is contemplating a possible restructuring of its existing public debt. The bank's severe difficulties originated in 2013, with a capital shortfall of £1.5 billion stemming from bad property loans. Its rescue was orchestrated by bondholders, primarily U.S.-based hedge funds, who speculated that increasing interest rates and a stringent efficiency program would restore the bank's profitability and yield a gain on their stake.

There’s all kinds of threats flying around these days — North Korea threatening Guam, China threatening to cut off trade to North Korea, and Donald Trump threatening pretty much everyone. Now you can add a new ultimatum to the list, this one from Nicolás Maduro Guerra, the son of the Venezuelan president. He didn’t take kindly to Trump’s pronouncement that he would use military force in Venezuela if necessary, and now Guerra says not only would he retaliate if that came to pass, that retaliation would come in the form of actually taking the White House by force.
“If the unlikely event of defiling the homeland came to pass, the rifles would arrive in New York, ” Guerra announced to Venezuelan state media. “Mr. Trump, we would arrive and take the White House.”
Ignoring for a moment that the White House is not in New York, this is Guerra’s comeback to Trump’s recent comment that “Venezuela is not very far away and the people are suffering, and they are dying. We have many options for Venezuela, including a possible military option if necessary.”
That was a response after Maduro’s recent dismissal of Venezuelan parliament and replacement with his own Constituent Assembly. At least for now, Venezuela’s military is busy keeping the peace in Caracas, where protests have broken out amongst Venezuelans tired of food shortages, worthless currency, the not-so-mysterious disappearance of their fellow citizens, and general chaos.
Guerra isn’t the only Venezuelan to respond to Trump’s threat, though. Venezuelan Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino said it would be a “crazy act” if Trump actually tried it. Not that it would it be the first time the U.S. involved itself in Venezuela’s political woes or the governments of Latin American nations. None of those contras have yet resulted in Venezuelans storming the White House, but as always, these are complicated situations with one very uncomplicated U.S. president in charge.
(Via CNN)
rewrite:
In the current climate, numerous dangers are being voiced globally. These include warnings from North Korea aimed at Guam, China's cautions about severing commercial ties with North Korea, and a variety of threats from U.S. President Donald Trump directed at numerous parties. A fresh provocation has now emerged from Nicolás Maduro Guerra, the son of Venezuela's leader. He issued a stark warning following Trump's statement that he would consider deploying the U.S. military to Venezuela. Guerra declared that any such intervention would be met with a counterstrike, specifically an armed assault to seize the U.S. presidential residence.

Addressing Venezuelan state-controlled media, Guerra stated, "Should the sacred soil of our nation ever be violated, our soldiers would land in New York. We would come for the White House, Mr. Trump." This retort, aside from its geographical error regarding the White House's location, directly answers Trump's earlier remarks. The U.S. president had noted Venezuela's proximity, the severe hardship and loss of life there, and affirmed that all alternatives, including potential armed intervention, remain under consideration.

Trump's comments were prompted by President Nicolás Maduro's move to disband the national legislature and install a handpicked constitutional assembly. Presently, Venezuela's armed forces are primarily occupied with suppressing unrest in Caracas. The capital has seen widespread demonstrations due to severe scarcity of food, hyperinflation rendering currency nearly valueless, numerous unexplained arrests, and widespread disorder.

Other Venezuelan officials have also reacted. Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino labeled any potential U.S. military action as "an act of madness." Historically, the United States has repeatedly intervened in the political affairs of Venezuela and other Latin American countries. While past conflicts have not led to Venezuelan forces attacking the White House, the present scenario remains tense, featuring intricate regional crises and a U.S. administration known for its direct approach.

(Source: CNN)

Shaner Elementary in Topeka is one of three elementary schools ceasing elementary operations after this year, and the students there are planning to give it a proper sendoff.
“At Shaner, we’re going to be holding a very special community publishing party,” said Communities in School coordinator Susan Ortega. “This is an opportunity for our students to sort of write a good-bye letter to Shaner, letting us know what their best memories and good times were, as well as if they have something they want to say to the building one last time before they head on to Jardine Academy.
The publishing party event is this coming Sunday, April 23rd from 2 p.m. to 4 p.m. at the school.
“We want our community members, either former students or former staff members to come back in and really have a chance to share their memories, as well,” said Ortega. “At 2:30 on the day of our celebration, we’re going to be recognizing all the former teachers and staff members.”
The Shaner group has been close knit from the beginning.
“We’re talking about a student population that’s been less than 190 students,” said Ortega. “When you consider some of the sizes of the other elementary schools in Topeka, that’s actually a pretty small school. We only have 11 total classes in our entire building. Getting to have that sort of intimate contact with students where you get to see them on a daily basis and you learn every person’s name, it’s been amazing.”
Shaner, Bishop and Avondale West elementary students will combine to form Jardine Academy beginning this fall.
rewrite:
Shaner Elementary in Topeka is among three primary schools that will close their doors for elementary education at the end of this academic year. To mark this transition, the school community is organizing a farewell event.

Susan Ortega, the coordinator for Communities in Schools, explained that Shaner will host a distinctive gathering for the public focused on publishing. The aim is to allow pupils to compose farewell notes to their school. These writings will express their fondest recollections and positive experiences, and offer any final thoughts they wish to share with the building before moving to Jardine Academy.

This publishing celebration is scheduled for Sunday, April 23rd, from 2:00 to 4:00 p.m., to be held at the elementary school. Ortega extended an invitation for previous attendees of the school, including alumni and past employees, to return and contribute their own stories. As part of the festivities, at 2:30 p.m., there will be a special acknowledgment of all former educators and staff members.

Ortega described the school as having always maintained a tightly bonded community. She noted that the enrollment has consistently stayed under 190 children. Compared to other Topeka elementary schools, this is a relatively modest size, with just eleven classes in total. This scale has fostered a familiar environment where staff interact with students daily and know each one by name, an experience Ortega characterized as remarkable.

Starting in the autumn, the student bodies from Shaner, Bishop, and Avondale West Elementary will merge to create the new Jardine Academy.

World production of major foods set records last year, according to this week’s outlook analysis from the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
Cereal stock levels have climbed to all-time highs.
A joint outlook prepared by the OECD and the United Nation’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) predicts weakening growth in global demand for agricultural commodities and food, while anticipating continuing productivity improvements in the sector.
As a result, prices of main agricultural commodities are expected to remain low for the next 10 years.
The report attributes the demand slowdown to a deceleration of demand growth in major emerging economies, stagnating per capita consumption of staple foods and a further gradual decline in global population growth rates.
The global agricultural and fish production is projected to grow by around 20 per cent over the coming decade, but with considerable variation across regions.
Strong growth is expected in developing regions with more rapid population growth, including Sub-Saharan Africa, South and East Asia, and the Middle East and North Africa. By contrast, production growth is expected to be much lower in developed countries, especially in Western Europe.
Declining demand growth for meat products will put a brake on the demand for cereals and protein meal used in animal feed.
With slower consumption and production growth, agricultural and fish trade are projected to grow at about half the rate of the previous decade.
Net exports are expected to increase from land-abundant countries, such as Canada and the Americas.
Countries with high population growth, in particular in the Middle East and North Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa and in Asia, will see rising net imports.
Demand for cereals and vegetable oil for the production of biofuels is expected to be largely unchanged over the forecast period, in contrast with the past decade, when biofuels expansion led to more than 120 million tonnes of additional cereals demand, predominantly corn.
With existing policies in developed countries unlikely to support biofuels expansion, most demand growth will come from developing countries that have introduced policies favouring biofuel use.
In particular, the use of sugarcane for biofuel production is expected to increase.
rewrite:
According to a recent forecast by the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), last year saw unprecedented global harvests for key food items. Inventories of grains have also reached unprecedented levels. A collaborative forecast from the OECD and the UN's Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) suggests that worldwide appetite for farm goods and foodstuffs will expand more slowly, even as farming efficiency keeps rising. Consequently, the costs of primary farm products are forecast to stay depressed over the coming decade.

This projected easing in demand is linked to several factors: key developing nations are seeing their demand growth moderate, per-person intake of basic foods is leveling off, and worldwide population increases are continuing to slow gradually. Overall output from agriculture and fisheries is predicted to rise by approximately one-fifth in the next ten years, though this growth will be unevenly distributed globally. Regions with faster demographic expansion, like Sub-Saharan Africa, South and East Asia, and the Middle East and North Africa, are poised for robust production gains. Conversely, developed nations, especially in Western Europe, will likely experience far more modest increases.

A slowdown in the demand growth for meat will subsequently curb the need for grains and protein meals utilized in animal feed. As both consumption and production expand more slowly, the volume of trade in agricultural and fish products is anticipated to increase at roughly half the pace seen in the last ten years. Nations with ample land resources, including Canada and other parts of the Americas, are expected to boost their net exports. Meanwhile, net imports are set to rise in areas with high population growth, notably the Middle East and North Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa, and parts of Asia.

The need for cereals and vegetable oils to manufacture biofuels is predicted to remain mostly stable in the outlook period. This marks a shift from the previous ten years, when biofuel sector growth drove demand for over 120 million extra tonnes of cereals, mainly corn. Since current policies in developed nations are not expected to encourage further biofuel expansion, any increased demand will primarily originate from developing countries that have enacted policies promoting biofuel consumption. Specifically, the utilization of sugarcane for biofuel production is forecast to rise.

(WFLA) – Wresting Hall of Famer Ric Flair remained hospitalized Monday as his representative made a public plea for prayers.
Over the weekend, Pro Wrestling Sheet reported that the WWE champion had been admitted to a hospital for heart-related issues.
Late Sunday night, Flair’s representative, Melinda Morris Zanoni with Legacy Talent, asked for prayers and positive energy for the wrestler.
“Are u a Fan/Friend of Ric Flair?If so, we need prayers & positive energy 4 our Living Legend as he is dealing w/some tough medical issues,” she said.
On Saturday, she tweeted that the wrestler was in the hospital.
“Yes,Ric in hosp 4routine monitoring.No reason2panic.Yes,many thx2his fiancé&hospstaff.No excuses Ric wld want u2go out 2nite NaturBoy style!”
Flair, age 68, gained fame as a big time wrestler in the late 1970s along with several other wrestlers such as Hulk Hogan, Andre the Giant and ‘Macho Man’ Randy Savage. Flair was especially popular for his antics.
Flair was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2008 and retired after a 36-year career.According to his website, Ric Flair’s robe, his trunks, and the boots he wore at Wrestlemania XXIV, are all on exhibit at the Smithsonian National Museum of American History in Washington DC.
rewrite:
Ric Flair, a celebrated member of the WWE Hall of Fame, was still under medical care on Monday. His agent issued a request for public support and well-wishes. This followed earlier reports over the weekend that the legendary fighter had been hospitalized due to a cardiac condition.

She had previously posted on Saturday to confirm his hospitalization, noting it was for standard observation and urging people not to be overly alarmed. She humorously added that Flair would want his supporters to enjoy their evening in his characteristic flamboyant fashion.

Source: Starrfmonline.com
2017-10-06
Sophia Akuffo, Chief Justice
The Chief Justice Sophia Akuffo has bemoaned the growing indiscipline at the BAR of Ghana as she charges newly enrolled lawyers to be of good behaviour.
According to Justice Akuffo, the high level of indiscipline amongst lawyers in Ghana is alarming and disappointing.
Addressing 208 newly enrolled lawyers to the Ghana BAR at the enrollment ceremony held at the Banquet Hall of the State House Friday, the Chief Justice said the Disciplinary Committee of the General Legal Council (GLC) is overwhelmed by the several misconduct complaints against lawyers.
She charged the newly enrolled lawyers to uphold all the rules governing the Profession they have chosen.
“We are witnessing these days a distressing increase in a number of disciplinary complaints that come before the disciplinary committee of the General Legal Council against lawyers especially the younger ones at the BAR.
“The root cause of most of these is lack of self-discipline and the desire to get rich quick on the part of new lawyers,” the Chief Justice said on Friday.
Justice Akuffo called on the lawyers to at all times observe the rules and ensure that none of them ever appears before the disciplinary committee of the General Legal Council.
rewrite:
On Friday, October 6, 2017, Chief Justice Sophia Akuffo expressed deep concern regarding a perceived decline in professional conduct among legal practitioners in Ghana. Speaking at an enrollment ceremony held at the State House Banquet Hall, she directly addressed 208 new attorneys admitted to the Ghana Bar. Justice Akuffo stated that the current lack of discipline within the profession is both shocking and disheartening.

She revealed that the Disciplinary Committee of the General Legal Council is struggling under the weight of numerous misconduct allegations filed against lawyers. The Chief Justice particularly noted a troubling rise in complaints involving newer members of the Bar. She attributed this trend primarily to a deficiency in personal integrity and an impatient ambition for rapid financial gain among some recent entrants to the field.

In her charge to the newly enrolled lawyers, Justice Akuffo emph urged them to strictly adhere to all ethical standards and regulations of their chosen career. She advised them to consistently uphold these principles, emphasizing that their goal should be to never face proceedings before the disciplinary body. Her message underscored the importance of maintaining professionalism and self-restraint from the very outset of their legal careers.

The club aims to conclude a decade-long absence from England’s highest division and is presently positioned to achieve this, holding second place in the Championship standings, which would secure automatic promotion.

Chelsea is widely known for sending a significant number of its emerging talents to other clubs on temporary arrangements. Their official site notes 37 individuals are currently away on such terms, including recent addition Kasey Palmer, who moved to Derby just before the transfer window closed. Prominent examples such as Tammy Abraham, Kurt Zouma, and Lewis Baker are included, alongside many younger academy products gaining senior-level playing time elsewhere.

A similar, though smaller-scale, practice is evident at Derby County. Last-minute temporary transfers for Chris Martin and Mason Bennett brought the total count of loaned-out Rams players to 17. This group encompasses both established senior squad members and developing talents seeking opportunities beyond the under-23 level.

Key players Jacob Butterfield and Craig Bryson departed during the summer for Sheffield Wednesday and Cardiff City, respectively. Meanwhile, Jason Shackell and Darren Bent are now with Millwall and Burton Albion. These four, along with Max Lowe, Charles Vernam, Callum Guy, Offrande Zanzala, Emil Jakobsen, Martin, and Bennett, have all exited in this transfer period.

Additional individuals who have had loan spells include Alex Cover (Alfreton), Kyron Stabana (Boston), and Kelle Roos (Plymouth). Farrend Rawson was temporarily at Accrington Stanley before making a permanent switch to Forest Green Rovers.

Below is the complete roster of Derby County players currently gaining experience on loan at other clubs:
Jacob Butterfield (Sheffield Wednesday), Craig Bryson (Cardiff City), Timi Max Elsnik (Swindon Town), Kellan Gordon (Swindon Town), Calum Macdonald (Barrow), Nick Blackman (Maccabi Tel Aviv), Henrich Ravas (Gainsborough Trinity), Matthew Taylor (Gainsborough Trinity), Max Lowe (Shrewsbury Town), Charles Vernam (Grimsby Town), Callum Guy (Bradford City), Offrande Zanzala (Accrington Stanley), Emil Jakobsen (VVV Venlo), Jason Shackell (Millwall), Darren Bent (Burton Albion), Chris Martin (Reading), and Mason Bennett (Notts County).
